title: YOUR STORY STARTS HERE.
text: EMBER CORPS / FIELD MANUAL 00 YOUR STORY STARTS HERE. A field guide for fresh Hunters, first-time roleplayers and veterans arriving from D&D 5e. START READING ↘ JOIN THE DISCORD ↗ 500 XP YOUR STARTING BUILD 2 / WEEK FREE DOWNTIME SLOTS NO ROUNDS CONTINUOUS COMBAT 01 GET STARTED 02 IC & OOC 03 LIFE ON DISCORD 04 SPEED & IC 05 FIRST DAY Naruto World: Ember Corps is a persistent, text-based Naruto-inspired roleplaying game. You make a Hunter, roleplay them with other players in Discord, improve them with XP and Downtime, and take them on missions and hunts in a shared world. If you are coming from D&D 5e, the most important thing to know is this: Ember Corps is not played as a weekly party campaign with six-second rounds. The server is the game table. Your character exists between missions. You can roleplay with other characters, train, craft, spar, investigate the world, join GM events and develop relationships whenever play is available. > 5e translation: think of your character sheet as your persistent character, Discord scenes as the campaign table, Missions as adventures, Jutsu as techniques/spells, and XP as both advancement and the currency used to buy much of that advancement. Join the Ember Corps Discord

title: Your First Five Minutes
text: 1. Make a Hunter. Every player character belongs to Haven Ember and the wider Ember Corps. New characters begin with 500 XP at Stray rank. 2. Get the sheet reviewed. A GM checks that the character follows the rules. 3. Roleplay in character. Find other Hunters, start scenes and let your character become part of the setting. 4. Join Missions and Hunts. These are GM-run adventures and major encounters. 5. Spend XP and Downtime. Learn techniques, buy abilities, develop talents, craft or invent equipment, research threats and improve your character. 6. Keep playing the person, not just the build. Relationships, rivalries, discoveries and consequences carry between scenes. You can ask for help. A new player is not expected to know every Jutsu tag, crafting option or combat interaction on day one.

title: IC and OOC: Two Different Worlds
text: If you have only played games around a physical or virtual tabletop, IC may be unfamiliar. IC means In Character. IC channels are the fictional locations where your Hunter speaks, moves and interacts with other characters. Keep all in-world writing in those channels. OOC means Out of Character. OOC channels are where you, the player, ask rules questions, organise scenes, discuss builds, chat and make jokes. IC and OOC always belong in separate channels—do not interrupt an IC scene with a rules question or treat an OOC conversation as something your Hunter heard. IMPORTANT: TWO MEANINGS OF IC In roleplay, IC means In Character . In combat, IC means Initiative Count . Same abbreviation, completely different jobs. IN CHARACTER / IC CHANNEL rp-thread · mission-ic · hunting-ic Write what your Hunter says and does in the appropriate roleplay, mission or hunting channel. OUT OF CHARACTER / OOC CHANNEL general-ooc · mission-ooc · hunting-ooc Ask questions, coordinate scenes and discuss rules in the matching OOC channel. Finding your way around Discord These are the actual channels you will use most often. Some are forum-style channels or threads, so open the relevant post rather than creating a new scene in the wrong place. What you want to do Where to go :--- :--- Ask a general question or meet other players general-ooc Find a roleplay partner or arrange a spar rp-and-spar-request Play a normal IC scene rp-thread Play out a spar sparing-thread Read the roleplay and sparring rules rp-and-spar-rules Find an available mission mission-posting Request a mission mission-requests Play or discuss a mission mission-ic / mission-ooc Keep mission records mission-log Find out about a hunt hunt-announcements or hunts Play or discuss a hunt hunting-ic / hunting-ooc Discuss the Wastes outside character the-wilds-ooc Example: See a mission in mission-posting, organise with the other players in mission-ooc, then write your Hunter's actions in mission-ic. For a hunt, use the corresponding hunting channels. Voice channels such as Mission VC 1/2 are for speaking to other players, not IC text scenes. Activity and XP: Activity is counted wherever you are actively participating on the server, whether that is an IC or an OOC channel. Activity being counted does not mean every message earns roleplay XP. The normal roleplay award of 4 XP per 30 minutes still requires active in-character interaction; follow the relevant rules when logging other activity. Never mix IC and OOC posts just to keep an activity timer going. For example: > IC: Ren pulls his coat tighter around himself and eyes the broken gate. "Something came through here. Recently." > > OOC (in the matching OOC channel): Does Survival apply to tracking whatever made the footprints? An IC scene is an interaction between characters, such as conversation, training or investigation. A GM is needed when the scene requires world information, adjudication or opposition. Example: If someone announces a monster's weakness in an OOC planning channel, your Hunter does not automatically know it. Discover that information through IC play or an appropriate GM-approved source. Your character does not automatically know something because you read it OOC. Likewise, hostility between characters is not hostility between players. Keep the two layers separate. FIELD TIP / 01 You don't have to wait for a GM to start playing. Introduce your Hunter, ask another player for a scene and arrange a scene in rp-and-spar-request, then write it in rp-thread. Keep planning and rules questions in OOC channels.

title: What Do I Actually Do on the Server?
text: Most play falls into four broad activities. 01 / SOCIAL ROLEPLAY Meet Hunters, make friends, create rivalries and earn XP. 02 / ADVENTURE MISSIONS GM-run expeditions, mysteries and dangerous jobs. 03 / DANGER HUNTS Investigate, prepare for and confront monsters. 04 / PROGRESSION DOWNTIME Train, research, craft and develop between scenes.

title: Roleplay
text: Talk to other characters and build a life in Haven Ember. Active IC roleplay awards 4 XP per 30 minutes. Meaningful moments can also earn Roleplay Beats for Bond, Reveal, Drive and Change.

title: Missions
text: Missions are GM-run jobs: expeditions, escorts, investigations, infiltrations, rescues, dangerous journeys and similar operations. They normally award XP based on time and danger, plus Ryō and whatever consequences or discoveries come from the mission.

title: Hunts
text: Hunts are encounters focused around monsters. They can involve preparation and investigation as well as the fight itself. Rewards depend on the creature and its Fight Value.

title: Downtime
text: Downtime represents meaningful work your Hunter does away from active scenes. You receive 2 Downtime Slots each week and can earn additional slots through play, up to 6 per week. Downtime can be used for things such as training, research, crafting and other long-term development. Completed Downtime actions using a slot grant 5 XP.

title: Your Character Sheet, Without the Panic
text: Ember Corps has more numbers than 5e, but you only need to understand what your own character uses. Your Attributes are the foundation of the character. They feed into secondary statistics such as Vitality, HP, Accuracy, Dodge and damage bonuses. Vitality is your first layer of staying power. Damage removes Vitality first. HP represents serious bodily harm. Once Vitality is gone, damage carries into HP. Stamina and Chakra power different parts of your kit. Techniques and strenuous actions cost resources; managing them matters. Skills cover learned competencies outside and inside combat. Abilities are purchased improvements and special capabilities. Talents are larger packages of expertise that develop over time. Jutsu are specific techniques. Their Rank, cost, Speed, Accuracy, damage and tags tell you how they function. Equipment matters. Weapons and armor have their own rules, and players who do not want to craft from scratch can use the pre-made catalogues. You do not need to optimise all of these simultaneously. Pick a character fantasy first, then make the numbers support it.

title: Your First Build: Start With a Job
text: Choose a primary role and two or three Actions that support it. 01 / IDENTITY PICK YOUR FANTASY A lightning-fast melee Hunter, a Hyūga duelist, a ranged scout or a battlefield controller. Choose one primary role first. 02 / ATTRIBUTES SUPPORT YOUR PLAN All five attributes start at 20. Distribute 25 extra points, no more than 10 in one attribute. STR supports physical power, RES durability, CHA chakra, DEX precision and AGI speed. 03 / CORE LOOP CHOOSE 2–3 GO-TO ACTIONS Pick a reliable attack, a defence or escape, and a useful second option. Check their Speed, costs, accuracy and range together. 04 / BACKUP COVER A WEAKNESS Can you handle a distant enemy? What happens when Chakra or Stamina runs low? Do you have a useful skill outside combat? A sample beginner build: the fast close-range Hunter This is a concept, not a mandatory or fully costed character sheet. Prioritise AGI and the attributes your chosen attacks use. Take one quick, affordable melee technique, one defensive option and a way to approach or escape an opponent. Buy abilities that reinforce your chosen attack style rather than spreading XP across unrelated upgrades. Select a weapon from the pre-made catalogue if you want to avoid crafting initially. For example, a Speed 6 attack used twice can create more frequent opportunities than a Speed 12 attack—but only if you can afford its resource costs, reach the enemy and actually hit. A powerful technique that misses or leaves you unable to defend is not automatically a good choice. Spend your starting XP deliberately You begin at 500 XP, Stray rank. Spend XP on the attributes, Jutsu and abilities that make your central idea work. Starting characters also receive Skill Points based on total XP; use those for things your Hunter can do in and out of battle. Choose Uniques and heritage according to their own creation rules, then have a GM review your sheet. If you are under 1,500 XP, the Core Rules allow you to rework your sheet outside combat and events—so your first build is not a permanent trap. BUILD CHECK / BEFORE YOU SUBMIT Can you describe your character in three actions? “I close the distance, strike quickly, and dodge away.” If your chosen stats, techniques, abilities and gear all help you do that, you have a coherent starting build.

title: The Big Difference from 5e: Combat Has No Rounds
text: Combat runs on a continuous timeline called Initiative Counts, usually shortened to IC. Lower IC is earlier in time. Every action has a Speed. After you act, add that Speed to your current IC. The result is when you can act again. COMBAT / THE ONE FORMULA TO REMEMBER YOUR IC + ACTION SPEED = NEXT IC Lower Speed means you act again sooner. The action resolves on your current IC. Example: two Hunters Aya uses a Speed 8 Action on IC 0. Bo uses a Speed 4 Action on IC 3. IC What happens :--- :--- 0 Aya acts and uses a Speed 8 attack. Her next action is IC 8. 3 Bo acts and uses a Speed 4 attack. His next action is IC 7. 7 Bo acts again. 8 Aya acts again. Starting combat Everyone rolls: 1d20 + AGI/10 The highest Initiative roll begins on IC 0. Everyone else subtracts their roll from the highest roll; the difference is their starting IC. If the rolls are 16, 12 and 6, the characters begin on IC 0, IC 4 and IC 10 respectively. When actions happen at the same IC If two Hunters are due to act on the same Initiative Count, they declare and resolve their actions simultaneously. Both actions take effect at the end of that IC. This matters when two attacks might defeat one another, or when techniques physically collide. Advanced Clashes have their own rules; learn them after you are comfortable with the basic timeline. How Speed reductions work An ability or effect might reduce an action's Speed. Normally, its final Speed cannot fall below half its Base Speed, rounded up, and cannot be reduced below 3. Interrupts have special exceptions. A Speed 10 action therefore normally cannot be reduced below Speed 5. Combat time 100 IC = 30 seconds. IC measures actual combat time, not abstract rounds.

title: Reading a Jutsu Stat Block
text: When you find a technique you like, read it in this order: Rank tells you its tier; cost tells you what resource it consumes; Speed tells you when you act again; Accuracy affects whether it connects; Damage tells you what happens on a hit; and Tags determine which other rules and abilities interact with it. Some techniques have additional requirements, handseals, delays, conditions or special effects—read the entire entry before buying it. A quick attack is only useful if it fits your resources and the rest of your build. A slow technique can still be worthwhile if it creates an opening, controls the battlefield or deals enough damage to justify its time cost.

title: Defending Yourself
text: Defensive Interrupts let you respond outside your normal Action slot. Dodge avoids an attack, Parry turns it aside, and Block mitigates damage. Check the attack’s tags, legal timing and your available defences, then pay the chosen Interrupt’s costs and advance your IC. Ask the GM if you are unsure which defence applies.

title: Skills, Rolls and Non-Combat Play
text: Your twelve Skills cover everything from Athletics and Awareness to Research, Medicine, Survival, Espionage and Artisan. When an outcome is uncertain, a GM may call for a relevant roll against a Target Number (TN). Tell the GM what you are attempting and what you are using; do not roll repeatedly until you get a result you like. Researching a monster, preparing supplies and negotiating with another faction can matter as much as attacking it. Logs are your record of advancement and Downtime. Declare rolls in the appropriate bot channel when required, then link the result and describe your action in your log. Your sheet shows what your Hunter can do; your logs show how they got there.

title: Damage, Wounds and Fatigue
text: Vitality absorbs damage before HP. When attacks become serious, Wounds can impose consequences beyond raw damage. Fatigue tracks accumulated exhaustion and can make continued fighting increasingly dangerous. Qualifying combat can award additional XP for Fatigue and Wounds; see Combat XP.

title: Jutsu and Builds
text: Your clan, elements, Talents, equipment and abilities determine which techniques support your role. Start with a reliable attack, a defence or escape, and one useful alternative.

title: XP Is Not a 5e Level Bar
text: Spend XP to improve attributes, learn Jutsu and buy abilities. Total XP also unlocks Skill Points, Talent Points and other progression benefits. Your character therefore grows piece by piece. Two Hunters with similar total XP can spend it very differently and play nothing alike.

title: Hunter Ranks and Classes
text: Hunter progression represents your place within Ember Corps as well as mechanical development. Rank is not a direct replacement for a 5e character level, and Hunter Classes are not D&D classes. Do not assume that choosing one locks you into a traditional Fighter/Wizard/Rogue progression. Treat them as Ember Corps progression systems. Read them after you understand your basic character concept rather than trying to build around unfamiliar labels immediately.

title: Money and Gear
text: Ryō buys equipment. The Equipment & Crafting volume contains the full building system for players who enjoy designing gear, but you do not need to learn crafting to begin. The Pre-Made Weapon Catalogue and Pre-Made Armor Catalogue exist specifically so you can buy functional equipment without becoming an armorsmith on your first day. STILL CONFUSED ABOUT SPEED? Forget everything else for a moment: act when your IC arrives, resolve your action, add its Speed, and write down your next IC. The timeline moves to the next character due to act. READ THE FULL COMBAT RULES ↗

title: A Good First Day
text: If you have just joined, this is enough: 1. Read this guide. 2. Look through Character Creation in Core Rules. 3. Decide what your Hunter is like as a person and what they are good at. 4. Build a 500 XP Stray with help from the community if you want it. 5. Get the sheet reviewed by a GM. 6. Introduce the character IC. 7. Join a scene. 8. Before your first fight, pick one reliable attack and one defence; check their costs and Speed. When combat happens, remember current IC + Speed = next IC. 9. Learn the more detailed rules when they actually become relevant. Nobody benefits from you trying to memorise the entire archive before writing your first IC post. YOUR NEXT MISSION MAKE YOUR HUNTER. JOIN THE STORY. Start with a character concept. The community can help you with the numbers. ENTER THE DISCORD ↗

title: World & Lore
text: EMBER ARCHIVE / WORLD RECORD THE WORLD BEYOND THE WALLS. The old nations are gone. The Bloom is not. Here are the places, events and people a Hunter might know before setting foot in the Wastes. 01 / History 02 / The World 03 / Haven Ember 04 / Haven Figures 05 / Renowned Hunters 06 / The Uncharted World

title: History
text: The Age of Shinobi Before the Wastes, the Five Great Nations divided much of the known world. Their Hidden Villages—Konoha, Suna, Kiri, Kumo and Iwa—trained shinobi, commanded armies and fought wars that reshaped entire regions. Clans guarded their bloodlines and techniques; Kage ruled villages whose names could inspire either loyalty or fear. Fragments of those histories survive in family traditions, damaged manuscripts and the ruins of settlements that have not seen a living inhabitant in generations. The old names still matter. A Hunter might inherit a Hyūga eye, an Uchiha technique or a Yuki tradition, but the loyalties of the Five Great Nations have given way to the immediate demands of survival. Bloodline and birthplace are no longer the same thing. The Bloom The Bloom changed the natural world. Chakra surged through soil, water and living things. Forests swallowed roads and settlements; rivers shifted their courses; ordinary animals grew into creatures with elemental abilities, unnatural armour, regenerative bodies and, in some cases, intelligence. Regions once held by armies became hunting grounds for monsters. The old nations fought to retain their borders. As their territory broke apart, their villages lost contact, trade failed and survivors retreated behind whatever defences they could maintain. The exact beginning of the Bloom has been lost among contradictory records and the generations of upheaval that followed. Its consequences are visible everywhere. The Age of Havens Survivors rebuilt around water, shelter, workable land and whatever old-world infrastructure remained usable. Walls rose around wells and workshops. Sealing arrays were repaired, adapted and passed between settlements that could still trade. The great powers of the old world gave way to Havens: communities whose survival depended on what they could defend and what their Hunters could bring home. Every Haven has its own customs, leaders and relationship with the Wastes. Some protect trade routes; others live behind closed gates. Beyond their walls, the Bloom continues to shape the land, and even familiar territory can become dangerous after a monster migration or a change in the weather.

title: The World Now
text: The Wastes The Wastes are everything beyond the safety of settled territory: overgrown roads, abandoned villages, monster nesting grounds, ruined industrial districts and stretches of wilderness that no living map describes reliably. Herds and predators move between regions. Raiders, scavengers, cults and independent expeditions follow the same routes as merchants and Hunters, each for their own reasons. A journey through the Wastes is as much a test of preparation as combat. A creature's feeding habits may reveal a safe crossing; a fresh trail may mean a migration has begun. A route cleared last season can disappear beneath new growth or fall inside the territory of something far larger than the patrol that first mapped it. Ruins of the Old World Beneath the growth lie the remains of the Five Great Nations: broken fortifications, sealed archives, workshops, transport lines and settlements whose names have outlived their people. Their ruins hold tools, medicines, records and Jutsu that modern Havens can no longer reproduce easily. Recovering them is dangerous work. Some sites are occupied by monsters, while others retain traps, damaged sealing arrays or defence systems built long before the Bloom. Scavengers return with everything from useful scrap to manuscripts that change what a clan believes about its own history. Life Between Havens Trade caravans carry food, medicine, machinery, monster materials and news between settlements. Hunters escort them, chart safer passages and pursue threats that cannot be left for the next convoy. A Haven's relationship with its neighbours may depend on a single road remaining open. Stories travel the same way. A Hunter's title can reach another settlement long before the person does, embellished by frightened witnesses, grateful survivors or rivals with their own version of events. The Bingo Book and the reports carried by returning expeditions help put names to those stories.

title: Haven Ember
text: Built around an underground water system and a pre-Fall transport hub, Haven Ember is one of the larger independent settlements of the Wastes. Several thousand people live within its repaired inner walls and the scrap-built districts that have grown around them. Old sealing arrays reinforce the defences, while the water system beneath the settlement remains central to daily life. Inside the Walls Ember is a working Haven. Farmers tend the land that keeps its people fed; mechanics and smiths salvage and repair the equipment that keeps its gates standing. Clinics treat injuries brought back from the Wastes, markets fill with caravan goods and workshops turn monster materials into tools and weapons. Shrines, homes and training yards occupy the spaces between them. At the monster-processing hall, the remains of a successful hunt become resources for the next. The outer districts are a reminder that the Haven is still growing. Every expansion demands more food, more maintenance and more ground to defend. When a patrol fails to return or a trade route closes, the effects reach far beyond the Corps. The Ember Corps The Ember Corps brings together the people willing to go beyond the walls. Its Hunters include frontline fighters, scouts, Pathfinders, medics, salvagers, researchers, mechanics and specialists whose work rarely earns them a place in a battle song. Crews assemble for particular assignments and change as Hunters recover, train and take on new work. A mission may mean clearing a migration route, escorting a caravan, recovering a lost expedition, studying a new monster or defending a neighbouring Haven. The Corps also trains Strays, maintains the knowledge gathered by its veterans and prepares for threats too large for a single patrol. The Hunters of Ember The Haven's most recognisable Hunters are not all celebrated for the same reasons. Some have earned their names in open battle; others are known for the lives they have saved, the knowledge they have recovered or the defences they have held. Their methods, ambitions and loyalties differ, but their stories meet at Ember's walls. Veterans instruct new Hunters in the training yards, command expeditions and return to duties within the settlement between missions. For a Stray, a renowned Hunter might be a mentor, a superior, a patient in the clinic or simply the person standing watch when the gates open.

title: People of Haven Ember
text: HAVEN LEADERSHIP / CHIEF ADVISOR Giari Uzumaki · Fūinjutsu Giari serves as the Haven’s Chief Advisor and is associated with advanced sealing arts and the preservation of Uzumaki techniques. His recorded distinctions include Seal Savant, Living Archive, Impossible Formulae, Fūinjutsu Master, Sun-Sealer and Grand Sealwright. His expertise in Fūinjutsu and the old Uzumaki arts makes him a formidable presence in the Haven's leadership. CORPS RECORD / STRAY Kagetsu Yoton Yōton · Stray A Hunter of Haven Ember whose recorded traits include Strong-Willed, Energetic and Surging Power. Strong-willed and energetic, Kagetsu is a young Hunter whose surging power has already become part of his reputation among those who know him.

title: Renowned Hunters
text: Huntsmen and Wardens serving Haven Ember.

title: Amot “The Dragon”
text: FRONTLINE / TRAINER Amot “The Dragon” Huntsman · Slayer · Hoshigaki A wyrm-like descendant of the Hoshigaki who turned from his lineage’s usual association with water to Katon. Amot pairs fire Ninjutsu with an enormous sword and is rarely far from the heaviest fighting. Years of combat have made him a fearsome instructor. He drives his trainees hard, sometimes beyond their limits, and his arrogance and recklessness are familiar to anyone who has fought beside him. Yet when the Haven is threatened, Amot is usually found where the fighting is fiercest. Whatever his faults, he wants the next generation to survive the battles he knows are coming.

title: Seiza “Red Hood”
text: RECONNAISSANCE / WALL WATCH Seiza “Red Hood” Huntsman · Pathfinder · Hyūga Raised among stories of legendary Hunters, Seiza came to distrust the pursuit of fame. She believes the strongest Hunters are often those whose names never travel beyond the people they save. She can often be found observing Strays in training or keeping watch from the Haven’s walls. In the field, she favours poison-tipped arrows and the blade, moving with the patience of a Hunter who has no need for an audience. Those who have crossed the Red Hood speak of an enemy who sees them long before they see her.

title: Rias “The Black Asp”
text: BEAST STUDIES / MONSTER TAMING Rias “The Black Asp” Warden · Chirurgeon · Clanless Raised in the wilderness, Rias is more comfortable among beasts than crowds. A pioneer of monster taming and raising, she ventures beyond the walls with her constant companion, Seto. Her understanding of monster behaviour and anatomy makes her an authority on both their care and their destruction. She studies how beasts hunt, feed, heal and react to danger, knowledge that serves her equally well when tending a creature or finding the quickest way to kill it. Though she lacks the raw strength of Ember’s frontline legends, few Hunters understand the monsters of the Wastes as intimately as the Black Asp.

title: Noriko “The Unstoppable Force”
text: BREACH / EMERGENCY RESPONSE Noriko “The Unstoppable Force” Huntsman · Breaker · Jūgo Where many of the Jūgo bloodline struggle to restrain their battle instincts, Noriko meets danger head-on. She earned her title by smashing through Haven Ember’s own walls to reach Strays stranded outside during a monster attack. With a pack of monsters closing on the stranded patrol, Noriko chose the shortest route to them: straight through the fortifications. The rescued Strays and the hole left in Ember’s wall have kept the story alive ever since. She throws herself into a fight with the same abandon, and the Corps has learned that sometimes the fastest way through an obstacle is to let Noriko reach it first.

title: Ikidomari “The Mercifully Bloody Blade”
text: MEDICAL LOGISTICS / RESTRICTED DEPLOYMENT Ikidomari “The Mercifully Bloody Blade” Warder (Legend) · Slayer · Ouyoku Older than she appears, Ikidomari belongs to the same generation as Genzo Arakane, a fact known to only a few senior Corps members. In her youth she was among Ember’s most bloodthirsty Hunters, the central figure in stories of sword sages. An incident brought her close to becoming a Frenzied Hunter before the Ember Lord subdued her; she was subsequently barred from active combat without permission. She now oversees the Corps’ medical logistics and is widely respected as a gentle, maternal physician. Years away from the battlefield have softened her manner, and many younger Hunters know her only as the reassuring presence who oversees their treatment and supplies. Among the Corps’ older generation, the memory of her sword has never entirely faded.

title: Tsundora “The Tundra”
text: CLAN PATRIARCH / CORPS COMMAND Tsundora “The Tundra” Huntsman · Trapper · Yuki Patriarch of the diminished Yuki clan and a leading traditionalist in Haven Ember’s internal politics, Tsundora demands discipline from relatives and comrades alike. His responsibilities to his clan and the Corps often collide. He has forced his granddaughter Yuna towards the Hunter’s path against her wishes, straining their relationship. Within the Corps he commands with a hard sense of duty, prepared to sacrifice a few to protect the many. That resolve is tested whenever the interests of Haven Ember and the future of his own bloodline pull him in different directions.

title: Idetara “Forgotten Son”
text: TRACKING / RECORD RESTRICTED Idetara “Forgotten Son” Warden · Hound · Uchiha A solitary, gloomy Hunter whose arrival and history remain unclear even to those who work beside him. Rumours insist that anyone who grows close to him dies, and that hearing him speak your name seals your fate. Few can say when he first arrived at Ember or what he was before joining the Corps. He speaks little and rarely stays close to others for long. Patrols that follow in his wake find monsters reduced to ash, the ground blackened around them. Whether the stories about his curse are true or not, the Forgotten Son has given the Wastes plenty of reasons to fear his name.

title: Shiki “The Boundary”
text: DEFENCE / EVACUATION Shiki “The Boundary” Huntsman · Anchor · Shiin Shiki enters a battlefield with the confidence of a performer stepping onto a stage. She earned her title during the defence of another Haven, where she raised an enormous Fūinjutsu barrier and held it long enough for civilians to escape. She measures success less by the enemies she defeats than by the people a threat never reaches. For those sheltering behind her, her flamboyance is a promise that the line will hold.

title: Chisato “The Library’s Crow”
text: ARCHIVES / RUIN RECOVERY Chisato “The Library’s Crow” Warden · Scavenger · Clanless Chisato’s family has reportedly preserved fragments of the old world for generations: burned scrolls, damaged journals, forgotten records and broken Jutsu manuscripts. She continues that work in ruins beyond the Havens, recovering knowledge regardless of whether it is useful, dangerous or forbidden. Her command of reconstructed and obscure Jutsu makes her fighting style difficult to anticipate; no two encounters seem to reveal the same repertoire. Some whisper that her knowledge cannot possibly have come from manuscripts alone. Chisato pays little attention to such talk. The possibility that humanity might forget what it once knew frightens her more than the dangers buried in the ruins. The Ember Lord and Genzo Arakane The Ember Lord stands among Haven Ember’s legendary figures. When Ikidomari came close to becoming a Frenzied Hunter, it was the Ember Lord who subdued her, an encounter that ended her unrestricted service on the battlefield and began her long years in medical logistics. Genzo Arakane belongs to the same generation as Ikidomari, a connection known to only a few of the Corps’ senior members. The names of these older Hunters belong to an era whose battles still cast a shadow over the Haven. The Bingo Book Across the Wastes, the Bingo Book gives Hunters a way to identify notable people, track dangerous opponents and recognise names that surface in reports from other settlements. A title may follow a famous rescue, a feared fighting style or a long history of service. Reputation travels faster than its owner, and the same name can inspire admiration in one Haven and dread in another.

title: The Uncharted World
text: Beyond the routes maintained by the Corps lie other Havens, abandoned strongholds and territories where no expedition has returned with a reliable map. Records of the Bloom differ from one settlement to the next, and the fate of many old-world sites remains a mystery. New routes, recovered histories and the stories of returning Hunters continually reshape what Ember knows of the world. For those willing to leave the walls, there are still ruins to explore, creatures to understand and names yet to be written into the history of the Wastes.

title: Minecraft Server
text: EMBER CORPS / MINECRAFT 1.12.2 / PLAYER PACK 1.2.3 BUILD A HOME. HUNT THE WASTES. Ember Corps has a Minecraft world of its own: a dangerous multiplayer survival server where you become a ninja, explore the Wastes, hunt monsters, discover strange places and help turn scattered shelters into thriving Hunter outposts. DOWNLOAD PLAYER PACK ↓ HOW TO PLAY EMBER CORPS PLAYER PACK 1.2.3 EMBER CORPS SERVER JOIN THE WASTES SERVER ADDRESS 216.201.79.143:25565 Minecraft Java 1.12.2 GET THE PLAYER PACK ↓ BECOME A NINJA Choose your path and grow stronger HUNT & EXPLORE The wilds are full of threats BUILD TOGETHER Create outposts worth returning to QUEST & DISCOVER Learn the pack as you play

title: Welcome to the Wastes
text: This is Ember Corps translated into Minecraft: a persistent world built around the fantasy of being a Hunter beyond the safety of Haven. You might spend one night tracking monsters through unfamiliar country, the next expanding a communal kitchen, and the next disappearing underground looking for something nobody else has found yet. Ninja abilities sit alongside dangerous creatures, strange ruins, farming, cooking, modular equipment, ritual magic, engineering and a much harsher wilderness than vanilla Minecraft. You do not need to know every mod before joining. The quest book introduces the important parts as you play. WHAT ARE WE TRYING TO DO? Explore the Wastes and leave your mark on them. Grow from a newly arrived ninja into an experienced Hunter, bring back rare discoveries, establish safe places beyond Haven and build a world that becomes richer because people actually lived in it.

title: Get the pack
text: CURRENT PLAYER VERSION Ember Corps 1.2.3 Minecraft 1.12.2 · Client pack · CurseForge-ready ZIP DOWNLOAD PLAYER PACK ↗ Download the ZIP above and import it into CurseForge as a new profile. Launch the pack from that profile, then use the current server details from the Ember Corps community to join. The pack is already configured for the server. You should not need to assemble the mods yourself.

title: Your first night
text: 01 Choose Your Origin Your first major choice is what kind of ninja you are. Reveal your available Origins, read through them and choose the one that sounds the most fun to play. 02 Follow the Quest Book The quests are your tour through the pack. They introduce survival, ninja training, hunting, building, food, crafting and technology without expecting you to know everything immediately. 03 Make Somewhere Safe Get a bed, food, light and somewhere to store what you find. The world outside is dangerous enough that having a place to return to genuinely matters. 04 Go Hunting Once you have supplies and a few tricks of your own, head out. Explore, fight, loot, find new terrain and bring something useful—or at least a good story—back with you.

title: Controls
text: Most of Minecraft works exactly as you expect. These are the extra controls worth knowing when you first join. If you ever lose a binding, press F7 to print your current Ember Corps controls. Action Default / How :--- :--- Charge chakra Hold Y Ninja dash Sprint, then use your Ninja Dash binding while you have stamina Wall movement Run into a wall while moving and use your ninja movement controls to climb; keep chakra and stamina available Origin Selection F6 Show Ember Corps controls F7 Voice chat menu V Push to talk Caps Lock Lock onto a target G Scout Zoom Hold Z View an item's recipe Hover it in JEI and press R See what an item is used for Hover it in JEI and press U Quest Log Esc → QUEST LOG You can rebind anything from Options → Controls. Movement feels faster than vanilla. You can step smoothly up blocks, use ninja movement abilities and lock the camera onto enemies during fights. Sneak when you want normal, careful movement. Use JEI whenever you are confused by an item. The item list beside your inventory is effectively your recipe book: hover something and press R to learn how to make it or U to see what it can become. CHAKRA IS YOUR LIFELINE Hold Y to charge chakra whenever you have breathing room. Your techniques and mobility depend on it, and running dry in the middle of a hunt can turn a winning fight into a very short trip home. Stamina matters too: dashing and repeated movement can leave you unable to escape when you need it most.

title: Becoming a stronger ninja
text: Your character has two kinds of growth to care about. Ninja XP advances your overall ninja progression, while individual Jutsu have their own XP. Using and training a technique improves that technique toward its next unlocks rather than instantly mastering your entire arsenal. Hold your Ninjutsu caster to inspect the techniques available to you and their progress. Training Scrolls are especially valuable: hold the scroll in your main hand and the appropriate caster in your offhand, then use the scroll to train the selected Jutsu. A training scroll grants +75 Jutsu XP when that technique can still gain XP, and is not consumed if it cannot. The quest book is one of your most reliable early sources of Ninja XP and Training Scrolls. Hunt, complete objectives, train the techniques you actually want to use and keep checking your caster as new options open up. 01 Charge Before Trouble Top up your chakra before leaving shelter, entering a cave or committing to a dangerous fight. 02 Mobility Keeps You Alive Dash to create distance, use vertical terrain and learn to move along walls instead of fighting everything from the ground. A ninja who can disengage gets another attempt. 03 Train Your Favourite Jutsu Jutsu improve individually. Put your Training Scrolls and practice into techniques you enjoy rather than expecting every ability to grow together. 04 Prepare Like a Hunter Ninja powers do not replace food, armour, storage or common sense. Carry supplies, know the route home and do not spend every resource before the real fight begins.

title: Great powers of the ninja world
text: The server starts you as a ninja. It does not expect you to stay ordinary. 眼 DŌJUTSU Eyes that change the fight Sharingan, Byakugan, Rinnegan and other rare eyes exist within the world. Dōjutsu can completely change what your character is capable of, and some of the rarest eye powers are prizes worth building an entire journey around. 尾 TAILED BEASTS Power with a heartbeat The Tailed Beasts are part of the world. Finding one is one thing; surviving the encounter and reaching the point where its power can become part of your story is another. They are major goals, not starter equipment. 禁 FORBIDDEN HEIGHTS There is always something beyond you Bloodline powers, transformations, advanced Jutsu and exceptionally rare discoveries can push a character far beyond their beginnings. The strongest rewards are things to chase, discover and earn through play. Discover rare powers through exploration and play.

title: What can I do?
text: There is no single correct way to play. The server is at its best when people develop their own corner of the world and then cross paths with everyone else's. 忍 Become a Ninja Choose an Origin, learn techniques, collect training rewards and gradually build a character with their own fighting style. 狩 Hunt the Wastes Leave the roads, explore new country and take on creatures that make ordinary Minecraft mobs look like wildlife. 築 Build an Outpost Turn a hole in the ground into somewhere Hunters recognise: beds, kitchens, workshops, farms, storage, roads and places worth visiting. 探 Find Something New Ruins, resources, creatures and useful locations are scattered through the world. Exploration is valuable even when you are not looking for a fight. A good way to start Don't try to speedrun the modpack. Follow the opening quests, get a backpack, make yourself a proper home and learn how your ninja abilities work. Then pick a direction and go far enough that returning safely starts to feel like an achievement. As you settle in, decide what your character contributes. Maybe you are the person who hunts dragons. Maybe you cook for expeditions, build roads between settlements, obsess over weapon crafting, run a farm, maintain the workshop or keep wandering until the map has no blank spaces left.

title: A few things you'll meet
text: CRAFT YOUR GEAR Tetra Build modular tools and weapons at your workshop, then change their parts as you find better materials and decide what kind of equipment suits you. SEE TETRA ↗ BIG PROBLEMS Ice and Fire The wilderness contains creatures you are absolutely not expected to punch on sight. Dragons and other monsters turn expeditions into actual hunts. SEE ICE & FIRE ↗ WITCHCRAFT & RITUALS Roots Grow herbs, prepare strange ingredients and experiment with nature magic. It gives builders, farmers and explorers another path beyond machines and combat. SEE ROOTS ↗ BUILD A WORKSHOP Actually Additions Turn your outpost into a working base with generators, powered processing and useful machines that make long-term settlement feel worthwhile. SEE ACTUALLY ADDITIONS ↗ ORGANISE THE HAUL Simple Storage Network Connect the chests in a developed outpost into one searchable storage system. The more your settlement grows, the more useful it becomes. SEE SIMPLE STORAGE ↗ STAY OUT LONGER Improved Backpacks Carry the supplies and loot an expedition actually needs. Better packs mean longer journeys before you have to turn back for home. The pack also expands food, farming, storage, decoration, exploration and workshop machinery. You will discover most of it naturally through quests and other players.

title: Life at an outpost
text: Outposts are the heart of the server. They are places made by players for players: a safe bed after a long trip, a stocked kitchen before a hunt, a workshop for new equipment, a storehouse full of materials or simply somewhere memorable enough that people start using its name. START Survive the night. Make shelter, light the area, find food and give yourself somewhere safe to return to. GROW Make it useful. Add farms, storage, kitchens, workshops and whatever your group needs to stay away from Haven for longer. LEAVE A MARK Make it a place. Build roads, lodges and settlements. Name them. Give other Hunters reasons to visit. Let the server develop its own geography and history.

title: Hunting, death and getting home
text: Keep Inventory is enabled. Dying will not erase hours of equipment progress, but it still leaves you vulnerable for a while. Bring food. Bring light. Bring enough inventory space. Know roughly how you are getting home. If you see something enormous in the distance, remember that turning around is also a ninja technique. Loot beams help valuable drops stand out after fights, and backpacks let you stay away from home much longer than vanilla inventory would. As your outpost improves, preparing for expeditions becomes quicker and the places you can safely reach become farther away.

title: Play together
text: The server includes proximity voice chat. Press V to set up your microphone and use Caps Lock to talk. Voices become quieter with distance, so stumbling across another Hunter in the wild feels very different from sitting together at an outpost. You are free to wander alone, but the world is deliberately more fun when players rely on one another. Share discoveries. Build places together. Rescue somebody who went too far from home. Organise hunts. Leave supplies at distant shelters. Create things future players will stumble across. READY TO ENTER THE WASTES? Make a ninja. Pack your supplies. See how far you get. title: Clans & Lineages
text: Clans & Lineages

title: Heritage Rules
text: Every player character belongs to Haven Ember and serves in the Ember Corps. Heritage describes ancestry, inherited physiology, family techniques, or surviving schools of training; it does not grant citizenship or allegiance to an old Hidden Village. Choose one Primary Heritage. Mixed ancestry is valid narratively, but only your Primary Heritage grants its starting features, affinities, exclusive abilities, and clan-jutsu access unless a rule explicitly says otherwise. Heritage Cost is paid from the 6 Unique Points granted at character creation. It is not a Unique, does not count toward Creation Uniques, and is not paid again later.

text: 0 UP: Sarutobi, Fūma, Yotsuki, Ouyoku, Karatachi Family, Funato, Iburi, Shiin, Clanless. 1 UP: Nara, Yamanaka, Kamizuru, Hokori, Hoshigaki, Silverhand, Samsara, Jinrō, Jashin Worshipper, Insect Glaive Corps, Vanguard Corps 2 UP: Aburame, Akimichi, Hyūga, Inuzuka, Senju, Uzumaki, Kazekage Clan / Jiton, Shakuton, Yōton, Hōzuki, Yuki, Futton, Jūgo's Bloodline, Ballistic Corps 3 UP: Uchiha, Bakuton, Kaguya, Karashi (Puppets).

title: Clanless
text: HERITAGE — SELF-MADE Clanless Hunters come from families without a surviving bloodline or secret technique. Some are refugees or settlers; others have lost their ancestral teachings or chosen a different path. They build their skills through practice, shared instruction and experience in the Wastes.

title: No Inheritance
text: While those around you spent their early days inheriting power from their ancient bloodlines, all you inherited was hard work and debt. You start with 100% additional Ryo (100,000 Total), and instead of the Usual 25 Stat Points, you start with 30. Finally, all abilities with the Willpower type cost 50% XP for you, at all stages. Additionally, you gain an additional Talent point every 1500 XP earned (1500XP, 3000XP, 4500XP…)

title: Self-Taught
text: Clanless hunters are not locked into an inherited curriculum. During each Week's Rest, you may retrain one or more non-Heritage Jutsu or Abilities with a combined XP cost of up to 10. Remove the chosen options, then immediately spend the same amount of XP on other non-Heritage Jutsu or Abilities you currently meet the requirements for. You cannot retrain Talents, Uniques, Attributes, Skills, Heritage options, or anything granted for free. Retraining never grants XP, and any unused portion of this 10 XP allowance is lost when that Week's Rest ends.

title: Jack of All Trades
text: Clanless hunters are used to reaching for whichever tool works, rather than waiting for the one technique their family taught them. When you make an Attack, Defensive Roll, Skill Check, Status Resistance Roll, Stamina Exhaustion Roll, or Chakra Exhaustion Roll, you may use Adaptability to add +2 to the roll after rolling but before the result is resolved. After using Adaptability, you cannot use it on the same kind of roll as your previous use for the rest of combat. Attack, Defense, Skill, Status Resistance, Stamina Exhaustion, and Chakra Exhaustion are separate kinds of roll. Outside combat, Adaptability may be used once per scene instead.

title: Dig Deep
text: Once per Battle, when you or an ally within 10 yards would fail an Attack, Defensive Roll, Skill Check, Status Resistance Roll, Stamina Exhaustion Roll, or Chakra Exhaustion Roll, you may advance 1 Fatigue Level to add +5 to the result. This can turn a failure into a success. You cannot use Dig Deep if advancing Fatigue would Incapacitate you.

title: Fūma
text: CANON CLAN Fūma descendants preserve a weapon tradition built around giant shuriken, wire and deceptive trajectories. Haven Ember employs them in ranged combat and pursuit.

title: Fūma Skill
text: The Limit for the Quick Hands ability is DEX/18 instead of DEX/20 for you.

title: Fūma Power
text: Whenever you would throw a Shuriken of any kind or size, or any shuriken-like object, you may use your DEX, AGI, STR or CHA for its damage bonus. Additionally, you ignore up to one singular penalty to the Accuracy of your Shuriken or Shuriken-like attacks. This could be a wound, or it could be a single level of Fatigue. Treat this like “Strong-Willed” in the way it works, as whenever something else would hinder the Accuracy of your Shuriken, you may swap to ignoring that, and take the new penalty that you would ignore. In relation to conditions, this could ignore all ranks of that Condition.

title: Fūma Mastery
text: Your thrown weapons have no need for ranges. You can hit anything you can physically see, regardless of range. If used in combat, or to attack, the attack gets a -1 to it’s ACC for every 3 yards outside the weapon’s normal range the target is.

title: Fūma Arsenal
text: Type: Ability Base Cost: 8 Scale: 6 Limit: 4 Effects Increase the maximum Range of thrown weapons by 5 yards per rank. Increase the number of weapons you can throw as part of a Multi-Throw by 1 per rank. Once per Attack, reduce Visibility penalties against a thrown weapon by 1 per rank.

After seeing the target's first Defense result, you can force them to reroll that Defense against the second trajectory. If you do, the attack deals 75% Final Damage and cannot inflict a Wound above Major. C-Rank

title: Fūma Shuriken: Engetsu - Returning Crescent
text: C-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank C Stamina: 14 Damage: As Weapon Accuracy: -1 Range: Weapon Range +10 Speed: As Weapon +4 Tags: Attack, Projectile, Weapon Effects Choose one bend point within half the Attack's maximum Range. Draw the projectile's path from you to that point and then to the target; both segments must be physically clear. Measure the projectile’s clear path from its bend point. It may pass around a corner but cannot pass through a solid obstacle or sealed barrier. After the Attack resolves, the weapon returns along the same path if that route remains clear. Catching it is Speed 0.

title: Funato
text: CANON ANIME CLAN - RARE Funato descendants retain the gill-like markings and maritime techniques of their ancestors. They patrol waterways, recover submerged supplies and hunt aquatic monsters.

title: Sea Legs
text: Funato are comfortable on moving decks, in surf, and under water long before they learn to weaponise the sea. Gain +2 Athletics and +2 Survival on checks primarily involving swimming, diving, currents, navigation, boats, or remaining stable on a moving vessel. Mundane water, waves, rain, and the motion of a vessel do not impose an Awareness penalty on you by themselves. This does not remove supernatural terrain or environmental effects.

title: Sea Dragon Blood
text: Type: Ability Cost: 20 Scale: 10 Limit: XP/500 Effects You can breathe underwater and move through natural bodies of water at +10% movement per rank. Suiton techniques using at least 20 gallons of natural water cost 1 less Chakra per rank, minimum 1.

On a full hit, choose whether each target is pushed toward the far end or pulled toward the near end. .

title: Iburi
text: CANON ANIME CLAN - RARE The Iburi can transform their bodies into chakra-bound smoke. Their training emphasises infiltration and escape, alongside protection from winds that can disperse them.

title: Passives
text: No additional Heritage passives.

title: Smoke Body
text: Type: Ability Cost: 15 Upkeep: 4 Speed: 5 Limit: 1 Effects While active, you can pass through non-chakra-reinforced openings at least an inch wide and gain +4 Dodge against non-AoE physical attacks. You may move through a creature’s occupied space if there is a physically open path for smoke, but may not end movement inside another creature. While fully smoke-bodied you cannot normally use weapons, make Taijutsu attacks, use Handseals or Cast Jutsu. You can however use Grapple Jutsu. When you do, the opposing creature gains advantage on all associated Grapple Defence moves, you cannot - however, deal damage with any grapple technique while smoke-bodied. You gain the following Link while Smoke Body is active:

title: Partial Reformation — [Chakra 5, Speed +2, Link]
text: Link this to a Melee Attack, Grapple action, item interaction, or Perform Handseals action. You reform the body parts required to perform that action. Until the linked action fully resolves, you are treated as solid and do not receive Smoke Body’s +4 Dodge bonus. Afterward, you immediately return to smoke if Smoke Body is still active. Ending Smoke Body is Speed 3. Fūton attacks against you while Smoke Body is active gain +3 Accuracy. On a full hit, end Smoke Body and suffer Stun 6 in addition to the attack’s normal effects.

text: D-Rank

title: Kemuri Kakure - Vanishing Haze
text: D-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 12 Speed: 8 Tags: Utility, Self, Smoke Requires: Smoke Body active Effects Until the end of your next Action, reduce penalties to Stealth caused by moving by 5 and treat your body as ordinary environmental smoke for the purpose of mundane attempts to identify which part of a larger smoke cloud is you. Attacking, forming obvious handseals through Partial Reformation, or leaving all smoke or concealment ends this effect. C-Rank

title: Kemuri Utsusemi - Smoke Cicada Escape
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 20 Speed: 4 Tags: Interrupt, Self, Movement Effects Requires Smoke Body active. Use as a Defensive Interrupt against a non-AoE attack. Make a Dodge with +2. On success, move up to NDB yards to a location air could physically reach and end Smoke Body. On failure, resolve the attack normally and Smoke Body remains subject to its usual weaknesses.

title: Karatachi Family
text: CANON FAMILY Descendants of old Mist leadership, the Karatachi preserve a tradition of discipline and public service. Their family name grants no office in Haven Ember.

title: Stand Your Ground
text: After you finish an Action without voluntarily moving during that Action, you become Braced until the start of your next Action. While Braced: - Gain +2 to Block and Parry. - Gain +3 to rolls made to avoid Aborting an Action because of damage. - Reduce hostile Knockback, pulls, or other forced movement by 2 yards, minimum 0. - Gain +2 on any roll specifically made to remain standing or resist being moved. Braced ends immediately if you voluntarily move. Being moved by an enemy does not end Braced until that movement has fully resolved.

title: Mist-Born Discipline
text: Type: Ability Base Cost: 8 Scale: 6 Limit: 3 Effects Gain +1 per rank to Stamina Exhaustion rolls and to Resistance rolls against fear-based Immobilization effects. While Braced, also gain +1 per rank to rolls made to resist Stun, Immobilization, Knockback, forced movement, or an effect that would make you Prone, when that effect allows a roll. Once per combat, after rolling one of the above rolls or a roll to avoid Aborting an Action, you may add +2 per rank before the result is resolved.

title: Ouyoku
text: RARE LINEAGE - SETTING ORIGINAL The Ouyoku descend from observatory families. Their Junsugan helps them see through darkness and across distant or difficult sightlines, making them valued reconnaissance specialists.

title: Passives
text: No additional Heritage passives.

title: Junsugan
text: Type: Dōjutsu Ability Cost: 20 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 1 Limit: 1 Effects While active, gain 240-foot-equivalent Darkvision and 120-foot-equivalent Chakra Sight for narrative-scale perception. In combat, extend ordinary visual Search Range to the battlefield limit unless terrain blocks sight. With this you can see around corners, through invisible barriers such as glass, and off of reflections. This gives you utter visual knowledge of the battlefield from all angles. It does not automatically reveal people or chakra, simply extending your visual sight to everywhere. You can see everything on the battlefield that is not behind an opaque barrier or wall of some kind. Gain +4 Search against targets 20 or more yards away and ignore the first -3 Visibility penalty from distance, darkness, smoke, or weather. The Junsugan does not see through solid obstacles and does not identify techniques automatically.

title: Jutsu
text: C-Rank

title: Kyōkai Ayumi - Boundary Step
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 20 Range: Self Speed: 8 Tags: Utility, Self, Movement, Dōjutsu Effects Requires Junsugan active. Move up to to a location you can clearly see. This movement cannot pass through barriers, creatures, or sealed space. If used from Stealth it reduces your Stealth TN by 5 but does not automatically break Stealth.

title: Sarutobi
text: Sarutobi families preserve fire techniques, weapon training and generations of teaching. Their broad training serves Haven Ember’s patrols and instructors.

title: Passives
text: No additional Heritage passives.

title: A Thousand Familiar Lessons
text: Type: Ability Base Cost: 10 Scale: 10 Limit: XP/500 , Max 3 Effects Rank 1: Choose Accuracy, Dodge, Parry, or Chakra Exhaustion. Gain +1 to the chosen value, this increases by +1 for each rank you gain in this ability. Rank 2: Gain Elemental Affinity: Jutsu. This special Affinity applies to all Ninjutsu, Genjutsu and Taijutsu, following the normal rules for Affinity. Your ranks in this Affinity are equal to your XP/200, with a Maximum of 10. This does not grant Aptitudes you don’t normally have access to, even if you have Affinity for Lightning, you may not learn Lightning Jutsu without the appropriate Aptitude. Rank 3: Using the Mentor downtime action, you can learn any Jutsu that you have witnessed, without the help of a teacher. This includes Jutsu that are limited to certain clans, and speciality jutsu that you would normally not apply for. For each rank above your normal limit this Jutsu is, increase it’s costs by 50% (including seal speed), and if that clan would require a special Clan feature that you don’t possess, such as a Sharingan, or a Kekkei Genkai that you don’t have, you also double any CE/STM penalties that Jutsu would give you.

title: Tanjun Hien - Simple Flying Swallow

For that Attack, increase the weapon's Reach by 1 yard and ignore 2 points of Damage Reduction per point you beat their defences by. The Attack also counts as dealing +10% damage for the purpose of determining Wounds per point you beat their defence. A weapon must have a defined striking edge or point to use Hien. C-Rank

title: Haisekishō - Burning Ash
text: C-Rank Type: Katon Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 24 Damage: 18d8>!8 Range: 20 Area: 15 Speed: 14 Seal Speed: 16 Special: Ignite 4 Tags: Attack, AoE, Environmental, Energy Effects The ash persists for 30 IC. Visibility inside it is -2. You can detonate the cloud with any damaging Katon that touches it. When detonated, creatures inside defend against this technique using the original Accuracy; afterwards the cloud ends.

title: Shiin
text: CANON ANIME CLAN - OLD SOUND The Shiin preserve a closely guarded memory-altering tradition from the old Sound. Haven Ember watches its use in intelligence work and teaches strict limits on its deployment.

title: Memory Reader
text: You can deliberately skim a recent sensory memory from another person.

title: [Speed 10, Chakra 10, Utility, Touch, Genjutsu] Read Memory
text: Against a willing or unconscious living target, no attack roll is required. Against a resisting target, make a normal Genjutsu Attack at Touch range. On a full hit, ask one specific question about something the target personally saw, heard, smelled, tasted, or physically felt within the last 24 hours. The answer is limited to what the target actually perceived; it does not reveal deductions, secret information they never knew, or memories already removed or supernaturally sealed. A target can be unwillingly read by you only once per scene. A willing target can share any number of memories at the GM’s discretion.

title: Sound-Hidden Tradition
text: Shiin Clan Genjutsu may use a flute, ocarina, whistle, song, or other clearly audible performance as their casting medium instead of handseals. Doing so does not reduce the technique’s Speed or other costs. A creature that cannot hear the performance cannot be affected by a Shiin technique cast this way. Silence or an effect that completely blocks sound prevents the casting.

title: Abilities
text: No Heritage-specific purchasable abilities.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Oto Genjutsu: Karigoe - Borrowed Voice
text: D-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 10 Range: 25 Speed: 8 Tags: Utility, Genjutsu, Sound Effects Create a voice or other sound you have personally heard, originating from any point in Range. The sound may speak words you choose, but it cannot convincingly reproduce information, accents, passwords, or verbal habits you have never heard from the source. If you have successfully Read Memory containing the sound or voice, the reproduction is exact. A suspicious observer may contest your Genjutsu Accuracy with Awareness to identify it as false.

title: Kioku Utsushi - Memory Projection
text: D-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 14 Range: 15 Area: 6 Speed: 10 Tags: Utility, Genjutsu Effects Project a short sensory scene from a memory you have personally experienced or successfully read. Choose up to 30 seconds of sight and sound. Creatures in the Area perceive the scene as an illusion layered over the real environment. This technique does not control behaviour or conceal physical interaction with the real world. It is useful for showing witnesses exactly what someone remembers, reconstructing a crime scene, creating a distraction, or demonstrating a face, route, voice, or event without relying on description. C-Rank

title: Magen: Kuzureuta - Broken Refrain
text: C-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 22 Accuracy: -1 Range: 20 Area: Cone 8 Speed: 14 Special: Stun 2 Tags: Attack, Genjutsu, Sound, Control Effects A discordant phrase catches in the target’s perception and repeatedly interrupts the transition between thought and action. On a full hit, apply Stun 2. Until the end of the target’s next Action, the first Utility Action they declare has its final Speed increased by 3. If cast through Sound-Hidden Tradition, targets must be able to hear you when the technique resolves.

title: Kioku Sōshitsu - Memory Blocking Technique
text: C-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 24 Accuracy: -1 Range: 15 Speed: 14 Seal Speed: 18 Tags: Attack, Genjutsu Effects On a full hit, choose one specific event, face, place, or piece of information the target personally experienced within the last month. For 1 hour they cannot consciously recall it.

title: Yotsuki
text: CANON CLAN The Yotsuki preserve the bodyguard training of the old Cloud. They specialise in physical conditioning and protecting their companions from incoming attacks.

title: Bodyguard’s Instinct
text: When you declare Take the Hit for an ally, you may move up to 2 yards toward that ally before resolving the action. This movement costs no AP or Speed, cannot pass through occupied spaces or solid barriers, and can only be used to enter or maintain a legal position for Take the Hit. If Take the Hit succeeds, the protected ally gains +2 on their next Defensive Roll before the end of their next Action. This bonus is lost if they use it against the same attack that you intercepted.

title: Shoulder of the Cloud
text: Type: Ability Base Cost: 8 Scale: 6 Limit: 4 Gain +1 per rank to Take the Hit rolls. When you successfully Take the Hit for an ally, regain 2 AP per rank, up to your normal maximum. After a successful Take the Hit, reduce the intercepted attack’s Final Damage against you by 5% per rank, counting after all other reductions. After that attack resolves, the protected ally may move up to 1 yard per rank without AP or Speed.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Raiton: Ikazuchi Ayumi - Thunder Intercept
text: D-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 12 Speed: +2 Tags: Link, Raiton, Movement, Interrupt, Self Effects Link this technique to Take the Hit or to a Defensive Interrupt made against an Attack targeting an adjacent willing ally. Before that defense resolves, move up to AGI/10 yards toward a legal interception point. This movement must end within reach of the ally or on a space that allows the linked defense to function. If linked to a successful Take the Hit, gain +2 on your first valid Defensive Interrupt against the intercepted Attack. Thunder Intercept cannot move through barriers or effects that would normally stop movement. C-Rank

title: Raiton: Raimei Tate - Thunder Guard
text: C-Rank Type: Raiton Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 22 Speed: +3 Tags: Interrupt, Link, Raiton, Self Effects Link this to Take the Hit, a Block Interrupt, or use it on it’s own as a Speed 3 interrupt when you would take damage or effects. Reduce the Final Damage you take by NDB × 4, counting after all other reductions, then the attacker gains Paralysis 2 for 20 IC if they were within 2 yards.

title: Heritage Up 1
text: 1 UP HERITAGES 11 ENTRIES

title: Hokori
text: RARE LINEAGE - DUST RELEASE Haven Ember’s archives use Hokori as a catch-all name for the vanishingly rare descendants capable of maintaining the three-way elemental equilibrium behind Dust Release. Fire provides compression, Wind gives the boundary direction, and Earth stabilizes the structure long enough for chakra to separate matter inside it. The old stories call that “erasure.” Modern Hokori instructors are less romantic: a failed boundary is usually harmless, but a successful one leaves very little behind. Hokori are therefore trained less like artillery and more like surveyors. They study angles, materials, sightlines, and where an enemy can be forced to stand. In combat, a Hokori is at their best when allies create the opening and the Dust user turns that opening into a precisely measured kill-zone.

title: Particle Intuition
text: Hokori training makes the structure of solid matter unusually intuitive. As a Speed 5 Utility Action while touching an unattended solid object, terrain feature, or created barrier, you may make a Chakra Control check in place of Research, Artisan, or Survival to determine its composition, approximate thickness, hollows, seams, and obvious structural weaknesses. The GM sets the TN based on complexity. This is analysis, not supernatural omniscience. It does not reveal hidden creatures, seals, poison, ownership, history, or chakra properties you could not otherwise sense, and it grants no direct Accuracy or Damage bonus.

title: Three-Nature Equilibrium
text: Type: Ability Cost: 25 Limit: 1 Requires: Katon, Fuuton, and Doton Aptitudes Effects Gain Elemental Affinity: Jinton. Jinton is treated as its own element and does not include its component elements. Whenever a Jinton Perform Handseals action is interrupted by damage, gain +3 to the Chakra Control check to maintain it. Jinton techniques cannot have their Seal Speed reduced below half their listed Seal Speed by any source.

title: Calibration
text: After combat begins, the first time a Katon, Fuuton, or Doton Jutsu with a Final Chakra Cost of at least 10 resolves and meaningfully affects another creature, object, or the battlefield, gain that nature’s Calibration. You may hold one Katon, one Fuuton, and one Doton Calibration at a time. They last until the end of battle or until spent. When declaring a Jinton technique, you may spend any Calibration you hold: Katon — Compression: You may reduce the technique’s Area by up to half. If you reduce it to half, reduce its inherent Accuracy penalty by 1, to a minimum penalty of 0. Fuuton — Projection: Increase the technique’s Range by 10 yards. Doton — Stability: Gain +5 on Chakra Control checks made to prevent that technique from collapsing. Perfect Equilibrium: If you spend all three different Calibrations on the same Jinton technique, also reduce its Delay by 3, to a minimum Delay of 3. A Jutsu cannot generate Calibration from Jinton itself, and spending a Calibration removes only the Calibration spent. This means a Hokori can build toward one perfect boundary or repeatedly use smaller pieces of their setup.

title: Jinton Techniques
text: C-Rank

title: Jinton: Keii Kekkai - Coordinate Lattice
text: Type: C Rank - Jutsu Chakra: 18 Damage: 20d4!o>3 Range: 30 Area: 12 Speed: 8 Seal Speed: 20 Tags: Utility, AoE, Energy, Jinton Requires: Three-Nature Equilibrium Effects Create a stationary, translucent geometric lattice centered on a point within range. It remains for 30 IC, and you may have only one Coordinate Lattice active at a time. When created, unattended nonliving objects and created barriers inside the Area take this technique’s damage. This damage cannot affect creatures or anything currently worn or carried. Against created barriers, it ignores Armor and doubles Final Damage. The first time you declare a damaging Jinton technique whose center is inside your Coordinate Lattice, you may consume the lattice and choose one: Focus — reduce that technique’s inherent Accuracy penalty by 1, to a minimum penalty of 0. Anchor — gain +5 on checks made to prevent that technique from collapsing. Guide — reduce that technique’s Delay by 2, to a minimum Delay of 3. The lattice is obvious to anyone who can see it. Enemies are free to leave it, which is exactly why Hokori crews value immobilization, forced movement, and coordinated positioning. B-Rank

title: Jinton: Genkai Hakuri - Boundary Detachment
text: Type: B Rank - Jutsu Chakra: 40 Damage: 40d6!o>4 Accuracy: -4 Range: 30 Area: 8 Speed: 22 Delay: 8 Seal Speed: 30 Tags: Attack, AoE, Energy, Jinton Effects This technique ignores Armor but not DR. Against unattended objects and created barriers, Final Damage is doubled. During the Delay, the forming boundary is visible. If you suffer a Major or worse Wound before it resolves, make Chakra Control TN 20; on failure the technique collapses and deals no damage. A-Rank

title: Jinton: Hakuri Kekkai - Detachment Prism
text: Type: A Rank - Jutsu Chakra: 55 Damage: 150d4!o>2 Accuracy: -5 Range: 45 Area: 15 Speed: 28 Delay: 15 Seal Speed: 40 Tags: Attack, AoE, Energy, Jinton Effects Ignore Armor and half DR. This attack cannot be made a surprise or sneak attack. From declaration until resolution, you cannot take non-Defensive Actions without aborting the technique. Any Major or worse Wound forces Chakra Control TN 25 or the technique collapses. If this attack wounds a limb, that limb is destroyed. If this attack inflicts a critical wound, the target dies, and their body evaporates into nothing. This technique destroys all objects, terrain, mists, or anything within it’s area.

title: Hoshigaki
text: CANON CLAN Hoshigaki descendants retain the shark-like physiology and water techniques of their Water Country ancestors. They serve in boarding crews, underwater recovery and aquatic hunts.

title: Passives
text: No additional Heritage passives.

title: Feeding Pressure
text: Type: Ability Base Cost: 8 Scale: 6 Limit: 4 Effects When you begin an Action while within 10 yards of a creature suffering Bleed or a Major+ open Wound, gain +1 Movement per rank for that Action. Additionally, you deal +10% damage per rank to creatures suffering Bleed or an open Major+ Wound for determining Wounds. After damaging such a target in melee, regain 1 AP per rank, up to your maximum.

title: Shark Physiology
text: Type: Ability Cost: 18 Scale: 10 Limit: XP/1000,2 Effects You can breathe underwater and suffer no ordinary penalties for fighting while submerged. Suiton Ninjutsu cannot force you to Suffocate, gain Immob, cause Bleeding or any Wound above Minor. Use AGI instead of STR for ordinary swimming calculations if higher. Gain +3 Awareness to detect bleeding creatures in the same connected body of water. At the second Rank of this ability, your speed doubles while swimming, and you deal an additional +25% damage with Suiton Jutsu.

title: Jutsu
text: B-Rank

title: Suiton: Sameodori Kekkai - Shark-Dance Water Prison
text: B-Rank Type: Suiton Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 34 Upkeep: 8 Range: 12 Area: 10 Speed: 18 Seal Speed: 22 Tags: Attack, AoE, Environmental, Suiton Effects On a full hit, create a mobile water sphere centered halfway between you and the target. You and hit targets are submerged while inside. The sphere follows you up to 3 yards per IC. A creature may leave by reaching the edge using normal movement; forced movement also works. While both you and a damaged target are inside, gain +2 Accuracy against that target. Raiton techniques affecting the sphere treat all creatures inside as valid targets where appropriate.

title: Insect Glaive Corps
text: WEAPON TRADITION - SETTING ORIGINAL The Insect Glaive Corps began with Wastes hunters who discovered that some chakra-active insects could do more than track prey. Properly bred, fed, and bonded, they could taste the different ways chakra moved through a living body - aggression in the limbs and jaws, motion through the legs and wings, stability through the torso and shell - then carry that stolen rhythm back to a hunter. The first glaives were practical hunting tools: long polearms for keeping claws and teeth away, hollowed through the haft so a bonded insect could launch, return, and nest against the wielder's arm. What began as monster-hunting fieldcraft became one of Haven Ember's strangest martial schools. Modern Corps hunters fight as a pair. The hunter creates openings, the Kinsect steals a fragment of the enemy's fighting rhythm, and the glaive turns that information into movement that should not be possible for a weapon that large. Kinsects are not kikaichu. Each is a single cultivated chakra-active companion raised alongside its hunter. Most are beetles, moths, mantises, dragonflies, or things that only resemble those species after generations in the Wastes.

title: The Hunter's Pair
text: You begin with a Bonded Kinsect and an Insect Glaive at no Ryo cost. An Insect Glaive is a Large, Two-Handed Polearm with both the Slashing and Piercing Damage Types. Under the normal Weapon Crafting rules, the additional Damage Type means the weapon begins with 2 Artisan Points before any other customization. Its internal Kinsect channel, launching fittings, and resting brace have no Artisan Point cost and function only for a member of the Insect Glaive Corps bonded to the Kinsect using them. The weapon otherwise follows all normal Equipment, Durability, Artisan Point, and wielding rules. If it is destroyed or permanently lost, a replacement must be obtained or crafted normally. A Kinsect is not destroyed merely because its glaive is lost. Your Bonded Kinsect is part of your equipment for rules purposes. It is not a Summon, Clone, Puppet, Swarm, or separate character; it has no independent Initiative, cannot take actions by itself, and cannot be used to provide flanking, block spaces, or absorb attacks. Commands that send it into danger are resolved through the actions and techniques below. All actions granted by this clan are counted as having the Chain X keyword, and Clan-Jutsu from this clan don’t break your Chain.

title: Extract Hunter
text: A trained Kinsect can briefly sample the chakra and physical rhythm of a resisting living creature. You can hold one Red, one White, and one Orange Extract at a time. Willing creatures cannot provide Extracts. A hostile living creature, living Summon, or comparable chakra-active beast can. Humanoids can always provide all three colors. Against stranger anatomy, Red is normally taken from an offensive structure, White from a locomotive structure, and Orange from a core, shell, or defensive structure. If a creature genuinely lacks an equivalent, the GM may rule that color unavailable. You gain the following actions while your Kinsect is housed on you: ● [Speed 5, Chakra 5, Attack, Projectile] Dispatch Kinsect - Target one valid creature within 10 + CHA/5 yards and make a normal Accuracy attack. This deals no damage and cannot inflict a Wound. On a hit, choose Red, White, or Orange. Your Kinsect becomes Deployed and carries that Extract. You cannot Dispatch it again while it is Deployed. On a miss, it immediately returns to you without an Extract. ● [Speed 2, Utility, Self] Recall Kinsect - Your Deployed Kinsect returns to you. If it is carrying an Extract, you gain that Extract. Recall requires the Kinsect to remain within your Dispatch Range; if you or the target move farther away, the Kinsect automatically returns at the end of the current Action and the carried Extract is lost. Extracts last 30 IC. Whenever you gain a new color, refresh the duration of all Extracts you currently hold to 30 IC. Gaining a color you already possess only refreshes that color; it does not count as gaining a new color for this purpose. Each color grants the following benefit: ● Red Extract - Your Insect Glaive Attacks gain +2 Accuracy. ● White Extract - Your movement speed is increased by 20%. Vault has its Speed reduced by 1, minimum 2, and its maximum distance is increased by 2 yards. ● Orange Extract - You gain +2 to Parries made with your Insect Glaive and reduce hostile Knockback or other forced movement against you by 2 yards, minimum 0. When you hold Red, White, and Orange at the same time, they immediately become Triple Up. Triple Up lasts 30 IC, during which you receive all three Extract benefits and your Insect Glaive Attacks gain +10% Wounding. Triple Up cannot be refreshed and you cannot gain new Extracts while it is active. When it ends, all three Extracts are lost.

title: Vaulting Form
text: The glaive is a weapon, walking stick, spring pole, and an extremely irresponsible answer to the question of whether hunters need terrain in order to jump. You gain the following action while holding your Insect Glaive and able to move: ● [Speed 4, Stamina 6, Utility, Movement] Vault - Move up to AGI/10 yards in any direction, with no more than AGI/20 yards of that movement being directly upward. This is not a Move Action. It may cross gaps and creatures but cannot pass through solid barriers. If you finish unsupported, you begin Falling normally after the Action resolves. A technique with the Aerial tag may be used while Falling as the direct result of your own Vault or another Insect Glaive Corps technique. The Aerial tag has no rules on its own beyond identifying techniques for Corps abilities and effects. At Trailhand or 2,500 total XP, whichever comes first, the Corps will reforge the glaive around the hunter who has actually survived long enough to understand it. Your Bonded Insect Glaive gains 5 bonus Artisan Points that may only be spent on Weapon Features, not Structure or Special Properties. These bonus points count toward tier prerequisites and the weapon's total Artisan Points for wielding restrictions, but do not require you personally to possess the Artisan ranks needed to craft them; the Corps armourers perform the work. You may redesign these 5 bonus points with one Downtime Slot. Replacing a permanently lost Bonded Insect Glaive removes these points until the replacement is reforged with one Downtime Slot.

title: Cultivated Kinsect
text: Type: Ability Cost: 10 Limit: 1 Effects Choose one Kinsect strain. This represents how your companion has been bred and trained; the exact species and appearance are cosmetic. You may change strain with one Downtime Slot if you have access to Haven Ember's breeders or an equivalent facility. Assist - When you hit with an Insect Glaive Attack while your Kinsect is housed, the Kinsect joins the strike. Add one additional weapon damage die. While Triple Up is active, add two weapon damage dice instead.
