Speed - Dispatch Kinsect has Speed 4 instead of 5, Recall Kinsect has Speed 1 instead of 2, and your Dispatch Range is increased by 5 yards. Powder - When Dispatch Kinsect hits, place Powder 1 on that target, to a maximum of Powder 3 from you. When you hit that target with an Insect Glaive Attack, you may consume any amount of your Powder on it. Add 1d8 Energy damage per Powder consumed. This added damage cannot independently inflict a Wound and is part of the triggering Attack for defenses and damage reduction.

title: Aerial Hunter
text: Type: Ability Cost: 10 Limit: 1 Effects While Falling as the direct result of your own Vault or an Aerial Insect Glaive Corps technique, ignore the normal Prone penalties from Falling for Insect Glaive Attacks and Defensive Interrupts. After you hit with an Aerial Insect Glaive Attack, you may move up to AGI/20 yards in any direction without Speed or AP. If at least 2 yards of this movement are upward, reset your current Falling IC and distance. This movement cannot exceed your normal Vault's vertical limit.

title: Mutual Instinct
text: Type: Ability Cost: 12 Limit: 1 Requires: Cultivated Kinsect Effects You and your Kinsect have stopped behaving like a hunter issuing commands to an animal and started behaving like one fighting style with an inconvenient number of wings. Immediately after you hit the creature your Kinsect is currently Deployed against with an Insect Glaive Attack, you may resolve Recall Kinsect at Speed 0. The Extract is gained after the triggering Attack fully resolves. Additionally, if an Insect Glaive Attack modified by Kinsect Mark misses, your Kinsect immediately returns instead of remaining Deployed.

title: Predator's Trinity
text: Type: Ability Cost: 15 Limit: 1 Requires: 2,500 total XP, Mutual Instinct Effects Triple Up lasts 40 IC instead of 30. When Triple Up ends normally, choose Red, White, or Orange. You retain that single Extract for 20 IC. This retained Extract cannot immediately trigger another Triple Up until you successfully gain at least one different color after the previous Triple Up ended.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Ryōchū no Shirushi - Kinsect Mark
text: D-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank D Stamina: 8 Speed: +3 Tags: Link, Weapon, Utility Effects Link this technique to an Insect Glaive Attack while your Kinsect is housed. If the linked Attack hits a valid Extract target, immediately resolve Dispatch Kinsect against that same target without additional Speed, Chakra cost, or a second Defense. Choose the Extract normally. The Kinsect becomes Deployed carrying it. Kinsect Mark cannot be linked to Dispatch Kinsect, Grand Harvest, or another technique that already sends the Kinsect away from you.

title: Nobori Kamakiri - Rising Mantis
text: D-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank D Stamina: 14 Damage: As Weapon Speed: As Weapon +2 Tags: Attack, Melee, Weapon, Movement, Aerial Effects Before making the Attack, move up to half your normal Vault distance. This movement may be vertical and follows the normal restrictions of Vault, but does not require a separate Vault Action or its Stamina cost. If you have White Extract, use your full Vault distance instead. If you finish the technique unsupported, you begin Falling normally.

title: Chōyaku no Mai - Vaulting Dance
text: C-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank C Stamina: 16 Damage: As Weapon Accuracy: +1 Speed: As Weapon +3 Tags: Attack, Melee, Weapon, Movement, Aerial Requires: You are Falling as a result of your own Vault or an Aerial Insect Glaive Corps technique Effects Twist around the haft and use the impact as another launch point. If the Attack hits, move up to AGI/20 yards in any direction after damage resolves. If at least 2 yards of this movement are upward, reset your current Falling IC and distance. If you have Red Extract, add two weapon damage dice.

title: Kariudo no Yobimodoshi - Hunter's Recall
text: C-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank C Stamina: 12 Speed: 6 Range: Dispatch Range Tags: Utility, Movement, Aerial Requires: Your Kinsect is Deployed Effects Your Kinsect turns back toward you and you use its chakra-threaded flight path as a guide for an explosive reposition. Move up to AGI/10 yards toward your Kinsect or the creature currently carrying it, then immediately Recall Kinsect. This movement may include up to AGI/20 yards vertically and does not require Ground. If the Kinsect is carrying an Extract, gain it after the movement finishes. If you have White Extract before this technique begins, increase the movement by 2 yards. If you finish unsupported, you begin Falling normally.

title: Daihōsaku - Grand Harvest
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 24 Speed: 10 Accuracy: +2 Range: Dispatch Range Tags: Attack, Projectile, Utility Requires: Kinsect housed, not in Triple Up Effects The Kinsect is flooded with chakra and sent through a target in a tight looping path, sampling more than one part of its fighting rhythm before returning. On a hit, choose two different Extract colors the target can provide. The Kinsect immediately returns and you gain both Extracts. This Attack deals no damage and cannot inflict a Wound. On a miss, the Kinsect immediately returns without an Extract. Grand Harvest cannot gain the same color twice and cannot be modified by Kinsect Mark.

title: Rakka Suisei - Falling Comet
text: B-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank B Stamina: 24 Damage: As Weapon + 4d10 Accuracy: +1 Speed: As Weapon +4 Tags: Attack, Melee, Weapon, Movement, Aerial Requires: You are at least 2 yards above the target Effects Drive the glaive downward and turn height into a single brutal thrust. Move to the nearest legal space within your weapon's Reach of the target as part of the Attack and end Falling after it resolves. For every full 3 yards you descend as part of this technique, gain +5% Wounding, to a maximum of +15%. If you have Orange Extract, reduce any Wounding penalty caused by a successful Block against this Attack by 10%, minimum 0. This does not change the Block's normal damage reduction.

title: Sandan Shōten - Threefold Ascension
text: A-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank A Stamina: 30 Damage: As Weapon + 6d10 Accuracy: +2 Speed: As Weapon +6 Tags: Attack, Melee, Weapon, Movement, Aerial Requires: Triple Up Effects Consume Triple Up on declaration. The Kinsect launches first, the glaive follows, and hunter and companion spiral through the target before the wielder kicks away into open air. Before the Attack, move up to your normal Vault distance in any direction. This movement may be vertical and ignores the usual requirement to begin Vault from a stable surface. The Attack gains +15% Wounding from the three consumed Extracts. If the Attack hits, after damage resolves choose one Extract color the target can provide. Your Kinsect becomes Deployed carrying that Extract without requiring Dispatch Kinsect or another Defense. You may then move up to AGI/20 yards away from the target. If you finish unsupported, you begin Falling normally. Threefold Ascension consumes Triple Up even if the Attack misses. Predator's Trinity does not retain an Extract when Triple Up is consumed this way.

title: Jashin Worshipper
text: RARE CULT PATH Jashinism is a faith, not a bloodline, and it sits uneasily inside Haven Ember. A playable worshipper is still bound by Ember Corps law and squad responsibility; the heritage represents ritual pain, profane vitality, and sympathetic blood curses without granting a licence to murder comrades, civilians, or anyone else the cult would rather call an offering.

title: Prayer Before Violence
text: You track Devotion, starting at 0 and with a maximum of 3. You gain the following Action:

title: [Speed 5, Utility, Self] Invocation
text: Offer a short prayer to Jashin and choose one hostile creature you can perceive as your Offering. You may have only one Offering at a time. Choosing a new Offering removes the previous one. When you either deal HP damage to your Offering with an Attack or voluntarily suffer HP damage as an explicit cost/effect of a Jashin Clan technique, gain 1 Devotion. Devotion returns to 0 at the end of combat. You may spend 1 Devotion in either of the following ways: - Conviction — after making a Stamina Exhaustion or Resistance roll, add +2 before the result is resolved. - Fervour — when declaring a Jashin Clan technique, reduce its final Speed by 2, minimum 1. You cannot spend more than 1 Devotion on the same roll or Action.

title: Sacramental Blood
text: The first time each combat that you inflict HP damage on your Offering with a Slashing or Piercing Melee Attack, you may collect the blood required for Jashin techniques as part of that Attack, provided you have a free hand, weapon, or container capable of retaining it. This does not create extra blood samples and does not bypass any requirement that the sample be fresh or belong to the correct target.

title: Profane Vitality
text: Type: Ability Cost: 15 Limit: 1 Effects Gain +3 Resistance against Bleed and Wound effects. While you have at least 1 Devotion, reduce penalties caused by your own Wounds by up to 2. This does not remove, heal, or reduce those Wounds. Once per combat, after suffering a Major or worse Wound, you may spend 1 Devotion to gain 3 AP, up to your normal maximum.

title: Jutsu
text: C-Rank

title: Seibetsu no En - Consecrated Circle
text: C-Rank Type: Fūinjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 16 Speed: 12 Area: 3 Tags: Utility, Ritual, Environmental Effects Draw and consecrate Jashin’s symbol beneath you. The circle lasts for the scene or until physically destroyed beyond recognition. You may have only one Consecrated Circle at a time. While standing inside your Consecrated Circle: - Gain +2 Resistance against fear-based Immobilization effects. - The Delay of your Jashin Ritual techniques is reduced by 5, minimum 0. - When you gain Devotion, gain 1 AP. Leaving the circle suppresses these benefits but does not end the circle. B-Rank

title: Jujutsu: Shiji Hyōketsu - Blood Rite Link
text: B-Rank Type: Fūinjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 30 Accuracy: -3 Range: 20 Speed: 18 Delay: 10 Seal Speed: 18 Tags: Attack, Ritual, Mark Effects Requires a fresh sample of the target's blood obtained during the current scene. During the Delay you must remain inside a ritual circle you draw as part of the technique. On a full hit, for 20 IC whenever you voluntarily deal HP damage to yourself, the marked target takes equal damage after DR, to a maximum of 10% of its maximum HP per instance. Self-damage from this technique cannot be reduced or redirected. Leaving the circle, losing the blood sample, or becoming unable to act ends the link.

title: Jinrō
text: RARE CURSED BLOODLINE The Jinrō inherit a predatory transformation that threatens their self-control. Corps training helps them manage its instincts and fight safely beside a crew.

title: Predator’s Jaw
text: Your Basic Unarmed Attacks may be Bite attacks. A Bite may deal Slashing or Piercing damage instead of Blunt and counts as an Unarmed Attack for Taijutsu and other compatible effects. When a Bite fully hits a creature you are Grappling, gain +1 Control after the attack resolves.

title: The Beast Hungers
text: Type: Ability Cost: 15 Limit: 1 Effects Hunger begins at 0. Whenever any one of the following occurs, gain 1 Hunger, maximum 5: - You deal HP damage to a hostile creature. - You take HP damage from a hostile creature. - You successfully gain Control in a Grapple against a hostile creature. Only one Hunger can be gained from this feature in the same 10 IC, even if several triggers occur. You can spend Hunger on Jinrō techniques. At Hunger 5, suffer -2 Diplomacy and -2 Genjutsu Defense against effects that directly provoke rage, predation, or appetite. Hunger returns to 0 after combat.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Hikisaki Tobi - Rending Pounce
text: D-Rank Type: Taijutsu, Rank D Stamina: 14 Damage: As Unarmed Speed: As Basic Unarmed Attack +4 Tags: Attack, Melee, Movement, Trapping Effects Before the Attack, move up to half your normal Movement toward the target. This Attack is a Bite. On a full hit, you may spend 1 Hunger to immediately establish a Grapple with the target and gain 1 Control. This does not require a second Attack or Defense. Rending Pounce cannot be used if you could not legally Grapple the target. C-Rank

title: Kamiawase - Lockjaw
text: C-Rank Type: Taijutsu, Rank C Stamina: 16 Damage: As Unarmed Speed: As Basic Unarmed Attack +3 Tags: Attack, Melee, Trapping Requires: You are Grappling the target Effects This Attack is a Bite and deals 75% Final Damage. On a full hit, gain 2 Control after damage resolves. You may spend 1 Hunger to gain 3 Control instead. Until the end of the target’s next Action, its Break Clinch and Escape Grapple actions have their final Speed increased by 2. Lockjaw can trigger Predator’s Jaw normally. B-Rank

title: Jūkei - Beast Form
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 25 Upkeep: 6 Speed: 10 Tags: Utility, Self, Transformation Effects Spend any amount of Hunger on activation. Gain +5 STR per Hunger spent, +5% Movement per Hunger spent, and natural Slashing unarmed attacks. At the start of each turn while at 4+ Hunger, if a living hostile creature is within Melee Range you must either attack a hostile creature before taking a Utility Action or spend 1 Willpower to ignore this urge for 20 IC. Ending Beast Form is Speed 5. While Beast Form is active, Bite attacks gain +1 Accuracy, and the first Hunger spent on each Rending Pounce or Lockjaw is refunded after the technique resolves.

title: Kamizuru
text: CANON ANIME CLAN The Kamizuru preserve a bee-keeping combat tradition. They breed swarms and prepare wax, honey and explosives for territory control and support.

title: Passives
text: No additional Heritage passives.

title: Living Hive
text: Type: Ability Cost: 18 Limit: 1 Effects Your Hive has a Swarm Pool equal to (CHA 5)+(Survival Ranks 5). Damage specifically dealt to your bees reduces this pool before any technique they are maintaining can continue. The Hive shares your Initiative Count and never receives independent Actions or AP. Bee techniques use your Actions, Interrupts, and costs normally. After a battle, the Swarm Pool returns to maximum after 1 hour if at least 1 point remained; if reduced to 0, restoring it requires one Downtime action or 5000 Ryo of breeding stock.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Hachimitsu Numa - Honey Mire
text: D-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 14 Damage: 5d10 + Xd4 Range: 15 Area: 8 Speed: 10 Seal Speed: 10 Tags: Attack, AoE, Environmental Effects Choose how much Swarm Pool HP to spend: 0, 10, 20, 30 or 40, leaving at least 1. X = 1 + HP spent/10. Pay this cost and Chakra when releasing the Jutsu, then attack a visible ground Area within Range. On a hit, apply Immobilization equal to half X, rounded up, reduced for Partial Defense. After the Attack, the ground becomes Honey Mire for 20+10X IC. It affects all creatures touching it, including allies and you. Targets above the ground avoid its terrain effects. Entering the Mire or travelling 2 yards within it adds 1 to its Immobilization on that creature, maximum 3, once per 5 IC. Use one Honey Mire total per caster even where fields overlap. A Move Action at half the creature’s current movement rate avoids this additional buildup; forced movement does not. Clean Honey — Speed 5 Utility Action: remove 1 Severity from yourself or a willing creature within Melee reach. The status ends after 10 IC outside all of your Mire or when the last field affecting it expires. Use only the strongest Immobilization when combined with other sources. C-Rank

title: Hachibakudan - Bee Bomb Swarm
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 22 Damage: 16d10 Range: 25 Area: 10 Speed: 16 Seal Speed: 14 Special: Stun 4 Tags: Attack, AoE, Projectile, Energy Effects Reduce your Swarm Pool by 10 when declaring this technique. If you cannot, it fails before costs are paid. If the attack fully hits, you can leave 5 bees behind as a visible hazard. The next creature to enter that 2-yard spot within 20 IC takes NDB × 3 Energy Damage; this follow-up cannot Wound. B-Rank

title: Mitsurō Bunshin - Beeswax Clone
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 28 Speed: 14 Seal Speed: 20 Tags: Utility, Clone, Creation Effects Create one clone using the normal Bunshin targeting rules. It has HP equal to CHA and shares your action economy; when you choose an Action, either you or the clone may be its point of origin where physically possible. When destroyed in melee, the attacker suffers Immobilization 3 for 20 IC from wax and bees unless they pass Resistance against your Chakra Control. Only one Beeswax Clone may exist at a time.

title: Nara
text: Nara families preserve shadow techniques and tactical training. They restrain opponents and create openings for their crews. Starting Features Nara may start with Elemental Affinity for Clan/General Ninjutsu.

title: Tactical Planning
text: You have IQ Points equal to total XP/500, rounded down. Restore them after a Week’s Rest. Pay a plan’s IQ cost alongside its listed Action, Chakra, Stamina and AP costs. Each plan uses the following rules; planning never reverses the current IC or changes an event that has already resolved. Queen’s Plan — 1 IQ, Speed +4, Interrupt, Link Link to an attack made by you or an ally within Max IQ × 10 yards. For Damage Bonus calculations, treat its Speed as its Base Speed +4. If it inflicts a Wound, choose a legal location for that damage type. Normal defensive and Wound-mitigation effects still apply. Knight’s Plan — 1 IQ, Speed 4, Chakra 10, Clan Ninjutsu, Interrupt Choose a point within Max IQ × 3 yards. Its distance from you is the radius of the affected sphere. Willing creatures in that sphere may immediately move up to its diameter in yards as Speed 0 Interrupts. They must follow legal paths, pay no AP for this movement, and remain subject to effects that prevent movement. Each creature may benefit from one Knight’s Plan per 10 IC. Pawn’s Plan — 2 IQ, Speed 0, AP X Choose an opponent you can see that has neither targeted nor affected you for at least 10 IC while engaged with another member of your crew. Spend X AP, up to Max IQ. Your next attack against it before your next non-Interrupt Action ends gains +X Accuracy. This does not grant additional Actions, change Surprise rules or stack with another Pawn’s Plan. Flow of Battle — 3 IQ, Speed 0, Utility Reduce your next non-Interrupt Action’s final Speed by 5, following the normal minimum and half-base-Speed limits. Use it before the end of your next non-Interrupt Action. This plan may be used once per 10 IC and cannot stack with itself. Your IC never moves backwards. Rook’s Plan — 4 IQ, Speed +2, Interrupt, Link Link to a valid defensive Interrupt against an incoming attack. Reduce the Damage Bonus used by that attack by your matching PDB or NDB, minimum 0. Resolve its dice, defence and other effects normally; reducing its Damage Bonus to 0 does not negate the attack. Checkmate — 5 IQ, Speed 50, Delay 50, Stamina 50, Chakra 50, Utility Study one opponent you can see. If it leaves your perception, you become Incapacitated, or you voluntarily end the Action, the plan fails. When the Delay resolves, identify one tactical opening supported by what you have observed. You and allies who can hear your instructions gain +3 Accuracy against that opponent and treat damage against it as 25% higher for Wounding for 50 IC. Multiple Checkmate plans do not stack. Attacks, defences and encounter objectives resolve normally. Outside combat, a completed Checkmate may instead ask the GM one question about the situation that your available evidence could answer. The GM supplies a truthful deduction from that evidence, or explains what information is missing.

title: Multiple Shadow Bind
text: Type: Ability Base Cost: 6 Scale: 4 Limit: CHA /30 Effects You can Target multiple people with the Kagemane and Kagenui Techniques. Every person beyond the first adds +5 to that Jutsu’s Chakra Cost, and for the case of Kagemane, +2 to its Upkeep. You can Target up to 1.5 (rounded down) additional people per Rank.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Kagemane no Jutsu - Shadow Imitation Technique
text: D-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 16 + 2X Upkeep: 5 Accuracy: −6 Range: CHA/5; doubled at dusk or dawn Speed: 16 Seal Speed: 12 Tags: Attack, Control Effects Extend your shadow to a creature’s shadow within Range and make a Ninjutsu Attack. The shadows need a continuous surface path; measure Range along that path. X is your prior successful Kagemane castings plus prior Shadow Sewing castings this battle. Fix X before paying costs; count each casting once, even with several targets. Any failed defense establishes possession, including a Partial Success. Begin Upkeep when the first victim is caught. Multiple Shadow Bind supplies its normal extra targets, costs and Upkeep. A new casting may add victims; a creature can be held by only one Kagemane at a time. While caught, a victim has no independent turns. It may speak, gains AP on normal IC ticks, and resolves timed effects and Fatigue normally. It copies your Actions as described below. Its periodic escape checks continue even while it is Stunned or Pinned. Escape TN = 20 + CHA/4 + Chakra Control/10 − 2X, rounded down. Record it for each capture. Each 15 IC after capture, and after each Fatigue category the victim gains, it makes a free Grapple Defense check against that TN. Add +2 per earlier failed escape from this capture. These checks cost no Action, Stamina or Delay and do not gain Break Clinch’s optional X bonus. Success releases the victim. For Shadow Neck-Binding, your shadow begins at Control 5 and the victim at 0. Linked Grapple Jutsu change Control normally; other copied Actions and damage to your body do not change this shadow Control. Control modifies the victim’s normal Grapple Defense, but is not added to the recorded escape TN. The victim counts as Clinched for linked techniques and for the +2 Base Speed of Dodge and Parry. Movement: mirror your displacement, including forced movement. Fix the mirror line halfway between you at capture: moving toward or away from each other reverses direction, while sideways movement keeps the same direction. Use your actual distance without a second Clinch reduction. The victim stops at obstacles; you may finish your own movement. Terrain affects the victim along its actual route. Forced movement applied directly to it moves only it. The connection ends if its surface path is blocked or exceeds twice the Range recorded at capture. Ordinary changes in lighting do not end it. Your shadow cannot be damaged as a separate object. An escape effect must end shadow control or possession to remove this connection; escaping a physical Grapple alone does not. Copying: whenever you perform a non-Interrupt Action or Offensive Interrupt, the victim attempts it simultaneously, using your declared Speed, Accuracy and Fatigue costs, with its own damage statistics and equipment. It pays its own Chakra or Stamina and special resources. An unknown Jutsu adds 2 to each listed Fatigue cost, or 5 if it also fails the learning requirements. If it lacks required anatomy, bloodline, equipment or expendable resources, it copies only the motion, with no cost or effect. Copy handseals when you form them and release the Jutsu when you release it. A held object blocking a required hand is dropped first. Discard Weapon can be copied even if your hand is empty. A copied maintained Jutsu uses the victim’s own Upkeep; its player may end that Upkeep normally. Your Defensive Interrupts copy only their movement; the victim chooses its own defense when allowed below. Copies never trigger further possession copies. Copied Actions do not advance a separate IC. Resolve a copied Action before its Fatigue-triggered escape checks. A victim unable to act because of Stun copies only the motion; reduce its remaining Stun by the copied Action’s Final Speed, minimum 0. Each copied non-Interrupt Action counts toward effects lasting until its next Action. Copied attacks: if you attack a victim directly, that victim attacks you. Otherwise, it attacks the same single target at −3 Accuracy. Reflect an Area’s centre using the capture’s mirror line. A target beyond the victim’s normal Range imposes −1 Accuracy per 2 full yards of shortfall; the Attack still needs a clear path. If it cannot reach through an obstruction, the victim performs the motion without an Attack. Declare all copied targets before resolving defenses. When a victim is attacked, choose Relax or Hold. Relax allows one normal legal Defensive Interrupt. Hold gives an immediate escape check with +5; success frees it before impact and lets it defend, while failure leaves it with passive mitigation only. Each failed check grants the usual +2 on later escapes. A victim’s defense costs its own resources and does not delay your IC. While it remains held, it has no independent IC to advance. Release one or all victims as Speed 0, ending their share of Upkeep. Release also occurs if you become unconscious or stop maintaining the Jutsu. Return the victim to initiative at current IC +1, then apply any remaining Stun. If it escapes before an incoming Attack and then declares a defense, add that Interrupt’s Speed normally. Other ongoing effects retain their remaining durations. C-Rank

title: Kage Nui no Jutsu - Shadow Sewing Technique
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 10 + 2X Upkeep: X Damage: (3X)d10 Accuracy: +2 Range: CHA/5 Speed: 12 Seal Speed: 14 Special: Immobilization X Tags: Attack, Piercing, Control Effects Choose X from 1–6 and attack within Range. A hit deals the listed damage and Immobilization X, reduced for Partial Defense. Track the Severity actually applied. Begin Upkeep only for a creature restrained by the hit. Break Needles — Speed 5 Utility Action: the victim rolls Resistance against your Chakra Control roll. On success remove 2 Severity, plus 1 per full 5 points it wins by. At 0 Severity the restraint ends. It also ends when its Upkeep ends or the victim moves beyond twice casting Range. Each casting increases Kagemane’s escalating-use value once, hit or miss. When you use Kagemane on a creature restrained by your Shadow Sewing, reduce its −6 Accuracy penalty by that restraint’s current Severity, minimum 0. If possession attaches, release that creature’s needles. Multiple Shadow Bind uses one shared Upkeep X for the casting; the last victim’s release ends it. A new application replaces your previous needles on the same creature rather than stacking.

title: Kagebuki Shibari no Jutsu - Shadow Neck-Binding Technique
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: +5 Speed: +2 Tags: Link, Control Requires: Target controlled by your Kagemane; a known compatible Grapple Jutsu Effects Link to a Grapple Jutsu you know with Trapping, Takedown, Ground Fighting or Submission. Target one of your Kagemane victims. Replace its Stamina cost with an equal Chakra cost, add Chakra 5 and Speed 2, and pay its Control cost. Retain any other costs. Your shadow supplies the required limbs. Use the shadow’s recorded Control and the linked technique’s positional requirements. Begin in a Clinch; a successful Takedown establishes a Pin for later Ground Fighting or Submission. The victim rolls Grapple Defense against Kagemane’s escape TN. On success it avoids this linked technique, but possession remains; on failure apply the linked effects in full. Use CHA for STR and NDB for PDB when the linked technique calculates damage or strength. The linked technique follows its own repeat-use and ending rules. Only this opposed check defends against it; Kagemane’s Hold-or-Relax choice is not used. While Pinned by your shadow, the victim remains stationary when you move; its usual Kagemane escape checks still apply. Ending possession ends all shadow holds and Submissions. A Submission ending adds 5 IC to your next Action, and lingering Suffocation fades normally. B-Rank

title: Kageyose no Jutsu - Shadow Endgame Technique
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 25 Upkeep: 6 Range: CHA/3 Speed: 16 Tags: Utility, Preparation Effects Create shadow tendrils extending along visible, unobstructed paths within Range. While maintained, choose one option after activation and then at least 10 IC after your previous option. Announce it before Actions are declared on that IC; resolve it simultaneously with them. On your own turn, you may use it immediately before or after your Main Action. You must be conscious, unstunned and free to direct the tendrils; you cannot use an option during handseals, a delayed Action or another Action requiring continuous attention. Options cost AP and do not advance your IC. Calculate their effective Speed for defenses and damage as if they were normal Actions, including Paralysis. For variable AP, pay half that Speed, rounded up. Extra AP can reduce effective Speed normally and is paid in addition. Defenders advance IC normally. Options receive no Links or Move-with-Attack movement. Recasting preserves the 10-IC timer. - Retrieve — 1 AP per object: pick up unattended objects or draw objects from your own inventory. Tendrils hold at most CHA/8 objects, rounded down, and can support Small or Medium weapons. Declare each object’s position; moving an object within Range is another Retrieve option. - Grab — 5 AP: attack one creature within Range using Grab’s Accuracy +2 and effective Base Speed 12. A full hit establishes a Clinch with one tendril. Determine Control normally using your Grapple statistics, CHA for STR and RES, and +4 Grapple Offense. The tendril supplies the required limbs. You may hold one creature at a time; its position is the tendril’s origin for Bind. - Bind — variable AP: perform a known Grapple Jutsu or basic Grapple Action through the hold. AP replaces Stamina and IC advancement; pay Chakra, Control and other costs normally. Use CHA for STR and NDB for PDB. Meet the usual Clinch or Pin requirement. Track Control using the tendril’s options and the victim’s Actions; your unrelated Actions and damage do not change it. The victim may Break Clinch or Escape Pin normally. The hold halves its movement, but does not drag you. A pinned victim remains stationary. - Attack — variable AP: make one Basic Weapon Attack or Multi-Throw using objects held by the tendrils. AP replaces Stamina; use your weapon Accuracy and NDB for PDB. Weapon Focus does not apply. Every target must be within both the weapon’s Range from its declared tendril position and this Jutsu’s Range from you. WDP accrues using the Attack’s normal Stamina cost. Tendrils have no separate HP; physical damage can hit held weapons but not the shadows themselves. They retract when their path is blocked or their end leaves Range, dropping the object or releasing the victim. Ending Upkeep retracts all tendrils. Ending a tendril Submission adds 5 IC to your next Action normally.

title: Samsara
text: RARE DŌJUTSU - SETTING ORIGINAL Samsara is a rare ocular lineage documented in scattered Haven records. Its bearers wield opposing powers of creation and destruction; the eye is distinct from the Rinnegan.

title: Soul Anchor
text: Samsara does not gain Willpower. And cannot access or use it in any way, shape or form. They can use the Limit Break ability, and the XP cost for Limit Break is reduced by 50%. However, Samsara still carry the Will of a Hunter within them, and their powers over life, death, creation and destruction grant them unique abilities unlike anything else. A Samsara can prepare for their next life. By spending 1 Downtime Slot, you may establish a Soul Anchor. An Anchor is a prepared combination of seals, Chakra imprinting and whatever physical vessel or method your character uses to facilitate their return. You may possess multiple active Soul Anchors at once, up to a maximum of 4 + (XP Earned / 1000), rounded down. You cannot establish another Soul Anchor while at this maximum unless one of your existing Anchors has first been consumed or destroyed. An Anchor is a physical thing somewhere in the world. It may be hidden. It may be moved. It may be found. And it may be destroyed. The exact appearance of an Anchor is chosen by the player and GM. One Samsara may use an elaborate sealing shrine, another a preserved biological vessel, while another may use technology recovered from the old world. Regardless of appearance, all Soul Anchors function identically. Each Soul Anchor created has a TN of 15+(Soul Anchors Active 5 ) , and when creating one you must succeed this roll with either Chakra Control or Stealth. On a fail, the Downtime is wasted, and you do not create a soul anchor. You may consume Soul Anchors to gain the normal benefits of Willpower destroying them forever, as well as Turn the Wheel.

title: Turn the Wheel
text: If you die while you possess an intact Soul Anchor, your Ember pattern attempts to return through it. This is not a combat revival. You are still dead for the purposes of the current Scene, Mission, Hunt, or Event. Whatever killed you succeeded, your body remains where it fell, and anything carried by that body remains with it. After the event has concluded, you reincarnate through your Soul Anchor. When reincarnating: - You retain your XP, Attributes, Skills, Abilities, Jutsu, Uniques and Samsara Heritage. - You retain your memories and personality. - You do not gain the Heritage, Kekkei Genkai, biological abilities, implants, or other special properties of whatever vessel is used. - Your new incarnation is mechanically treated as the same base character unless a GM explicitly approves otherwise. - Equipment left on your previous body does not magically return. The Soul Anchor is consumed. You return at Fatigue 2, recovering normally afterward. You cannot return to the same Scene, Mission, Hunt, or Event in which you died. Reincarnation cannot be deliberately used to respec a character, remove unwanted permanent mechanics, obtain another bloodline, duplicate equipment, or otherwise benefit from intentionally killing yourself.A Samsara without an Anchor is just as mortal as anyone else. Additionally, effects which explicitly seal, capture, consume, destroy, or prevent the movement of the soul/Ember identity may prevent Turn the Wheel at GM discretion.

title: Samsara Eye
text: Type: Dōjutsu Ability CE: 5 + (1 per time you use Turn the Wheel permanently) Upkeep: 3 + (1 per 5 times you use Turn the Wheel permanently) Speed: 2 Cost: 5 Limit: 1 Effects When activated choose Creation or Destruction. Switching modes is Speed 6 or can be done as part of the same action to change your past life echo. - Creation: gain +3 to Barrier, Creation, and crafting-related Jutsu Accuracy/rolls, including Fatigue rolls, Parry Rolls, rolls to maintain seals. This applies generally to all rolls relating to Barriers, creating things, or crafting things, regardless of context; created objects gain +NDB×2 HP, not including Summons. This does apply to Bushin. - Destruction: damaging Jutsu against objects, barriers, and summons deal +20% Final Damage, but your healing received is reduced by 20% while active. When activated, the Samsara Eye reveals the invisible continuity connecting Chakra, memory and identity. You gain a +(XP/200) bonus to all checks relating to Identify an individual's Chakra signature. Examine possession or soul-related phenomena. Investigate reincarnation. Identify Soul Anchors. Study techniques which directly manipulate identity or Chakra imprints. If you have previously personally encountered someone's true Chakra signature while your Samsara eye is active, mundane disguises and physical changes do not prevent you from recognising that it is the same individual, as long as your Dojutsu is active. The appearance varies between Samsara. Concentric rings, fractured pupils, pale halos and overlapping irises have all been recorded. Despite historical comparisons, the Samsara Eye is not the Rinnegan. Past Life Echo When activating the Eye, choose one Echo. Switching Echoes is a Speed 6 Action, or can be done as part of the same action you use to change between creation and destruction. - Warrior - Once per 20 IC, gain +2 to one Physical/Taijutsu Accuracy. Accuracy roll, Parry roll or Dodge roll. - Hunters - Once per 20 IC, gain +2 to one Ninjutsu or Genjutsu Accuracy, Accuracy roll, Barrier roll, or roll made to establish or maintain a Seal - Wanderer - Once per 20 IC, gain +4 to one non-combat Skill check. You cannot benefit from multiple Echoes on the same roll.

title: Jutsu
text: C-Rank

title: Rinne: Shiroi Kaji - Samsara: White Forge
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 24 Range: 10 Speed: 14 Seal Speed: 16 Tags: Utility, Creation Effects Requires Creation mode. Create a mundane object up to a 2-yard cube or a wall with HP CHA×3 and DR NDB. It lasts 50 IC. This can create anything mundane. You can create weapons with zero artisan points, or up to 50 units of ammunition with this. You cannot create poisons, pills, or kits. You can make ninja tools. Created weapons use ordinary equipment profiles and gain no free upgrades. B-Rank

title: Rinne: Kuroi Bunkai - Samsara: Black Reduction
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 32 Damage: 25d10 Range: 25 Speed: 16 Seal Speed: 22 Tags: Attack, Energy Requires: Destruction mode Effects Attack one target within Range. Roll 25d10 + NDB × Final Speed against an ordinary target, or 50d10 + NDB × Final Speed against a Barrier, Clone, Summon or created object. Destruction mode applies normally. Held weapons and worn equipment use the ordinary damage pool. When a qualifying creation intercepts the Attack, use the larger pool against it. If it breaks and its rules pass leftover damage onward, halve that leftover before it reaches an ordinary target; keep it unchanged against another qualifying creation. The reduction is made once when crossing from a qualifying creation to an ordinary target. Use the actual defense’s rules for how much damage reaches each target; do not roll a new pool. A barrier that negates or reduces an Attack without using HP resolves that effect normally. Successful Parry or Dodge still protects its target. Resolve any legal defense declared for overflow before applying the remaining damage; breaking an interceptor grants no additional defense. Effects other than damage pass through only when the interceptor’s rules permit them.

title: Silverhand
text: RARE TRADITION - SETTING ORIGINAL Silverhand is a tradition of performers, musicians and agitators whose chakra resonates through sound and crowds. Corps practitioners use it for communication, morale and disruption.

title: Passives
text: No additional Heritage passives.

title: Rocker Soul
text: Type: Ability Cost: 18 Limit: 1 Effects Choose Violence or Melody. Violence: after you take damage, gain +2 Accuracy on your next Melee or Sound-tagged Attack. Melody: after an ally within CHA/2 spends Willpower, they regain 2 AP and you gain 2 AP. A character may not hold both expressions unless a later Talent explicitly allows it.

title: Jutsu
text: C-Rank

title: Hankyō Kuzushi - Feedback Break
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 20 Damage: 16d8 Area: 8 Speed: 14 Special: Stun 4 Tags: Attack, AoE, Energy, Sound Effects Violence users increase Stun by 2 on a full hit. Melody users may instead exclude up to CHA/20 allies from the Area. This is a Sound effect and is blocked by effects that explicitly prevent sound propagation. B-Rank

title: Fukutsu no Sanka - Anthem of the Unbroken
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 30 Upkeep: 6 Area: CHA/2 Speed: 16 Seal Speed: 18 Tags: Utility, AoE, Sound Effects Allies in the Area gain +2 Resistance against fear-based Immobilization effects and Stun, and +1 to Willpower rerolls. Each ally can benefit from only one Anthem at a time. If you are silenced, unconscious, or unable to continue performing, the upkeep ends.

title: Vanguard Corps
text: WEAPON TRADITION - SETTING ORIGINAL Heritage Cost: 1 UP The Vanguard Corps are Haven Ember's front-line monster hunters: weapon masters trained to stand close enough to a beast to read the twitch before the charge, the shoulder before the claw, and the half-second opening after several tons of muscle commits to the wrong direction. Where other Corps traditions are built around a bloodline, a companion, or a piece of forbidden technology, the Vanguard Corps are built around practice. Their armouries are filled with oversized blades, crushing hammers, shielded lances, transforming weapons and field repairs scarred by things that should have killed the person holding them. Vanguard training covers weapon forms suited to different openings in a monster’s attacks.

title: The Vanguard Arm
text: You begin with one custom Melee Weapon worth up to 3 Artisan Points at no Ryo cost. It is your Vanguard Arm. Build it using the normal Weapon Crafting rules in Equipment & Crafting; it uses normal PDB, Durability, WDP, wielding, hands, Damage Type and Artisan Point rules unless this Heritage explicitly states otherwise. You may designate a different qualifying Melee Weapon as your Vanguard Arm during a Week's Rest by spending 1 Downtime Slot training, balancing and fitting it. You may only have one Vanguard Arm at a time. Morph mechanisms, shell chambers, bucklers and paired grips granted by a Vanguard Discipline are Corps-specific fittings. They do not grant Ballistic or Firearm access, do not count as separate weapons unless a rule says so, and only function while you are using the Discipline that grants them. All actions granted by this clan are counted as having the Chain X keyword, and Clan-Jutsu from this clan don’t break your Chain.

title: Corps Refit
text: At Trailhand or 2,500 total XP, whichever comes first, the Corps rebuilds your Vanguard Arm around the hunter you have become. Your Vanguard Arm gains 3 bonus Artisan Points that may only be spent on Weapon Features, not Structure or Special Properties. These bonus points may take the weapon beyond the normal 5 Artisan Point design limit, but do not increase the Artisan Point total used to determine whether you personally can wield your own Vanguard Arm. You may redesign these 3 bonus points during a Week's Rest by spending 1 Downtime Slot. If your Vanguard Arm is permanently lost or destroyed, the bonus points return after the replacement is rebuilt with 1 Downtime Slot.

title: Hunter's Opening
text: Immediately after you successfully Dodge, Parry, or Block an Attack made by a creature within your Vanguard Arm's Reach, you gain an Opening against that creature until the end of your next Action. Your next Melee Weapon Attack against that creature may consume the Opening to choose one: ● Reduce the Attack's Final Speed by 1. ● Add 1 Damage Die to the Attack. An Opening is lost if you attack a different creature first, become unable to perceive the creature, or no longer wield your Vanguard Arm.

title: Hunting Discipline
text: Choose one Vanguard Discipline from the list below. You only gain the rules of your current Discipline while wielding its Qualifying Weapon as your Vanguard Arm. You may change Discipline during a Week's Rest by spending 1 Downtime Slot training with a qualifying weapon. You cannot change Discipline during a scene. Unless a Discipline says otherwise, its Charges, Spirit, Notes, Shells, Phials and other stored resources are lost when the scene ends, when you stop wielding a qualifying Vanguard Arm, or when you change Discipline. A single Attack can generate a Discipline resource only once, regardless of Multi-Attack or effects that cause it to strike more than once. Certain Disciplines grant Vanguard Guard. While you have Vanguard Guard, you may use [Speed 6, Interrupt, Defense] Vanguard Guard to reduce the Damage of the triggering Attack by 25%. This counts as a Block for effects that care about Blocking. If another rule already allows you to Block, you may use either version, but their Damage Reduction does not stack. You do not need the Weapon Block crafting Feature or any other Ability to use Vanguard Guard.

title: Great Sword — True Charge
text: Qualifying Weapon: Large or Extreme Two-Handed Sword. Great Sword hunters accept that they will not swing often. The entire style is built around making the swing that matters. ● [Speed 3, Stamina 4, Utility] Charge — Gain Charge 1, to a maximum of Charge 3. If you voluntarily move more than 2 yards, make an Attack without consuming Charge, change weapons, or stop wielding the Great Sword, lose all Charge. ● Charged Slash — When declaring a Great Sword Attack, you may consume any amount of Charge. Add +2 Damage Dice per Charge consumed. If you consume Charge 2, the Attack also gains +1 Base Speed. If you consume Charge 3, it instead gains +2 Base Speed and +10% Wounding. ● Shoulder Tackle — When an Attack hits you while you have at least Charge 1, you may spend 8 Stamina to reduce any hostile forced movement caused by that Attack by 3 yards and retain all Charge. If the Attack moves you 0 yards after this reduction, gain Charge 1 after it fully resolves, to a maximum of Charge 3.

title: Long Sword — Spirit Edge
text: Qualifying Weapon: Medium or Large Two-Handed Sword. Long Sword hunters build rhythm rather than force. Every clean cut feeds the next until the blade seems to move ahead of the hunter. ● Spirit Gauge — When you either hit with a Long Sword Attack or successfully Parry with the Long Sword, gain Spirit 1, to a maximum of Spirit 3. ● Spirit Slash — When declaring a Long Sword Attack, you may spend Spirit 1 to add +1 Damage Die. ● Spirit Roundslash — When declaring a Long Sword Attack at Spirit 3, you may consume all Spirit. The Attack gains +3 Damage Dice, +2 Stamina and +2 Base Speed. If it hits, enter Red Spirit for 20 IC. While in Red Spirit, you may use Spirit Slash without spending Spirit. You cannot gain Spirit while Red Spirit is active.

title: Sword & Shield — Hunter's Guard
text: Qualifying Weapon: Small or Medium One-Handed Sword with your other hand free. The shield is not a wall. It is a fist, a wedge, a climbing hook and the half-second of safety needed to keep fighting. ● Hunter Buckler — While using this Discipline, you gain Vanguard Guard. The buckler is part of the Vanguard Arm and does not count as a second weapon. ● Free Hand — You may draw, stow, or use ordinary Small equipment without first sheathing your Vanguard Arm. This does not reduce the Speed or other cost of the item or Utility action. ● Shield Bash — When declaring a normal Vanguard Arm Attack, you may strike with the buckler instead. Change the Attack's Damage Type to Blunt, add +1 Damage Die and +2 Stamina. It remains a Weapon Attack and uses the sword's listed Speed, Accuracy and Delay.

title: Dual Blades — Demon Mode
text: Qualifying Weapon: A matched pair of Small or Medium One-Handed Swords, one in each hand. Dual Blade hunters trade patience for pressure, turning stamina into a storm of cuts that only stops when the hunter does. For this Discipline the matched pair is treated as one Vanguard Arm. Attacks use the statistics of one blade and do not gain the Two-Handed PDB bonus merely because both hands are occupied. ● [Speed 3, Utility] Demon Mode — Enter or leave Demon Mode. Demon Mode ends if you choose to leave it, stop wielding both Dual Blades, become Incapacitated, or the scene ends. ● While in Demon Mode, normal Dual Blade Attacks gain Final Speed -1 and +3 Stamina. Once per Attack when one hits, gain Demon 1, maximum Demon 3. ● Demon Dance — When declaring a normal Dual Blade Attack at Demon 3, consume all Demon. The Attack gains +3 Damage Dice and +2 Base Speed. After it fully resolves, Demon Mode ends.

title: Hammer — Impact Charge
text: Qualifying Weapon: Large or Extreme Two-Handed Club. Hammer hunters do not cut around a problem. They put enough force through it that the problem forgets what it was doing. ● [Speed 3, Stamina 4, Utility, Movement] Power Charge — Gain Impact Charge 1, maximum 3, and move up to 2 yards. Changing weapons or making a Hammer Attack without consuming Impact Charge removes all Impact Charge. ● Charged Impact — When declaring a Hammer Attack, you may consume any amount of Impact Charge. Add +1 Damage Die per Impact Charge consumed. ● Staggering Blow — When a Hammer Attack that consumed Impact Charge hits, increase that target's next Attack's Base Speed by the amount of Impact Charge consumed. If you consumed Impact Charge 3, the Hammer Attack also gains +5% Wounding. Creatures immune to interruption or physical staggering may ignore the Base Speed increase at the GM's discretion.

title: Hunting Horn — Echo Recital
text: Qualifying Weapon: Large Two-Handed Club. The Hunting Horn is a blunt instrument with excellent acoustics. A practiced Vanguard turns the cadence of impacts into signals that keep an entire hunting party moving together. ● Echo Notes — Once per Attack when you hit with the Hunting Horn, choose Power, Guard, or Pace and add that Note to your sequence. You cannot choose the same Note twice in a row. Hold a maximum of 3 Notes. ● [Speed 5, Stamina 8, Utility] Recital — Consume all 3 Notes and choose one melody represented among them. You and allies within 10 yards when the Recital resolves gain that melody's benefit. A creature can hold only one of your Recital benefits at a time. ● Power Melody — The creature's next damaging Attack gains +1 Damage Die. ● Guard Melody — The creature's next Parry or Block is reinforced. A Parry gains +1 Parry; a Block increases its Damage Reduction by 10 percentage points. The benefit is consumed after that defense resolves. ● Pace Melody — The creature's next Move Action or Utility action with the Movement tag gains Final Speed -1.

title: Lance — Iron Counter
text: Qualifying Weapon: Large Two-Handed Polearm. Lance hunters make a monster fight through the point of the weapon before it ever reaches the person behind it. ● Set Guard — While using this Discipline, you gain Vanguard Guard. If you have not voluntarily moved since the end of your previous Action, Vanguard Guard used with the Lance reduces Damage by 35% instead of 25%. Voluntary movement ends this increased reduction until the end of your next Action. ● Counter Thrust — After you successfully Block an Attack with the Lance, your next Lance Attack against that attacker before the end of your next Action gains Final Speed -2. ● [Speed 4, Stamina 6, Utility, Movement] Guard Advance — Move up to 3 yards. Until this action resolves, forced movement against you is reduced by 2 yards, minimum 0. This movement cannot pass through creatures or solid barriers.

title: Gunlance — Sealed Shelling
text: Qualifying Weapon: Large Two-Handed Polearm. A Gunlance is not a firearm. Its 'shells' are close-range sealed blast chambers built into the head of a polearm and vented through the strike itself. They do not use Ballistic Attacks, Ballistic ammunition, BDB, Reload rules, or any Ballistic Corps feature. While using this Discipline, you gain Vanguard Guard. ● Shell Chamber — Begin each scene with Shell 3, maximum 3. ● Shelling — Once per Attack when declaring a Gunlance Attack, you may consume Shell 1. Add 1d8 Energy damage and +2 Stamina to the Attack. This added damage is part of the same Attack and cannot independently inflict a Wound. ● [Speed 5, Utility] Reload Shells — Restore your Shell Chamber to Shell 3. This is not a Ballistic Reload and cannot benefit from effects that modify Reload. ● Wyvern Burst — When a Gunlance Attack hits, you may consume all remaining Shells, minimum 2. Add +1 Damage Die per Shell consumed and +5% Wounding.

title: Switch Axe — Morph Gauge
text: Qualifying Weapon: Large Two-Handed Polearm. The Switch Axe is a Corps-built transformation frame. In Axe Mode it creates space and stores momentum; in Sword Mode that stored force is pushed through a shorter, more violent cutting edge. A Switch Axe begins in Axe Mode. Its morph fittings have no Artisan Point cost and only function for a Vanguard using this Discipline. ● Axe Mode — Once per Attack when you hit, gain Switch 1, maximum Switch 3. While in Axe Mode, increase the weapon's Reach by 1 yard, to a maximum of Reach 4. ● [Speed 2, Utility] Morph — Change between Axe Mode and Sword Mode. ● Sword Mode — Sword Mode loses the extra Reach from Axe Mode. Each Sword Mode Attack consumes Switch 1 and gains +1 Damage Die. If you have no Switch, immediately return to Axe Mode. If an Attack consumes your last Switch, return to Axe Mode after it resolves. ● Zero-Sum Finish — When declaring a Sword Mode Attack while at Switch 3, you may instead consume all 3 Switch. This replaces Sword Mode's normal Switch cost and +1 Damage Die. The Attack gains +3 Damage Dice, +2 Base Speed and +5% Wounding. After it resolves, return to Axe Mode.

title: Charge Blade — Phial Engine
text: Qualifying Weapon: Medium or Large One-Handed Sword. The Charge Blade folds a guarding sword-frame into a two-handed axe head. The first form stores force; the second spends it. A Charge Blade begins in Sword Mode. Its shield and morph fittings have no Artisan Point cost and only function for a Vanguard using this Discipline. ● Sword Mode — While in Sword Mode, the weapon is treated as One-Handed, cannot receive the Two-Handed PDB bonus, and you gain Vanguard Guard. Once per Attack when you hit, gain Phial 1, maximum Phial 5. ● [Speed 2, Utility] Morph — Change between Sword Mode and Axe Mode. In Axe Mode, you lose Vanguard Guard from this Discipline and the weapon is treated as Two-Handed, gaining the normal Two-Handed PDB bonus if it was not already receiving it. This bonus cannot stack with another instance of Two-Handed. ● Phial Discharge — When declaring an Axe Mode Attack, you may spend up to 3 Phials. Add 1d8 Energy damage per Phial spent. This added damage is part of the same Attack and cannot independently inflict a Wound. ● Guard Point — Immediately after you successfully Block in Sword Mode, you may Morph into Axe Mode at Speed 0 after the Block fully resolves.

title: Partbreaker
text: Type: Ability Cost: 10 Limit: 1 Effects When a Melee Weapon Attack with your Vanguard Arm damages Armor Durability, a physical Barrier, an object, or a destructible monster part, deal +50% damage to that object's Durability. This bonus applies after the Attack's normal damage is determined.

title: Adaptive Arsenal
text: Type: Ability Cost: 10 Limit: 1 Effects Choose a second Vanguard Discipline for which you own a qualifying weapon. At the beginning of a scene, choose either of your prepared Disciplines as your current Discipline without spending a Downtime Slot. Once per scene, while wielding a qualifying weapon for your other prepared Discipline, you may change to it with a [Speed 5, Utility] action. All resources from the previous Discipline are lost. Corps-specific fittings for both prepared weapons remain functional, but only your designated Vanguard Arm gains Corps Refit bonus Artisan Points.

title: Veteran Hunter
text: Type: Ability Cost: 15 Limit: 1 Requires: 2,500 total XP, Partbreaker Effects When you consume Hunter's Opening, you may take both benefits instead of choosing one: the Attack gains Final Speed -1 and +1 Damage Die. This does not create a second Opening.

title: Kariudo no Ayumi - Hunter's Step
text: D-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank D Stamina: 10 Speed: +2 Tags: Link, Weapon, Movement Effects Link to a Melee Weapon Attack with your Vanguard Arm. After the Attack fully resolves, move up to 2 yards without AP. This movement cannot pass through creatures or solid barriers. If the linked Attack consumed Hunter's Opening, increase this movement to 3 yards.

title: Hakai Uchi - Breaker Strike
text: C-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank C Stamina: 16 Damage: As Weapon Speed: As Weapon +3 Tags: Attack, Melee, Weapon Effects Make a Melee Weapon Attack with your Vanguard Arm. It deals +50% damage to Armor Durability, physical Barriers, objects and destructible monster parts. If Partbreaker also applies, these bonuses are additive rather than multiplicative.

title: Chōbatsu Nuki - Punishing Draw
text: B-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank B Stamina: 22 Damage: As Weapon +2 Damage Dice Speed: As Weapon +3 Tags: Attack, Melee, Weapon Requires: Hunter's Opening against the target Effects Consume Hunter's Opening and make a Melee Weapon Attack against that creature. In addition to Punishing Draw's listed bonus Damage Dice, choose one normal Hunter's Opening benefit and apply it to this Attack. Veteran Hunter does not allow Punishing Draw to receive both Opening benefits.

title: Senjin Shokei - Vanguard Execution
text: A-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank A Stamina: 30 Damage: As Weapon +4 Damage Dice Accuracy: +1 Speed: As Weapon +5 Tags: Attack, Melee, Weapon Effects Make a Melee Weapon Attack with your Vanguard Arm. If the target currently has a Major Wound, destroyed Armor, or a destroyed monster part, the Attack gains +100% Wounding. After Vanguard Execution resolves, all stored resources from your current Vanguard Discipline are lost. This includes Charge, Spirit, Demon, Impact Charge, Notes, Shells, Switch and Phials. Red Spirit also ends. Sword & Shield and Lance have no stored resource to lose.

title: Yamanaka
text: Yamanaka families serve in intelligence and command. Their mind techniques allow silent communication, coordinated missions and dangerous intrusions into an opponent’s thoughts.

title: Passives
text: No additional Heritage passives.

title: Mind Network
text: Type: Ability Cost: 15 Limit: 1 Effects You can establish telepathic communication with willing creatures you know within CHA/2 yards. Maintaining a network of more than CHA/20 creatures has Upkeep 2. Once this network is established, you can maintain it across a distance of CHA/10 Miles. A willing linked creature may send a short warning, image, direction, or sentence to every other linked creature as part of declaring an Action or Interrupt. Mind Network does not read unwilling thoughts and does not reveal information a linked creature does not intentionally send.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Shindenshin no Jutsu - Mind Transmission Relay
text: D-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 12 Upkeep: 2+X Speed: 8 Seal Speed: 8 Tags: Utility, Clan Effects While maintained, the range of your Mind Network range increases by (50+(X50))% This does not let the network pass through effects that explicitly block chakra communication. Before a willing creature linked to your Mind Network makes an Awareness or Genjutsu Defense roll, you can spend 2 AP to grant that roll +2. You must be conscious and able to communicate through the network. Mind Transmission Relay does not share senses, memories, or unwilling thoughts. C-Rank

title: Shintenshin no Jutsu - Mind Body Switch Technique
text: C-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 24 Accuracy: -4 Range: CHA/2 Speed: 14 Delay: 6 Seal Speed: 14 Tags: Attack, Genjutsu, Control Effects Resolve this as an Accuracy Roll against the target's Genjutsu Defense. On a full success your body becomes Incapacitated and your mind occupies the target for up to 30 IC. While occupying them, you can cause ordinary movement, speech, Basic Actions, and non-clan physical actions. You cannot access their memories, bloodline, Jutsu, Uniques, or Willpower. Each time the controlled body suffers a Major or worse Wound, the target may spend 1 Willpower to immediately end the technique. You can end it as a Speed 0 action. B-Rank

title: Shinranshin no Jutsu - Mind Disturbance Technique
text: B-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 34 Accuracy: -3 Range: CHA/2 Speed: 16 Seal Speed: 22 Special: Confusion Tags: Attack, Genjutsu, Control Effects On a full hit, for 20 IC the target cannot willingly choose the same target for two consecutive hostile Actions and must spend 1 AP whenever they change targets. At the start of each of their turns they may spend 1 Willpower to ignore this effect until their next turn. This technique never forces self-harm or an action the target did not already have access to.

title: Heritage Up 2
text: 2 UP HERITAGES 14 ENTRIES

title: Aburame
text: Aburame families preserve their bond with kikaichū. The insects share the host’s chakra and serve in reconnaissance, tracking and battlefield control. Starting Features Aburame start with Kikaichu no Jutsu at no XP cost, ignoring its normal requirements. They may start with Elemental Affinity for Clan/General Ninjutsu.

title: Living Colony
text: Kikaichu training is part of the Aburame lineage rather than a separate purchase. You can use your bugs to make skill checks through your Kikaichu at range. The normal rules for communicating with Kikaichu and how long they can survive apart from the Host apply, except their survival away from the Host is increased to a week. GMs may apply a penalty of up to -10 on checks Kikaichu are ill suited for, or disallow checks they simply could not perform. You still perform any relevant actions and pay any associated cost. Awareness, Stealth, and Survival are common uses for spying, sneaking a bug into position, or tracking people. This does not meaningfully deplete the Swarm, and Kikaichu no Jutsu does not need to be active. A single Kikaichu can be trivially crushed by anyone who spots it. Once per 10 IC, when one of your Clan Jutsu successfully affects a creature inside the Swarm, restore CHA x 2 HP to the Swarm.

title: Predatory Cycle
text: When you place a female insect on a hostile target, you can immediately choose one: Feeding: the target suffers -1 on its next Chakra Exhaustion roll before the end of its next Action. Frenzy: the target suffers 1d4(NDB) Energy damage every 5 IC for the next CHA/2 IC. After that duration, the insect is removed. Proliferation: place one additional female insect after the normal Delay. This extra insect cannot trigger Predatory Cycle again. Recall: move the Swarm up to CHA/30 yards without AP or Speed. A target can suffer at most -3 from Feeding at once. When a hostile creature carrying at least one female insect declares a Chakra-costing Action, you can pressure the infestation before costs are paid. The creature chooses one: Purge — increase that Action's final Speed by 3. After it resolves, remove one female insect from that creature. Feed — resolve the Action normally. After it resolves, restore CHA × 2 HP to the Swarm and move the Swarm up to CHA/30 yards toward that creature without AP or Speed. This cannot trigger from Upkeep, passive Chakra loss, or an Action that is cancelled before its costs are paid. At 2,000 total XP, gain Crouching Mantis, Hidden Centipede at no XP cost if you do not already have it.

title: Crouching Mantis, Hidden Centipede
text: Cost: 10 Limit: 1 Effects The Aburame’s Kikaichu Swarm is now considered a separate character for Stealth. Clan Ninjutsu no longer end the Aburame’s Stealth, but will end the Swarm’s. If the Aburame is in Stealth when they use Kikaichu no Jutsu, the Swarm is created with the same Stealth TN. If the Swarm triggers a Chakra roll, its Stealth ends. The Aburame may have Hide and Improve Hiding affect their Swarm instead of themselves. Additionally, the Aburame gets access to the following actions: [Speed +10, Delay 10] Secrete Bugs - This action modifies Kikaichu no Jutsu while the Aburame is not in Stealth. The Swarm is created in Stealth 2. [Speed 0 Interrupt] Wait - You can declare a Kikaichu Swarm in Stealth is waiting. While waiting, the Kikaichu Swarm passively and discretely crawls on opponents, waiting to bite all at once. While the Swarm remains in stealth it adds 1 Female Insect every 25 IC (10 Minutes out of Combat). Out of combat, this increases Bugs to a maximum of 10. Out of combat this prompts an Awareness roll from anyone who gets Bugs.

title: Jutsu
text: E-Rank

title: Hijutsu: Konchū no Bōdō - Insect Insurrection
text: E-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank E Speed: +2; +5 on an Area Attack Delay: 5 after the hit, for insect placement only Tags: Link Effects Link to one Attack. After it hits a creature, an insect lands on that creature 5 IC later. A multi-hit Attack places one insect per target through this Link. The parent Attack uses its own normal timing; only insect placement is delayed. Placement remains scheduled if the target moves, but is cancelled if the target or insect is destroyed before it occurs. The insect is hidden at Stealth TN 25 + your Stealth bonus and may be found with Search. This placement does not use Hide. Placement triggers Predatory Cycle normally. Its Proliferation insect arrives 5 IC after that placement and does not trigger Predatory Cycle again. Remove Insects — Speed 5 Utility Action: after discovering your infestation, the creature removes up to two of your female insects from itself. This also ends effects supplied by those removed insects.

title: Hijutsu: Mushiyose - Secret Technique: Bug Gathering
text: E-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank E Chakra: 10 Speed: 10 Seal Speed: 12 Tags: Utility Effects This grants the Aburame a +5 bonus on relevant Survival, Awareness, and Research rolls, or +20 when the roll directly relates to finding or understanding insects. The Aburame may be able to get information not normally available, but there is no guarantee a bug's perspective will be useful. D-Rank

title: Hijutsu: Kikaichū Mushikui - Destruction Bug Bite
text: D-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank D Chakra: 15 Speed: 8 Area: As Kikaichū no Jutsu Tags: Attack, Self Effects Choose one creature inside your Swarm carrying at least one of your female insects. X is the number on it when you declare the Action. Pay Chakra, then the target makes the roll below. The target rolls 1d20 + its current Chakra Exhaustion modifier against TN 8+2X, capped at 10 + your Chakra Control bonus. Apply its existing exhaustion, Upkeep and Fatigue modifiers. This defensive roll neither spends Chakra nor changes Fatigue, and is the only defense against this technique. The target loses 10+3X HP, maximum 30. On a failed roll, increase that loss by 50%, rounded down. This flat HP loss ignores mitigation and causes no Wounds. Its next actual Chakra Exhaustion roll within 10 IC suffers −X, maximum −3; this and Predatory Cycle’s Feeding have a combined maximum penalty of −3. Your insects already on the target gain one Stealth Level, maximum 3. Their Stealth TN is unchanged, and insects already discovered remain discovered. Apply Living Colony’s recovery normally, once within its own trigger interval. C-Rank

title: Hijutsu: Mushidama - Bug Sphere
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 24 Upkeep: 4 Speed: 16 Accuracy: +X/3 Tags: Attack, Self, Control Effects Choose one creature within your Swarm. X is the female insects you have on it. Make a Ninjutsu Attack at +X/3 Accuracy, rounded down. Determine its AoE Dodge penalty using the Swarm’s radius before it contracts. On any hit, the Swarm encloses the target and applies Immobilization 2, reduced by Partial Defense. Begin Upkeep. The target counts as inside the Swarm; other creatures do not. Every 10 IC enclosed, place one female insect and resolve Predatory Cycle. A successful initial defense leaves the Swarm unchanged. The enclosed Swarm occupies the victim’s space. An Area Attack containing that space covers the entire Swarm for its normal damage rules. For gradual movement, it follows at CHA/30 yards per IC. For an instantaneous movement Action, it follows up to CHA/30 × that Action’s Final Speed yards along the route. Movement without an Action has Speed 0 for this purpose. Teleportation or movement beyond that allowance breaks the enclosure at the last reachable point. While enclosed, use the Swarm only for Bug Bite against that target, Insect Screen protecting a creature sharing its space, or Return. Ending Upkeep restores its previous radius around its current position and removes this Immobilization. Return uses its normal Speed and Range to bring the Swarm into you. Destruction of the Swarm ends the Jutsu. The same Swarm can enclose only one target.

title: Hijutsu: Mushikabe - Insect Screen
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 18 Speed: 8 Tags: Interrupt, Utility, Self Requires: Kikaichu no Jutsu active Effects Pull the Swarm across an incoming attack. Choose yourself or one ally inside the Swarm. The Swarm takes the attack's final damage before the protected character. If the attack is single-target and the Swarm still has HP remaining afterward, the protected character is considered not to have been hit. Area attacks still affect the protected character normally, but the Swarm takes only half of the damage it would normally suffer from that Area.

title: Mushi Bunshin no Jutsu - Bug Clone Technique
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 12 + 4X Upkeep: X Speed: 14 + X Seal Speed: 6 + 3X Tags: Utility, Clone Effects Create X Clones, to a maximum of 3. The Clones occupy anywhere in the Swarm, with swirling bug Swarms shifting their position. You don't need to track the clone's exact position and they are immune to area of effect attacks. While this Jutsu is maintained, using the Hide Among Clones action restores all Mushi Bunshin for free and the Area of your swarm is reduced by 20% per clone. If the Swarm is destroyed, this Jutsu ends. The Clones have the Aburame's Stats as though they were Fatigue 1. If they advance a Fatigue level, they are destroyed. Clones are created with copies of the items the user had, except for consumables, chakra-infused items, electronic items, and items with complex moving parts. While one or more Clones are active, the Aburame gain access to the following actions: [Variable AP] Attack: The Clone performs a Basic Unarmed Attack, Basic Weapon Attack, a Dual Weapon Attack, or a Multi-Throw. The attack can use any Weapons the Clone has and the attack is modified by Insect Insurrection. This costs half of the total Speed in AP, instead of Insect Insurrection's regular AP cost. Use the Aburame's CHA in place of their STR and Ninjutsu DB in place of their Physical DB. This attack is considered to be Held Back. The Clones can only target someone else who is inside of the Swarm. [1 AP] Defend - The clone may Dodge or Parry (using any weapon it has or no weapon) any attack aimed at it. This will not defend the Swarm, but it may prevent the clone from becoming dispersed. [Speed 10] Masquerade - With the Aburame’s direct help and guidance, the Swarm condenses down fully into a perfectly you-shaped area or returns to its normal shape. While you-shaped, it gains a +5 bonus on any rolls to convince other people that it is you. This action can only be used if there is only one clone.

title: Parasitic Destruction Insect Technique - Kikaichu no Jutsu
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Range: CHA/10 Area: Up to CHA/10 Speed: 12 Tags: Utility Effects You create a cloud of Kikaichu which cannot be dispersed by abilities that specifically end environmental effects. The Swarm has CHA10 HP. It can only take damage from Area effects and only takes half damage if the Area doesn’t encompass the entire Swarm. It’s immune to all conditions except for ignite and knockback. The Swarm's HP persists between uses, and heals at a rate of CHA3 every hour out of combat. At 0 HP this Jutsu ends and may not be used again until the Swarm recovers some HP. Kikaichu may be communicated without to a range of CHA/5 yards through minor fluctuations in the Host's Chakra. Kikaichu can operate beyond that range, and are surprisingly intelligent; but they may not receive new orders and will die after 24 Hours away from their Host. Kikaichu always know the distance and direction to their Host and any female insect within Chakra Control miles. Aburame gain access to the following actions to utilize their Kikaichu: [Speed 4 or +4] Return - If the Swarm is within range, it temporarily re-enters the Aburame's body ending any actions that modify the Swarm or Ignite status. This can be used as a link allowing the Swarm to benefit from an interrupt. After the Defense is resolved, whether it succeeds or fails, the Swarm returns to the Aburame's body. [AP X or Speed X] Move - The Swarm Moves at a speed of CHA/30 for the next X IC. The swarm can slip through tiny cracks and fly. B-Rank

title: Hijutsu: Mushitatsumaki - Devouring Cyclone
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 30 Speed: 18 Area: As Kikaichu no Jutsu Tags: Attack, AoE, Self, Piercing Effects Everyone hostile inside the Swarm is attacked. On a hit, deal irreducible HP damage equal to 8 + twice the number of female insects on that target, maximum 28, and place one female insect. A target with 3 or more female insects also suffers -2 to its next Chakra Exhaustion roll. After resolving this technique, the Swarm loses HP equal to CHA; if this would reduce it to 0, leave it at 1 instead.

title: Mushi Kame no Jutsu - Bug Jar Technique
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Speed: Variable Requires: Kikaichu no Jutsu active Tags: Utility Effects This is a variable Speed defensive action declared like a Block. You can declare another variable speed defensive action alongside Bug Jar such as Block, Guard, Full Defense, Defensive Formation, et cetera. While active, the Aburame and any of their allies inside the Swarm may choose to let the swarm defend them when attacked. If they do, they may not apply another defense, but damage is subtracted from the Swarm’s HP before the protected person. Attacks that have their damage completely prevented are not considered to have hit their target. Bug Jar will stop non-damaging attacks that need to hit, but it will not stop Genjutsu.

title: Akimichi
text: Akimichi families preserve techniques that turn stored calories into strength and enlarged bodies. They serve as shock troops and protectors.

title: Akimichi Energy Bars
text: Type: Item Cost: 20k Ryo each Effects Eating a bar is a Speed 4 action that raises your effective Calorie Conversion rank by 1 for 50 IC, increasing your current CP maximum by 5. Eating multiple bars stacks up to a maximum of 3. If a bar is still active when another one is consumed, its duration is extended until the last bar consumed ends. Each bar also restores 10 + RES/10 CP, up to your current CP maximum.

title: Calorie Engine
text: You gain 5 ranks of Calorie Conversion at no XP cost. Calorie Conversion uses Calorie Points (CP) as described under the Ability. You recover RES/5 CP after a Full Rest with proper food. You can overeat up to double your normal CP maximum. For every 10 CP above the normal maximum, suffer -1 Dodge and -1 Athletics until enough CP has been spent to remove the excess.

title: Mass Is Momentum
text: While Baika no Jutsu is active, every full 5 points of X also grants +1 yard of melee reach and +10% final damage to damaging melee Taijutsu. When you successfully Take the Hit, convert Baika's Dodge penalty into an equal bonus on that Take the Hit roll. After moving at least 5 yards in one direction, reduce the final Speed of your next Akimichi melee attack by 2. While Baika no Jutsu is active, when you hit with a melee Attack after moving at least 5 yards in a straight line, the target chooses before damage is resolved: Brace — it remains in place, but the Attack counts as 25% higher for Wounding. Yield — it is moved directly away from you by X/5 yards, minimum 3, after the Attack resolves. This is forced movement and does not gain the Brace Wounding increase. If Yield would move the target into a solid obstacle, the movement stops normally and causes no additional collision damage.

title: Three-Coloured Pills
text: An Akimichi may be issued one Green, one Yellow, and one Red pill per mission. Consuming one is Speed 5. Each later colour may only be taken after the earlier one. Green: restore half your normal CP maximum and gain +5 STR and RES for 50 IC. When it ends, gain Fatigue +1. Yellow: restore your normal CP maximum and gain +5 DEX and AGI for 40 IC. When it ends, gain Fatigue +1 and Poison 2. Red: restore CP to your true maximum, gain +10 STR, RES, DEX, and AGI for 25 IC, and immediately enter Butterfly Mode. When it ends, gain Fatigue +2 and Poison 4. You cannot reduce or ignore these costs.

title: Calorie Conversion
text: Type: Ability Base Cost: 1 Scale: 1 Limit: RES/15 Effects Each rank grants 5 Calorie Points (CP). Spend CP one-for-one to reduce the Chakra cost of an Akimichi Clan Jutsu, to a minimum of 0. If you reduce the Chakra cost to 0, no Chakra Exhaustion roll is required for that activation. CP spent this way remains spent until recovered. At 0 CP, you can pay 4 HP for each missing CP used to fuel an Akimichi Clan Jutsu.

title: Jutsu
text: D-Rank

title: Baika no Jutsu - Multi-Size Technique
text: D-Rank Type: Taijutsu, Rank D Chakra: 15 + X/2 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 10 Tags: Utility Effects X has a maximum of AGI/2. You subtract X points from your AGI, and add X/2 to your STR and RES. This increase does not increase your Current Vitality and HP but it does increase your maximums in each. The following effects apply during Baika no Jutsu: All your unarmed attacks gain Area X/10, or have their existing Area increased by that amount. You gain a damage reduction of X/2. You have a -X/2 penalty to Stealth rolls. You reduce the severity of any Stuns inflicted upon you by X/10, and any effects which would move you involuntarily will move you X/3 fewer yards. Your Taijutsu attacks have a reach of +1 yards.

title: Nikudan Sensha - Human Bullet Tank
text: D-Rank Type: Taijutsu, Rank D Chakra: 20 Upkeep: 2 Speed: 6 Requires: Baika no Jutsu or Chō Baika no Jutsu active Tags: Utility, Movement Effects Begin Rolling and maintain Upkeep 2. You are treated as Prepare Blocking throughout the form, including during movement and Rolling Crush. You may choose the normal Speed 0 Block against each incoming Attack instead of another Defensive Interrupt. While Rolling, you may Move, use Rolling Crush, defend, attempt Break Clinch or Escape Pin, or end the form. Dodge remains available; Parry, held weapons, new Grapples and handseals do not. Apply −5 Awareness. Drop held items when entering the form. Release any Grapple you control on activation. Against a Grapple holding you, gain +10 on Break Clinch and Escape Pin. External physical Immobilization below 10 is suppressed; Severity 10 or higher ends Rolling. Suppressed effects keep their remaining durations and return when the form ends. Ending Upkeep is Speed 0 and ends Rolling. Losing Baika or Chō Baika also ends it. You can replace Baika with Chō Baika without interrupting Rolling when the new size form takes effect in the same Action.

title: Kaiten Assai - Rolling Crush
text: D-Rank Type: Taijutsu, Rank D Stamina: 15 Damage: (STR/15)d8 Speed: 15 Range: Melee Area: As the active size technique grants this Unarmed Attack Requires: Human Bullet Tank or Spiked Human Bullet Tank active Tags: Attack, AoE, Blunt, Movement Effects Choose one creature or object in a straight, traversable path. Move toward it up to AGI × Final Speed/50 yards, applying your current movement modifiers. Stop within Unarmed reach and resolve one impact centred on the chosen target. Its Area is the radius granted to this Unarmed Attack by your active size technique. You are excluded; everyone else in that Area defends normally. If this charge covers at least 5 yards in one direction, double your base PDB for the Attack. Temporary DB bonuses are added afterward. Parry is at −3, or −5 after a qualifying charge. Apply Mass Is Momentum normally. Obstacles stop the charge; to strike one, declare it as the target. Rolling Crush leaves the rolling form active, hit or miss. It grants only the movement used to approach the impact; a miss does not create another charge or attack. C-Rank

title: Bubun Baika no Jutsu - Partial Multi-Size Technique
