Even if someone dodges Sawarabi no Mai, they do not escape its area; they simply avoid being skewered by spikes of bone erupting from the ground. After a few hours the bones will grow brittle as the chakra dissipates and begins crumbling. Within a day there will be nothing left but dust and bone chips. Skeletal Modifications: Any three.

title: Uchiha
text: CANON CLAN — 3 UP Uchiha families preserve the Sharingan and their fire techniques. The eye lets them read movement, imitate techniques and anticipate an opponent’s actions. Starting Features Uchiha begin with Elemental Aptitude for Katon and Elemental Affinity for Katon or Genjutsu. Genjutsu Affinity applies to either Diplomacy or Research when checking Genjutsu learning requirements, not both. Each Affinity rank reduces the chosen skill's requirement by 1. Count the reduction only once when checking a combined Diplomacy + Research requirement.

title: The Curse of Hatred
text: The Uchiha Clan have always had a strong connection to others. You are no different than the rest. Your emotions often overwhelm you, and you find yourself in places where you feel like the entire world is against you - even when everything around you says otherwise. Whenever an ally within your line of sight suffers a Wound, you may designate the enemy responsible as the object of your hatred. Until that enemy is defeated, you gain +2 Accuracy against them and your attacks against them deal +10% Final Damage. However, you suffer -2 Dodge against attacks from all other enemies. If the wounded ally is someone with whom you have an established in-character bond, your first attack against the responsible enemy also gains -2 Final Speed, but counts as its base speed for the purposes of dealing damage. You may only have one object of hatred at a time. If you are the one that lands the final blow on your Object of Hatred, you begin an emotional surge. Until the end of the scene, your character begins to resent the ally that was wounded. Your mind betrays you, twisting your affection into resentment, your concern into blame, and your relief into an overwhelming sense of emptiness. When the scene ends, choose one: Repression: You bury your emotions and pretend nothing happened. Your next Emotional Surge lasts until the end of the following scene instead. Confrontation: You openly blame the ally whose injury triggered your hatred. If you roleplay a meaningful confrontation with them, you gain +20% XP from it.. Acceptance: You acknowledge that your hatred has become misplaced. You immediately end your Emotional Surge, but cannot benefit from the Curse of Hatred again until you spend 1 Downtime slot recharging it.

title: Sharingan - Copy Wheel Eye
text: The Sharingan manifests as red irises marked by tomoe. It is a power one must unlock through suffering and pain. Activating Sharingan is Speed 0, may be linked to another Action or Interrupt, and has Upkeep 2. None of its abilities function while the Uchiha suffers a Visibility penalty of -6 or worse or otherwise cannot clearly perceive the relevant creature. The mature Sharingan has three stages and stops at three tomoe in this volume.

title: Sharingan, Stage 1
text: You gain Dousatsugan and Saimingan at no XP cost and ignore their normal rank or skill requirements.

title: Sharingan, Stage 2
text: You gain Yogengan and Shouningan at no XP cost. While Sharingan is active, gain +1 to all Skill rolls.

title: Sharingan, Stage 3
text: You gain Magen: Kyouten Chiten and Senchigan at no XP cost. While Sharingan is active, the Stage 2 Skill bonus increases to +2. At Stage 3, Genjutsu used through Saimingan and attacks made with a technique currently retained through Dousatsugan gain +1 Accuracy.

title: Dousatsugan - Eye of Insight
text: Requires: Stage 1 Sharingan You can see chakra flow and read the physical construction of techniques. Gain +4 to defense rolls against Genjutsu. Whenever you clearly witness a valid Taijutsu technique, or a Ninjutsu or Genjutsu that uses handseals, you can copy it. You must still satisfy elemental Aptitudes, special access, and physical requirements; Clan Jutsu, custom Jutsu, Master Techniques, bloodline-exclusive techniques, and effects that rely on physiology you do not possess cannot be copied. You can copy techniques one rank above what you could normally learn. A witnessed valid technique may be used for the remainder of the in-character day without paying XP. In addition, you can retain two copied techniques per Sharingan Stage indefinitely without paying XP, maximum six at Stage 3. Replacing a retained copy requires witnessing a valid replacement. If you later purchase a retained copied technique permanently, reduce its XP cost by 25%, rounded up. Copying never removes the normal Action, Chakra, Stamina, Seal Speed, equipment, or positioning requirements of the technique.

title: Reading the Fight
text: While Sharingan is active, whenever a hostile creature you can clearly see completes an Attack, defensive action, handseal sequence, or movement technique, gain 1 Read on that creature, maximum equal to your Sharingan Stage. A creature can grant only 1 Read per 10 IC. Before rolling against that creature, spend Reads one-for-one for +1 Accuracy or +1 to a defensive roll, maximum +3 on a single roll. After a creature with 2 or more Reads rolls a defense against you, you can spend 2 Reads to impose -2 on that defense after seeing the roll but before the outcome is declared. All Reads on a creature are lost if you cannot perceive it for 20 consecutive IC. At Stage 2 or higher, once per creature per 10 IC, when a creature with at least 2 Reads declares the same named Action, defensive action, movement technique, or Jutsu that you have already watched it complete this battle, you can spend 2 Reads before costs are paid. It chooses one: Break Pattern — cancel that declaration and declare a different legal Action whose final Speed is no lower than the original. It pays only the new Action's costs. Be Read — keep the declaration. Before it resolves, you can either move up to 2 yards without increasing your IC or reduce the final Speed of one legal defensive Interrupt you use against that Action by 2. If it cannot legally change Actions, it must Be Read. This cannot trigger from basic movement that is not an Action.

title: Saimingan - Eye of Hypnotism
text: Requires: Stage 1 Sharingan You can perform single-target Genjutsu without handseals through direct eye contact. The target may avoid eye contact; as a Speed 0 non-interrupt, they may look away. Doing so imposes a Visibility penalty of 4 until they use a Speed 0 action to look at you again, or take a Major or higher Wound, breaking their focus. At Stage 2, Genjutsu cast this way reduce their final Speed by 4. At Stage 3, reduce it by 8 instead and gain +1 Genjutsu Accuracy. Saimingan cannot convert an Area Genjutsu into an eye-contact attack.

title: Shouningan - Eye of Recognition
text: Requires: Stage 2 Sharingan You can read lips when they are clearly visible, reproduce handwriting after watching a short sample, speed-read, and retain visual detail with near-photographic accuracy. Gain +4 to Awareness rolls that materially rely on sight; this stacks with the Stage 2 or Stage 3 Sharingan Skill bonus. Once per scene after watching a creature perform a mundane physical task, you can use your own relevant Skill in place of an untrained Skill roll to reproduce the procedure, though you do not gain tools, passwords, hidden information, or supernatural access you did not observe.

title: Yogengan - Eye of Prediction
text: Requires: Stage 2 Sharingan Once per Fatigue category, when you make a defensive roll against a visible attack, you can treat the d20 as a 10 rather than rolling. At Stage 3, treat it as a 12. You can also take Observe as a Variable Speed Action similar to Guard/Total Defence/Block. Until Observe ends, when a creature you can see attacks you, you can use Yogengan without consuming its once-per-Fatigue-category use.

title: Senchigan - Eye of Foresight
text: Requires: Stage 3 Sharingan When declaring an Action against a creature you can clearly see, name a technique category and a final Speed. The target declares and resolves any legal defense against that declaration. After seeing the defense result, choose any technique you know or currently retain of that category whose final Speed is no greater than the Speed you declared. Resolve the chosen technique using its normal damage calculation, but the declared Speed determines interruption legality and when you next act. Increase the chosen technique's Chakra or Stamina cost by 4. If your chosen technique invalidates the defense the target committed to, the defense still pays its normal costs but does not protect it.

title: Three-Tomoe Mastery
text: At 3,000 total XP your mature Sharingan becomes more efficient. Your maximum Reads on a creature increases by 2 Senchigan increases the chosen technique's Chakra or Stamina cost by 2 instead of 4. Once per 10 IC, when a creature reaches 4 Reads, mark it Mapped until you lose all Reads on it. Your first Attack and first defensive roll against a Mapped creature each 10 IC gain +2. Retained copied techniques used against the creature you copied them from cost 3 less Chakra or Stamina, minimum 1. When Magen: Kyouten Chiten successfully reflects Genjutsu from a Mapped creature, you can spend all 4 Reads to reduce the reflected technique's Speed increase by 4, minimum Speed +0.

title: Uchiha Fire Doctrine
text: Katon Jutsu reduce their Seal Speed and Chakra cost by 2 per Sharingan Stage, minimum Chakra 1. Damaging Katon Jutsu gain +1 Accuracy at Stage 2 and +2 Accuracy at Stage 3. At Stage 3, a Katon Jutsu that inflicts a Wound increases any Ignite or Burns it applies by 2. If it does not normally apply Ignite or Burns, it instead applies Ignite 2 on a full hit.

title: Uchiha Shuriken Doctrine
text: While Sharingan is active, reduce penalties applied to a Multi-throw to a maximum reduction of 3. After a visible enemy successfully Dodges one of your Projectile Weapon attacks, gain 1 Read on that enemy and retrieve one thrown weapon that could plausibly be recovered by wire or ricochet as Speed 0.

title: Abilities
text: No Heritage-specific purchasable abilities.

title: Jutsu
text: C-Rank

title: Katon: Hōsenka Tsumabeni - Phoenix Flower Crimson Nail
text: C-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank C Chakra: 22 + 2X; also pay the Multi-Throw’s Stamina Damage: 6d10!o>9, then the Multi-Throw Range: 25 Area: Up to 4 targets within 8 yards of one another Speed: 14 + X for the linked Action Seal Speed: 10 Special: Ignite 3 Tags: Attack, Projectile, Katon, Weapon, Link Requires: Sharingan active Effects Link this technique to a Multi-Throw of shuriken or senbon. X is the total number of weapons thrown, using the normal Multi-Throw limit and one weapon type. Divide them among up to four targets, assigning at least two weapons to each. All targets must be within 25 yards, within the weapons’ Range, and within 8 yards of one another. Declare the targets and weapon allocation before rolling. Perform the handseals, then pay this technique’s Chakra and the Multi-Throw’s normal Stamina, making both Fatigue rolls. The linked Action has Base Speed 14+X; advance your IC by its modified Final Speed once. Separately calculate each target’s Multi-Throw Speed using its assigned weapons and normal modifiers, minimum 5. Use those separate Speeds for the weapon stages’ damage and defense legality. Fire stage: roll 1d20 + your Ninjutsu Accuracy modifiers, omitting the usual base 10. Make one attack roll and compare it with each target’s defense. Each target declares one legal defense before the roll. Use the linked Action’s Final Speed for fire damage and defense legality. On a full defensive success, that target avoids both the fire and its concealed weapons. On a Partial Defense, apply the reduced fire damage and Ignite, then resolve the weapon stage. On a full defensive failure, apply full fire damage and Ignite, then resolve the weapon stage. Fire damage is 6d10!o>9 + NDB × Final Speed. Each original die showing 9 or 10 adds one extra d10; extra dice do not explode. Apply Ignite 3 after a damaging fire hit, reduced for Partial Defense. Uchiha Fire Doctrine applies normally. Weapon stage: each target reached by the fire makes a second defense against its assigned Multi-Throw, using that Multi-Throw’s normal static Accuracy, Speed, weapon damage and bonuses. Declare this defense after the fire stage resolves, using the target’s resulting position, Fatigue and statuses. If the target has left the weapons’ Range or their path is blocked, resolve that obstruction or miss normally. Each stage allows one defense, with its own legality, costs and IC advancement. A fire-stage defense does not also defend against the weapons. Calculate each stage’s damage and mitigation separately; the fire’s Partial Defense does not reduce the weapon stage. Apply the normal Multi-Throw Wound reduction to weapon damage only. All weapons committed to this technique are destroyed when the Action resolves, including those stopped by the fire-stage defense. They cannot be recovered.

title: Uchiha Ryū: Sōfūshasan no Tachi - Manipulated Windmill Triple Blade
text: C-Rank Type: Bukijutsu, Rank C Stamina: 16 Damage: As Weapon Range: Weapon Range + 10 Speed: 12 Tags: Attack, Projectile, Weapon, Control Requires: Sharingan active Effects Throw up to three wired or chained projectile weapons and resolve them as one Attack. Gain +1 Accuracy per Read on the target spent when declaring the technique, maximum +3. On a full hit, choose one: apply Immobilization 3 for 20 IC; move the target up to 4 yards toward a legal point along the wires; or disarm one held weapon if its wielder fails an opposed STR or DEX check against your DEX. If the attack misses but is a partial, the weapons remain positioned around the target until your next Action. Your next Projectile Weapon attack against that target gains +2 Accuracy. B-Rank

title: Katon: Gōryūka no Jutsu - Great Dragon Fire Technique
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 34 Damage: 11d12 Range: 35 Area: Line 5, 25 Speed: 18 Seal Speed: 16 Special: Ignite 5 Tags: Attack, AoE, Projectile, Energy, Katon Effects Launch a dragon-shaped mass of flame down the line. If you spend 2 Reads on one creature in the Area, bend the line once by up to 90 degrees at a point you can see; that creature also suffers -2 Dodge against the attack. Terrain still blocks the flame normally. If the attack creates a Wound, leave a burning path across its Area for 20 IC. A creature crossing 3 or more yards of the path takes NDB x 3 Energy damage once per Action.

title: Magen: Kageutsushi - Demonic Illusion: False Opening
text: B-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 28 Range: Eye Contact Speed: 10 Tags: Attack, Genjutsu, Control Requires: Stage 2 Sharingan Effects On a successful Genjutsu attack, the target sees a deliberate opening where none exists. Until the end of its next Action, it suffers -2 to defenses against you and cannot gain a bonus from having observed, Prepared against, or Read your Action. If the target attacks you before the effect ends, gain 2 Reads on it after that attack resolves. At Stage 3, you can spend 2 Reads on the target when declaring this technique to increase the defense penalty to -4.

title: Sharingan: Gyakuyomi - Sharingan: Counter-Read
text: B-Rank Type: Ninjutsu, Rank B Chakra: 18 Speed: 5 Tags: Interrupt, Defense, Counter Requires: Stage 3 Sharingan Effects When a creature with at least 2 Reads targets you with a single-target Attack, spend 2 Reads and make a legal Dodge or Parry. Gain +2 to that defense. On success, after the attack resolves you can immediately take one of the following without increasing your IC: move up to 4 yards; make a Basic Weapon or Unarmed Attack at -2 Accuracy; or use a retained copied technique with final Speed 6 or less at 75% Final Damage. Pay all normal costs of the chosen option.

title: Magen: Kyouten Chiten - Demonic Illusion: Mirror Heaven and Earth Change
text: B-Rank Type: Genjutsu, Rank B Chakra: As reflected technique Speed: 6 + X Tags: Interrupt, Genjutsu Requires: Stage 3 Sharingan Effects Immediately after you successfully defend against a Genjutsu targeting you, you can reflect it through Eye of Hypnotism at its original user. X is half the reflected technique's final Speed, rounded up. Use the result of your successful Genjutsu Defense as the reflected technique's Accuracy and pay its normal Chakra cost. You must know or currently retain the reflected technique through Dousatsugan.

title: Core Rules
text: Character creation, attributes, skills, advancement, abilities, combat, wounds and downtime. The Fall of the Old World Nobody agrees on exactly when the old world ended. The oldest surviving records speak of the Five Great Nations, hidden villages with armies of shinobi, great clans, Kage, and wars that could reshape the land. Konoha, Suna, Kiri, Kumo, and Iwa still survive in names, ruins, bloodlines, and half-trusted records. Then came what modern people call the Bloom. Natural chakra surged across the world. Animals changed. Forests grew in days. Rivers shifted course. Creatures developed chakra organs, elemental abilities, armour, regeneration, intelligence, and instincts that turned ordinary hunting into war. The nations tried to fight the new world as they had fought one another. They lost. Within generations, the map stopped being divided by borders. It became divided by what could kill you there. The World Now Humanity does not control the Wastes. It occupies small pieces of them. Most settlements survive because they possess something worth defending: water, fertile soil, an old reactor, a mine, a sealed archive, a defensible canyon, or access to a trade route. The land between Havens is claimed by predators, migrating herds, raider gangs, scavenger crews, cults, caravans, old-world defence systems, and creatures whose territories are measured in hundreds of miles. Maps are temporary. Information about where a creature sleeps, when it migrates, what it hunts, and what makes it flee can save more lives than a single powerful jutsu. Haven Ember Every player character begins in Haven Ember, one of the larger independent settlements surviving beyond the direct rule of any major power. Several thousand people live around an old underground water system and the remains of a pre-Fall transport hub. Scrap-built outer districts surround older inner walls reinforced with sealing arrays recovered and repaired over generations. Ember has farms, workshops, clinics, markets, shrines, garages, training yards, a monster-processing hall, and more people than its current resources comfortably support. Its greatest advantage is a large, organised Hunter corps willing to take anyone useful enough to help keep the settlement alive. The Ember Corps Every player character belongs to the wider Ember Corps. The Corps is not a standing army in the old sense. It is a loose network of hunters, scouts, medics, salvagers, couriers, guides, researchers, mechanics, negotiators, and combat hunters who form temporary crews for specific jobs. A mission is posted. A crew forms from whoever is available and suited to the work. They leave Ember, handle the problem, and return with whatever they managed to save, learn, recover, kill, or accidentally make worse. The next mission may have a completely different team. Characters are expected to be people who can work with others when it matters. Rivalries, grudges, factional disagreements, criminal histories, and ideological conflict are welcome. Refusing to cooperate with the wider community as a basic character premise is not.

title: Getting Started
text: Welcome to Naruto World: Ember Corps. Below is the information required to make your character.

title: Character Concept
text: Start with a name, a role in the Corps, a heritage or a few personality traits. Build the rest of your character around that idea as you choose their abilities.

title: Haven Ember and Heritage
text: Your character begins in Haven Ember and serves in the Ember Corps. They may also belong to a clan household, guild, caravan, faith or faction. Choose one Primary Heritage from Clans & Lineages; mixed ancestry does not grant additional heritage mechanics. The old Hidden Villages survive as ancestral homes, ruins and traditions. They are not current player allegiances. Inherited abilities require the heritage that grants them, unless an explicit rule allows another method of acquisition. Choose Uniques Begin with 6 Unique Points (UP). Pay your Heritage Cost from this pool, then spend or save the remainder. Creation Uniques can only be chosen at character creation. See Uniques for costs and restrictions.

title: Character Creation Modes
text: Choose Standard Mode or Realistic Mode when creating your Hunter. Unless stated otherwise, both modes use the normal starting XP, attributes, skills and 6 Unique Points.

title: Standard Mode
text: Choose one Primary Heritage from the Heritage Cost Index in Volume III and pay its listed UP cost. Mixed ancestry is valid for your character's story, but it does not grant a second set of heritage mechanics.

title: Realistic Mode
text: Realistic Mode uses the lineage table below to generate heritage options. Pay 1 additional UP to enter Realistic Mode, then roll d100 to determine your Primary Heritage using the table below. Pay that heritage's normal UP cost separately from your remaining starting UP. You receive +10% base XP while playing in Realistic Mode. This modifies XP earned, not your starting XP or heritage cost. You may reroll the d100 lineage result any number of times without sacrificing XP; once you commit to a result, record it on your character sheet and use that heritage. A reroll replaces the earlier result rather than adding another heritage. Your rolled Primary Heritage follows all ordinary restrictions and prerequisites.

title: Realistic Lineage Table
text: d100 Primary Heritage :--- :--- 1–5 Funato 6–10 Shiin 11–15 Ouyoku 16–20 Karatachi Family 21–25 Fūma 26–30 Yotsuki 31–35 Iburi 36–40 Sarutobi 41–43 Silverhand 44–46 Kamizuru 47–49 Hoshigaki 50–52 Yamanaka 53–55 Jinrō 56–58 Jashin Worshipper 59–61 Nara 62–64 Samsara 65–67 Hokori 68–70 Akimichi 71–73 Inuzuka 74–75 Karashi (Puppets) 76–77 Aburame 78–79 Yōton 80–81 Futton 82–83 Shakuton 84–85 Yuki 86–87 Hōzuki 88–89 Kazekage Clan / Jiton 90–91 Jūgo's Bloodline 92–93 Uzumaki 94–95 Hyūga 96–97 Senju 98 Bakuton 99 Kaguya 100 Uchiha

title: Determine Attributes
text: Attributes (also known as Stats) represent your character’s raw capabilities. The five attributes are: Strength (STR), Resilience (RES), Chakra (CHA), Dexterity (DEX), and Agility (AGI). More information is covered in the Attributes chapter. A new character starts with 20 in all Attributes. They also begin with 25 points to distribute among their attributes as they like, with no more than ten in a single attribute.

title: Choose Skills
text: A new character gains 1 Skill Point for every 20 XP. These Skill Points can be spent on any of the game's 14 skills.

title: Experience Costs
text: With your uniques, starting attributes, and skills decided, it's time to spend your XP! XP can be used to learn new Jutsu and abilities, and to increase your attributes! These options are further explained in their respective chapters. Novice Hunter often learn the E-Rank Ninjutsu techniques Kawarimi, Henge, and Bunshin during their initial training. These are not mandatory, but they can be very useful. A rank in the Elemental Aptitude ability (detailed in the Chakra Abilities chapter) can also be useful. Suggestions aside, you may spend your XP on whatever you feel makes most sense for your character.

title: Jutsu
text: Jutsu are chakra-based techniques: Taijutsu enhances physical combat, Ninjutsu shapes chakra into external effects, and Genjutsu alters perception. See the Jutsu Compendium for techniques and learning requirements.

title: Abilities
text: Spend XP on Abilities to develop your character’s trained capabilities.

title: Downtime
text: Between scenes, spend Downtime Slots on work, training, crafting and research. Record Actions and linked rolls in your Logs.

title: Starting XP
text: Begin with 500 XP at Stray rank. Your total XP determines starting Skill Points, Skill limits and any XP-based prerequisites.

title: Character Review
text: When you feel your sheet is complete, have a Gamemaster (GM) review it to make sure everything is in order. It is optional but recommended to include a character background. It does not have to be particularly long or complex, only enough to give the GM personal character hooks for future play.

title: Final Creation Rules
text: Unique Points, Experience Points, and Skill Points cannot be spent during combat, or during any events that you are a part of; they may only be spent before or after. And provided you are under 1.5k XP, you may rework any aspect of your sheet.

title: Primary Stats
text: The five Attributes measure strength, resilience, chakra, dexterity and agility. Ordinary human Attributes are around 20; chakra conditioning lets Hunters exceed them. Strength (STR) Strength is a measurement of your ability to exert physical force on the world around you. Exceptionally strong people may be correspondingly muscular, though hunters have developed many training methods which leave them deceptively lean. - Your physical damage bonus is STR/18. - Your Vitality is (RES6 + STR3) Resilience (RES) This is your body's ability to endure hardship without suffering from debilitating injuries. Many hunters believe that it's best to avoid being hit entirely... but nobody will say that not being able to take a blow is a good thing. - Your Vitality is (RES6 + STR3) - Your HP is (RES2 + CHA) - You add 1 + RES/12 to your Stamina rolls Chakra (CHA) Every hunter is fueled by chakra, a mystical force that suffuses the world and fills the bodies of all living things, much like 'ki' in certain belief systems. This stat measures both your reserves of raw chakra and your ability to harness them. - Your ninjutsu damage bonus is CHA/18. - You add 1 + CHA/12 to your Chakra Exhaustion rolls. Dexterity (DEX) Representing your deftness, precision, and ability to quickly respond to changes in your environment, dexterity is very important in combat, as it is what enables you to actually hit things that are moving (such as other hunters). - Your base Accuracy bonus is DEX/10. - Seal Speed of jutsu you perform is reduced by DEX/10. Agility (AGI) The sister attribute to dexterity, agility is how quickly you can react to danger, how fast you can move, and, as the name suggests, how agile you are overall. - You add AGI/10 to your Dodge rolls. - You add AGI/10 to your Initiative rolls.

title: Secondary Stats
text: Vitality (Vit) Vitality measures your character's ability to shrug off damage, to turn a dangerous blow into a glancing one, and to take a beating without being seriously injured. You have a current and maximum vitality; whenever you take damage, you reduce your current vitality by that amount, though your maximum Vitality is unaffected. - Your vitality equals your (RES6 + STR3). Hit Points (HP) Hit points are like your 'life force', representing injuries that have significantly harmed you and caused serious damage to your body. After your Vitality reaches 0, you take damage to your Hit Points; an attack which depletes your Vitality has the rest of its damage carry over into your HP. - You have (RES2 + CHA) Hit Points. Damage Bonus, Physical (PDB) As the name would suggest, this increases the damage you do with physical attacks. Full details on how can be found in the Combat chapter. - Your damage bonus is STR/18. Damage bonus is unique in that it is calculated to a single decimal place. For example, with STR 25, your Physical Damage Bonus is 25/18 = 1.388..., recorded as 1.3 when truncated to one decimal place. Damage Bonus, Ninjutsu (NDB) Applies to attacks powered by chakra, usually Ninjutsu. It follows the same calculation and rounding rules as Physical Damage Bonus. - Your damage bonus is CHA/18. Willpower (WP) Your determination and ability to push beyond your normal limits. - You have a base WP of 3 which can be increased mainly through uniques (such as Hidden Potential) or the Determined ability.

title: INFAMY
text: Infamy measures how widely your name and deeds are known. It covers celebrated Hunters, feared criminals and public figures alike. High Infamy can bring recognition, influence or unwanted attention; it does not measure combat strength.

title: Gaining Infamy
text: Gain +1 Infamy per 500 total XP and +2 per A-Rank Jutsu learned. These are automatic progression awards. GMs may also award Infamy for public accomplishments, discoveries, crimes or other events. Event awards require your involvement to become known. Witnesses, reports and rumours can spread your reputation, even when their account is inaccurate.

title: Infamy Scale
text: 0–5 — Unknown You are largely another face in the crowd. People within your immediate community may know who you are, but your reputation rarely extends beyond your friends, family, and colleagues. 6–15 — Recognized You have begun building a local reputation. Other Hunters, hunters, merchants, or travellers around Haven Ember may recognize your name or remember something you have done. 16–30 — Notable Stories about you have begun travelling beyond the people who know you personally. Your exploits may be discussed between crews, caravans, neighbouring settlements, or organisations. 31–50 — Famous Your name carries weight. People who have never met you may know your reputation, clan, accomplishments, or signature techniques. Important victories and failures may follow you from settlement to settlement. 51–70 — Renowned You are well known throughout large portions of the world accessible to travellers. Experienced Hunters and hunters may recognize you immediately and may already have an idea of what you are capable of. 71–90 — Legendary Your reputation has become larger than the person behind it. Stories about you travel enormous distances, enemies may actively prepare for the possibility of encountering you, and your involvement in an event can change how others approach it. 91–99 — Living Legend Your name has become part of modern history. Even people far removed from hunters affairs may have heard stories about you. Governments, Havens, organisations, and powerful individuals are unlikely to treat your presence casually. 100 — Icon Your name is known across the world. You have become one of the defining figures of your era, the kind of person whose actions will be remembered long after they are gone

title: Skills
text: Skills measure broad competencies. Describe how your character uses a Skill, then resolve the task with its normal roll. Your skills all have a limit of 5 +(your total XP)/200 Ranks. A lot of them benefit from practical application and general worldliness. Actually increasing your skills up to that limit, however, requires you to spend skill points. Your Skill Point total is total XP divided by 20, rounded down. A single skill point raises a single skill by one rank. At 600 XP you have 30 Skill Points and a normal rank limit of 8 per skill. A skill roll is 1d20 + your ranks in that skill. Untrained skills may be rolled with no rank bonus.

title: Athletics
text: You use athletics when you perform acrobatics, leap across a chasm, try to navigate difficult terrain, weave your way between traps, swim across a river, or so forth. You can flip, tumble, and keep your balance under difficult circumstances.

title: Awareness
text: How perceptive you are. This applies to things like hearing a faint noise, noticing that you're being followed, spying on a single conversation in a crowded room, and finding an enemy hiding from you in combat.

title: Chakra Control
text: This is your ability to control the flow of the chakra within your own body, using it efficiently and shaping it precisely to do what you want. To a limited extent, it also represents how intuitively aware you are of the nature of chakra in general, and might allow you to notice when something's unusual about the surrounding chakra.

title: Ninshou
text: Your study and practice of jutsu: chakra theory, elemental shaping, handseals and the principles behind techniques. Learning Elemental Ninjutsu requires both Ninshou and Chakra Control; see Jutsu Requirements.

title: Lore
text: Knowledge of history, oral traditions, old-world records, monsters and earlier Hunts. Lore may always replace the listed skill for any Hunt roll, including Track, Research, Study Weakness and Prepare.

title: Espionage
text: Something of a catch-all skill, this includes most things shady and underhanded. Pickpocketing, lock-picking, setting and disarming (or sabotaging) traps, forging documents, sleight of hand, and disguising yourself all fall under the umbrella of espionage.

title: Medicine
text: You have knowledge of the human body and how it works. This includes biology, first aid, and at higher levels actual medical procedures and requirements. With a few ranks, you can probably apply a tourniquet; with enough, you might even deserve a 'Doctor' in front of your name (but good luck actually getting any respect!).

title: Research
text: Book smarts, overall knowledge, and an ability to gather information. Research can be used to solve complicated code and ciphers, find information in a library, and get up to date on the latest gossip when in a new town.

title: Resistance
text: Not to be confused with resilience, this is how well your body is able to fend off the ravages of the environment and all sorts of unpleasantness that might befall it, from blistering heat to poison to burns. This is primarily useful for fighting off unpleasant status effects that may afflict you, both in combat and out.

title: Stealth
text: Stealth determines whether an opponent can locate you and which attacks can benefit from concealment.

title: Survival
text: This lets you forage for food and move easily through hostile environments. While resistance might keep sunburn at bay while stranded in the desert, survival will help you find the nearest oasis and make an umbrella out of palm fronds. It's also used to track people and animals, and avoid being tracked.

title: Diplomacy
text: Your innate charisma and ability to speak, this allows you to speak convincingly in any form. From logical analysis proving your point beyond a shadow of a doubt, threatening them to agree to what you want, to saying trust me bro and people believe you because you’re just a trustworthy guy.

title: Artisan
text: The skill that defines crafters as it allows you to well…craft. When you take this skill you must specify Weapon, Armor, or Craftsman choosing the types of equipment you specialize in.

title: Toxicology
text: This represents overall familiarity with poisons. While high enough medicine might be able to identify a poison, its symptoms, and how to treat it, toxicology knows what plant or animal that poison comes from, how long it takes before effects set in, and just how deadly it can be. Many medics have enough of this skill to be helpful in their work... but it's also very handy if you find yourself needing to poison someone. For practical applications of all fourteen skills, see Skill Actions.

title: Attributes
text: XP can be spent to increase any of your five basic attributes. Starting out, the cost to do this is 4 XP per 1 point in any single attribute. The primary restriction on this is the poorly-named 'rule of 3'. What this means is: the amount you have increased an attribute may not be more than 3 points higher than the next highest amount you have increased an attribute by. Because an example will make it clearer: You could raise your STR by 3 points (for 12 XP). To raise it to 4 points, a single other attribute would need to have been raised by at least 1, for a total of (4+1)4 = 20 XP. Say you had raised your STR and RES by 12 each, your CHA by 9, your AGI by 6, and your DEX by 3. You could raise your STR or your RES to 15 right away, but to raise both of them to 13 you'd need to raise your DEX, AGI, and CHA by 1 each (in that order). And, to be clear, only the amount you have raised an attribute by using XP matters; its starting value, or bonuses from uniques (or any other sources), is not part of this limit. Aside from that restriction, raising attributes summons from a degree of diminishing returns. The first 50 points in an attribute cost, as stated, 4 XP; the next 50 cost 5 XP per +1, the next 50 cost 6 XP per +1, and so forth. Thus, to raise your STR by 62 points you would have to spend a total of (504 + 125) = 260 XP... not counting what you'd have to spend on other attributes to satisfy the 'rule of 3'. Finally, you may spend no more than half your total XP on stats. So, if you had 1000 XP, you could spend no more 500 XP on raising your stat points.

title: Abilities
text: The full details of spending XP to learn abilities are discussed in Chapter 4. But, in brief: it varies from one ability to another, with the costs being listed in individual abilities.

title: Jutsu
text: A hunter who intends to be successful would do well to have a wide variety of techniques at their disposal. The actual restrictions on what you can and can't learn are discussed in detail in Chapter 6. Once you meet the requirements to acquire a jutsu you want, to learn (or 'purchase') it you spend an amount of XP determined by its rank, as listed... below: E: 4 D: 6 C: 9 B: 18 A: 36

title: Other
text: Anything else you can spend XP on will likely explain the rules for doing so in its description.

title: Experience Bonuses
text: Clanless characters, and certain clans (which will say so in their description), get what is called an experience bonus. This is an amount beyond your Total XP which you can spend. Experience Bonuses are given in percentages--for example, Clanless characters have a 10% XP Bonus. Take, for example, a clanless character who's earned 100 XP from RP, 100 from fighting, and 23 from events, on top of his starting 100 XP. This means that his Total XP is 323, just like any normal character. However, he also has a 10% XP bonus; this means that his bonus XP is 32. Thus, in his Spent XP log (you'll read more about logs later in this chapter) he would record XP Total as 323, "XP Bonus (%)" as 32 (and change the % to 10%), and "Total + Bonus" as (323+32) 355. Your total amount of XP spent can go up to your Total + Bonus. However, your bonus is not actually part of your Total XP. Many things are based on your Total XP, such as bonuses to Genjutsu rolls, your Skill Points, and Talents. XP bonuses have no effect on these.

title: Roleplay
text: Roleplay is interacting with others while playing as your character. Every half hour of active in-character play awards 4 XP. You must remain reasonably active throughout this. Thus, if you were playing for an hour and a half, but had to take a twenty minute break in the middle for whatever reason, you would get 8 XP, counting only the hour and ten minutes during which you were actually RPing. In addition, meaningful character moments can award bonus XP. These are called Roleplay Beats. Each Beat is worth 3 XP, and each type of Beat may only be claimed once per scene. Bond: A relationship with another character meaningfully develops, changes, or is put under strain. Reveal: Your character reveals something important about themselves, or learns something important about another character. Drive: Your character meaningfully pursues one of their goals, beliefs, loyalties, flaws, or other established motivations. Change: The scene causes your character to make a meaningful decision, commitment, or change which carries forward beyond the scene. You can earn a maximum of 12 bonus XP from Roleplay Beats in a single scene. These are not rewards for mentioning your backstory, repeating the same character trait, or forcing four boxes to be ticked every time you RP. Something should actually happen. When in doubt, use common sense.

title: Combat
text: Combat awards 4 XP per 30 minutes, with a minimum duration of 30 minutes. At the end of a fight, apply the following: - Bonuses: +1 XP per ending Fatigue level, maximum +5 XP; +3 XP for each Wound category suffered during the fight, maximum +12 XP across Minor, Major, Severe and Critical. - Penalties: -2 XP per starting Fatigue level and -1 XP per starting Wound, regardless of severity. - If reward-granting Fatigue is recovered through a method other than standard Rest, such as a Soldier Pill, remove the XP awarded for that Fatigue. You cannot gain XP for fighting the same opponent again within 24 hours. A larger group containing opponents you have not fought during that period can still qualify. Combat remains roleplay and can earn Roleplay Beats. At the end of the scene, choose Combat Bonuses or Roleplay Beats; you cannot claim both. Do not claim two time-based XP awards for the same period.

title: Events
text: Although the game revolves around the PCs, the world they're in does not. Things are constantly going on off-screen, separate from casual roleplaying. Sometimes, GMs will make this known through an Event. These are often Ember Corps missions posted for whoever is available and suited to the work: escorting a caravan, hunting a monster, recovering salvage, mapping a route, protecting a settlement asset, investigating a threat, or dealing with whatever else has crawled out of the wastes this week. While taking part in an Event, you do not gain normal Roleplay or Combat XP. Instead, the Event awards XP for its entire duration. The GM running the Event determines its rewards.

title: Missions
text: Missions award 8 XP per 30 minutes, modified by the danger of the Mission. No Danger: ×0.5 Average Threat: ×1 Extreme Danger: ×1.25 This gives 4, 8 or 10 XP per 30 minutes respectively. Danger is based on the Mission as a whole, not simply whether combat occurred. An expedition through dangerous terrain, a tense infiltration, or an investigation where failure has serious consequences can still be dangerous without turning into a fight. Fatigue and Wounds suffered during a Mission award XP as normal. Mission Ryo depends on the job. As a rough guideline, low-end work pays around 2,000 Ryo, ordinary missions around 8,000 Ryo, and major operations 12,000 Ryo or more.

title: Hunts
text: Hunts award 8 XP per 30 minutes, modified by the Fight Value of the Monster. Weak: ×0.75 Regular: ×1 Above Curve: ×1.25 This gives 6, 8 or 10 XP per 30 minutes respectively. Fatigue and Wounds suffered during a Hunt award XP as normal. Hunt Ryo is calculated as: Category × Monster XP Value × Fight Value Where Fight Value is 0.75 for Weak, 1 for Regular, and 1.25 for Above Curve. Additional rewards such as Monster Parts or other unusual materials may be given separately.

title: Other
text: You may get XP in some other fashion. Usually, this will involve a GM telling you how much you got, and for what reason. You can never gain more than one source of time-based XP for the same period of play. If a spar becomes a long conversation, a conversation becomes a fight, or an Event contains both, you do not need to stop a timer and start doing maths. Use the rules for the scene you're actually playing and, as always, use common sense.

title: What Abilities Are
text: Abilities grant trained methods and lasting improvements. Purchase them with XP using the costs below. You may choose to hold back an Ability’s effects.

title: Purchasing Abilities
text: Abilities are acquired by spending XP. Some abilities will list only a "Cost"; for those abilities, you spend that much XP and acquire the ability, and that is it. Others will list both a "Cost" and a "Scale." These abilities can be purchased more than once. The first time, you pay the Cost in XP; each future purchase has its cost increased by the Scale. For example, the Enhanced Hearing ability has Cost 4, Scale 3. One rank of Enhanced Hearing would cost 4 XP. The second would cost (4+3) 7 XP, and the third would cost (4+3+3) 10 XP. So, the total XP spent to get all three ranks would be (4 + 7 + 10) 21 XP. Abilities with more than one rank will also include a Limit entry. This is what controls how many ranks of the ability you can have. So, if an ability (such as Attentive) said "Research /5" and you had 12 ranks of Research, you could buy that ability twice. Many abilities will include in their limit line a maximum, such as "Limit: CHA /10, max 4". This means that you may take that ability up to that many times (so in that example, 4). Certain abilities will also say "Requires: (something)". You cannot take any ranks in that ability unless you meet the requirement.

title: Brute Force
text: Your training puts greater force behind physical attacks. Each rank increases your physical damage bonus by 0.2. Cost: 5 Limit: STR /10 Requires: 80 STR

title: Endurance
text: Your extensive physical conditioning has given you an almost preternatural ability to shrug off damage Each rank in this ability increases your Block by 5%. While Prep Blocking, each rank instead increases your Block by 10%. This can only increase your Block to a 75% reduction. Cost: 8 Scale: 2 Limit: RES/20, max 8

title: Fortitude
text: Every rank of this ability gives you a +2 bonus to Resistance rolls when you block an attack (even if you are doing so reflexively); if you've declared that you're blocking, this also applies to any effects requiring a Resistance roll which you wouldn't normally get to defend against (such as the B-rank Poison Mist). If you've declared you're blocking and take another defense half of this abilities bonus will still apply to your rolls. Cost: 2 Scale: 2 Limit: STR /20, max 5

title: Good Lungs
text: All this hunter work has left you well beyond what peak physical condition would be for an ordinary person. In addition to being able to fight and exert yourself for abnormally long times, you recover from such exertion almost supernaturally fast. When you use the Rest action to lower your Stamina penalty, it's reduced by 1 more per rank (so at two ranks, a Speed 5 Rest action would decrease your Stamina penalty by 3). Cost: 10 Scale: 5 Limit: RES /80

title: Hard to Kill
text: You prove distressingly difficult to make dead. Your max Vitality and HP are increased by 10% per rank. However, Wounds are calculated off your unmodified ("true") maximums. For example, if you had 1000 Vitality and 3 ranks of Hard to Kill, you'd have 1300 Vitality. However, your "true" maximum would still be 1000, and wounds would be determined based on what percent of 1000 Vitality their damage was. Cost: 6 Scale: 1 Limit: RES /20 Requires: 80 RES

title: Rigorous Training
text: You've spent time training in, or just being exposed to, extreme conditions; sitting under waterfalls, trudging through sand dunes, or enduring intense cold without the proper clothing are all examples of how this might come about. You have a +1 bonus to Resistance rolls per rank. Cost: 2 Scale: 2 Limit: RES /20

title: Healthy
text: You get plenty of exercise, and probably eat healthily. When your job places serious physical demands upon you (such as leaping across chasms and running over rooftops), this can be useful. You have a +1 bonus to Stamina rolls per rank. Cost: 5 Scale: 1 Limit: Athletics /5

title: Power Attack
text: You put extra force behind your unarmed strikes, turning your feeble punches into fearsome punches! Or... something like that. Each rank allows you to increase the Stamina cost, and die size, of your basic unarmed attack by 2. So at rank 1, you could deal Xd6 damage for 7 Stamina; and at rank 4, you could deal Xd12 damage for 13 Stamina. Cost: 4 Scale: 1 Limit: (STR - 30)/15, max 8

title: Unarmed Focus
text: You've trained to improve your sheer physical prowess; even when resorting to simple, non-jutsu attacks, you hit hard. May or may not be the result of deciding to train by punching trees until your knuckles bleed. Each rank lets you roll one more die when making a basic unarmed attack. Cost: 3 Limit: (STR - 20) /10

title: Taijutsu Expertise
text: You have chosen the path of taijutsu, the superior method of fighting. Through training you've developed enough tricks to improve your ability to land these types of attacks. This gives you a +1 bonus to Taijutsu Accuracy (but not parry) per rank. Cost: 5 Scale: 2 Limit: STR / 40

title: Evasive
text: You're big on not being around when people try to violently end your life. Every rank gives you a +1 bonus to dodge, it's awesome! Cost: 6 Scale: 1 Limit: AGI /20, max 10

title: Swift
text: Swift, adjective; happening quickly or promptly. Your swiftness allows you to react faster, and makes it harder for your opponents to keep up with you. Each rank gives you +1 to Accuracy. Cost: 5 Scale: 1 Limit: (AGI - 50) /10, max 10

title: Nimble
text: When targeted by an area-of-effect attack that gives you a dodge penalty based on its size, that penalty is reduced by 2 per rank, to a minimum of 0. Cost: 4 Scale: 1 Limit: AGI /20

title: Runner
text: You train for both speed and endurance. Every rank in this ability increases your AGI for the purpose of movement by 10% when you're taking a Move action; moving as part of an attack, or techniques such as Shunshin, do not receive Runner's bonus. Cost: 3 Scale: 2 Limit: Athletics /3, max 5

title: Sudden Attack
text: You sacrifice power for speed and precision, trying to overwhelm or overcome your opponent's defenses before they have a chance to protect themselves. For every rank, you may take a bonus of up to +1 on a Damage-Dealing non-Weapon Taijutsu Attack's Accuracy. Each +1 applied reduces that Attack’s Damage by 10%. Cost: 4 Scale: 1 Limit: DEX /20, max 5

title: Evasive Training
text: You’ve trained to be aware, awake and always on the defence, you gain +1 to Dodge per rank, and +1 to Parry every other rank. Cost: 5 Scale: 3 Limit: Lower of AGI /20 or DEX /20, max 10 Requires: Basic Training 2+

title: Combo Master
text: You have mastered the art of Combo Taijutsu. Your Combos are more lethal and go farther. The first time you hit a combo target in a combo your CC is increased by half your ranks in this ability (rounded down). Cost: 6 Scale: 2 Limit: Special You can have 1 rank in this ability for each rank of combo jutsu you know at least one technique from. Thus, if you knew an E-rank, D-rank, and B-rank move, you could have 3 ranks of Combo Master.

title: Shadowboxer
text: Even when people hide from you, you manage to look for them without losing steam for a while. By reducing your Combo Counter by 1 point, you can perform a Search action without breaking your Combo. Cost: 10 Requires: Combo Master 1

title: Momentum Sprinter
text: You have trained to keep your eyes on the ball, even if you need to chase it all around the field you never lose momentum. You may take up to Combo Counter x 4 IC of Move Action without breaking your current Combo. This does not have to be continuous so you could move for 5 IC attack, then move for another IC. Cost: 10 Requires: Combo Master 3

title: Somatic Caster
text: You weave Ninjutsu into a combo to strengthen an attack or overcome a defense. You can use one non-interrupt Ninjutsu technique at any point during your current Combo. This reduces your CC equal to the rank of the jutsu used. Cost: 10 Requires: Combo Master 5

title: Signature Move
text: You've trained yourself to be deadly efficient with one specific finisher. “I had to give him the three piece … with the soda” - Old Haven proverb. Choose one jutsu you know with the Finisher tag. Every time you use that finisher the damage penalty from using Sudden Attack is reduced by 10% per CC you have to a minimum of 0. Cost: 20 Requires: STR 80

title: Grapple Expertise
text: You have trained to take control of an opponent the moment you get your hands on them. Each rank gives you +1 to Grapple Offense. Cost: 10 Limit: RES / 40, rounded down, maximum 3

title: Grapple Mastery
text: Your knowledge of grappling techniques makes every hold and counter more effective. Each rank gives you +1 to Grapple rolls. Cost: 2 Scale: 4 Limit: Number of distinct Grapple Jutsu you know

title: Pressure
text: You use your weight and leverage to drive pressure into vulnerable points. Each rank gives you +1 to your Grapple Offense. Cost: 4 Limit: Resistance / 2, After 10 reduced to / 3

title: Grip Fighting
text: You’re fast with your hands blocking opponents' attempts to gain control while forcing your own. You gain access to the following Link: Reposition (Stamina: X2, Speed:+ X, AP: X Link). This is added on to any jutsu with the Trapping or Ground Fighting tags, or the Break Clinch or Escape Grapple Actions. You gain X Control (prior to the opponent's defense being rolled). X has a maximum of your ranks in this ability. Cost: 6 Scale: 2 Limit: Athletics/5, max 4

title: Escape Artist
text: You use your weight and leverage to drive pressure into vulnerable points. Each rank gives you +1 to your Grapple Defense. Cost: 6 Scale: 1 Limit: Survival /5

title: Elemental Affinity
text: Every hunter has a natural affinity for one of the five primary elements, though some may not discover it until later. This ability can be taken for any one of the five elements, even one your character cannot use. For each rank, you get a +1 bonus to Chakra Exhaustion and Chakra Control rolls involving your favored element. When learning Elemental Ninjutsu of your chosen element, reduce either its Chakra Control or Ninshou minimum by 1 per Affinity rank, and reduce the combined minimum by the same amount. Choose the skill for each requirement check; count Affinity only once. Cost: 0 Scale: 3 Limit: CHA /20, max 5 Special: You may only take this ability for a single element, ever.

title: Elemental Aptitude
text: The hunters of the world recognize five primary elements of chakra: fire, water, wind, earth, and lightning. These elements and their properties form the basis of most modern ninjutsu techniques. However, actually using elemental chakra requires the ability to convert one's own chakra to the appropriate element, which is what this ability provides. In simpler terms, when you take Elemental Aptitude, select one of the five elements; you may use elemental ninjutsu of that element. Each additional rank of this ability allows you to use another element. Cost: 5 Scale: +25 Limit: 3 Certain clans begin with one or more ranks in this ability. In these cases, they have the first one or two ranks in this ability for free, but must pay the scaled cost when buying the next one. For example, a Yuki begins with elemental aptitude for Water and Wind. Normally, this would cost (5 + (5+25)) 35 XP; instead, it costs 0. However, when they buy access to their third element, doing so costs 55 XP instead of (55 + 35) 90 XP.

title: Elemental Expression
text: When you declare a Jutsu with the Katon, Suiton, Doton, Fūton, or Raiton Keyword, you may spend 1 Willpower to replace one of those Keywords with another of the five primary elemental Keywords for which you possess Elemental Aptitude. This choice must be made when the Jutsu is declared, before any rolls are made, and lasts only for that use of the technique. For that use, the Jutsu is treated as belonging to the new element for all purposes. Its damage type changes to the appropriate type, it loses all inherent properties granted by its original element, and gains all inherent properties granted by the new one. It also gains some new effects based on it’s new element; Katon (Fire) Attack Jutsu: It’s damage gains !>X where X is it’s maximum Dice Value Defence Jutsu: Alongside any elemental advantages, reduce the Jutsu’s base speed by 2, to a minimum of 3. Utility Jutsu: The Jutsu creates a bright light, and reduces darkness based Vis by 5 within an X yard radius, where X is the rank while active. Doton (Earth) Attack Jutsu: For each damage die rolled, add +1d4 damage to the Jutsu’s final damage for the purposes of determining wounds. Defence Jutsu: Alongside any elemental advantages, you gain DR equal to the Jutsu’s Rank 5 until your next action, this stacks with itself. Utility Jutsu: The technique may create or manipulate mundane earth, stone, or similar natural terrain appropriate to its existing effects. Fuuton (Wind) Attack Jutsu: The Jutsu cannot be blocked, but gains no wounding advantage Defence Jutsu: Alongside any elemental advantages, you may reduce the final Chakra cost of the Jutsu by 2 Utility Jutsu: The Jutsu creates a strong wind, clearing any smoke-based effects of it’s rank or lower in X IC where X is 20-(Rank2) Suiton (Water) Attack Jutsu: You may expend 0>(X2) gallons for the Jutsu, where X is it’s rank, for every Gallon spent, increase the final damage by 5% Defence Jutsu: Alongside any elemental advantages, you may expend 0>X gallons for the Jutsu, where X is it’s rank, it reduces it’s final speed by 1 per 2 Gallons spent. Utility Jutsu: You may expend 0>X gallons for this Jutsu, where X is it’s rank, for every Gallon spend, decrease the Jutsu’s final speed by 2. Raiton (Lightning) Attack Jutsu: The Jutsu inflicts Paralysis equal to it’s Rank on a successful hit Defence Jutsu: Alongside any elemental advantages, the jutsu counts as X Speed less, to a minimum of 1 for the purposes of determining how much your IC increases, where X is its Rank. Utility Jutsu: N/A If a Jutsu qualifies as more than one type, choose whether it is treated as an Attack, Defence, or Utility Jutsu when Elemental Expression is used. It gains only that Expression. Cost: 50 Scale: 0 Limit: 1 Special: You require access to all 5 elements for this ability.

title: Homing
text: You are able to twist and bend your Jutsu to become more accurate, and gain the focus to land your hits. For every rank, you may take a bonus of +1 on a damaging non-area Ninjutsu attack’s Accuracy. Each +1 applied increases Jutu's charka cost by +4. Cost: 20 Scale: 15 Limit: CHA/50, Max 5.

title: Improved Area
text: This supplements your Ninjutsu and Genjutsu Techniques, increasing their Area (So long as they have the appropriate tag) by up to your Ninjutsu Damage Bonus; to a max increase of half of the original Area. Purchasing the second Rank of this Ability changes it to NDB1.5 to a max of double of the original Area. you can use some, all, or none of this effect on a given technique, as you please. Cost: 20 Scale: 15 Limit: CHA/50, Max 2.

title: Improved Range
text: You're able to keep your chakra coherent for longer; the further it can travel before dissipating (or the faster you can propel it, or whatever)... well, the advantages should be obvious. This increases the range of any ninjutsu techniques you use by up to double your ninjutsu damage bonus in yards. This bonus cannot exceed the technique's base range. Cost: 30

title: Potent Chakra
text: You're able to increase your chakra's density, and in turn preserve some of the energy that would dissipate into the atmosphere around you in whatever sort of attack you're using. But all you really care about is that it makes your ninjutsu hurt more! Each rank increases your ninjutsu damage bonus by 0.2. Cost: 5 Limit: CHA /10 Requires: 80 CHA

title: Ninjutsu Expertise
text: You have chosen the path of ninjutsu, the superior method of fighting. Through training you've developed tricks to improve your ability to land these types of attacks. This gives you a +1 bonus to Ninjutsu Accuracy (but not parry) per rank. Cost: 5 Scale: 2 Limit: CHA / 40

title: Refined Chakra Control
text: Your precise control of chakra allows you to spend it more efficiently, wasting less and getting more out of what you do spend. Each rank of this ability gives you a +1 bonus on your Chakra Exhaustion rolls. Cost: 5 Scale: 1 Limit: Chakra Control /5, max 10

title: Wall Walking
text: This is standard Ember Corps chakra-control training, commonly taught to new hunters in the training yards. Training involves focusing a fixed amount of chakra at the bottom of one's feet and using that to adhere to a wall, tree, or other vertical surface. With this ability you can scale vertical surfaces, stand on ceilings, and so forth, at your normal movement speed. Cost: 10 Requires: 8 Chakra Control

title: Water Walking
text: You can stand on water! Hunters do this in the same way they'd adhere to a vertical surface, though actually pulling it off is much harder because the water is constantly moving underneath them, meaning the strength and distribution of chakra has to be constantly changed. Once a hunter is skilled enough, though, this becomes second nature, just like keeping one's balance on an unsteady surface. Cost: 15 Requires: 15 Chakra Control, Wall Walking

title: Genjutsu Training
text: You've mastered the art of... yeah, okay, no. You are able to use entry-level Genjutsu techniques. It's not much, but it's a start. Cost: 20 Requires: Diplomacy or Research 4

title: Attentive
text: You pay lots of attention to details! Beyond that, you're keen to pick up on things that other people wouldn't. Maybe that species of deer isn't native to this area, or the wood of an illusory wall is a type that isn't found in this part of the world. On the other hand, the more you know about these kinds of things, the more likely you are to get them right. Each rank gives a +1 bonus to your genjutsu rolls. Cost: 6 Scale: 1 Limit: Research /5

title: Genjutsu Awareness
text: You're good at picking up little details in your environment that aren't quite what they should be. Maybe it's that the ringing noise in your head isn't reverberating right, maybe it's that whoever constructed an illusion around you forgot to put door handles on all the doors. Whatever it is, it gives you a +1 bonus to defensive Genjutsu rolls per rank. Cost: 6 Scale: 1 Limit: Combined Enhanced Hearing or Enhanced Sight ranks

title: Genjutsu Competence
text: Genjutsu is notoriously difficult; very few hunters are able to just 'pick it up' without difficulty. Even being mediocre with genjutsu requires a significant amount of training and practice--which this ability represents. Each rank gives you a +1 bonus to your offensive Genjutsu rolls. Cost: 4 Limit: First 10 Diplomacy / 2, Then Diplomacy / 3

title: Genjutsu Expertise
text: You have chosen the path of genjutsu, the superior method of fighting. Through training you've developed tricks to improve your ability to land these types of attacks. This gives you a +1 bonus to your Genjutsu Offense per rank. Cost: 5 Scale: 2 Limit: CHA / 40

title: Genjutsu Mastery
text: Okay, NOW you've mastered the art of Genjutsu. Each rank gives you a +1 bonus to genjutsu rolls. Cost: 6 Scale: 4 Limit: Special You can have 1 rank in this ability for each rank of genjutsu you know at least one technique from. Thus, if you knew an E-rank, D-rank, and B-rank move, you could have 3 ranks of Genjutsu Mastery.

title: Reality Made False
text: There is very little that can stop you shaping your reality. Even when others tell you to wake up to it. Whenever you would spend a Willpower to reroll a Genjutsu Offence, or Genjutsu defence roll, you may spend an additional Willpower per rank, to increase that roll by +5. This stacks with all other modifiers Cost: 25 Scale: 10 Limit: Cha /50, max 3.

title: Illusion Multi-Targeting
text: This allows you to apply a genjutsu which normally must target a single person at once to any number of people. Every 1 point of Willpower spent allows your genjutsu to target two more people, at no additional cost and using your same genjutsu roll. Cost: 25 Requires: Genjutsu Mastery 3

title: Accurate
text: You've got good hand-eye coordination, which lends itself towards hitting with your attacks. You have a +1 bonus per rank to your Accuracy. Cost: 6 Scale: 1 Limit: DEX /20, max 10

title: Instinct
text: You've learned to rely on your instincts to guide you in battle, helping to improve your reaction time. Not by much--but enough to matter. Each rank gives a +1 bonus to dodge. Cost: 6 Scale: 2 Limit: Survival /5

title: Guarded
text: You know when to turn an offence into your best defence. Each rank gives a +1 bonus to Parry Cost: 10 Scale: 3 Limit: Survival /5

title: Sixth Sense
text: Hunter really do seem to have one, and no experienced hunters will deny it, not once they've faced down an opponent and actually, physically felt the killing intent radiating from them, or experienced a half-second of dread in the instant before an ambush was sprung. Nobody can quantify it, or say for sure what causes it, but hunter who don't want to die do well to listen to it. You begin each day with Sixth Sense equal to your ranks in this ability. For every current Sixth Sense you have a +1 bonus to Awareness and dodge rolls per rank. Whenever you would be sneak attacked this activates automatically, causing the attack to be treated as a surprise attack instead. You can always spend up to half your current Sixth Sense ranks in AP on defenses made vs surprise or sneak attacks, regardless of whether you’ve chosen to activate your sixth sense or not. Cost: 10 Scale: 4 Limit: CHA /40

title: Enhanced Hearing
text: Your hearing isn't actually (much) better than a normal person's, but you've learned how to not do what everyone normally does: tune out quiet, 'insignificant' background noises. You still can if you need to, but you can also avoid doing that, when you need to, say, listen for a skulking opponent. This gives you a +1 bonus to Awareness rolls per rank. Cost: 9 Scale: 1 Limit: CHA /25, max 4 Special: The two "Enhanced (Sense)" abilities share a Scale. That is, if you already had four ranks of Enhanced Sight, the first rank of Enhanced Hearing would cost (9+(14) = ) 13 XP.

title: Enhanced Sight
text: You're very good with attention to detail. You notice things that other people overlook, and as it turns you, that's a pretty useful job-related talent for a hunter. This gives you a +1 bonus to Awareness rolls per rank. Cost: 9 Scale: 1 Limit: (CHA - 10) /25, max 4 Special: Shares Scale with Enhanced Hearing.

title: Blind Fighting
text: Between smoke bombs, stealth missions at night, and hostile ninjutsu, hunters often find themselves operating with their vision impaired. This ability represents training to fight while relying on your other senses. Each rank of Blind Fighting reduces the maximum visibility penalty you can suffer from by 1. Cost: 7 Scale: 2 Limit: Enhanced Hearing ranks, max 4

title: Keen Senses
text: You're very good at picking up on tiny things that are just everso-slightly out of place! Normally, you get a cumulative +2 bonus every time you attempt to find someone using a Search action in combat. This raises that to +3 at the first rank, and +4 at the second. Cost: 8 Scale: 4 Limit: (Enhanced Sight ranks) /2

title: Basic Training
text: Hunter with the ability to use chakra can get away with not solving every problem through the application of stealth and cunning, it's true. But, to be viewed as a proper hunter, they need to be keenly aware of their surroundings, masters of deception, and able to vanish like a shadow. In practice, Stray find those things exceptionally boring, especially when they could be learning how to shoot fireballs instead. Every rank gives you a +1 bonus to Accuracy, defensive rolls, and skill checks. Cost: 10 Scale: 5 Limit: Lower of Awareness /5, Espionage /5, and Stealth /5; max 10

title: Basic Survival Tactics
text: You know how to fend for yourself, in the wilderness and on missions. It encompasses a lot of things, but one of the basics for a hunter is being able to not be discovered when their opponents; discretion is absolutely the better part of valor, after all. Each rank gives a +1 bonus to Stealth and Survival rolls. Cost: 6 Scale: 2 Limit: AGI /10, max 5 Requires: Survival 5

title: Advanced Survival Tactics
text: Not getting caught by one's opponents is always preferable when outmatched, but sometimes that's not an option. You now know how to fend for yourself in combat, as well! Each rank gives a +1 bonus to dodge and Survival rolls. Cost: 5 Scale: 1 Limit: (DEX - 50) /10, max 10 Requires: Basic Survival Tactics 5

title: Defensive Formation
text: You take up a position protecting someone from harm. Very useful on escort missions when you have to keep some blubbering civilian safe! This is a variable Speed Action, you designate one or more (up to 1+XP/1000) targets within AGI/20 yards of you. If one of those people is attacked before you take a non-interrupt action, you may immediately attempt to Take The Hit as a Speed 0 Interrupt, with a +10 bonus. The designated targets must be within AGI/20 of you for this ability to take effect. They can move out and back in at will. Designating new targets requires another use of this Action. Cost: 25

title: Total Defense
text: You abandon all forms of attack and focus on staying alive. This is a variable Speed Defensive Basic Action. Until your next non-interrupt action, your Dodge action becomes a Speed 0 Interrupt and has a +3 bonus. Cost: 20 Requires: 45 AGI

title: Guard
text: You ready yourself for an impending attack. This is a variable Speed Defensive Basic Action. Until your next non-interrupt action, you have a +3 bonus to accuracy when parrying enemy attacks (including with jutsu, such as Halting Blow and Crossroads of Heaven). Your Parry action itself becomes a Speed 0 Interrupt. Cost: 20 Requires: 45 DEX

title: Safety Dance
text: This does not actually have anything to do with dancing. Indeed, if you are dancing, you probably won't be able to pull this off! You stay on edge while recuperating mid-battle, never letting your guard down. When you take a Rest action, you may increase its speed by one to be considered to be Blocking until your next nonInterrupt action. Cost: 40 Requires: 60 STR

title: Cunning
text: You're an expert at misdirection; you know the signs people look for and pick up on in battle, and you know how to either give the wrong ones, or none at all. This gives you a +1 bonus to Accuracy per rank. Cost: 6 Scale: 2 Limit: Espionage /5

title: Cunning Blow
text: After you successfully defend against an attack that targeted you, your next Attack against that opponent gains +4 Accuracy if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. Cost: 50 Requires: 20 Espionage

title: Stalker
text: Somewhere along the way you picked up the unpleasant, but highly effective talent of being able to follow people for prolonged periods of time without being noticed. You gain +1 to your Accuracy with Sneak Attacks and half as much (rounded down) to surprise attacks. Also each rank increases your Stealth TN by 1. Because this applies after you have already hidden, it is not counted against anything which allows an opponent to make an automatic search check. Cost: 8 Scale: 2 Limit: DEX /25, max 5

title: Subterfuge
text: You are all kinds of sneaky. You know how to lie and make it seem like you're telling the truth, or how to tell the truth while convincing anyone listening that it's a lie. Every rank gives you +1 to Espionage and Stealth rolls. Cost: 3 Scale: 2 Limit: Espionage /3, max 10

title: Initiative
text: Roll Initiative when combat begins, then use each Action’s Speed to determine when you act again.

title: Defensive Reflexes
text: You're always ready to protect yourself, even when caught off guard. You may declare use of this ability when rolling your initiative for combat. You are considered to be blocking at the start of battle, but take a -4 penalty on your initiative roll. This penalty is reduced by 1 for each rank beyond the first. Cost: 10 Limit: RES/20, max 3

title: Reflexes
text: You have excellent twitch reflexes. Mostly, this comes in handy for a hunter; you respond to danger before even fully determining what that danger is. This can be kind of awkward off-duty, when you respond to somebody trying to startle you by punching them in the gut and then flipping them over your shoulder, but that's what they get for trying to startle a hunter anyway. Each rank gives you +1 Initiative and each even rank gives a +1 Athletics bonus. Cost: 7 Limit: AGI /10, Max 20

title: Rush
text: You don't waste time doing things like getting warmed up and taking stock of the battlefield, instead opting to rush right into battle and make things up as you go along! You start battle with AGI /20 AP for each rank in this ability. Cost: 4 Scale: 2 Limit: AGI /20, max 5

title: Preparation
text: You may, as part of your Initiative roll, activate one or more techniques with Upkeeps that affect only yourself. You must pay their Chakra or Stamina costs normally. The total of the (Speed + modified Seal Speed) of all the techniques you use cannot exceed whatever you rolled for your initiative. Cost: 40 Requires: 60 DEX

title: Active
text: You get a lot done in combat. Whether it's quickly assessing the battlefield, exploiting an opening, or having that extra bit of adrenaline, you're already doing what needs to be done. Every rank in this ability increases the AP you naturally gain each 20 IC by 1. Thus, if you had 3 ranks of Active, you'd get (5 + 3) 8 AP every time the IC reached a multiple of 20. Cost: 1 Scale: 2 Limit: AGI /20

title: Principle of Motion
text: You're able to act blindingly fast, beyond what all reason suggests should be possible. You may at any time cause your next action to come 1 IC earlier for every 2 AP you spend. For example, say it's initiative count 200, and you just took a speed 12 action. Your action ends that IC, moving the battle onto IC 201; normally your next action would occur on IC (200 + 12) = 212. By spending 22 AP, you could act on (IC 212 - 11) 201, in other words, immediately. This only allows your next action to come sooner; it does not let you finish an ongoing action sooner. As such, Principle of Motion can't be used to make you finish Handseals early, or while you are in the process of using any action with a Delay. Similarly, you can not use Principle of Motion to reverse time. You may use Principle of Motion only to bring your next action to what the current initiative count is. This means that if you take an action on IC 16, once it is resolved IC 17 begins--and that is the earliest you could activate Principle of Motion, meaning you would be unable to act twice on the same initiative count. You may not use Principle of Motion while stunned. Cost: 60 Requires: 100 DEX, 100 AGI

title: Surge
text: You can spend AP to improve an attack's accuracy, or a defensive action's roll. This costs 8 AP per +1 Accuracy, and 5 AP per +1 to a defensive roll. Either way, Surge may give a maximum of a +5 bonus, and is declared when the roll (or attack) is made. Cost: 40 Requires: 80 AGI

title: Determination
text: Your force of will is as powerful an advantage in combat as your strength of body. Each rank of this ability increases your Willpower by 1. Cost: 25 Limit: XP /1000

title: Desperation
text: Being faced with truly dire straits brings out remarkable characteristics: in animals, in civilians, and in hunters. Thankfully, you're one of those! You can activate this ability when defending against an attack by spending a point of Willpower. Your Interrupt only needs to be double or less the Speed of the attack you're defending against, rather than half or less. This effect persists for the duration of 10 ICs; if you're being attacked four times in that duration, then all four defenses would receive this benefit. Cost: 30 Requires: Determination 1

title: Focus
text: Being left reeling and disoriented is an all-too-common experience for hunters. Sometimes it's the result of genjutsu, other times it's a lucky blow to the solar plexus (or... lower). You're able to bring yourself back to the presence, by sheer mental fortitude, though doing so is bound to wear you out faster in the long run. By spending 1 Willpower, you end any Stuns you're suffering from and become immune to any other instances of that status effect until the end of the current Initiative Count. Cost: 40 Requires: Determination 2

title: Guts
text: You refuse to go down in battle. So long as you're physically able to breathe, you will not stop fighting when your values are on the line. This can get downright frightening to behold, depending upon the circumstances. Whenever you would be reduced to 0 HP or lower, roll a TN 25 Stamina check. If you succeed, you are left with 1 HP, and cannot have your HP reduced until the end of that initiative count. If you fail, in addition to your Fatigue progressing you take the damage you normally would have from the attack. Damage negated through this ability still wounds you normally. Cost: 50 Requires: Determination 3

title: Limit Break
text: Through sheer determination you force yourself to perform above your own capabilities. Once per day, per rank, you may Willpower a roll but instead of expending a Willpower you immediately proceed to the next Fatigue category. You may only use Limit Break once per action but you may use a Willpower normally in the same action. Cost: 20 Limit: Determination

title: Tag Concealment
text: Hunters do love their explosions. However, they also like being sneaky and unseen; this combines the two! When placing an exploding tag, you can hide it from the casual observer. This requires something for it to be hidden under (such as loose soil, or leaves; you cannot 'hide' them in plain sight in a featureless room). Hiding a tag is a Speed 10 action, and anyone watching you will realize what you're doing and where it is (meaning it cannot be accomplished outside of stealth in combat). When you hide the tag, make an Espionage roll. Anyone who enters the tag's range is allowed an Awareness roll against the result, without any bonuses they may have from the Enhanced Hearing ability. Success means they've spotted the tag. Once a tag has begun its countdown to detonation they start to sizzle and spark, alerting anyone to their presence and approximate direction (though not exact location), giving them a chance to escape before time runs out. Cost: 10

title: Explosive Tag Connection
text: As a Speed 10 + 5 X action, you can attach X tags to a kunai's hilt or an arrow, and prime them. These can be attached pre-battle as a matter of convenience, but the action to prime them is still necessary. You can have up to (Chakra Control) /5 tags primed this way at once. Each item (kunai or arrow) may only have a single tag attached to it. You can trigger these tags as part of a multi throw, or do so later (such as by the Remote Detonation technique). When the kunai is thrown (or arrow shot) the tag(s) will detonate 15 IC after impact (with the target, or the ground at the target's feet on a miss). When used as a multi-throw, each tagged kunai counts as two weapons for the purpose of determining multi-throwing limits. You can include up to one tag per rank in this ability in a single throw. If a target is struck by the arrow or kunai, they're assumed to pull it out as a non-action and can try to escape the area. Justu including exploding tags that cause them to explode on contact supersede these rules. Cost: 5 Scale: 3 Limit: Chakra Control /5

title: Icha Icha Novels
text: Icha Icha is a series of best-selling novels written by the legendary ninja sage Jiraiya. They are comedic (and adult) recounts of Jiraiya's experiences in love. The titles include Icha Icha Paradise, Icha Icha Violence, Icha Icha Tactics, and Icha Icha Utopia.
