When a Slashing Wound inflicted by this weapon applies Bleed, increase that Bleed by 1, maximum once per Attack. Hooked Head — 3 AP. Gain +2 Accuracy on Disarm Attacks made with the weapon. Fine Point — 4 AP. Requires Piercing. Reduce the Accuracy penalty of Called Shots made with the weapon by 1. Crushing Crown — 4 AP. Requires Blunt. Deal +25% Final Damage to physical Barriers, unattended objects, and destructible terrain. Broad Edge — 4 AP. This weapon gains a +5% Wounding bonus when dealing Slashing Damage.

title: Grip, Haft & Balance
text: Counterweight — 2 AP/Rank. Reduce Base Delay by 1 per Rank. This cannot reduce Base Delay below half its original value, rounded down. Weighted Heft — 3 AP/Rank. Whenever you declare a damaging Attack with this weapon, increase that Attack's Delay by 1 per Rank and its Final Damage by 5% per Rank. Apply the additional Delay after reductions to the weapon's Base Delay. Maximum 3 Ranks. Lightweight — 3 AP/Rank. Reduce Base Stamina by 1 per Rank. Maximum reduction is one quarter of the weapon's original Stamina, rounded down. Hand Guard — 3 AP/Rank. Gain +1 Parry per Rank. Maximum 2 Ranks. Perfect Balance — 4 AP/Rank. Reduce Base Speed by 1 per Rank. Maximum 2 Ranks. Wide Guard — 4 AP. Reduce the Base Speed of Parry with this weapon by 1. Quick Recovery — 5 AP/Rank. Gain +1 Accuracy per Rank. Maximum 2 Ranks. Oil Quenched — 7 AP. Increase the weapon's Damage Die size by 2. Extreme weapons instead gain +2 Damage per Damage Die. Maximum 1 Rank. Secure Grip — 2 AP/Rank. Disarm Attacks targeting this weapon suffer -1 Accuracy per Rank. Maximum 2 Ranks. Extended Haft — 4 AP/Rank. Gain +1 Reach per Rank. Maximum 2 Ranks; Small weapons may purchase only 1. Shortened Grip — 2 AP. Reduce Reach by 1, minimum 0, and gain +1 Parry. Cannot be combined with Extended Haft. Sliding Grip — 4 AP. Requires Reach 1+. At the start of each Attack choose Long Grip (+1 Reach, -1 Parry until it resolves) or Short Grip (-1 Reach, +1 Accuracy for that Attack). Reach cannot fall below 0. Forward Balance — 3 AP. When declaring a Basic Weapon Attack, you may increase its Final Speed by 1 to gain +1 Damage Die. Rear Balance — 3 AP. When declaring a Basic Weapon Attack, you may reduce its Damage by 1 Damage Die to reduce its Final Speed by 1, following normal minimum Speed rules.

title: Structural Components
text: Layered Construction — 5 AP. Gain Weapon Block [Speed 6, Interrupt, Defense]. It reduces the triggering Attack's Damage by 25% and counts as a Block. Reinforced Layering — 2 AP/Rank. Whenever you Block while wielding this weapon, increase that Block's Damage Reduction by 5 percentage points per Rank. Maximum 3 Ranks. Reinforced Spine — 2 AP/Rank. Reduce WDP gained from resistant armor contact by 1 per Rank, minimum 0. Maximum 3 Ranks. Flexible Construction — 3 AP. Reduce WDP explicitly inflicted on this weapon by enemy techniques by 2, minimum 0. Shock Mounting — 3 AP. When you Block with this weapon, reduce Knockback suffered by 3 yards, minimum 0. Reinforced Collar — 3 AP. Medium or larger. Effects which directly break, sever, or destroy the weapon without using Durability must overcome an additional 20 Durability first. This does not increase ordinary Durability. Replaceable Sections — 2 AP. Treat your Artisan result as +5 when using a normal Repair Downtime Action on this weapon.

title: Deployment & Reach Systems
text: Quickdraw Fittings — 3 AP. Small or Medium only. Drawing and Sheathing this weapon are Speed 3. Combat Sheath — 4 AP. Requires Quickdraw Fittings. Sheathing this weapon is Speed 1. Snap Deployment — 3 AP. When an effect already lets you draw this weapon at Speed 0, its first Basic Weapon Attack before the end of your next Action gains +1 Accuracy. Segmented Construction — 4 AP. When declaring a Basic Weapon Attack, you may extend the weapon for +2 Reach and -2 Accuracy. It returns to normal after the Attack resolves. Telescoping Shaft — 3 AP. Medium or larger. As a Speed 2 Utility action, switch between Compact (-1 Reach, +1 Parry) and Extended (+1 Reach). Minimum Reach 0. Reclaiming Line — 2 AP. Requires Thrown or Chain. Retrieve the unattended weapon from within 10 yards as a Speed 3 Utility action if the path is unobstructed. Reinforced Line — 2 AP/Rank. Requires Reclaiming Line. Increase retrieval distance by 10 yards per Rank. Maximum 3 Ranks.

title: Guard Components
text: Guard Mount — 3 AP. Gain the Guard tag. If the weapon possesses Layered Construction, reduce Weapon Block's Base Speed by 1. Bracing Spike — 3 AP. Large or Extreme Two-Handed only. If you have not voluntarily moved since the end of your previous Action, reduce hostile Knockback against you by 2 yards. Defensive Lug — 3 AP. After successfully Parrying with this weapon, gain +1 Parry against the next Attack made against you before your next Action. Catching Guard — 4 AP. Requires Hand Guard. After fully Parrying a Weapon Attack, gain +2 Accuracy on your next Disarm Attack against that weapon before the end of your next Action.

title: Chain Components
text: Weighted Chain — 3 AP/Rank. Chain only. Gain +1 Grapple Offense per Rank while maintaining a Weapon Grapple with this weapon. Maximum 2 Ranks. Locking Links — 3 AP. Chain only. After starting Control is determined for a Weapon Grapple made with this weapon, gain +1 Control. Reel Assembly — 4 AP. Chain only. After succeeding on a Grapple Roll through this weapon, you may move the Grappled target 1 yard toward you. You may do this once per Action. Reinforced Cable — 2 AP/Rank. Chain only. Increase Durability by 10% per Rank. Effects specifically trying to sever the Chain while it maintains a Weapon Grapple deal 10% less Final Damage per Rank, maximum 30%. Ground Anchor — 4 AP. Chain only. As a Speed 5 Utility action, attach the Chain to solid terrain within Reach. Until detached, Weapon Grapple Range may originate from you or the anchor. Detaching is Speed 1.

title: Thrown Components
text: Throwing Balance — 3 AP. Small or Medium One-Handed only. Gain Thrown and Projectile. Range is 5 + STR/4. Use the weapon's normal Speed, Stamina, Damage, and Delay. Aerodynamic Profile — 3 AP/Rank. Requires Throwing Balance. Increase maximum Range by 5 yards per Rank. Maximum 3 Ranks. Returning Balance — 5 AP. Requires Throwing Balance. Ten IC after a thrown Attack resolves, the weapon returns along the same unobstructed path. Catching it is Speed 0. Ricochet Geometry — 4 AP. Requires Throwing Balance. Ignore up to 2 points of Visibility penalty on thrown Attacks.

title: Multi-Function & Impact Mechanisms
text: Secondary Grip — 3 AP. Two-Handed only. You may release one hand to perform an Action requiring one free hand. You cannot Attack, Parry, or Weapon Block with the weapon until the hand returns at Speed 0. Reversible Grip — 4 AP. Sword, Club, or Polearm. As a Speed 0 action choose Offensive (+1 Accuracy, -1 Parry) or Defensive (+1 Parry, -1 Accuracy). The state remains until changed. Rotating Head — 4 AP. Requires at least two Damage Types. If you declare a different Damage Type from your previous damaging Attack with the weapon, gain +1 Accuracy. Modular Head — 3 AP. Choose one purchased Edge, Head, or Striking Surface Component worth 4 AP or less. During a Week's Rest, replace it with another legal Component of equal or lower AP cost without rebuilding the weapon. Impact Chamber — 5 AP. Club only. When declaring an Attack with Knockback, you may add +3 Stamina. If Knockback applies, increase the resulting Knockback by 2 yards after the Status Roll and before Partial Success. Recoil Assembly — 4 AP. When an Attack with this weapon successfully causes at least 3 yards of Knockback, move 1 yard directly away from the target after the Attack resolves. This costs no Speed or AP and cannot trigger another Recoil Assembly. Momentum Core — 4 AP. Large or Extreme only. If your previous non-Interrupt Action was a damaging Attack with this weapon that fully hit, your next damaging Attack with it gains +1 Damage Die and +1 Stamina. Does not stack with itself. Momentum Brake — 4 AP. Large or Extreme only. When declaring a damaging Attack, reduce its Final Speed by 1 and its Damage by 1 Damage Die. Normal minimum Speed rules apply. Overdrive Piston — 5 AP. Medium or larger. When declaring a Basic Weapon Attack, add +4 Stamina to gain +2 Damage Dice. Shock Vent — 4 AP. Requires Impact Chamber or Overdrive Piston. Reduce that Component's added Stamina by 1. Duelist's Balance — 4 AP. Sword only. After fully Parrying an Attack, your next Basic Weapon Attack against that attacker gains +1 Accuracy. The benefit is lost after your next non-Interrupt Action. Driving Point — 4 AP. Polearm only. If the target begins your Attack outside its own natural Melee Reach but within yours, gain +1 Accuracy.

title: Chakra Engineering
text: Chakra Conduit — 3 AP. The weapon may act as a valid weapon focus or conduit for techniques that permit one. Gain +1 on Chakra Control rolls specifically made to maintain or control a technique channelled directly through it. Capacitor Seal — 4 AP/Rank. Requires Chakra Conduit. Maximum 3 Ranks. When using a Chakra-costing technique through the weapon, you may increase its Chakra Cost by 3 to store 1 Charge after it resolves, up to your Ranks. A later Chakra-costing technique through the weapon may consume Charges; each reduces its Chakra Cost by 2, minimum 1. Charges disappear at scene end. Sealing Socket — 3 AP/Rank. Gain one Socket per Rank, maximum 3. A Socket may hold a compatible seal, cartridge, talisman, or similar object granted by another rule. Sockets have no effect by themselves. Elemental Channel — 4 AP. Requires Chakra Conduit. The weapon may receive elemental crafting effects granted by Clan, Talent, Jutsu, or another rule. This does not grant an element by itself. Resonance Chamber — 4 AP. Requires Chakra Conduit. When a technique explicitly uses this weapon as a conduit and has both a Chakra Cost and Stamina Cost, gain +1 on one of the two Exhaustion rolls, chosen when declaring it. Chakra Insulation — 3 AP. Requires Chakra Conduit. Reduce additional WDP caused specifically by channeling Chakra through the weapon by 3, minimum 0.

title: 3. Special Properties
text: 3. Special Properties Special Properties are unusual constructions beyond ordinary Components. Unless another rule grants access, crafting a Special Property requires Master Artisan. Add together all Property Load on the weapon. Property Surcharge equals Base AP × total Property Load, rounded up. If the weapon has any Property Load, the surcharge is at least 1 AP. Final Artisan Points equal Base AP + Property Surcharge.

title: General Properties
text: Textured Grip — +0.50 Property Load. The weapon requires one fewer hand to wield. A Two-Handed weapon used with one hand loses the Two-Handed PDB increase. A no-hand weapon only functions this way for effects that explicitly support it, and only one may be actively wielded this way. Dual Balancing — +0.30 Property Load. Small or Medium One-Handed only. The weapon is made as a matched pair and gains Dual. The pair counts as one crafted weapon for purchase and crafting. Compound Weapon — +0.30 Property Load. Choose a second legal Shape. The weapon possesses both Shape tags. When declaring an Attack or Parry, choose which Shape is active; only that Shape's Accuracy, Parry, Reach modifier, and Shape rule apply. Transforming Frame — +0.40 Property Load. Create two legal configurations of the same Size and Components. The configurations may use different Shapes, Hefts, and Damage Types. Change configuration as a Speed 2 Utility action. Only the active configuration applies. Heritage fittings granted directly by a Corps or Heritage do not need to be repurchased as Components or Special Properties.

title: Wondrous Materials
text: A weapon may normally contain one Wondrous Material. Wondrous Materials are Special Properties and require mastery of that material through Master Artisan. Skysteel — +0.15 Property Load. Halve the weapon's Base Delay, rounded down. Ironheart — +0.20 Property Load. Whenever WDP would increase, reduce that increase by 5, to a minimum of half the original increase. Angelskin — +0.20 Property Load. Whenever you gain Bleed, reduce this weapon's WDP by three times that Bleed's severity. This can reduce WDP below 0 but cannot reverse Damage Levels. Crypstone — +0.25 Property Load. Deal +50% Damage to Armor and Weapon Durability. Mindglass — +0.30 Property Load. Gain +5% Wounding for every Upkeep currently affecting the target. Voidglass — +0.40 Property Load. The weapon may Parry Projectile Ninjutsu at -2 Parry. Feathersteel — +0.20 Property Load. Reduce Base Stamina by 2, minimum 1, and reduce Durability by 20%. Deepstone — +0.20 Property Load. Medium or larger. While wielded Two-Handed, reduce hostile forced movement against you by 2 yards, minimum 0. Increase Base Stamina by 1. Echo Brass — +0.25 Property Load. After fully Parrying an Attack, your next damaging Attack with this weapon against that creature gains +1 Accuracy. The benefit is lost after your next non-Interrupt Action. Shiversteel — +0.25 Property Load. After you Draw this weapon, if your next non-Interrupt Action is a damaging Attack with it, that Attack gains +10% Wounding. If you take another non-Interrupt Action first, the benefit is lost. Drawing the weapon again grants the benefit again normally. Living Wood — +0.25 Property Load. Recover 5 WDP every 10 IC in which the weapon neither makes an Attack nor is used to Parry or Block. This cannot recover Damage Levels. Prismite — +0.15 Property Load. The weapon counts as possessing Chakra Conduit without paying its AP cost. Whenever a Jutsu explicitly uses this weapon as a conduit or weapon focus, gain +1 on its Chakra Exhaustion roll. Anchorite — +0.25 Property Load. Large or Extreme only. If you have not voluntarily moved since the end of your previous Action, gain +1 Parry and reduce hostile Knockback against you by 2 yards. Both end when you voluntarily move. Ghostsilver — +0.30 Property Load. Deal +50% Damage to physical Barriers and chakra-created objects. Bloodglass — +0.30 Property Load. Against a creature suffering Bleed, gain +5% Wounding. Against Bleed 5+, gain +10% Wounding instead. Stormsilver — +0.30 Property Load. Gain +1 Parry against Projectile Attacks. After successfully Parrying a Projectile Attack, your next Parry before your next Action gains +1. Black Jade — +0.30 Property Load. Whenever you Block while wielding this weapon, increase that Block's Damage Reduction by 10 percentage points. Whenever you Block this way, the weapon gains 5 additional WDP after all reductions. Phaseglass — +0.35 Property Load. Full hits with the weapon ignore 5 Damage Reduction. This does not bypass Blocking, Armor Absorption, or percentage-based mitigation.

title: 4. Elemental Upgrades, Created Weapons & Reforging
text: 4. Elemental Upgrades, Created Weapons & Reforging Weapon upgrades granted by Jutsu, Clan, Heritage, or another rule spend Artisan Points at their listed cost and use the limits written by that effect. A Jutsu that creates a weapon with X Artisan Points uses these Structure and Component rules. Special Properties and Wondrous Materials require the creating effect to explicitly allow them. Standard Weapons and existing crafted weapons may be used as the base for Reforging through the normal Crafting Downtime rules. Reforging may add legal Components and Properties while following the existing restrictions on what may be removed or changed. Bukijutsu uses the weapon's current statistics. If a weapon has innate Delay, attacking Bukijutsu gains Delay equal to half the weapon's current Base Delay, rounded down, unless the technique says otherwise.

title: Ranged Weapon Crafting
text: Ranged Weapon Crafting lets you build bows, crossbows, launchers and reusable thrown weapons with the same Artisan Point structure as ordinary Weapon Crafting. The weapon determines how the attack is delivered. Ammunition and loaded projectiles determine what is being fired. Mechanical launchers and crossbows are not Firearms. They do not use Ballistic Damage Bonus, Ballistic Loads, Burst, Full Auto, Modification Points, specialist Ballistic ammunition, or Firearm-specific Talents unless a rule explicitly allows it.

title: 1. Core Rules
text: 1. Core Rules A ranged weapon's Final Artisan Points cannot exceed your Artisan ranks when you craft it. Crafting TN is 15 + (4 × Final Artisan Points). Crafting Cost is the weapon's listed Frame price + (750 × Final Artisan Points). Standard unmodified weapons use their catalogue price instead. Ranged weapons still use the normal equipment restriction: you cannot wield a weapon with Final Artisan Points greater than Athletics +10 without the normal over-limit penalties. Ranged weapons purchase Components with Artisan Points. For every 6 AP spent on Components, increase the weapon's Base Damage by +1 Damage Die and its Base Stamina by +1. Structure costs, ammunition AP, Special Properties, and Wondrous Materials do not count toward this threshold. For Bows, this adds Damage Dice to the dice generated by STR. For Crossbows, it adds Damage Dice to the Crossbow's listed Damage. For Launchers, it adds Damage Dice to attacks made through that Launcher and applies only once to any attack that fires multiple projectiles.

title: Weapon and Ammunition AP
text: A ranged weapon and the ammunition fired through it are separate crafted items. Weapon AP determines the weapon's Crafting TN, wielding restriction, Component bonuses, Property Load, and Special Properties. Ammunition AP determines the complexity of an ammunition pattern. Ammunition AP does not increase the weapon's Final Artisan Points, does not count toward the every-6-Component-AP bonus, does not affect the wielder's Athletics requirement, and uses its own crafting rules. Reusable weapons such as Kunai and Shuriken are crafted as weapons rather than ammunition.

title: 2. Weapon Families
text: 2. Weapon Families

title: Bows
text: Bows are Strength-scaling weapons built around Aim, mobility, sightlines, and powerful individual shots. The existing Yumi and Daikyu retain their current statistics and Aim rules.

title: Crossbows
text: Crossbows are mechanically drawn weapons with fixed Damage Dice, strong prepared attacks, and mandatory Reloading. They use normal Physical Damage Bonus, but do not receive the Yumi's ×1.5 or the Daikyu's ×2 Physical Damage Bonus multiplier.

title: Kunai Launchers
text: Kunai Launchers are compact projectile weapons built around utility, Ninja Wire, and adaptable projectile delivery. The Launcher supplies the attack profile, while the loaded Kunai supplies its Damage Dice, Damage Type, and projectile-specific effects.

title: Shuriken Launchers
text: Shuriken Launchers trade the hand-thrown Shuriken's extreme Speed for greater Range, magazine capacity, Volley, and heavy Fūma deployment.

title: 3. Bow Frames
text: 3. Bow Frames

title: Yumi
text: Cost: 7,500 Ryō. [Medium, Two-Handed, Bow, Projectile]. Speed 14; Stamina 15; Damage (STR/10)dS; Accuracy -8; Range STR/2; Delay 2. The ammunition determines dS. The Yumi uses 1.5 times your normal Physical Damage Bonus. Aim [Speed 8, Utility]: Gain +3 Accuracy on your next Yumi Attack. You may Aim up to twice for the same Attack. You may Dodge while Aiming, but doing so increases that Dodge's Speed by 3.

title: Daikyu
text: Cost: 12,500 Ryō. [Large, Two-Handed, Bow, Projectile]. Speed 20; Stamina 20; Damage (STR/8)dS; Accuracy -10; Range STR; Delay 4. The ammunition determines dS. The Daikyu uses twice your normal Physical Damage Bonus. Aim [Speed 10, Utility]: Gain +4 Accuracy on your next Daikyu Attack. You may Aim up to twice for the same Attack. Taking any action which requires movement, including Dodging, removes all accumulated Daikyu Aim bonuses.

title: 4. Crossbow Frames
text: 4. Crossbow Frames Crossbows store mechanical tension rather than relying on the wielder's Strength to determine their Damage Dice. The loaded Bolt determines the Damage Die size and Damage Type. Standard Bolts use d10.

title: Hand Crossbow
text: Cost: 6,000 Ryō. [Small, One-Handed, Crossbow, Projectile]. Speed 11; Stamina 10; Damage 4dS; Accuracy -4; Range 20 + STR/5; Delay 2; Capacity 1; Reload 5; Durability 35.

title: Hunting Crossbow
text: Cost: 10,000 Ryō. [Medium, Two-Handed, Crossbow, Projectile]. Speed 13; Stamina 13; Damage 7dS; Accuracy -5; Range 30 + STR/4; Delay 2; Capacity 1; Reload 6; Durability 45.

title: Heavy Arbalest
text: Cost: 15,000 Ryō. [Large, Two-Handed, Crossbow, Projectile]. Speed 16; Stamina 17; Damage 9dS; Accuracy -6; Range 40 + STR/4; Delay 4; Capacity 1; Reload 9; Durability 60. The Heavy Arbalest must be operated with both hands and cannot be Reloaded while moving.

title: Crossbow Aim
text: Crossbow Aim [Speed 5, Utility]: Your next Crossbow Attack gains +2 Accuracy if you do not voluntarily move before declaring it. You may only benefit from one Crossbow Aim at a time. The bonus is lost after making a Crossbow Attack.

title: 5. Reload
text: 5. Reload Crossbows and Launchers have Capacity and Reload values. Reloading is a Utility action using the weapon's listed Reload Speed. Reload may refill any number of empty spaces in the weapon up to its Capacity, but partially Reloading still uses the full Reload Speed. You must possess the ammunition or projectiles being loaded. A loaded weapon may be carried, Drawn, Sheathed, or otherwise transported normally unless another rule says otherwise. Loaded ammunition remains inside the weapon until fired, unloaded, or lost. A weapon cannot contain more projectiles than its Capacity. Reload Speed is not Attack Speed and does not increase the weapon's Damage.

title: 6. Launcher Frames
text: 6. Launcher Frames A Launcher supplies an attack's Speed, Stamina, Accuracy, Range, and Delay. The loaded projectile supplies Damage Dice, Damage Type, and projectile-specific effects. A launched Kunai or Shuriken does not also use its printed thrown Speed, Stamina, Range, or Delay. Launcher Range is provided by the mechanism and does not scale with STR unless a specific frame or effect says otherwise. When making a single-projectile Called Shot through a Launcher, reduce the Called Shot's Accuracy penalty by 1. This does not apply to Volley.

title: Wrist Launcher
text: Cost: 5,000 Ryō. [Small, One-Handed, Launcher, Kunai, Projectile]. Speed 8; Stamina 8; Accuracy +0; Range 15; Delay 1; Capacity 3; Volley Limit 3; Reload 5; Durability 30. The Wrist Launcher may make single-projectile Basic Weapon Attacks. It does not possess Volley unless it purchases the Volley Mechanism Component.

title: Repeating Kunai Launcher
text: Cost: 9,000 Ryō. [Medium, Two-Handed, Launcher, Kunai, Projectile]. Speed 10; Stamina 10; Accuracy +1; Range 25; Delay 1; Capacity 6; Volley Limit 5; Reload 6; Durability 40. The Repeating Kunai Launcher possesses Volley.

title: Rotary Shuriken Launcher
text: Cost: 9,000 Ryō. [Medium, Two-Handed, Launcher, Shuriken, Projectile]. Speed 8; Stamina 9; Accuracy -1; Range 25; Delay 1; Capacity 8; Volley Limit 6; Reload 6; Durability 40. The Rotary Shuriken Launcher possesses Volley. A Shuriken's printed +2 Accuracy still applies when fired through a Launcher, so a Rotary Shuriken Launcher firing ordinary Shuriken has +1 total Accuracy.

title: Heavy Shuriken Launcher
text: Cost: 13,000 Ryō. [Large, Two-Handed, Launcher, Shuriken, Projectile]. Speed 12; Stamina 15; Accuracy -2; Range 35; Delay 2; Capacity 8; Volley Limit 4; Reload 7; Durability 55. The Heavy Shuriken Launcher possesses Volley and may purchase the Fūma Cradle Component. A Shuriken's printed +2 Accuracy still applies when fired through it.

title: 7. Launcher Volley
text: 7. Launcher Volley Volley [Attack, Projectile, Multi-Throw]: A weapon with Volley may fire several loaded projectiles in a single Attack. Choose at least 2 loaded compatible projectiles of the same projectile type, up to the weapon's Volley Limit. You cannot fire more projectiles than your remaining Capacity. Volley Limit is determined by the Launcher frame and may be modified by Components. The Attack uses the Launcher's Base Speed. Increase Final Speed by +1 for every 2 projectiles fired beyond the first 2, rounded up. Increase Stamina by +1 for every 2 projectiles fired, rounded up. Make one Accuracy roll. Each projectile contributes its normal printed Base Damage Dice. Physical Damage Bonus is calculated using the normal Multi-Throw rule, increasing the user's Physical Damage Bonus by +0.25 for each projectile fired. Wounds inflicted by Volley have their severity reduced by one category, to a minimum of Minor, as with ordinary Multi-Throw. Every projectile fired is removed from the Launcher's Capacity.

title: Crafted Projectiles
text: Additional Damage Dice from projectile Components apply only once to the entire Volley. The same is true of the bonus Damage Die gained for every 6 Component AP spent on a crafted projectile. Attack-wide Accuracy and Wounding bonuses from identical projectile patterns also apply only once. Launcher Component bonuses, including the Launcher's every-6-Component-AP bonus, apply only once to the entire Volley. Effects which belong to an individual projectile apply only to that projectile where relevant.

title: Volley Restrictions
text: A Launcher may only use one Volley as part of an Attack. Volley cannot be combined with ordinary hand-thrown Multi-Throw, Ballistic Burst, Ballistic Full Auto, or another effect that already represents firing multiple projectiles unless that effect explicitly allows it.

title: Mixed Magazines
text: A Launcher may contain any mixture of compatible ordinary and crafted projectiles. Whenever you make a single-projectile Attack, declare which loaded projectile is being fired. Volley normally requires every projectile fired to use the same projectile pattern. Split Feed allows a Volley to contain up to two different loaded projectile patterns of the same projectile type.

title: 8. Ranged Components
text: 8. Ranged Components Ranged weapons may purchase any ordinary Weapon Component whose effect can function with that weapon. Components which require an unrelated Shape, Melee Reach, a Melee-only Attack, a Melee Parry, or another incompatible trait cannot be purchased for a ranged weapon. Reinforced Bowstring — 3 AP. Bow or Crossbow. Reduce WDP explicitly inflicted on this weapon by enemy effects by 2, minimum 0. Long-Limb Design — 3 AP/Rank. Bow or Crossbow. Increase listed Range by 10% per Rank. Maximum 3 Ranks. Sighting Bead — 3 AP/Rank. Bow or Crossbow. Gain +1 Accuracy per Rank on Attacks which consume an Aim bonus. Maximum 2 Ranks. Quick-Draw Mechanism — 4 AP. Bow only. Reduce Aim Speed by 2, minimum 3. Quiet String — 3 AP. Bow only. Gain +2 on Stealth rolls made to remain hidden after firing the weapon. Pivoting Grip — 4 AP. Yumi only. You may voluntarily move up to 2 yards without losing accumulated Yumi Aim bonuses. Reinforced Riser — 4 AP. Bow only. The Bow may Parry Melee Weapon Attacks at -2 Parry. This does not allow it to Parry Projectile Attacks. Stabilised Sight — 3 AP. Bow or Crossbow. When making an Aimed Attack, ignore up to 2 points of Visibility penalty. Steady Draw — 4 AP. Bow only. If you have not voluntarily moved since the end of your previous Action, your next Aimed Bow Attack gains +5% Wounding. Quick Windlass — 4 AP. Crossbow only. Reduce Reload Speed by 2, minimum 3. Reinforced Winch — 5 AP. Crossbow only. Gain +2 Base Damage Dice, +2 Reload Speed, and +1 Base Delay. Maximum 1. Double Channel — 5 AP. Hunting Crossbow only. Capacity becomes 2. Increase Reload Speed by 2. Expanded Magazine — 2 AP/Rank. Launcher only. Increase Capacity by 2 per Rank. Maximum 3 Ranks. Capacity does not increase Volley Limit unless another effect explicitly says it does. Volley Mechanism — 4 AP. Launcher only. Gain Volley. Rapid Index — 4 AP. Requires Volley. Ignore the first +1 Final Speed increase imposed by Volley. This cannot reduce the Attack below the Launcher's normal Base Speed. Split Feed — 3 AP. Launcher only. A Volley may contain up to two different loaded projectile patterns of the same projectile type. Extended Guide — 3 AP/Rank. Launcher only. Increase Range by 5 yards per Rank. Maximum 2 Ranks. Retrieval Spool — 3 AP. Kunai Launcher only. May fire Kunai attached to up to 10 yards of Ninja Wire. A launched Kunai may be retrieved as a Speed 3 Utility action if its path is unobstructed. Reinforced Housing — 3 AP. Launcher or Crossbow. Increase Durability by 20%. Fūma Cradle — 7 AP. Heavy Shuriken Launcher only. Gain a dedicated Fūma chamber and the Fūma Launch action. Ranged Components count normally toward the every-6-Component-AP Damage Die and Stamina bonus.

title: Existing Components
text: Existing ordinary Components such as Sturdy, Reinforced Edge, Honed Geometry, Lightweight, Perfect Balance, Counterweight, Weighted Heft, and Chakra Conduit remain available when they have a valid interaction with the weapon. A Launcher does not gain access to Melee Components merely because the ammunition loaded into it can also function as a Melee weapon.

title: 9. Fūma Cradle
text: 9. Fūma Cradle Fūma Cradle — 7 AP. Heavy Shuriken Launcher only. The weapon gains a separate chamber capable of holding one Fūma Shuriken. This chamber does not consume ordinary Shuriken Capacity. Loading or Reloading the Cradle uses its own Reload action.

title: Fūma Launch
text: Fūma Launch [Speed 16, Stamina 18, Delay 5, Attack, Projectile]: Fire the Fūma Shuriken loaded in the Cradle. Fūma Launch uses the loaded Fūma Shuriken's normal (4 + STR/12)d12 Damage Dice, +10% total Damage for each point the Attack hits by to its normal maximum, +25% Damage for Wounding calculations, and Slashing Damage Type. Use whichever Range is higher: the Heavy Shuriken Launcher's current Range or the Fūma Shuriken's normal STR/3 Range. Firing removes the Fūma Shuriken from the Cradle but does not affect the Launcher's ordinary Shuriken magazine. Fūma Launch cannot Volley or Multi-Throw. Reloading the Fūma Cradle is a separate Speed 8 Utility action. The Fūma Cradle contains only one Fūma Shuriken and cannot satisfy a technique requiring multiple Fūma Shuriken unless another effect provides them.

title: 10. Custom Kunai and Shuriken
text: 10. Custom Kunai and Shuriken Kunai and Shuriken are reusable weapons rather than consumable ammunition. Throwing or launching one does not ordinarily destroy it. A crafted Kunai or Shuriken is an individually crafted weapon which can be thrown normally or loaded into a compatible Launcher.

title: Kunai
text: Cost: 150 Ryō. [Piercing, Thrown, Melee, Projectile]. Speed 8; Stamina 8; Damage 2d6; Accuracy +0; Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 1.

title: Shuriken
text: Cost: 150 Ryō. [Slashing, Thrown, Projectile]. Speed 5; Stamina 5; Damage 1d6; Accuracy +2; Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 0. A custom Kunai or Shuriken costs its stock price + (1,500 × Final AP). Its Crafting TN is 15 + (4 × Final AP). A crafted projectile's Final AP cannot exceed the creator's Artisan ranks and follows the normal Athletics +10 wielding restriction.

title: Matched Projectile Batches
text: You may craft a matched batch of up to five identical Kunai or Shuriken during the same Crafting Downtime action. Make one Crafting attempt using the pattern's normal TN and pay the full crafting cost for every weapon created. Every weapon in the batch is mechanically identical. Loss, destruction, or transfer of one weapon does not affect the others.

title: Projectile Components
text: Reinforced Edge — 2 AP/Rank. Gain +1 Base Damage Die per Rank. Honed Geometry — 2 AP/Rank. Gain +5% Wounding per Rank. Maximum 3 Ranks. Aerodynamic Profile — 3 AP/Rank. Increase Range by 5 yards per Rank. Maximum 3 Ranks. Calibrated Balance — 3 AP/Rank. Gain +1 Accuracy per Rank on single-projectile Attacks. Maximum 2 Ranks. Barbed Point — 3 AP. Kunai only. If a Piercing Wound inflicted by this weapon applies Bleed, increase that Bleed by 1, maximum once per Attack. Razor Edges — 3 AP. Shuriken only. Gain +5% Wounding when dealing Slashing Damage. Armor-Piercing Tip — 4 AP. Kunai only. Reduce Base Damage by 1 Damage Die. On a full hit, treat Armor Absorption as 10 percentage points lower, minimum 0%. Reinforced Ring — 2 AP. Kunai only. Gain +2 Accuracy when using this weapon to attach or deliver Ninja Wire through a compatible Jutsu or rule. Splitting Star — 4 AP. Shuriken only. On a single-projectile full hit, gain +1 Damage Die. Does not function during Multi-Throw or Volley. Returning Wire — 3 AP. Small Thrown weapon only. When attached to Ninja Wire, retrieve the unattended weapon from within 10 yards as a Speed 3 Utility action if its path is unobstructed. Other ordinary Components may be selected where applicable.

title: Crafted Projectiles and Multi-Throw
text: Multi-Throw continues to use its normal rules for number of weapons, Speed, Stamina, Damage Bonus, Accuracy, and Wound severity. Crafting does not multiply bonuses simply because several crafted weapons are thrown at once. When multiple crafted weapons are included in a Multi-Throw, base projectile Damage Dice are added normally. A Shuriken still contributes 1d6, a Kunai still contributes 2d6, and so on. Additional Damage Dice from Components apply only once to the entire Attack. The every-6-Component-AP bonus applies only once. Crafted Accuracy bonuses apply only once. Attack-wide Wounding bonuses apply only once. Identical Attack-wide special effects apply only once. If several different crafted patterns contribute to the same Attack, use only the highest applicable Attack-wide bonus of each type. Effects which trigger from an individual projectile still require that projectile to meet their normal condition. A normal single-projectile Attack receives all of that weapon's crafting benefits normally.

title: 11. Bow and Crossbow Ammunition
text: 11. Bow and Crossbow Ammunition Bows and Crossbows use consumable ammunition patterns. Arrows and Bolts are purchased and crafted in batches of ten. Unless another effect says otherwise, firing an Arrow or Bolt consumes one piece of ammunition. Ammunition recovered after an encounter may be reused where appropriate. An ammunition pattern may have a maximum of 2 Ammo AP. Ammunition may be crafted using Artisan (Weapon) or Artisan (Craftsman). Crafting TN is 15 + (4 × Ammo AP). Batch Cost is 2,500 Ryō + (1,000 × Ammo AP). Each crafting attempt produces a batch of ten identical pieces of ammunition. You must possess Artisan ranks equal to or greater than the pattern's Ammo AP.

title: Ammunition Patterns
text: Standard Arrow — 0 AP. Arrow. d12 Piercing. No additional effect. Piercing Arrow — 0 AP. Arrow. d8 Piercing. Ignore Armor, as the existing Piercing Arrow. Standard Bolt — 0 AP. Bolt. d10 Piercing. No additional effect. Bodkin Bolt — 1 AP. Bolt. d8 Piercing. On a full hit, treat Armor Absorption as 10 percentage points lower, minimum 0%. Razorhead — 1 AP. Arrow or Bolt. d10 Slashing. Gain +5% Wounding when dealing Slashing Damage. Blunt Head — 1 AP. Arrow or Bolt. d10 Blunt. On a full hit, may attempt Knockback 2 using the normal Status rules. Longshot — 1 AP. Arrow or Bolt. Reduce the ammunition's Damage Die size by one step. Increase the Attack's listed Range by 20% and increase its Delay by 1. Tracking Head — 1 AP. Arrow or Bolt. d8 Piercing. On a full hit, mark the target with alchemical dye and scent. Gain +2 Survival to track that target for the rest of the scene. Barbed Head — 2 AP. Arrow or Bolt. d10 Piercing. If the Attack inflicts a Wound which applies Bleed, increase that Bleed by 1, maximum once per Attack. Wireline — 2 AP. Arrow or Bolt. d8 Piercing. Leaves up to 10 yards of attached Ninja Wire at the point of impact. This does not automatically Grapple or Immobilize the target.

title: Ammunition Recipes
text: A normal specialized ammunition recipe contains one Head pattern, up to one compatible flight or utility modification, and no more than 2 total Ammo AP. Special ammunition changes the projectile fired, not the Bow or Crossbow itself. A Bow or Crossbow may freely choose which carried ammunition pattern it uses when declaring an Attack. Switching ammunition does not require an additional Action unless another rule prevents the character from accessing their ammunition.

title: Multiple-Arrow Techniques
text: A technique consumes the number of Arrows or Bolts it actually fires. If a Bukijutsu fires two Arrows, it consumes two. If it fires three, it consumes three. When several separately resolved projectiles are created by a Bukijutsu, each projectile uses its own ammunition Damage Type and applicable ammunition effects unless the technique explicitly replaces them. Ammunition crafting bonuses do not create additional copies of an effect where the technique combines several projectiles into one Attack.

title: Poisons and Other Enhancements
text: Poisons use the normal poison-coating rules. Explosive Tags, elemental ammunition, chakra enhancements, sealing effects, monster trophies, and similar upgrades require whatever Jutsu, Talent, Clan feature, mission reward, or other rule normally provides them. Ordinary ranged crafting does not grant access to Ballistic Corps specialist ammunition.

title: 12. Special Properties and Wondrous Materials
text: 12. Special Properties and Wondrous Materials Crafted ranged weapons may gain compatible Special Properties through the normal Weapon Crafting rules. A Special Property which depends on an impossible interaction does not gain a new function merely because it is placed on a ranged weapon. Property Load and Final Artisan Points are calculated normally. Crafted ranged weapons may use compatible Wondrous Materials after gaining the appropriate Master Artisan mastery. A weapon may normally contain one Wondrous Material. Existing Wondrous Materials retain their normal Property Load and effects. If a Wondrous Material specifically depends on Parrying, Melee Attacks, weapon Reach, a certain Shape, or another incompatible function, it does not gain a replacement effect.

title: 13. Bukijutsu Compatibility
text: 13. Bukijutsu Compatibility Crafted ranged weapons use their current statistics when used with Bukijutsu. If a ranged weapon has innate Delay, attacking Bukijutsu gains Delay equal to half the weapon's current Base Delay, rounded down, unless the technique says otherwise. Additional Attack Delay from effects such as Weighted Heft is applied afterward.

title: Crossbows and Bow Bukijutsu
text: Crossbows count as Bow weapons for Bow Bukijutsu that involve firing a projectile, attacking a sightline, marking a target, targeting barriers, intercepting a projectile, or another effect which does not specifically depend on manually drawing a bowstring. Where a compatible technique refers to an Arrow, read it as a Bolt when used with a Crossbow. A Crossbow cannot use a Bukijutsu which specifically depends on drawing a bow, maintaining a drawn bowstring, nocking an Arrow by hand, or manipulating the bow while moving. Quick Nock and Mobile Draw remain Bow-only.

title: Launchers and Thrown Bukijutsu
text: A Kunai or Shuriken Launcher Attack counts as a Thrown Weapon Attack for compatible Thrown Bukijutsu. A technique which explicitly requires the projectile to be thrown by hand cannot be performed through a Launcher. The Launcher supplies its normal Attack statistics unless the Bukijutsu replaces them. The projectile continues to supply its relevant Damage Dice, Damage Type, and projectile effects. Fūma Launch cannot perform a technique which requires more Fūma Shuriken than are currently available.

title: 14. Example Crafted Weapon
text: 14. Example Crafted Weapon

title: The Black Rain
text: Heavy Shuriken Launcher. 13 Component AP. Fūma Cradle 7 AP, Extended Guide 1 3 AP, Expanded Magazine 1 2 AP, Sturdy 1 1 AP. Crafting TN is 15 + (4 × 13), for a total of 67. Crafting Cost is 13,000 + (750 × 13), for a total of 22,750 Ryō. The Black Rain has Capacity 10 for ordinary Shuriken and a separate Fūma Cradle holding one Fūma Shuriken. Because it has spent at least 12 AP on Components, it gains +2 Base Damage Dice and +2 Base Stamina. These bonus Damage Dice apply once to an ordinary Attack, Volley, or Fūma Launch, rather than once per projectile. It may fire a single Shuriken, fire a Volley, or launch its loaded Fūma Shuriken using Fūma Launch. The ordinary magazine and Fūma chamber are Reloaded separately.

title: Armor Crafting
text: Craft armor by choosing its structure, protected location and traits. You can craft armor with X Artisan Points up to a max of your Artisan Ranks which you can spend on its traits (see below). Armor has a crafting TN of 15 + 3X and a cost of 2,500 + (500 × X) Ryō, where X is its Final Artisan Points. This consists of the cost for resources, tools, and any extra parts necessary.

title: Armor Category
text: Every armor piece and armored monster part has one category, separate from its weight or Structure. Choose a category when crafting; unclassified existing armor uses the migration table below. Category Strong against Weak against :--- :--- :--- Dense Slashing Piercing, Blunt Layered Blunt Slashing, Piercing Shaped Piercing Slashing, Blunt Against the strong type, multiply this armor's Absorption or armor-specific DR by 1.5. Against a weak type, multiply it by 0.5. Round flat DR down and cap Absorption at 100%. Energy uses the unmodified protection. Apply this only to protection supplied by this armor or part, not unrelated DR, Blocking or natural resilience. Ordinary armor still loses Durability equal to damage it absorbs. Direct attacks against Armor Durability or a monster part's break threshold deal 50% damage with the strong type and 150% with a weak type; this modifies damage to that object or part only, not damage to the creature. Do not also apply this direct-object multiplier to ordinary absorbed-damage wear. A weapon that physically hits intact armor or a part strong against its declared damage type gains 5 WDP, once per weapon per Attack. No wear occurs if the Attack is fully avoided, the armor is bypassed entirely, or the part has already lost its protection. Fired ammunition takes contact wear instead of its launcher; spent ammunition is consumed normally. Choose one physical damage type before resolving an Attack with a weapon that offers several types. Distinct damage components are assessed separately, but the weapon's 5 WDP trigger still occurs only once. Existing armor Default category :--- :--- Mobile / padded or flexible protection Layered Protective / mail or dense reinforcement Dense Encased / shaped plate Shaped Monster hide or dense scales Dense Monster fur, padding or overlapping flexible layers Layered Monster shell, carapace or rigid plate Shaped A monster profile may assign different categories to different parts. Flesh without an armor or protection entry has no armor category. A broken armored part loses its category benefit and causes no matchup weapon wear.

title: 1. Structure
text: 1. Structure Structure is, put simply, the general materials and processes used to craft your armor. Regardless of the actual details of its construction, all armor is divided into three simple categories of protectiveness, Mobile, Protective, and Encased. The more that the armor covers, and the more metal is used in its construction, the better it is at protecting its wearer. But that also comes with the downside of it becoming heavier and restricting its wearer’s movement. Mobile (1): Designed out of padded clothing or hardened leather, and barely considered armor, Mobile armor is favored by those who value their freedom of movement above all else, yet still don’t want to go fight other superhuman hunters without SOME level of protection. Durability: 100 / Absorption: 5% / Penalty: -1 Immobilization and -1 to Stealth rolls Protective (0): Mostly designed out of chainmail or half plate, this type of armor is the most popular amongst Hunters as it offers the perfect balance between all important aspects of a piece of armor. Durability: 200 / Absorption: 10% / Penalty: -2 Immobilization and -2 to Stealth rolls Encased(2): Full steel plates and the such are the staple of this type of armor. Heavily favored by the average soldier who actually would rather not die in a fight, thank you very much. As well as by the legendary and fearsome samurai. Durability: 300 / Absorption: 15% / Penalty: -3 Immobilization and -3 to Stealth rolls

title: 2. Body Parts
text: 2. Body Parts There are four different Body Parts that armor can protect: The Head, the Torso/Abdomen, the Arms, and the Legs. In the case of the Arms and Legs, your armor will cover both arms or legs if that is the Body Part chosen. It is important to determine which location on the body that piece of armor was built to protect, as this will determine its shape and surface area, providing unique benefits and penalties related to that location. The severity of the penalties will also be determined by the Structure you’ve chosen. If the Immobilization of your armor is reduced to 0 you halve all penalties inherent to the type of armor, rounded down potentially to nothing. (2) Head (Speed 10, Delay 5): The Visibility Penalty caused by Flash Bombs and jutsu is halved for you. Mobile: -2 Awareness. Protective: -4 to Awareness Checks and consecutive search actions provide one less bonus per search. Encased: -5 to Awareness Checks and consecutive search actions provide two less bonus per search. (3) Torso/Abdomen (Speed 16, Delay 8): Your armor gains a further +5% Absorption and +50 Durability. Mobile: -1 to Dodge Rolls. Protective: -3 to Dodge Rolls. Encased: -4 to Dodge Rolls. (1) Arms/Hands (Speed 12, Delay 6): You can parry Weapon Attacks while Unarmed, and Blocking them no longer suffers from that inherent -25% Penalty to Block, however half the damage blocked is dealt to the armor. Mobile: +2 to Seal Speed of Jutsus. Protective: +3 to the Seal Speed of Jutsus, -1 to Parry Rolls. Encased: +4 to the Seal Speed of Jutsus, -2 to Parry Rolls. (1) Legs/Feet (Speed 14, Delay 7): You reduce the knockback received from any source by 25%, or 50% if its encased. Mobile: -10% Movement Speed, -2 to Athletic Checks. Protective: -15% Movement Speed, -3 to Athletic Checks. Encased: -20% Movement Speed; -5 to Athletic Checks.

title: 3. Basic Features
text: 3. Basic Features Basic Features are the parts and enhancements to a piece of armor that truly distinguishes one from another and shows the true skills of its maker. Basic Features modify or add something to the base traits or stats of the Armor. They come in a few forms, but most either reduce some sort of penalty, or increase the defensive capability of the armor. (1) This armor’s Durability is increased by +5%. Taken several times, combine the percentage additively then multiply them with the base Durability of the Armor. (3) This armor’s Absorption is increased by +1%. This can be taken several times, the benefit is additive with the base Absorption of the armor. (1) This armor reduces the Knockback you receive from an effect by -1. This can be taken several times. (1) This armor reduces the Bleed you receive from an effect in that location by -1. This can be taken several times. (1) This armor reduces the Stun you receive from an effect in that location by -1. This can be taken several times. (1) This armor reduces the Burns you receive from an effect in that location by -1. This can be taken several times. (1) The Base Speed to remove this armor is reduced by 1 to a minimum of half the original Speed. (2) This armor gains a +1 bonus to Stealth. This can be taken to a max of 3. The total Stealth bonus that all of your pieces of armor can give you cannot exceed +5.

title: 4. Unique Features
text: 4. Unique Features

title: General
text: These Features are only accessible with the Master Artisan Talent, and represent more extreme and complex modifications to a piece of armor. Each Armor piece can only choose 1 option from each category. (x0.3) When somebody hits you with a Melee Attack in this armor’s location, they take one tenth of its max Durability as Piercing Damage. (x0.2) When this armor’s durability would go down to 0 it halves the leftover Damage of the Attack that destroyed it. (x0.4) When you are inflicted with a minor wound in that location you may pay 30% of this weapon’s max Durability to prevent the wound. (x0.5) The first wound you take in that location is reduced by 1, potentially to nothing.

title: Wondrous Materials
text: (0.15x) Angelskin: This armor gains a +1% bonus to its Absorption every time it’s wearer has their bleed status reduced to a maximum of 25%. This lasts until the end of the fight. As a Speed 5 action the wearer may give themselves a Bleed status equal to 1 + half the % bonus provided by this armor piece. (0.2x) Skysteel: The Armor-Based Immobilization penalty of this Armor is reduced by -1 (0.3x) Ironheart: Increases Armor's Base Durability by 50. (0.3x) Mindglass: This armor keeps the wearer's mind clear and calm by absorbing the negative mental energy onto itself. Every time the wearer would be affected by a Genjutsu (Before they roll Gen Defense), this armor loses 100 Durability and the wearer becomes able to roll Genjutsu Defense twice and use the higher result. (0.35x) Voidglass: This armor's Absorption is treated as twice its normal value against Ninjutsu Attacks. (0.4x) Crypstone: When this armor is struck with a Melee Attack, and the enemy's Attack's Damage is enough to deal Wound to its Wearer, the enemy also receives a Piercing Minor Wound within the same location.

title: Standard Armor
text: Standard Armor is ready-made armorsmith equipment for Hunters who would rather buy protection than design it. Each entry is one armor piece, not a full suit. The listed price replaces the normal custom-crafting cost; buying one requires no Artisan ranks or crafting choices. The listed Artisan Points are the sum of its Structure and Body Part costs. All patterns use their normal Structure, location benefits and location penalties, with no additional features or wondrous materials. Standard Armor can be modified later using the normal Armor Crafting rules. Armor Immobilization and Stealth penalties stack across all worn pieces. Reduce combined Armor Immobilization by (RES + STR/30), to a minimum of 0, as described in Armor Penalties. When reduced to 0, halve the inherent location penalties of the affected armor types, rounded down; Stealth penalties are never reduced this way. Durability and Absorption apply only when an attack strikes the protected location. Arm and leg armor covers both limbs. Mobile Armor Hooded Scout Cowl — 4,000 Ryō. AP 3. Mobile Head armor. Durability 100; Absorption 5%; Armor Immobilization -1; Stealth -1; Equip Speed 10; Remove Delay 5. Flash and jutsu Visibility Penalties are halved. -2 Awareness. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Padded Hunter Vest — 4,500 Ryō. AP 4. Mobile Torso / Abdomen armor. Durability 150; Absorption 10%; Armor Immobilization -1; Stealth -1; Equip Speed 16; Remove Delay 8. +50 Durability and +5% Absorption. -1 Dodge. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Leather Bracers — 3,500 Ryō. AP 2. Mobile Arms / Hands armor. Durability 100; Absorption 5%; Armor Immobilization -1; Stealth -1; Equip Speed 12; Remove Delay 6. Parry weapon attacks unarmed; blocking weapons ignores the inherent -25% Block penalty, but half the blocked damage is dealt to this armor. +2 Seal Speed. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Trailrunner Greaves — 3,500 Ryō. AP 2. Mobile Legs / Feet armor. Durability 100; Absorption 5%; Armor Immobilization -1; Stealth -1; Equip Speed 14; Remove Delay 7. Reduce Knockback by 25% (50% for Encased). -10% Movement Speed; -2 Athletics. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Protective Armor Reinforced Field Helm — 3,500 Ryō. AP 2. Protective Head armor. Durability 200; Absorption 10%; Armor Immobilization -2; Stealth -2; Equip Speed 10; Remove Delay 5. Flash and jutsu Visibility Penalties are halved. -4 Awareness; consecutive searches gain one less bonus. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Hunter Half-Plate — 4,000 Ryō. AP 3. Protective Torso / Abdomen armor. Durability 250; Absorption 15%; Armor Immobilization -2; Stealth -2; Equip Speed 16; Remove Delay 8. +50 Durability and +5% Absorption. -3 Dodge. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Chainmail Vambraces — 3,000 Ryō. AP 1. Protective Arms / Hands armor. Durability 200; Absorption 10%; Armor Immobilization -2; Stealth -2; Equip Speed 12; Remove Delay 6. Parry weapon attacks unarmed; blocking weapons ignores the inherent -25% Block penalty, but half the blocked damage is dealt to this armor. +3 Seal Speed; -1 Parry. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Steel-Shod Legguards — 3,000 Ryō. AP 1. Protective Legs / Feet armor. Durability 200; Absorption 10%; Armor Immobilization -2; Stealth -2; Equip Speed 14; Remove Delay 7. Reduce Knockback by 25% (50% for Encased). -15% Movement Speed; -3 Athletics. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Encased Armor Ironclad War Helm — 4,500 Ryō. AP 4. Encased Head armor. Durability 300; Absorption 15%; Armor Immobilization -3; Stealth -3; Equip Speed 10; Remove Delay 5. Flash and jutsu Visibility Penalties are halved. -5 Awareness; consecutive searches gain two less bonus. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Fortress Cuirass — 5,000 Ryō. AP 5. Encased Torso / Abdomen armor. Durability 350; Absorption 20%; Armor Immobilization -3; Stealth -3; Equip Speed 16; Remove Delay 8. +50 Durability and +5% Absorption. -4 Dodge. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Full Plate Gauntlets — 4,000 Ryō. AP 3. Encased Arms / Hands armor. Parry weapon attacks unarmed; blocking weapons ignores the inherent -25% Block penalty, but half the blocked damage is dealt to this armor. +4 Seal Speed; -2 Parry. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Bastion Sabatons — 4,000 Ryō. AP 3. Encased Legs / Feet armor. Durability 300; Absorption 15%; Armor Immobilization -3; Stealth -3; Equip Speed 14; Remove Delay 7. Reduce Knockback by 25% (50% for Encased). -20% Movement Speed; -5 Athletics. No additional Basic Features, Unique Features or Wondrous Materials. Browse the illustrated Pre-Made Armor Catalogue

title: Craftsman
text: Craft tools and supplies for a hunter’s kit, from flash bombs and lockpicks to weapons. Upon gaining 1 Rank in the Artisan (Craftsman) Skill, you gain the ability to create equipment from the gear and exploding tags category. This requires you to spend a Downtime Slot on an “Equipment Crafting” Action, rolling your Artisan Skill vs a TN of the Artisan Points (explained below) determined by the item. You may pool your rolls until you amass enough to match the TN, which may take a number of Slots and/or Downtime Cycles.

title: Basic Gear
text: This covers any item not listed in the lower sections. These items have a TN based on their cost and a Ryo cost representing the materials required to make it. To find these values take the cost of the item you want to make. The cost is one-fourth that value and the TN is that amount divided by 200. When crafting you can also declare multiple quantities of the same item setting its cost and TN using the total price. For example a Flash Bomb has a cost of 3k Ryo. That means it will have a TN of 15 and a cost of 750 Ryo. If you wanted to craft four of them it would be a TN of 60 and 3k Ryo. You can also make any items from the Ranged Weapons section except for those of large size.

title: Smoke Bombs
text: While Smoke Bombs are a basic item that can be crafted using the rules above, you can customize their effects to suit your needs. From increasing duration, size, or even adding in custom poisons (though this won’t let you make the poisons). The modifications available are listed below and are augments of a regular Smoke Bomb. The Ryo cost of an upgrade is added to the base 3k and used as the total for determining the TN and Materials Cost: Basic Upgrades Visibility Penalty: -1 Vis, 1k Ryo, Max -10 Duration: +5 IC, 2k Ryo, Max 30 IC Radius: +5 Radius, 1.5k Ryo, Max 25 Yards Range: Divisor -1, 3k Ryo, Max STR/3 Specialty Poison: +1 Poison, 10k Ryo, Max 1 Imbue any Inhalation Poison into the Smoke Bomb (consuming one dose). When used, anyone who spends longer than 10 IC in the area must make a Resistance roll against your Toxicology or be poisoned. This method reduces the poison’s duration by half but it does not begin reducing until they are out of the area (or it ends).

title: Antidotes
text: Antidotes are tricky as most poisons are made using custom recipes from each individual. While you can target specific ones like those imbued by Snake Summoners, it’s often more useful to create general counters for a broader range of effects: When countering a specific poison you must have a sample or have been poisoned by it personally. The TN is the same as the Poison you are countering but the cost is half that much of the original. If you are forming a general counter, choose any Poison effect from Poison crafting besides Potent. You can create a specific formula to counteract those symptoms. The TN equals whatever the TN for that Poison would be at that tier times 1.5 (rounded down) and the cost would be half that amount. Following the Poison Point cost guide you can only make antidotes up to your Artisan Ranks /4. For example if you wanted to make a Lethality 2 Antidote: The base cost is 10k and its Poison TN is 8 with a scale of 5 so TN 21. So at 2nd rank your antidote would be 1.5x the TN for 31 and 5k Ryo. Antidotes that act quickly enough to be useful in emergencies, such as combat, aren't gentle on the body, applying a -2 penalty to your Accuracy and all d20 rolls for 100 IC. However, for that duration you are immune to the poison in question. Antidotes used in succession do not stack the penalties, but they do refresh the duration.

title: Uncraftable
text: The following items require technology unavailable to ordinary crafters: - Flashlight - Camera - Camera Film Roll - Ninja Comm Device

title: Poisons
text: Poisons are nasty business, and one of the murkier aspects of ninja tactics. Certainly, before the days when shinobi had discovered the secrets of chakra manipulation, poisons were a vital part of their arsenal. The proper use of poisons, however, is hard to learn, and in most circumstances just isn't as useful as being able to shoot fireballs and run up walls. Some hunter, however, still find uses for them. This section is for them!

title: Brewing
text: Getting your hands on some Poison isn’t an easy thing, those who have mastered its use understandably don’t advertise that or their inventory of deadly chemicals. And you aren’t going to find some on the open market either. Which means that you’ll have to gather the ingredients and make it yourself. But that imposes its own complications, most techniques for cultivating deadly venoms are tightly held secrets, and figuring out the best ratios and ingredients is an arduous if not expensive process. To even begin, you’ll need to acquire the appropriate talent, which typically means you’ll have to find one of those previously mentioned masters and convince them to not use their tools of death on you and instead teach you how to use them on your enemies. Once you do, you can begin with the process detailed below.

title: Poison Points and TN
text: You have Toxicology/4 Poison Points. A Poison’s effects cannot exceed that total. Furthermore, Poisons tend to take a while to make. As your skills progress, you’ll figure out better techniques to distill the ingredients and brew your venoms, but the more complex a Poison you make, the more time it’ll take to finish brewing it. Brewing Poisons requires a Poison TN, a Target Number you must reach using Toxicology rolls during Downtime Actions. The Poison TN is determined by the individual effects that the Poison has. All effects have a base increase to Poison TN, and a scaling increase should the effect be taken again. For example, Severity has a base increase to Poison TN of 3, and a scale of 2. Meaning the first time it is taken, it increase the base Poison TN of 10 to 13, but if Severity were taken again for the same Poison, it gains an extra 5 (Base 3+2) to TN, becoming a Poison TN of 18, if Severity was taken a third time, the TN increase is 7 (5+2) making the final Poison TN a 25. Toxicology rolls carry over to the next Downtime until you’ve reached the TN, however, any extra points leftover after that are completely gone.

title: Doses and Costs
text: Poisons are measured in doses. A dose is how much of the substance is required to poison a hunter and apply the effects of a particular brew. Whenever you Brew a new Poison, this is how much you make. Once, the main measurement unit was how many whales or elephants the poison could kill (The bare minimum needed to even begin affecting hunter) but we’ve long since moved past such archaic measurements. Pay the total Ryō cost of the poison’s effects to obtain the ingredients, reagents and tools for the batch.

title: Types of Poison
text: Choose how the poison is delivered: Contact, Injury, Inhalation or Ingestion. Contact: Contact Poisons can be applied to any blunt or slashing weapon, and as long as you hit with the Contact Poison, even if you deal no damage, you apply a dose of the Poison. Contact Poisons gain no other effects. Injury: Injury Poisons can be applied to any Piercing or Slashing weapon, but require the attack to deal a Minor Wound at the minimum to apply a dose of their effects. Doses of Injury Poisons won’t be used up until a Wound is applied. Injury Poisons are quite versatile and deadly, they gain an extra 3 Poison Points worth of effects. Ingestion: Ingestion Poisons are effectively useless in combat, but can be used to lace someone's food or somehow trick a person into eating it. When chosen, the Brewer can choose whether the effects apply immediately once eaten, or up to [Toxicology/5] hours from the time of ingestion, to a max of 8 hours. All effects of Ingestion poisons are doubled due to their lethality. Inhalation: Inhalation Poisons typically require esoteric methods to apply them, the most common of which is the Poison Smoke Bomb. But they are also frequently used as parts of traps and such. Inhalation Poisons are hard to avoid, so long as somebody is within the Poison’s area, they automatically receive. But this gaseous nature means the Poison is more distilled, Inhalation Poisons have 2 Poison Points less than normal. No matter how many poisons you're afflicted by, or their type, similar effects do not stack. Thus, if you had an Injury Poison that gave Poison Severity 4 and Immobilization 2 for Duration 50, and an Inhalation Poison that gave Poison Severity 2 and Immobilization 1 for Duration 75, you would take 4 damage per initiative count and have Immob 2 for 50 IC, and then for the next 25 you'd take 2 damage per IC and have Immob 1. Any additional effects apply regardless, as long as they don't overlap (Paralysis 1 and Paralysis 3 is just Paralysis 3, as normal).

title: Time
text: In combat or similarly stressful situations, Poison Duration is measured in IC and its effects apply each IC. Outside combat, or while the target is incapacitated, use minutes instead. For example, Poison Severity 5 with Duration 75 lasts 75 minutes outside combat, dealing 5 Vitality or HP damage each minute.

title: Resisting Poison
text: Whenever you’re hit by a weapon with Contact poison, or damaged by one with Injury poison, you roll Resistance against the poison user’s Toxicology + 10. If you fail this roll (which does receive the benefits or partial defense), you have been poisoned. You’re afflicted by the poison’s status effects (Poison of some value, and sometimes other effects, described in the individual poison) for its Duration. If partial defense applies, it reduces the Duration, not the severity.

title: Applying to Weapons
text: One dose of poison is enough to coat the business end of a weapon. As a Speed 10 action you can apply up to 1 + Toxicology/10 doses worth of poisons to your weapons, in any combination. For instance, if you applied 4 doses, you could poison: - 1 weapon with 4 doses - 4 weapons with 1 dose each - 1 weapon with 2 doses and 2 more weapons with 1 dose each - etc Each time the weapon hits something, it loses one dose, the order in which it applies doses should be declared on poison application (i.e. First layer Yew, Second layer Centipede, Etc). If you apply a new poison or poisons to the weapon, any remaining poison is wiped away. Due to the care it takes to not poison yourself when throwing Shurikens and Kunai, coated ranged weapons cannot be used in multi-throws.

title: Resisting and Identifying Poisons
text: Overcoming Poisons isn’t simple, they’re kind of made to be deadly, but Hunters are known for being able to do the impossible. Having a supercharged immune system is the least of their talents. Whenever you have a Dose of Poison applied to you, you must roll Resistance against the Toxicology TN of the original creator. When you or someone else has been poisoned, it's possible to identify the venom just based on the symptoms. you can roll a Toxicology, or Medicine skill check (your preference) against the Poison’s Toxicology TN -5. Success means you've identified the Poison and know its effects and can begin working on an Antidote so long as you have the proper Toolkit. You cannot repeat this roll.

title: Poison Effects
text: All Brewed Poisons have a base foundation of Severity 2, and Duration 50 and have a base Poison TN of 5. They may gain the following effects by paying the requisite Poison Points and Ryo. And increasing the TN by the mentioned amounts.

title: Lethal
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 2.5k Poison TN: 8 Scale: 5 Effects: This increases a Poison’s Severity by +1.

title: Festering
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 1.5k Poison TN: 6 Scale: 6 Effects: This increases a Poison’s Duration by +25.

title: Destabilizant
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 2.5k Poison TN: 8 Scale: 3 Effects: This adds or increases a Poison’s Immobilization by +1.

title: Dazzler
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 2.5k Poison TN: 8 Scale: 3 Effects: This adds or increases a Poison’s Visibility by +1.

title: Feverish
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 2k Poison TN: 8 Scale: 2 Effects: This adds or increases a Poison’s Burns by +2.

title: Irritant
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 5k Poison TN: 1 Scale: 10 Effects: This gives all skill rolls except Resistance a -3.

title: Paralytic
text: Poison Point Cost: 2 Ryo Cost: 7.5k Poison TN: 8 Scale: 4 Effects: This adds or increases a Poison’s Paralysis by +1.

title: Potent
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 1.5Ryo cost Poison TN: 30 Scale: 20 Effects: This provides an extra Dose of the Poison.

title: Esoteric Poison Effects
text: These require the Exotic Venoms Talent.

title: Hallucinogen
text: Poison Point Cost: 1 Ryo Cost: 10k Poison TN: 6 Scale: 5 Effects: Reduces the Victim’s Genjutsu Defense by -1.

title: Asphyxiant
text: Poison Point Cost: 2 Ryo Cost: 10k Poison TN: 20 Scale: 10 Effects: This adds or increases a Poison’s Suffocation by +1.

title: Depressant
text: Poison Point Cost: 2 Ryo Cost: 12.5k Poison TN: 20 Scale: 20 Effects: When Victim fatigues, they only reduce Stamina and CE penalties by half rather than reset them. Buying this a second time makes Stamina and CE penalties irreducible by Fatigue.

title: Asthmatic
text: Poison Point Cost: 2 Ryo Cost: 12.5k Poison TN: 20 Scale: 20 Effects: Every time the Victim receives an increase to CE or Stamina penalties, the other increases by half and vice versa (Rounding Up). Buying this a second time makes them increase by the full amount.

title: Sickening
text: Poison Point Cost: 2 Ryo Cost: 12.5k Poison TN: 25 Scale: 10 Effects: Reduces a Victim’s Attribute by 10% to a max of 50%. The Specific Attribute must be chosen during the Brewing of the Poison.

title: Obtaining Equipment
text: Hunters in the Naruto universe have an advantage which real hunter lacked: namely, magical chakra-based powers that let them perform superhuman physical feats, stand on water, and breathe fire. Even so, a wise hunter, magical or not, will equip themselves with a wide variety of tools. True, you could create a thick bank of fog instead of throwing down a smoke bomb--but that smoke bomb's faster, and less taxing. Every piece of equipment has a cost in Ryo, the world's most commonly-used currency. You can get Ryo through missions, events, and on character creation where you have 50k to start out with. Items can be divided into two broad categories: Consumable and non-consumable. Consumable items are gone once you use them once. These are things like smoke bombs, poisons, and explosives. Non-consumable items can be broken, destroyed, or lost, but usually aren't. These are things like ropes, weapons, and lockpicks. Ranged weapons are not destroyed on use (hit or miss).

title: Restrictions
text: While any hunter can pick up a common sword to wield items of higher power it takes a certain competence. As such the weapons and armor you can utilize are limited by your capabilities: Weapons: Cannot wield weapon with Artisan points more than Athletics +10 Armor: Cannot wear armor with Artisan points more than Resistance +10 Attempting to use an item you aren’t qualified for reduces your accuracies, offenses, and d20s by 2. You also have your fatigue bonuses and damage bonuses halved.

title: Draw Weapon
text: (Speed 5) Weapons are typically carried attached to one's person somehow; swords have sheathes, a pair of tonfa might be tucked through belt holsters, a fan could be strapped across your back, and so forth. Drawing a weapon is retrieving it from wherever you have it stored and placing it in your hands. At this point you can use it to attack, parry, or whatever else you please, the downside being that your hands aren't free for, say, handseals. You may also draw a weapon at the start of combat (when you roll initiative), without taking an action to do so. If you wish, you can draw two weapons as a single Speed 5 action. Note that you only needed to Draw weapons you intend to hold and use in melee. This Speed to attack with thrown or multi-thrown weapons includes the time needed to retrieve them from holsters. Be aware: While holding one or more weapons, you can still make basic unarmed attacks. You cannot, however, use Unarmed or Combo jutsu. Grappling is still possible as long as you have at least one hand free.

title: Sheathe Weapon
text: (Speed 5) You put a weapon you're holding away, in some secure fashion. If you're holding two weapons, you can put them both away at the same time.

title: Discard Weapon
text: (Speed 1, or Speed +2) You drop or toss aside a weapon. Done normally, this is a Speed 1 action. However, it may also be used alongside an Interrupt (such as a defensive ninjutsu technique) by increasing that action's Speed (after AP reductions) by 2.

title: Retrieve Weapon
text: (Speed 5) You pick up a weapon on the ground. This can be your weapon, or someone else's, as long as nobody's currently holding it. You can only pick up one melee weapon at a time with this action, and must be able to physically reach it (which may require you to move first). You can also pick up DEX/10 used throwing weapons and holster them appropriately.

title: Disarm
text: (Weapon's Speed +4) You use a weapon you're holding to knock an enemy's out of their grasp, usually by hitting it at such an angle, and with enough force, that it becomes physically impossible for them to hold onto it. This is a basic weapon attack that does no damage, but if it hits you knock any item they’re holding STR/10 yards in any direction (if straight up, the weapon lands at their feet but cannot be retrieved for STR/10 IC). Trying to Parry a Disarm attempt has a -3 penalty. Small weapons cannot disarm Large or Extreme weapons, and Extreme weapons lack the finesse to be used to disarm at all.

title: Transfer Item
text: (Speed 3) You may transfer any item from your inventory into another person's inventory, as long as you are both at a distance of 0 from each other. Note that these items are not automatically held, so if you were to transfer a Katana to someone else they would still have to take a Draw Weapon action to wield it. Item modifications made before the transfer are retained-thus, if you poisoned a kunai and handed it over, the kunai would still be poisoned. Both parties must agree to the Transfer for Transfer Item to function.

title: Weapon Durability
text: Each weapon has a Weapon Damage Pool (WDP), starting at 0 each scene. Its wear threshold is its Durability + DEX/10, rounded down. Ordinary attacks, Jutsu, being Parried, Parries and Blocks do not generate WDP. Gain WDP only from resistant armor contact as described above or an effect explicitly causing weapon damage. When WDP exceeds the wear threshold, increase Damage Level by 1 and reset WDP to 0. Damage Level penalties stack. At the end of a scene, reduce Damage Level by 2, never below its level at the start of that scene. Repairs use the normal equipment repair rules.

title: Damage Levels
text: Level Effect :--- :--- 1 -1 Damage Die 2 -5% Wounding 3 -1 Parry 4 -2 Damage Dice 5 -5% Wounding 6 +1 Stamina Cost 7 Die size reduced by 2, -10% Wounding 8 -1 Accuracy, -1 Parry 9 +2 Speed 10 The weapon breaks. A broken weapon may still be used to attack, but has 0 Artisan Points and uses the base stats of a weapon one size smaller. Small weapons cannot be used this way.

title: Armor Protection
text: All pieces of armor have Durability and Absorption. Durability can be seen as the HP of the armor, whilst Absorption is given as a percentage value and determines how much of an Attack’s Damage the armor actually protects you from. Whenever you receive Direct Damage to a location with armor, you reduce the Damage you’d have received by the Absorption percentage, and then take the amount the Damage was mitigated by, and reduce your armor’s Durability by that amount. Once a piece of armor has reached 0 Durability, it no longer Absorbs a part of an Attack’s Damage, nor does it provide any of the benefits of its Basic and Unique Features, only all of the penalties remain. It is broken for all intents and purposes, and can never be repaired or recovered. It’s best to remove a broken piece of armor as soon as possible if it happens in the middle of a fight, as it is just dead weight by that point

title: Armor Penalties
text: All pieces of armor have immobilization and stealth penalties that stack between all pieces of armor. The combined Armor-based Immobilization of all of your armor is reduced by (RES+STR/30) to a minimum combined total of 0. Potentially allowing you to don several pieces of armor with little to no Immobilization, assuming you’re strong enough. If the Immobilization of your armor is reduced to 0 you halve all penalties inherent to the type of armor, rounded down potentially to nothing. Note: This reduction does not apply to the Stealth penalty, no matter how strong you are, you can’t stop the restriction of movement and the sounds that boiled leather and worked metal cause.

title: Melee Weapons
text: Every Melee Weapon has Shape, Damage Type, Size, and Heft tags. These tags determine which abilities, Bukijutsu, and other weapon effects can use it. Sword: Weapon Shape. Polearm: Weapon Shape. Club: Weapon Shape. Chain: Weapon Shape. Fan: Weapon Shape. Slashing, Piercing, Blunt: Damage Type tags. If a weapon has more than one Damage Type, choose the type used for a Wound after its severity is confirmed and before its location is determined, unless an effect requires the type earlier. Small, Medium, Large, Extreme: Size tags. Extreme Weapons suffer -3 Accuracy when Parrying and use Base Speed 4 for Parry. One-Handed: Requires one hand. Two-Handed: Requires two hands and increases the wielder's normal Physical Damage Bonus by 50%. This does not multiply Damage Bonus from Weapon Focus, Ninjutsu, or other additional sources. Versatile: May be wielded One-Handed or Two-Handed. Changing hand placement is a Speed 0 non-Interrupt action. The Two-Handed PDB increase applies only while wielded with two hands. Dual: A matched pair built to use the Dual Wield rules. Weapons with the Dual property use their natural weapon Speed for Damage calculations during a Dual Wield Attack.

text: Standard Weapons are ready-made workshop patterns. Buying one requires no Artisan ranks and no Weapon Crafting choices. Their Artisan Point value still counts for wielding restrictions.
