Use the greater of the current Launcher Range and STR/3 for Fūma Launch; retain the Fūma Shuriken’s normal hit-margin and Wounding effects.

title: Ready-Made Kunai and Shuriken
text: Edge-Honed Kunai — 1,125 Ryō. AP 2. Kunai frame. Speed 8; Stamina 8; Damage 3d6; Accuracy +0; Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 1. Installed Components: Reinforced Edge 1. Precision Kunai — 2,500 Ryō. AP 5. Kunai frame. Speed 8; Stamina 8; Damage 3d6; Accuracy +0 (+1 on single-projectile Attacks); Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 1. Installed Components: Reinforced Edge 1, Calibrated Balance 1. Breacher Kunai — 3,250 Ryō. AP 6. Kunai frame. Speed 8; Stamina 9; Damage 3d6; Accuracy +0; Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 1. Installed Components: Armor-Piercing Tip, Reinforced Edge 1. On a full hit, treat Armor Absorption as 10 percentage points lower, minimum 0%. Wirehook Kunai — 2,500 Ryō. AP 5. Kunai frame. Speed 8; Stamina 8; Damage 2d6; Accuracy +0; Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 1. Installed Components: Reinforced Ring, Returning Wire. Gain +2 Accuracy when attaching or delivering Ninja Wire through a compatible Jutsu or rule. When attached to Ninja Wire, retrieve the unattended weapon from up to 10 yards away as a Speed 3 Utility action if its path is unobstructed. Longwing Kunai — 3,250 Ryō. AP 6. Kunai frame. Speed 8; Stamina 9; Damage 3d6; Accuracy +0 (+1 on single-projectile Attacks); Range 10 + STR/4; Delay 1. Installed Components: Aerodynamic Profile 1, Calibrated Balance 1. Quickstar — 1,500 Ryō. AP 3. Shuriken frame. Speed 5; Stamina 5; Damage 1d6; Accuracy +2 (+1 on single-projectile Attacks); Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 0. Installed Components: Calibrated Balance 1. Precision Star — 2,500 Ryō. AP 5. Shuriken frame. Speed 5; Stamina 5; Damage 2d6; Accuracy +2 (+1 on single-projectile Attacks); Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 0. Installed Components: Reinforced Edge 1, Calibrated Balance 1. Razor Star — 3,500 Ryō. AP 7. Shuriken frame. Speed 5; Stamina 6; Damage 2d6; Accuracy +2; Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 0. Installed Components: Honed Geometry 2, Razor Edges. +15% Wounding when dealing Slashing Damage. Splitter Star — 3,250 Ryō. AP 6. Shuriken frame. Speed 5; Stamina 6; Damage 3d6; Accuracy +2; Range 5 + STR/4; Delay 0. Installed Components: Splitting Star, Reinforced Edge 1. On a full hit with a single-projectile Attack, add +1 Damage Die, for 4d6 total. Splitting Star does not function during Multi-Throw or Volley.

title: Ready-Made Ammunition
text: All prices below purchase one batch of ten identical Arrows or Bolts. Ammo AP is separate from Weapon AP and does not count toward wielding requirements. Each shot consumes one piece of ammunition; recovered ammunition may be reused where appropriate. Standard Arrow — 2,500 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 0. 10 Arrows; d12 Piercing. Piercing Arrow — 2,500 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 0. 10 Arrows; d8 Piercing. Ignore Armor. Standard Bolt — 2,500 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 0. 10 Bolts; d10 Piercing. Bodkin Bolt — 4,000 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 1. 10 Bolts; d8 Piercing. On a full hit, treat Armor Absorption as 10 percentage points lower, minimum 0%. Razorhead Arrow or Bolt — 4,000 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 1. 10 Arrows or Bolts; d10 Slashing. +5% Wounding when dealing Slashing Damage. Blunt Arrow or Bolt — 4,000 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 1. 10 Arrows or Bolts; d10 Blunt. On a full hit, may attempt Knockback 2 using the normal Status rules. Longshot Arrow — 4,000 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 1. 10 Arrows; d10 Piercing. Increase listed Attack Range by 20% and Delay by 1. Longshot Bolt — 4,000 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 1. 10 Bolts; d8 Piercing. Increase listed Attack Range by 20% and Delay by 1. Tracking Arrow or Bolt — 4,000 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 1. 10 Arrows or Bolts; d8 Piercing. On a full hit, mark the target with alchemical dye and scent. Gain +2 Survival to track it for the rest of the scene. Barbed Arrow or Bolt — 5,500 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 2. 10 Arrows or Bolts; d10 Piercing. If a Wound inflicted by the Attack applies Bleed, increase that Bleed by 1, maximum once per Attack. Wireline Arrow or Bolt — 5,500 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 2. 10 Arrows or Bolts; d8 Piercing. Leaves up to 10 yards of attached Ninja Wire at the point of impact. Razorhead Longshot Arrow or Bolt — 5,500 Ryō per ten. Ammo AP 2. 10 Arrows or Bolts; d8 Slashing. +5% Wounding when dealing Slashing Damage; increase listed Attack Range by 20% and Delay by 1. Fūma Shuriken cost 5,000 Ryō each. Ninja Wire costs 500 Ryō per 5 yards and is purchased separately. Retrieving or recovering fired Kunai, Shuriken, Arrows, or Bolts uses the normal Equipment rules and the applicable weapon effects.

title: Senbon [Piercing, Thrown, Projectile]
text: Large metal needles, traditionally used in acupuncture. Rarely, particularly skilled shinobi will use these with devastating efficiency. Frequently, particularly overconfident shinobi will use this with depressing ineptitude. Cost: 250 Speed: 10 Stamina: 5 Damage: 1d4 Accuracy: -2 Range: 5 + STR/5 Delay: 0 Special: Ignore armor. Cannot be used in Multi Throw (See Abilities).

title: Boomerang [Blunt, Thrown, Projectile]
text: A mysterious weapon discovered in underground caves with proficient users seemingly always able to have it return to them. There has to be some hunter magic involved…probably. Cost: 1,250 Speed: 10 Stamina: 10 Damage: 8d8 Range: 5 + STR/3 Delay: 3 Special: After throwing this weapon it always returns to your hand 10 IC later. If you have no weapons to catch it the boomerang simply flies off lost until you retrieve it after the battle.

title: Fuuma Shuriken [Slashing, Thrown, Melee, Projectile]
text: A fairly complex device, a fuuma shuriken is four curved blades that can fold together and be used as an improvised blade in melee combat, or unfolded and locked open, taking on a pinwheel shape, to be thrown. Cost: 5,000 Speed: 14 Stamina: 15 Damage: (4+STR/12)d12 Range: STR/3 Delay: 4 Special: For every point you hit by, you add 10% to the attack's total damage, to a maximum of +200% (so, if they dodged and you hit by 3 points you'd do 1.3 times damage, and that number would be reduced by the effects of partial defense); this does not apply if it is blocked. If no defense is declared then the attacker hits by their full accuracy value. This weapon's damage is considered 25% higher for the purpose of inflicting wounds. You may also use the Fuuma Shuriken as a melee weapon, in which case it loses all of its other special effects, deals only 4d12 damage and has the following Tags: Slashing, Small, One-Handed.Because these are large and encumbering, they are typically worn somehow strapped to the back; for each Fuuma Shuriken beyond the first you are carrying you have a -1 penalty to dodge rolls.

title: Blank Scroll
text: A large scroll. Most of the time these are carried rolled up to save space. They're useless, aside from the fact that a few sealing jutsu make use of them. Cost: 1.25k Ryo

title: Blood Increasing Pill
text: These pills contain a peculiar mix of chemicals that, when consumed by someone capable of using chakra (such as a hunter) will allow their body to rapidly replenish lost blood. When you take one of these pills you regain RES/50 HP (but not Vitality) each IC, for 50 IC. During this duration you take only one third damage from poison, and no damage from effects caused by bleeding (such as certain wounds). Using a Blood Pill is a Speed 10 action. Cost: 7.5k Ryo

title: Caltrops
text: Small bits of metal that are basically just four short spikes attached at a center; no matter how they land, there'll always be a metal spike pointing upwards. The typical use is to scatter them across the ground to impede movement through an area. You can deploy Caltrops as a Speed 5, Area 5, Range 5 action. Anyone that moves as part of an attack into, within or out of the caltrops’ area, suffers Piercing damage equal to 5d4+25. You can deploy Caltrops as a Speed 1 Interrupt anytime you suffer from a Knockback effect of at least 5 Yards. When used in this manner, the Caltrops’ area center is always 5 yards away from the attacker in the direction of the Knockback (that means the attacker is always at the edge of the area, and the area is always between the attacker and the defender). This responsive use of the Caltrops still have the range of 5 yards. This means that if used in response to a ranged knockback attack, your caltrop throw will place caltrops between yourself and your opponent with the center placed up to 5 yards away from you. Cost: 1k Ryo for enough caltrops to cover one 5 yard area

title: Cloth, Per Yard
text: Broad, sturdy cloth that looks like bandages, or perhaps mummification wraps. This comes in large rolls of up to 200 yards; carrying more than one roll inflicts a -1 immobilization penalty for each beyond the first (not due to weight, but because they're bulky). Confine Scroll Seals can carry one roll each. Cost: 150 Ryo

title: Container, Small
text: A container, usually a gourd, clay jug, or waterskin, commonly worn at the hip. One container can hold 2 gallons of water or another substance. For every two small containers or fraction thereof beyond the second, you suffer a -1 penalty to dodge due to encumberance. Cost: 2.5k Ryo

title: Container, Large
text: A large gourd or other sort of container, several feet long and usually worn on the back. It's heavy and bulky, but not quite enough to restrict the mobility of a well-trained hunters. It can hold up to 8 gallons of water, but you can only carry one with you (due to its size!). Cost: 7.5k Ryo

title: Flash Bomb
text: Flash bombs are devices which, when ignited, produce brilliant flashes of light. Anyone who doesn't know to close their eyes when you throw one suffers a -4 visibility penalty for the next 10 IC. You can throw these up to STR/5 yards. Throwing one is a Speed 4 action. You may also drop a flash bomb when dodging, in which case your dodge's Speed is increased by 4. Flash bombs have an Area of 10 and if used with a dodge the User is the center of it. Every time you throw a flash bomb as part of a dodge, after the first time it’s been done, you need to succeed at an opposed espionage check vs your opponent for them to not know to close their eyes in time. They have a bonus of +3 to this roll for every time they’d already had to take this roll in this fight. Cost: 1.5k Ryo

title: Ninja Wire
text: High tension 16-gauge wire. It is generally only available in hunter villages, and comes in spools with various lengths of wire. Cost: 0.5k Ryo per 5 Yards.

title: Rope
text: I refuse to explain what this is. Individual lengths of rope can be purchased up to 300 feet (100 yards), but there's nothing stopping you from tying a few together. Tying somebody up requires 10 yards of rope, and the person in question to not be resisting. You can tie someone up with ropes. If so, roll Espionage +10 to see how good your knots were. The result, or 20, is the TN for escaping. The user can try to slip the knots (Espionage skill roll, +DEX/10) which takes 5 minutes to attempt (they can hide that they are doing so via an opposed Espionage roll). This can be attempted repeatedly. You can also attempt to snap the ropes using brute force. This calls for a roll of 1d20 + (Athletics /5) + (STR /10) against a TN of 30, requires a Stamina 25 roll, and is done instantly, but repeated attempts cannot be made (either you're strong enough to break the ropes, or you're not). Cost: 0.5k Ryo per 5 Yards.

title: Smoke Bomb
text: Paper balls small enough to be easily held in one hand, when thrown at the ground they burst and release wide clouds of smoke. Smoke bombs have a range of STR/5 yards, and can be thrown as a Speed 4 action. When thrown, it releases a cloud of thick smoke that causes a -6 visibility penalty to all people within its 5 yard radius, for 20 IC. Once 10 ICs have passed, the Visibility penalty of the Smoke Bomb is halved. Cost: 1.5k Ryo

title: Soldier Pill
text: The proper name is 'military ration pills', but the term soldier pill is more commonly used among hunters. They're less rations than fast-acting performance-enhancing drugs. Though every village has a slightly different recipe, the pills are all marble-sized and black or dark brown. When eaten, they have the approximate flavor and texture of sawdust. These stimulants lower Fatigue by one category and give +10 to your next Chakra Exhaustion or Stamina roll. Doing so is a Speed 10 action in battle. You may only take one per battle, and no more than RES/50 per day. Cost: 12.5k Ryo

title: Compass
text: A small, typically handheld device that has a needle inside a metal case (with a glass cover, so it can be seen) that points, approximately, to magnetic north when held level. These aren't exactly precise, but they're good enough most of the time. Notably, they can have trouble working underground or if they get zapped by a lightning jutsu. When trying to navigate the wilderness, having a compass gives a +2 bonus to any Survival rolls. If you also have a map of the country you're in, this is raised to +4. Cost- 2.5k Ryo

title: Map
text: A map of a given country. It's usually a really, really good for at least one person on every hunter team to have a map of any country they expect to be going through. These have only basic information about terrain, landmarks, and settlements. Maps come with scroll cases for ease and safety of Transportation. A map gives a +4 bonus to any Survival rolls made in the appropriate country, within reason (they would help tracking someone, or finding shelter, but not exploring the inside of a cave). Cost- 5k Ryo

title: First Aid Kit
text: Bandages, antiseptics and basic treatment supplies. Use a kit with Stabilise or a treatment listed by a Wound. A kit can also end non-Wound Bleed or Burn. This is a Touch Utility Action with Speed equal to twice the effect’s Severity, minimum 3. A single kit can treat one Bleed and one Burn before it is expended. Treating a Wound instead consumes the entire kit and takes Speed 15 per category: Minor 15, Major 30, Severe 45, Critical 60. Apply only the treatment benefits permitted by that Wound’s entry. Cost: 2,500 Ryō.

title: Flare
text: A handy little pyrotechnic device, a cylinder usually a bit too large to fit comfortably in the palm. When lit (most have built in starters or strikers, to avoid the need for matches) they shine brilliantly, enough that it can be painful to look directly at them without squinting, and become blisteringly hot. They burn out quickly, within half a minute. The vast majority of flares are projectiles, with built-in propellant. Aimed upwards, they'll launch into the air. During the day, this is typically unnoticed if you're doing anything other than staring at the spot it's launched up waiting to see it, and know exactly where it will be. In twilight and darker conditions, however, a flare can be seen for a considerable distance; they're often used for signalling, though suffer from not being too discrete. Cost: 2k Ryo

title: Flashlight
text: Flashlights are popular because hunter like to be able to see in low-light environments! They're also useful because they can be turned off, or on, as needed. Quite handy for staying hidden when you hear unwanted company approaching. Flashlights have a battery life of about half an hour. A spare set of batteries (for another half hour of use) costs 500 Ryo. Cost: 4k

title: Glow Stick
text: A transparent small (around six inches long, usually) cylinder filled with chemicals that, when mixed, glow brightly. A swift blow to the stick (usually striking it against one's knee; simply bending it with enough force will also work) will shatter the internal glass dividers, mixing the chemicals and producing a pleasing illumination. A glow stick will glow for about an hour; it cannot be turned off once activated, short of breaking it completely and letting the luminescent fluid inside it drain out (in which case you just have a glowing puddle). They're available in a variety of colors, with the most popular ones being green and blue. Cost: 2k

title: Oxygen Mask
text: This is a small 'mask' that covers the wearer's mouth and nose, and is held in place by elastic bands which form an airtight seal. Rather than filtering air out, it has two possible fixtures (usually one on each side of the mouth) for an oxygen tank to be attached. When wearing the mask, the user has a -3 penalty to all Stamina rolls, as it takes a slight effort to breathe through it. Putting this on in combat is a Speed 5 action, or +2 Speed if used as part of an Interrupt. Removing the mask is a Speed 5 action. Wearing an oxygen mask with at least tank attached makes the wearer immune to external suffocation penalties (being inside an unbreathable cloud would not affect them; being physically choked would) and provides a +8 bonus to Resistance rolls against statuses that would be inflicted by breathing something in (such as poison mist); the mask is not perfectly air-tight. Cost: 20k Ryo

title: Oxygen Tank
text: Tanks of compressed, breathable air, usually strapped to one's back. They're basically useless by themselves, but each comes with a hose that can be attached to an oyxgen mask. Each tank provides 30 minutes of breathable air. Cost: 5k Ryo per tank5

title: Camouflage Kit
text: Everything you need to blend in with the environment, like a truly sneaky hunter. These come in four flavors: forest/plains, desert, mountainous/rocky, and 'other' (covering anything not one of those). A kit may only be used in its corresponding environment. Using a kit takes 15 minutes, and is enough to conceal a person at level 3 Stealth; the stealth roll is made after they're fully hidden. The exact contents are fairly nonspecific, but regardless, each kit is good for only one use. Cost: 7.5k Ryo

title: Camera
text: Cameras are rare devices, and ones suited for use by hunter even more so. Styles vary, but they are all small, and usually handheld. However, they are large enough that they cannot be effectively concealed while in use. The exact designs may vary greatly, though Sunagakure is fond of a model worn like a circlet on the head, with the lens covering one eye. Most models include a flash that allows blurry pictures to be taken in the dark. Each image uses a single piece of film, acquired separately. Facilities to develop the film are rare, but exist in all major hunters villages, along with trained staff who will do so overnight for urgent matters, or within a week for personal needs. Cost: 25k Ryo

title: Camera Film Roll
text: These are specially treated, light-sensitive pieces of paper. A single roll of Camera Film is good for 10 pictures. Due to the lack of standardization among models, pieces of film generally cannot be exchanged from one camera to another. These are usually stored inside the camera itself; if exposed to light before capturing an image they become useless, though afterwards there will be no effects from direct light on the paper. Cost: 2.5k Ryo

title: Grappling Hook
text: A three- or four-pronged sturdy metal hook. The typical use is to attach it to the end of a rope then throw it over a wall, up a tree, or across a small chasm, and hope it catches on something (such as a piece of architecture, a branch, or an appropriately-shaped rock). The user then climbs the rope to get to their destination! These see limited use among experienced hunter, who typically have ways of easily doing the same thing, but beginners often find them useful, and they can be situationally helpful even for more advanced hunters. Cost: 1.5k Ryo

title: Lockpicks
text: A set of small tools, easily carried in a pocket, used for opening locks in absence of the key. These allow an Espionage roll to be made to open a lock, and also provide a bonus to said roll. That bonus has a maximum of +5, or the user's Espionage skill ranks, whichever is lower; you have to actually know how to use them to get any benefit. These are reusable, though a roll of 5 or lower on the Espionage check means they break in the attempt (which may still be successful). Cost: 5k Ryo per +1

title: Ninja Comm Device
text: The pinnacle of technological advancement in the hunter world, these are small wireless radios. They're typically worn as headsets with an ear insert and a microphone held suspended near the wearer's mouth. Normal comm devices can be tuned to transmit and receive on any of a dozen frequencies by the user, allowing any set of devices to be synchronized with one another. Though each village also has a few sets of specially made comm devices built to operate on "secure" frequencies, these are not typically given to hunters on missions. Commonly used in missions that require precise coordination or infiltration, these always receive, and are touch-activated to broadcast. They have a range of half a mile. Be aware that while these are generally a secure means of communication, it's (theoretically) possible for enemies to find your frequency if you're making continual use of the comms, they know you're using them, and they're actively trying to do so. If you suffer a Major or greater Head wound while wearing a comm device, it breaks as a result of the damage. A comm device broken this way is too badly damaged to be repaired, and will need to be replaced. Cost: 12.5k Ryo

title: Telescope
text: A small pocket telescope, which telescopes out from two inches to close to six. It allows you to effectively see what's going on up to a mile away, and read reasonably sized text (assuming you have clear line of sight) up to half a mile away. Mechanically, this means that any Awareness rolls at a distance up to its maximum (to, say, see when a guard leaves his post) have no penalty. Cost: 10k Ryo

title: Shinobi Pharmaceuticals
text: A soldier pill is not the only thing a modern hunters can swallow before doing something regrettable. Licensed clinics, field medics, black-market chemists, and village quartermasters sell combat pharmaceuticals across the hunters world. Drugs are ordinary purchasable gear. You do not need a clan, Talent, or medical background to use one. The trade-off is simple: the body gets the bill later.

title: Drug Rules
text: Taking a pill or using a prepared vial on yourself is Speed 6. Injecting an unwilling creature requires an appropriate Melee Attack or Grapple permission. Unless stated otherwise, a Drug lasts 30 IC. The same Drug does not stack with itself. Taking another dose while the same Drug is active resets its duration but doubles the listed Crash. Every further redose adds another copy of the Crash and immediately forces a Resistance TN 15 + 5 per previous redose; failure advances Fatigue by 1. A Crash begins when the Drug ends and lasts for the same duration as the Drug unless stated otherwise. Drugs are chemicals for interactions with Medical Jutsu, poison analysis, and effects that explicitly accelerate or purge chemicals. Redline Cost: 2,000 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Reduce damage you take by 10% for Wounding purposes. Crash: damage you take counts as 10% higher for Wounding. Quickstep Cost: 1,000 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Increase Movement by 10%. Crash: reduce Movement by 10%. Iron Lung Cost: 1,500 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Treat your Stamina penalty as 1 lower for checks and costs. Crash: increase Stamina penalty by 1. Blue Focus Cost: 1,500 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Treat your Chakra penalty as 1 lower for checks and costs. Crash: increase Chakra penalty by 1. Morphine Field Ampoule Cost: 3,000 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Ignore the penalties of one Minor or Major Wound in a chosen location. Gain Paralysis 2 while active. Crash: the suppressed Wound returns normally and you gain Stun 4. Amphetamine Combat Dose Cost: 5,000 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Treat your Fatigue category as 1 lower for thresholds and access, but retain the actual penalties of your real Fatigue. Crash: increase both Stamina and Chakra penalties by 5. Ketamine Counter-Gen Dose Cost: 4,000 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Roll 2d20 and take the higher for Genjutsu Defense. Crash: Visibility 2 and -2 Awareness for 30 IC. Diethylamide Reflex Dose Cost: 7,500 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Reduce the Final Speed of your Actions and Interrupts by 2, respecting normal minimums. While active, after every Action or Interrupt you take unreducible HP damage equal to 3 × that action's Base Speed. Crash: Stun 8 and advance Fatigue by 1. Combat Steroid Cost: 3,500 Ryo Duration: 30 IC Gain +10 STR, AGI, and DEX for derived calculations. Crash: suffer -20 STR, AGI, and DEX for the same duration. Attributes cannot fall below 1. Kotarō Extract Cost: 6,000 Ryo - Rare Duration: 30 IC Treat both Stamina and Chakra penalties as 1 lower and gain +3 Resistance against Poison. Crash: increase both penalties by 2. A character without Kodon metabolism also suffers Stun 5.

title: Exploding Tags
text: Rectangular slips of paper inscribed with special seals, centered around the kanji for "explode". They're infused with chakra, but normally inert. A tag can be "primed" by focusing a small amount of chakra into them, at which point they can stick to most surfaces (like walls, or the underside of bridges; even unsuspecting people) and will detonate on their own after some time. Fire will not cause tags to explode, nor will they explode in a "chain reaction". A tag that is blown up or burnt, even a primed one, is just destroyed. Tags are destroyed if they receive any damage before exploding. Tags do 5+5d10!>5 damage, in Area 10. If multiple tags are set off on the same IC (and someone is hit by them all), the damage is increased by 2+1d10!>5 per tag. Exploding Tags inflict Energy wounds. When detonated, tags count as a Speed 8+2 per tags attack for the purpose of valid interrupts that cannot be reduced. They cannot be dodged and are defended as if they were a B rank Area Katon jutsu. There are many ways to Prime a Tag, as described below. Tags are tied to their primer, hence no one but the person using the Tag can use the Detonation options. The last application of any of the below options overrides any previous application.

title: Contact Detonation
text: This means priming the Tag while you are holding it or touching it. Chakra: 5 Speed: 10 Prerequisite: Stray. Contact detonation is taught during Corps training. Effect: You can set the Detonation time between 10 IC and (10+Chakra Control Ranks) IC.

title: Remote Detonation
text: This is the safe approach at Detonating Exploding Tags. By focusing the Chakra from a distance, you can Prime a tag from a few yards away. Chakra: 10+3X Speed: 12 Seal Speed: 4+2X Range CHA/10 yards Prerequisites: Trailhand, or 10 Ranks in Chakra Control Effect: X is the number of Tags. You can set the Detonation time between 10 IC and (10+Chakra Control Ranks) IC.

title: Instant Remote/Triggered:
text: This is the most advanced form of Tag Detonation. You can instantly set off a Tag within your range or you can set up a condition for the detonation that is independent of the time elapsed. Chakra: 10+Y Speed: 12 Seal Speed: 6 Range CHA/10 yards Prerequisite: Huntsman, or 20 Ranks in Chakra Control. Effect: Y is distance to the Tag in yards. You can set the Detonation time between 0 IC and (10+Chakra Control Ranks) IC or On Trigger. The Trigger is a Distance between 0 and CHA/10 yards, whenever someone enters this radius, the Tag instantly detonates. Other than placing a Tag by hand, there are two other ways to use them: Attaching to a Weapon: As part of a ranged attack, multi-throw or jutsu that uses ranged weapons, you can add a Chakra 10 cost (or +10 if it already had one), Seal Speed 6 (or +6) and Speed +5 to the attack in order to attach 1 Tag to the attack. Whether it hits or misses, the Tagged weapon always ends up at the position of the target. It will Detonate 15 IC after the attack resolves (unless a new Detonation application is used before it explodes). Attaching after Failed defense: Against any type of Melee Attack that hits you, you can perform a Spd 1 Interrupt (after resolving the attack, but before advancing IC) to attach 1 Tag to your attacker (in the relevant part of their body or weapon). Anyone who has a Tag attached to them in this manner rolls the higher of Awareness or Survival vs the one who attached the Tag’s Espionage or Stealth whichever is higher, on a success, they realise the Tag is attached and immediately detach it, leaving it at the position that the attack took place. If this check fails, the attacker notices the Tag too late and it then requires a Spd 5 action to remove (removed Tags are dropped at the location they were removed, they cannot be thrown or reattached to something else). If a Tag explodes while still attached to someone, they cannot defend against it. Blocking does work against attached Tags, however. Requires: Stray Rank Cost: 2,500 Ryo

title: Exploding Tag, Type 2
text: Type 2 tags are issued to Trailhands trained to handle stronger explosives. Type 2 tags function identically to regular exploding tags in most regards, though they deal 10d10.open(5) damage and have an Area of 20. Additionally, they deal double damage to inanimate objects (such as walls, including jutsu based defenses). Requires: Trailhand Rank Cost: 7,500 Ryo

title: Exploding Tag, Type 3
text: The end-all and be-all of 'mundane' explosives, reserved for Huntsman simply because of how difficult they are to produce, which is in turn reflected in how troublesome they are to get ahold of. Type 3, like Type 2, deal double damage to inanimate objects. They deal 20d10.open(5) damage, and have an Area of 30. Requires: Huntsman Rank Cost: 15,000 Ryo FIELD ARMORY — WEAPON CATALOGUE Browse illustrated ready-made melee weapons, bows, crossbows, launchers, kunai and ammunition. Each weapon links back to its full equipment rules. EXPLORE WEAPONS ↗

title: Hunting
text: CORE RULES / FIELD REFERENCE Hunting Track dangerous beasts, learn how they fight, prepare for the encounter, then bring them down—or bring them home alive. 01 Up to 4 Hunters 02 Downtime Activity 03 Shared Intel 04 Kill or Capture Starting a Hunt Hunt Actions Intel Monster Tribes Combat Classes Start the Hunt Hunt Combat Clinging Injury & Part Breaks Exertion Capture A Hunt is a special Downtime activity in which a small team tracks, studies, prepares for, and ultimately confronts a dangerous creature. The work your Team does before the fight can determine what you know, what advantages you begin with, and whether you are ready for what the monster can do. 01 Find It Track the target and learn its territory. 02 Learn It Research its nature, habits and abilities. 03 Prepare Build the tools and advantages you need. 04 Confront It Choose when the Team knows enough to strike. 05 Finish It Kill, capture, drive off, or neutralise it. ---

title: Starting a Hunt
text: Up to 4 players may form a Hunting Team and take part in the same Hunt. You may only be part of one active Hunt at a time. Once the Hunt begins, the Team may spend Downtime gathering information and making preparations before choosing to confront the target. The Team does not have to complete every possible investigation before starting the encounter: deciding when you know enough is part of the Hunt. Intel and preparations gained during a Hunt belong to that Hunt and are available to the Hunting Team. 4 Maximum Team Size. A Hunting Team can contain up to four players, and all Intel and Preparation earned for that Hunt is shared by the Team. ---

title: Hunt Actions
text: While participating in an active Hunt, you gain access to special Hunt Actions. Each Hunt Action costs 1 Downtime Slot. Choose the skill listed in the monster’s Hunt profile or Lore for every Hunt roll. Lore is always a valid alternative, including for Track, Research, Study Weakness and Prepare. Different creatures are found, understood, and prepared for in different ways, so each monster may call for different Skills or approaches. Hunt Action · 1 Downtime Track Follow trails, chakra residue, disturbed terrain, witnesses, feeding grounds, discarded remains, or other signs of the creature. Success → Tracks Intel Learn where the creature is, where it travels, how it moves through its territory, and how best to approach it. Hunt Action · 1 Downtime Research Study old records, field reports, remains, sightings, survivors, folklore, previous encounters, or similar sources. Success → Nature Intel Learn what kind of creature you are dealing with, how it behaves, and what it may be capable of. Hunt Action · 1 Downtime Study Weakness Investigate the creature's anatomy, habits, injuries, feeding patterns, shed material, chakra, or previous fights in search of exploitable vulnerabilities. This will often require some Nature Intel first. Success → Weakness Intel Learn how to create openings, disable important parts, avoid dangerous abilities, or exploit a major vulnerability. Hunt Action · 1 Downtime Prepare Create or arrange something specifically intended to help against the target: traps, bait, antidotes, seals, special ammunition, environmental preparations, escape routes, or similar measures. Success → +1 Preparation · Max 3 Preparation must represent something established before the encounter; it is not undefined equipment that becomes whatever the Team needs later. ---

title: Intel
text: Intel is shared across the whole Hunting Team. There are three categories: 01 Tracks Where the monster is, how it moves through its territory, and how the Team can approach it. 02 Nature What the monster is, how it behaves, its broad abilities, tribe, and fighting tendencies. 03 Weakness What can be exploited, broken, avoided, interrupted, or turned against the creature. Each category has 3 levels. 1 Rumors Basic information, signs, hearsay and early clues. 2 Reliable Dependable information with useful mechanical value. 3 Hunter's Insight Critical information and an encounter advantage. Gaining a higher level includes the information from lower levels. The exact information revealed depends on the monster being hunted. Typical Hunter's Insight benefits include Tracks 3 avoiding an ambush or choosing your starting position, Nature 3 identifying a Signature Ability before it is used, and Weakness 3 revealing how to trigger or exploit a major weakness.

title: Failed Hunt Actions
text: A failed Hunt Action may cause a Complication. The creature might relocate, realise it is being hunted, supplies may be lost, terrain may worsen, or another threat may become involved. A failure does not automatically end the Hunt. It means the situation has become more difficult, urgent, or dangerous. ---

title: Monster Tribes
text: Tribe describes a monster's broad body-plan and hunting identity. It tells you the kind of creature you are dealing with before you know every individual ability. Tribe is not a complete stat block: mutations, elements, individual anatomy and Combat Class can make two monsters from the same Tribe behave very differently. Fang Jackal · Hound · Hyena · Lynx · Panther Pursuit predators built around scent, speed and isolated prey. Fang monsters want the Hunt stretched out: one hunter falls behind, a route opens, and the creature commits hard. Skirmisher Ambusher Bruiser Hunter read: stay grouped, deny long approaches, and be wary when its tracks begin circling the weakest trail. Colossus Boar · Bear · Ape · Gorilla · Elk Massive terrestrial monsters that win space through weight, momentum and heavy limbs. Their attacks are often obvious, committed and extremely dangerous once they begin moving. Bruiser Tank Grappler Hunter read: bait commitment, attack supporting limbs, and do not let the creature dictate the centre of the battlefield. Chitin Mantis · Beetle · Scorpion · Crab Armoured monsters with layered shells, jointed natural weapons and a tendency to make terrain part of the kill. Chitin creatures are at their strongest when you fight exactly where they want you. Grappler Tank Controller Hunter read: attack joints, separate them from prepared ground, and treat discarded shell or a suspiciously narrow lane as a warning. Sky Roc · Moth Winged predators that control height and approach angles. Sky monsters decide when contact happens, attacking from places ordinary hunters cannot easily threaten. Skirmisher Artillery Controller Hunter read: break line of sight, watch high ledges for feathers or scales, and breaking the wings can change the entire Hunt. Coil Serpent · Wyrm Long-bodied monsters that fight through flexible reach, constriction and restricted routes. A Coil can turn its own body into a wall, divide a Team, and disappear through spaces hunters cannot follow. Grappler Ambusher Artillery Hunter read: avoid narrow lanes, force it to uncoil, and investigate long furrows that vanish beneath rubble or earth. Mire Salamander · Crocodile · Tortoise Durable amphibious monsters that use water margins to wear prey down. Mire creatures are patient, difficult to dislodge and dangerous when they can drag a fight into their preferred terrain. Tank Grappler Controller Hunter read: fight from firm ground, deny access to water where possible, and take drag marks ending at opaque water seriously. Colony Rat-King · Locust Cloud · Leech Colony A distributed creature coordinated around one or more vulnerable concentrations. A Colony may look like many enemies, but its threat comes from the body acting as a single organised whole. Swarm Controller Ambusher Hunter read: use area pressure, identify the coordinating core, and follow repeated small trails back toward the place where they converge. ---

title: Combat Classes
text: Tribe tells you what a monster is. Combat Class tells you how it prefers to fight. A Combat Class is a tactical identity, not a restriction. A monster can still possess attacks outside its speciality, but its Class tells you what kind of pressure it is best at creating and what behaviour you should expect once the fight develops. BR Bruiser Close-range pressure, force and direct threat. Bruisers pick a target, make it move, and punish anyone who lets them stay in striking distance. Read: expect commitment and heavy contact; make it spend movement and punish overextension. SK Skirmisher Mobility, angles and repeated hit-and-run attacks. Skirmishers want a clear escape route and become much less comfortable when pinned into a bad position. Read: cut off exits, threaten multiple angles, and do not chase blindly. CT Controller Space denial, separation and battlefield manipulation. Controllers want to split hunters, close routes or make parts of the battlefield unsafe before committing. Read: protect formation and recognise that the terrain may be the real attack. AR Artillery Long sightlines and powerful ranged pressure. Artillery monsters prefer distance, obstacles and time to line up attacks rather than prolonged close combat. Read: break sightlines, break line of sight, and force the fight into ranges where its best attacks are awkward. AM Ambusher Concealment, sudden bursts and disengagement. Ambushers attack from advantage, then break contact rather than trading blows on equal terms. Read: deny hiding places, watch likely approach routes, and expect it to disappear after striking. GR Grappler Isolation, restraint and forced movement. Grapplers catch one target and turn the encounter into a rescue problem for everybody else. Read: preserve escape tools, stay within support range, and react quickly when somebody is seized or dragged away. TK Tank Area holding, durability and objective protection. Tanks are comfortable sitting on a choke point, nest, resource or other position that forces hunters to come through them. Read: do not waste the entire Hunt attacking the strongest angle; displace it, flank it, or attack what it is protecting. SW Swarm Distributed pressure from a mass of smaller bodies. A Swarm may fill a large area and threaten several hunters at once while still resolving as a single monster actor. Read: area effects and control matter; spreading the mass does not necessarily mean you have split it into separate enemies. Reading a Hunt Profile Tribe + Class is your first tactical shorthand. A Colossus Grappler is a very different problem from a Colossus Tank; a Fang Ambusher hunts differently from a Fang Bruiser. Nature Intel can reveal enough about a target to turn those labels into useful expectations before every individual technique is known. ---

title: Starting the Encounter
text: The Team may choose to confront the target at any time. When the Team starts the final encounter, every participating player spends 1 Downtime Slot. Investigation ends and the Hunt becomes a played encounter using the monster's Hunt rules. Any Intel and Preparation the Team has earned carries into that encounter. A Hunt is completed when the target is killed, captured, driven away, or otherwise neutralised in a way that resolves the Hunt. Everyone who participates in the final encounter counts as having Completed a Hunt for weekly Downtime rewards. Rare creatures may also provide unique materials, crafting components, trophies, or other rewards. ---

title: Wild Hunt Combat
text: Some Hunt targets are too large, resilient, or dangerous to fight like ordinary enemies. These creatures use additional Wild Hunt rules during their encounter. 01 Injury Lasting deterioration as damage pushes the monster through major stages. 02 Open Wounds Short-lived opportunities to attack exposed anatomy. 03 Broken Parts Lasting damage that removes or weakens specific capabilities. 04 Exertion How hard the creature has pushed itself and how close it is to collapse. Some large monsters can also be Clung to, allowing hunters to climb across their bodies to reach otherwise difficult locations. Not every Hunt target uses every rule on this page; its profile tells you what applies. ---

title: Clinging
text: Clinging is a special Grapple state used when you attach yourself to part of a large creature instead of attempting to wrestle its entire body. It uses the normal Grapple Control system. A climbable monster has connected locations, such as Forelegs ↔ Shoulders ↔ Back ↔ Head, with another connection such as Back ↔ Tail. These locations determine access and reach; they do not have separate Vitality totals. Getting On Use the normal Grab action and declare that you are attempting to Cling to a reachable location. On a successful Grab, determine Control normally. Each climber has their own Control contest and Control is never pooled. While Clinging - You move with the creature whenever it moves. - Its Movement is not halved merely because you are attached. - It does not suffer ordinary Clinch penalties merely because you are attached. - You suffer the Clinch's +2 Base Speed to Dodge and Parry interrupts. - You must keep at least one hand free to maintain your grip. - Your other hand, legs, weapons and techniques can be used if you meet their requirements. - Ordinary movement by the creature does not force additional grip checks. - Dodging away, teleporting away, being thrown off, or otherwise leaving the creature ends your Cling. Normal Grapple Control losses still apply to your own actions, damage, Wounds and relevant conditions. The creature attacking somebody else does not make it lose Control against you. Secure Grip Speed 5 Stamina 5 Control 0 Make Grapple Offense against Grapple Defense. On success, shift 3 Control toward yourself. Grip Fighting's Reposition Link may be used. Clamber Speed 6 Stamina 8 Control 2 Move to an adjacent Climbable Location. You must have at least 2 Control in your favour before paying the cost. Release Speed 0 End the Cling voluntarily on your action. Resolve resulting movement or falling normally. Attacking While Clinging You may attack normally while Clinging, including Pummel and other techniques you can physically perform. Attacking affects Grapple Control normally. When making a Called Shot against the body location you occupy, reduce its base Accuracy penalty from −4 to −2. Apply other Called Shot reductions afterward, to a minimum of 0. Shake Off Speed: 8 Exertion: +1 The creature makes Grapple Offense against each climber's Grapple Defense separately. On success, shift 3 Control toward the creature. If this leaves it with at least 5 Control against you, you are thrown off. Some creatures possess additional anti-climber abilities such as rolling, scraping against terrain, diving, taking flight, igniting their body, or attacking specific locations. Takedowns Against Giant Creatures Clinging to a giant creature does not mean you can wrestle its entire body. Normal Takedowns, Pins and similar whole-body Grapple effects only work when the creature's rules or current situation make them possible, such as while Toppled or appropriately restrained. --- Armor and armored parts use Armor Categories. Record Dense, Layered or Shaped beside each protected location. These matchups modify protection and part damage; unrelated monster DR is unchanged.

title: Injury, Open Wounds, and Broken Parts
text: Wild Hunt Monsters become visibly worse as a Hunt continues. Damage still matters normally, but major accumulated damage pushes the creature through Injury Gates. Injury Conditions Condition What changes ------ Healthy Full capabilities. Bloodied The creature has suffered visible damage. Wounded Heavy actions generate +1 additional Exertion. Injured Movement is reduced by 20%. Badly Injured Exertion cannot recover below 4. Critical Exertion cannot recover below 6 and it can become Capture-Ready. Felled It can no longer continue fighting. These effects are cumulative. A sufficiently powerful attack may push a creature through more than one stage at once, and individual creatures may gain additional behaviours at particular stages. Open Wounds Crossing an Injury Gate can create an Open Wound on the location struck. Particularly effective targeted attacks can also open one without crossing a Gate. 20 IC Open Wound Duration +25% Final Damage When Exploited An Open Wound represents cracked armour, exposed muscle, damaged organs, torn tissue or another temporary vulnerability. Closing means the easy opening has passed, not that the injury healed. Only targeted attacks against that location gain the damage bonus. Each location can have only one Open Wound at a time, and further hits do not refresh its duration. Breaking Parts Repeatedly exploiting an Open Wound can Break that body part before the opportunity closes. The creature's profile tells you what happens when a particular part is Broken once that information becomes known. Broken Part Possible Effect ------ Foreleg A charge or movement option becomes unavailable. Wing The creature can no longer fly. Horn A horn attack is weakened or lost. Tail A tail attack loses Reach or becomes unavailable. Armour Plate Protection over that location is reduced or removed. Chakra Organ An associated elemental ability becomes more exhausting to use. A Broken part stays Broken for the rest of the Hunt and cannot be repeatedly broken for additional effects or rewards. Area attacks do not automatically exploit every Open Wound or break every part they overlap. ---

title: Exertion
text: Wild Hunt Monsters use Exertion to represent how hard they are pushing themselves. Exertion ranges from 0 to 10. Exertion State Effect ---:------ 0–1 Energetic No penalty. 2–3 Worked Visible effort; no numerical penalty. 4–5 Winded −1 Accuracy and defensive rolls. 6–7 Tired −2 Accuracy and defensive rolls; −20% Movement. 8–9 Exhausted −3 Accuracy and defensive rolls; −40% Movement; cannot use Heavy actions. 10 Spent Collapses for 10 IC. Use only the penalties from the current state. Injury and Exertion Movement reductions stack to a maximum reduction of 60%. Exertion is gained after an action resolves. Gaining Exertion Action Exertion ------: Ordinary movement, observation, waiting, standard defenses 0 Basic attack, Shake Off, ordinary offensive technique +1 Heavy attack, major breath, massive charge, powerful area attack +2 Exceptional signature technique +3, when specifically listed An attack generates Exertion whether it succeeds or fails. Ordinary defensive interrupts do not normally generate Exertion. Catch Breath Speed: 10 Delay: 10 When the Delay completes, remove 3 Exertion, never below the minimum imposed by Injury. Taking damage, being forcibly moved, performing another action, or performing an interrupt before completion spoils the recovery. The creature may Abort normally. Spent At 10 Exertion, the creature immediately collapses and becomes Prone for 10 IC. It cannot take non-interrupt actions, but may use physically possible defenses with its Exhausted penalties. Additional Exertion cannot extend the collapse. At the end, reduce Exertion to 7, or to its Injury minimum if higher. It must then stand normally. Effects That Cause Fatigue If one of your abilities would directly advance a Wild Hunt Monster's Fatigue, it instead adds 2 Exertion per Fatigue level. Other Stamina or Chakra Exhaustion interactions work as described by the Hunt encounter or ability, and ordinary statuses do not disappear simply because an Exertion threshold is crossed. ---

title: Capture
text: Weakening a monster is not enough to capture it. A successful capture requires the Team to injure it, exhaust it, restrain it, and secure the opportunity before it recovers or escapes. 01 Push it to Critical 02 Reach 8–10 Exertion 03 Apply a valid restraint 04 Complete Secure Capture Capture-Ready A Wild Hunt Monster becomes Capture-Ready while it is both Critical and Exhausted or Spent at 8–10 Exertion. Capture-Ready creatures should be visibly struggling. You do not need to guess a hidden Vitality percentage to know whether capture is possible. Restraining the Monster The monster must be held by an appropriate restraint: a specialised trap, binding, sealing technique, monster-specific device, or another effect capable of containing that creature. Ordinary Immobilization is not automatically sufficient, and merely Clinging to the monster does not restrain it for capture. Secure Capture Speed: 10 Delay: 10 Requires a Capture-Ready monster, an appropriate restraint currently holding it, and the necessary sedative, suppression seal or other established capture method within reach. When the Delay completes, the creature is captured if it is still both Capture-Ready and restrained. If either condition stops being true, the attempt fails. You may Abort normally. Capture Is Not Taming Capturing a creature does not make it friendly, loyal or usable as a companion. Capture determines whether it is taken alive; later acquisition, taming and training follow the normal Monster Taming rules. ---

title: The Hunt Loop
text: Before the Encounter Track it. Find the creature and learn its territory. Research it. Discover its Tribe, habits and likely capabilities. Study it. Learn what can be exploited. Prepare. Build the traps, tools, routes and countermeasures you want available. Choose when to strike. More information costs more Downtime; starting sooner means accepting more unknowns. During the Encounter Read its Class. Recognise the kind of pressure the monster is trying to create. Injure it. Push it through its Injury stages. Create openings. Target important locations and watch for Open Wounds. Exploit them. Coordinate attacks before those openings close. Break important parts. Remove dangerous attacks, mobility, armour or other capabilities. Wear it down. Force Exertion and prevent it from Catching Breath. Climb when necessary. Reach locations that cannot safely be attacked from the ground. Choose the ending. Fell it, drive it away, or hold it at Critical long enough to capture it.

title: Bow Bukijutsu
text: ← ALL JUTSU TYPES

title: Bow Bukijutsu
text: Bow techniques reward patience and a clear sightline. Mark your quarry, pin its movement and choose the shot that brings it down.

title: Shirushi no Ya - Marking Shot
text: E-Rank The first arrow is used to establish a sightline rather than chase immediate damage. Rank: E Stamina: +3 Damage: +max(2, floor(STR/15))dS Speed: -1 Accuracy: +1 Tags: Chain 1, Bow, Attack Effects: Bow only. On a full hit, Mark the target until your Chain against it ends. Your next Bow Chain 2 against it gains +Athletics/5 Accuracy, increased by 1 if it voluntarily moved after being Marked. That Attack consumes the Mark. A new Mark replaces your previous one.

title: Nuidome no Ya - Pinning Shot
text: E-Rank The arrow catches clothing or equipment, hampering the target’s movement. Rank: E Stamina: +3 Damage: +max(1, floor(STR/15))dS Speed: +0 Special: Immobilization 2 Tags: Chain 1, Bow, Attack Effects: Bow only. Resolve Immobilization with severity equal to the greater of 2 or Athletics/10, maximum 6. It ends when the target removes the arrow with a Speed 3 Utility Action.

title: Shahō - Angle Shot
text: E-Rank You send the arrow toward an exposed angle in the defender’s guard. Rank: E Stamina: +5 Damage: +max(3, floor(STR/15))dS Speed: +2 Tags: Chain 2, Bow, Attack Effects: If the target uses the same broad Defense it used against your Chain 1, that Defense takes −Athletics/5.

title: Tasha - Multiple Shot
text: E-Rank The bow is used as a platform for several distinct releases in one action. Rank: E Stamina: +8 Speed: +5 Damage: +max(2, floor(STR/15))dS Tags: Chain 3, Bow, Attack Effects: Fire two arrows. Each uses the weapon dice plus this technique’s Damage dice; divide Speed×PDB evenly between them. Declare targets and roll Accuracy separately. Both may target your chained creature, or one may target a held weapon or worn armor piece on it using normal Called Shot penalties, item defenses and structural damage rules. Combine successful hits on the creature for Wounding only; item damage does not also damage its wielder.

title: Hayatsugae - Quick Nock
text: E-Rank You nock the next arrow in the same motion that lowers the bow, keeping the string, grip, and sightline ready before the target sees a reset. Rank: E Stamina: 3 Speed: 2 Tags: Chain X, Bow, Utility Effects: Nock an arrow. Your next Bow Chain attack has -2 Speed, minimum Base Speed 3.

title: Issei Shageki - Volley
text: E-Rank A high arc of arrows claims an area instead of one target, filling the space with descending shots and forcing everyone beneath it to find an answer at once. Rank: E Stamina: 7 Speed: 10 Area: 4 at a point within Bow Range Damage: +floor(STR/15)dS Tags: Bukijutsu, Bow, Attack Effects: Fire a volley; attack all chosen creatures in Area. Each target takes weapon damage with only 50% of Speed×PDB.

title: Futatsuya - Twin Arrow
text: D-Rank Two arrows share one draw and release timing but remain separate attacks. Rank: D Stamina: +8 Speed: +4 Damage: +floor(STR/10)dS Tags: Chain 2, Bow, Attack Effects: Fire two arrows at the chained target, each at 60% Final Damage. Roll Accuracy separately; the defender declares one legal defensive method, pays its cost and Speed once, and rolls it separately against each arrow. If either fully hits and you know Marking Shot, establish or refresh your Bow Mark. Resolve Chain progression once; Partial Defense applies to each hit normally.

title: Seimitsu Shageki - Precision Shot
text: D-Rank The final arrow is chosen for penetration and wound placement. Rank: D Stamina: +11 Damage: +max(6, floor(STR/10))dS Speed: +5 Tags: Chain 3, Bow, Attack Effects: Gain +30% Wounding. Reduce the target armor’s Absorption and flat DR by 50% for this Attack, after its damage-type matchup. If the target has your Bow Mark, consume it when declaring to gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy.

title: Kiriya - Cutting Arrow
text: D-Rank An arrow is fired at another projectile rather than the attacker. Rank: D Stamina: 6 Speed: 3 Tags: Chain X, Bow, Utility, Interrupt Effects: Consume an arrow to Parry a targeted Ranged Taijutsu or Projectile Attack with +Athletics/5. This does not defend against AoEs.

title: Hiki Shibori - Held Draw
text: D-Rank The bow is held in a disciplined firing posture, the sightline settling more firmly each moment the target remains predictable. Rank: D Stamina: 9 Upkeep: 2 Speed: 7 Tags: Bukijutsu, Bow, Utility Effects: While maintained, Bow attacks gain +Athletics/5 Accuracy against targets that have not moved since your last action. If you move for any reason, you lose this bonus until your next action.

title: Itotōshi - Threaded Shot
text: C-Rank You place the arrow directly through one target’s line and keep enough force behind it to threaten the body standing behind them. Rank: C Stamina: +8 Damage: +max(4, floor(STR/7))dS Speed: +2 Accuracy: +1 Tags: Chain 1, Bow, Attack Effects: On a full hit, you may also attack one creature directly behind the target within the bow’s remaining Range for 60% Final Damage, using the same Accuracy result. It defends separately. The secondary hit cannot establish or advance Chain.

title: Ugoki Hiki - Mobile Draw
text: C-Rank The draw is maintained through movement so the user can relocate without throwing away the shot, keeping shoulders, string, and target line stable while the feet change position. Rank: C Stamina: +7 Speed: +0 Tags: Link, Bow, Attack, Movement Effects: Link to a Bow Attack. Move with that Attack using its full final Speed, in any legal direction. The movement does not remove Held Draw’s benefit for this Attack. If the target Dodges, double its Defense Speed when advancing its next action; Interrupt validity is unchanged. Bow only.

title: Kyōka no Ya - Reinforced Arrow
text: C-Rank Chakra is fed into the ammunition as it leaves the bow, hardening the arrow’s flight and edge so it can bite cleanly into both flesh and chakra-made structures. Rank: C Chakra: 16 Upkeep: 3 Speed: 8 Tags: Bukijutsu, Bow, Utility Effects: Ammunition fired from one bow counts as chakra-enhanced, gains +20% Wounding, and may damage chakra constructs normally.

title: Ikari no Ya - Anchor Shot
text: B-Rank The arrow is driven through gear or flesh and fixed into nearby terrain, turning a hit into a hard limit on where the target can go. Rank: B Stamina: +14 Damage: +max(6, floor(STR/5))dS Speed: +4 Tags: Chain 2, Bow, Attack Effects: On a full hit, resolve Immobilization with severity equal to the greater of 3 or Athletics/10, maximum 6. If there is solid terrain within the target’s Reach, you may instead anchor it there; it cannot voluntarily move away until it removes the arrow as a Speed 5 Utility Action or destroys the anchor. The ordinary Immobilization ends when the target removes the arrow with that same Action.

title: Shasen - Sightline
text: B-Rank You study the wind, the sightline and the target’s movement before drawing. Rank: B Stamina: 9 Speed: 4 Tags: Chain X, Bow, Utility Effects: Make a Search with +Athletics/5 Awareness. Your next Bow Attack against a located target ignores Visibility penalties and gains +50% Range if it is your next non-Interrupt Action. The projectile still requires a clear path.

title: Tenraku no Ya - Skyfall Shot
text: A-Rank You send the arrow high above the target, then bring it down in a steep, plunging shot. Rank: A Stamina: +24 Damage: +max(12, floor(STR/3))dS Speed: +6 Tags: Bukijutsu, Bow, Attack Effects: Choose a clear arcing projectile path within Bow Range and ignore Visibility penalties against a creature you can locate. Gain +25% Final Damage and +30% Wounding. On a full hit, resolve Prone using Athletics against Resistance. This adds no Delay beyond the weapon’s normal Bukijutsu Delay.

title: Kariudo no Mihari - Hunter's Watch
text: A-Rank You settle into a firing lane and punish movement through it instead of waiting for a perfect stationary shot. Rank: A Stamina: 13 Upkeep: 4 Speed: 6 Tags: Utility, Self, Upkeep, Bukijutsu Effects: Choose a 90-degree arc within Bow Range. While maintained, when a creature voluntarily moves in that arc, you may make a Bow Basic Weapon Attack against it at full damage as an Offensive Interrupt. Pay that Basic Attack’s normal Stamina and final Speed. One movement Action can trigger one shot from you. The shot resolves at a point in its path that you can perceive and legally target. ← ALL JUTSU TYPES

title: Bukijutsu Rules
text: ← ALL JUTSU TYPES

title: Bukijutsu
text: Bukijutsu adds strength-scaled damage and weapon-specific effects to Basic Weapon Attacks. Use Chains to pressure a target and set up a finisher.

title: Learning Requirements
text: E-Rank Bukijutsu is universally available to player characters. E-Rank — Athletics -; Research -. D-Rank — Athletics 4; Research 5. C-Rank — Athletics 10; Research 12. B-Rank — Athletics 20; Research 22. A-Rank — Athletics 30; Research 32. B-Rank and A-Rank use the normal mentor rule. You must be taught the technique unless you exceed the relevant learning requirement by 50%, following the general Jutsu rules.

title: Buki Attacks
text: Unless a technique lists fixed Damage or Speed, an attacking Bukijutsu starts from the Basic Weapon Attack of the weapon being used and applies the modifiers printed in the technique. “dS” uses that weapon’s base damage die size. A weapon attack may only be modified or replaced by one Bukijutsu unless another technique explicitly has the Link tag. Chain tags are not Link tags. If your weapon has an innate delay, any Bukijutsu you cast gains a Delay equal to half your weapon’s delay. If a Bukijutsu calls for an attack roll, that means a 1d20 + your Accuracy - 10. When a technique refers to the same Defense, it means the same broad defensive action: Dodge, Parry, Block, Take the Hit, and so on. Different named Parry techniques are still Parry unless a technique specifically says otherwise. Bukijutsu use Move with an Attack normally unless a technique says otherwise. If a technique lets you use Move with an Attack in another direction, calculate the distance normally from half the Attack's final Speed. It changes the direction or timing of that movement; it does not create a second movement allowance. If you already spent some of your Move with an Attack distance before the strike, only the remainder is available afterward.

title: Scaling and effect timing
text: When these techniques use Athletics/5 for a roll bonus, penalty or extra weapon allowance, round down, with a minimum of 2 and maximum of 6. Other attribute divisions used for yards, status severity, Control or target counts round down and use their printed minimums and caps. Damage Bonus calculations retain the normal one-decimal rule. Reach and Range percentage increases use the weapon or technique's value before maintained Bukijutsu and setup bonuses. Calculate each increase from that same value; do not compound them. Final Damage and Wounding percentages use their normal system rules. PDB × Speed and percentage effects use the final Attack normally. A bonus for your next Chain Attack is consumed by that Attack and ends if that Chain ends. Other one-use benefits end when used or when the combat ends. Repeated applications of the same named effect do not stack. An Interrupt must explicitly allow AoE defense to Parry an AoE; such a Parry has no Partial Defense.

title: Rank-scaled weapon damage
text: Damaging Bukijutsu add weapon-sized dice that grow with STR. Their Damage line uses the greater of the technique’s printed floor and the following count: Rank Additional weapon dice --- --- E floor(STR/15)dS D floor(STR/10)dS C floor(STR/7)dS B floor(STR/5)dS A floor(STR/3)dS Add this dice package to the weapon’s normal dice, then add Damage Bonus × final Speed. The printed floor and STR count are alternatives, not two bonuses. These extra technique dice are not limited by the cap on Basic Unarmed dice. For techniques that resolve several weapon hits, include this dice package in each hit before applying that hit’s damage percentage or dividing damage as directed by the technique. A secondary hit copying an Attack’s Final Damage already includes the package; never add it again. Multi-Throw distributes one package across its projectiles per target, not one package per projectile. Techniques that divide damage among targets still do so. Links, non-damaging actions and counters expressly making a Basic Weapon Attack do not receive a separate rank dice package. Using several Links does not grant several packages. Defense-Speed multipliers from Bukijutsu do not stack; use the highest. Each named Bukijutsu Link can modify an Attack once; techniques requiring a setup or Chain still require it.

title: Specials and Status Rolls
text: Bukijutsu use the normal Special and Status Roll rules. If a Bukijutsu lists a status in its Special line, use Athletics for the Status Roll unless the technique says otherwise; the target rolls Resistance normally. Stun follows its normal rules and is not separately resisted. A Special attached to a damaging Attack only applies if the Attack still produces an effect after defenses and damage reduction, following the normal rules for statuses. Partial Success reduces a numeric Special in the same way it reduces the rest of the Attack's effects unless the technique says otherwise. Knockback: Bukijutsu that list Knockback are allowed to hit harder when the user wins the Status Roll decisively. After a successful Athletics vs Resistance Status Roll, increase the listed Knockback by 1 yard for every full 3 points the target failed by, to a maximum of double the listed Knockback. Apply Partial Success to the resulting Knockback normally. If a technique changes the direction of Knockback, it will say so. This still counts as Knockback and forced movement; it is not a separate Pull or Shift status.

title: Chain
text: Chain Value: A Chain is tracked against one target and has a value of 0, 1 or 2. It has no passive damage bonus. Chain 1 — Entry: May be used at Chain 0 or 1. On a hit, establish Chain 1 against that target. A successful Chain 1 during an existing Chain keeps the value at 1. Chain 2 — Pressure: Requires Chain 1 or 2 against that target. On a hit, set the Chain to 2. Further Chain 2 techniques may be used while at 2 and keep the value at 2. Chain 3 — Finisher: Requires Chain 2 against that target. The Chain ends after the technique resolves, hit or miss. A Chain 2 or Chain 3 Attack must include the chained target; extra targets do not provide additional Chain advances or Openings. Chain X — Utility: May be used at any Chain value, including 0. It never increases or decreases Chain value. Chain Window: A Chain ends if 20 IC pass without you using a Chain-tagged Bukijutsu or making a Basic Weapon Attack against the chained target. A Basic Weapon Attack refreshes the window but does not change Chain value. Chain X refreshes this window unless its own text says otherwise. Breaking a Chain: The Chain ends if you Wait, fully miss a Chain 2, become Stunned, lose access to the required weapon, use a non-Chain Attack against another target that is not Chain 1, or use a non-Chain non-Interrupt action other than a Basic Weapon Attack against the chained target. Ordinary movement, purely defensive Interrupts, and Bukijutsu Utility actions compatible with your weapon do not break Chain; unless they are Chain X, they do not refresh the Chain Window. No Repeat Acceleration: A Chain 2 never gains a stacking Speed reduction merely because a Chain 2 was used before it. Technique-specific repeat bonuses cannot reduce Speed unless they explicitly say so, and no repeat bonus may stack with itself. Repeat Debuffs: A temporary Accuracy, Defense, Parry, Dodge or similar numerical penalty caused by the same named Bukijutsu does not stack with itself unless the technique explicitly says otherwise. A new application refreshes or replaces the old one. Changing Weapons: Chain value belongs to the target, not the weapon. Changing or readying weapons must cost Speed 0 or be handled by Chain X; otherwise the equipment change breaks Chain. Cross-Class Finishers: To use a Chain 3 from a weapon class different from the class that began the Chain, at least one successful Chain 1 or Chain 2 since the Chain began must have used a weapon compatible with that Chain 3’s class. Dual counts as compatible only with the specific weapons actually used by that Dual attack. Finisher Weapon: A Chain 3 uses only the properties of the weapon used for that Chain 3. Damage, dual-hit percentages, wound riders, reach changes and similar benefits from earlier attacks do not carry into it unless the Chain 3 explicitly says they do.

title: Chain Openings
text: The first time you advance from Chain 1 to Chain 2 during a Chain, gain one Opening against that target. Repeating Chain 2, returning to Chain 1 or using a multi-hit Attack does not grant another Opening in that Chain. Before a later Attack against that target is rolled, spend the Opening on one of these benefits: - Precision: reduce one Called Shot Accuracy penalty by Athletics/5, minimum 0. - Control: gain +Athletics/5 on one Special Status Roll caused by that Attack. Declare which Special when spending the Opening. It does not increase Stun, skip a Resistance roll or improve a Genjutsu offense roll. - Assist: give one willing ally +Athletics/5 Accuracy on its declared Attack against that target instead of benefiting your own Attack. Use the Opening owner’s Athletics, rounded down with a minimum of 2 and maximum of 6. A benefit affects only the chained target, even in an AoE. Each Attack can receive one Opening benefit, including a Team Attack. Spend it before the affected roll; a miss does not refund it. You may spend Precision or Control on a non-Chain Attack of your own, then end the Chain normally. An ally can receive Assist without using Bukijutsu. Unspent Openings end when the Chain ends. A Chain 3 may use the Opening before ending the Chain, but neither generates a second Opening nor refunds a spent one.

title: Combining pressure effects
text: Apply only the highest Bukijutsu bonus to any one Accuracy, Defense or Special roll, and only the highest Bukijutsu penalty to any one roll. This includes stances, prepared effects, Links and Openings. Ordinary weapon statistics and non-Bukijutsu abilities follow their own stacking rules. Called Shot reductions granted by Bukijutsu likewise use the highest; other sources follow their own rules. Extra projectile allowances from Bukijutsu use the highest, not their sum. Speed multipliers from Bukijutsu use the strongest reduction or increase of each kind rather than compounding; normal Speed minimums still apply. A target can be forced to reroll its Defense once per Attack by weapon/Bukijutsu effects, including Weapon Mastery. A technique that makes a second strike against the same target cannot also force a Defense reroll against it. Multi-hit attacks retain their explicitly printed separate defenses; they do not generate additional Chain advances or Openings. A counterattack granted by Bukijutsu can be defended normally, but resolving that Defense cannot generate another counterattack.

title: Fan Bridge
text: Seamless Wind may carry one Fan-tagged Fuuton through an active Chain. The Fuuton remains Ninjutsu, never becomes Chain 1/2/3, receives no Bukijutsu damage or status riders, and does not refresh the Chain Window. Your Chain remains active. You can do this once per Chain.

title: Bukijutsu Stances
text: Stances are Self Upkeep Bukijutsu. Maintain only one at a time; activating another ends the first. Attacking, moving and defending do not end a Stance. Stances use normal Upkeep and Preparation rules, but do not receive effects restricted to Ninjutsu Upkeep. Bukijutsu Stances do not cost XP to learn and are automatically unlocked when you meet the relevant Bukijutsu rank requirements. Bukijutsu Stances cannot be chosen as Signature Moves unless another rule explicitly allows it.

text: C-Rank You circulate elemental chakra through your weapons, coating them in flame, stone, lightning or another nature you can use. Raiton - Disrupting Current Lightning races across the weapon in bright, jagged arcs. Shields and conventional guards offer little protection against a blade that reaches beyond its own steel. The weapon gains +3 Reach, and its Attacks cannot be Blocked. Advanced Elements Advanced elements require their corresponding Heritage or another source of access. Hyōton - Frozen Fang Crystalline ice spreads across the weapon, forming a razor-sharp surface that freezes whatever it cuts. A sufficiently deep wound can leave flesh and bone permanently encased in ice. Attacks gain +25% Wounding. When inflicting a Major or worse Wound, you may replace it with Hyōton's Permanent Freeze of the corresponding Severity. Mokuton - Rootbound Weapon Living wood coils around the weapon, growing thorns and twisting roots along its surface. Every successful strike sends those roots plunging into the surrounding ground, turning the battlefield into a tangled forest of hungry growth. On a full hit, create an Area 3 of Sea of Thorns 1 beneath the target, lasting 20 IC. Yōton - Volcanic Weapon Lava Release changes the weapon's substance according to its wielder's particular expression. Some weapons drip with molten stone, others harden like cement, while others bend and recoil like living rubber. Gain the effect matching your Volcanic Expression: - Magma: The weapon drips molten rock that erupts across the ground on impact. Damaging hits create an Area 3 of Magma 3 for 10 IC. - Quicklime: A coating of pale, reactive lime spreads from the weapon, hardening around anything it touches. Damaging hits inflict Quicklime Immobilization 3, increasing by 2 on subsequent hits, maximum 8. - Rubber: The weapon stretches and recoils with elastic force, launching enemies away or throwing its wielder out of danger. Attacks gain Knockback 5, redirectable by up to 90 degrees. After fully Parrying, you may move 3 yards without increasing IC. Shakuton - Withering Edge The weapon radiates a dry, suffocating heat. Rather than burning its victims, it steals the moisture from their bodies, leaving brittle flesh and withered wounds in its wake. The weapon ignores Armor Absorption and inflicts Dehydration 2 on damaging hits. Jiton - Magnetic Conduction Magnetic chakra circulates through the weapon, attracting loose fragments of metal and surrounding its surface with a faint electromagnetic hum. Each strike imparts a charge, allowing subsequent attacks to accelerate towards or repel their victims. Choose Positive or Negative polarity for each Attack. Damaging hits apply one Magnetize Charge of that polarity. Against an oppositely Charged target, reduce the Attack's Base Speed by 2 per existing Charge, retaining its original Speed for Damage calculations. Normal Speed minimums apply. Futton - Boiling Conduction Superheated steam hisses from the weapon's surface. The user may vent this pressure to propel themselves through combat or concentrate it into a corrosive coating capable of eating through armour. Gain the effect of your active Futton Mode: - Pressure: Damaging hits generate 1 Steam, maximum once per Action. After attacking, you may spend 1 Steam to move 6 yards without increasing IC. - Corrosion: Attacks ignore 25 percentage points of Armor Absorption and deal +25% Final Damage to Barriers. Bakuton - Detonating Edge Explosive chakra gathers along the weapon, erupting in a violent burst whenever it strikes. Even a glancing blow can release enough force to hurl an opponent backwards, while more precise strikes leave dangerous explosive marks behind. Weapon Attacks gain Blast 4 and count as Bakuton Melee Attacks for the purpose of placing Detonation Marks. Jinton - Particle Edge A thin, geometric boundary forms around the weapon, its surface shimmering as matter begins to lose cohesion. Rather than cutting through resistance, the weapon disassembles the chakra holding that resistance together. The weapon ignores 50% of the target's DR and deals double Final Damage against chakra-created Barriers and Constructs.

title: Chain Weapon Bukijutsu
text: Chain weapons catch limbs, drag enemies out of position and hold them at a distance.

title: Weapon Grapples
text: Chain Weapon Bukijutsu use the existing Grapple system rather than a separate restraint system. When a technique says it initiates a Weapon Grapple, the Chain weapon acts as the limbs maintaining the hold. The user is still the grappler for Grapple Offense, Grapple Defense, Control, Pressure, Grip Fighting and every other rule that modifies Grapples. Initiating the Grapple: If a Chain Bukijutsu says it initiates a Weapon Grapple, resolve its weapon Attack first. On the required hit, the target enters a Clinch with the Chain weapon as though it had been hit by Grab, except the Grapple may be established at the Chain weapon's Range. Determine starting Control using the normal opposing Grapple checks. This is not a second attack or Defense. Using Grapple Jutsu through the Chain: Chain Bukijutsu with Pummel, Trapping, Takedown, Ground Fighting, or Submission use those tags exactly as written in the normal Grapple rules. The Chain weapon supplies the limbs required to perform those techniques, so these Bukijutsu ignore the normal requirement that all four of the user's limbs be free. A Chain weapon actively maintaining a Weapon Grapple can also deliver the qualifying ordinary techniques listed under Weapon-Assisted Grapple Taijutsu. Ordinary Grapple jutsu do not gain range simply because you are holding a Chain weapon; the Weapon Grapple and the technique's required hold must already be established. Remote Clinch: The target suffers the normal effects of a Clinch. The wielder does not suffer the Clinch's Dodge/Parry, movement, Ignite-transfer or Stealth restrictions solely because the Chain is holding the target at range. The wielder still loses Control normally for actions they take while maintaining the Grapple. The target may use Break Clinch and other legal escape effects against the wielder's normal Grapple values. Weapon Pin: When a Chain Bukijutsu successfully uses Takedown, the target becomes Pinned by the Chain. The target suffers the normal effects of a Pin, including the normal escape rules, but the wielder does not become Prone and does not have their Speed reduced to 0 simply because the weapon is maintaining the Pin. Ground Fighting and Submission techniques delivered by Chain Bukijutsu function normally from this state. Occupied Weapon: A Chain weapon maintaining a Weapon Grapple is occupied. It may only make attacks or use techniques that explicitly function during that Weapon Grapple. Releasing, losing, destroying, or using that same Chain weapon to establish a different Weapon Grapple ends the first. Range and Movement: A Weapon Grapple does not cause the wielder and target to automatically move together as a normal Clinch does. The target cannot voluntarily end an Action farther from the wielder or current anchor than the Chain weapon's Range allows. If either participant is moved so the Chain can no longer reach, the Weapon Grapple ends unless a technique says otherwise.
