title: Capabilities
text: Capabilities

title: Eight Gates
text: Opening the body’s chakra limiters grants extraordinary strength at the cost of injury.

title: Core Talent
text: Gain access to the first three Gates under the normal Eight Gates rules.

title: Developments
text: Controlled Opening — Reduce the final Speed of Actions used specifically to open, close, or change your active Gates by 2, minimum 1. Explosive Entry — The first Taijutsu Attack you make after opening a higher Gate gains +2 Accuracy. Iron Conditioning — Gain +3 on rolls made specifically to resist, survive, or remain conscious through the self-inflicted consequences of the Eight Gates. This does not prevent unavoidable consequences. Second Opening — Gain access to Gates 4 through 6. Use this improved self-wounding chance: (4 × Gates Open + Final Speed + Half AP Spent)%. Final Opening — Requires Second Opening. Gain access to Gates 7 and 8.

title: Mastery
text: Perfected Release — Once per battle, when opening or maintaining Gate 6 or lower would inflict a self-inflicted Wound, Fatigue increase, or similar consequence that can vary in severity, reduce that consequence by one step. This cannot negate the fixed consequences of Gate 7 or Gate 8.

title: Kage Bunshin
text: Shadow Clones divide a shinobi’s effort between fighting, reconnaissance and training.

title: Core Talent
text: Learn Kage Bunshin no Jutsu and gain access to the Shadow Clone rules, ignoring any normal requirement that would prevent you from learning the technique solely because of its rarity.

title: Developments
text: Coordinated Assault — If one of your Kage Bunshin has successfully attacked a target since the end of your previous Action, your next Attack against that target gains +2 Accuracy. Shadow Screen — After you successfully Dodge an Attack, you may exchange positions with one of your Kage Bunshin within 3 yards. Both positions must be legal for the respective characters. Memory Relay — When a Kage Bunshin is dismissed, you may deliberately review what it learned. Once per Hunt or Mission, a clone that spent meaningful time scouting, studying, or observing may grant +3 to one subsequent Research, Study Weakness, Awareness, Survival, or Espionage roll based on that information. This does not generate additional Intel by itself. Legion Method — When creating three or more Kage Bunshin at once, reduce the total Chakra cost of the technique by 10%, minimum 1. Perfect Double — While you are maintaining exactly one Kage Bunshin, that clone gains +2 on Defensive Rolls and +2 Accuracy on its Attacks.

title: Mastery
text: Many as One — When one of your Kage Bunshin fully hits a creature, your next Attack against that creature before the end of your next Action has its final Speed reduced by 2, minimum 1. This may stack with Coordinated Assault.

title: Medical Training
text: Medical Ninjutsu combines precise chakra control with knowledge of anatomy and treatment.

title: Core Talent
text: You may learn D- and C-Rank Medical Ninjutsu. You also gain Triage: [Speed 5, Utility, Touch] Triage — Examine a willing, helpless, or unconscious living creature. Learn its current HP category, Fatigue Level, and the severity and location of any physical Wounds you could reasonably diagnose. This does not automatically reveal curses, poisons, hidden seals, or supernatural conditions that require their own checks.

title: Developments
text: Combat Medic — When one of your Medical Ninjutsu restores HP to an ally during battle, that ally may either remove 2 Stun or regain 1 AP, up to their normal maximum. Anatomist — After successfully using Triage or a Medicine check to examine a living creature, gain +2 Accuracy on your next Attack against that creature before the end of the scene. This represents anatomical knowledge and does not apply when the creature's anatomy is completely alien to what you examined. Chakra Surgeon — You may learn B-Rank Medical Ninjutsu without Advanced Medical Training. All other learning requirements still apply. Emergency Medicine — Once per battle, when a living creature within reach is reduced to 0 HP or lower without dying, you may use Stabilise as a Speed 5 Interrupt. Pay its normal equipment cost and make its Medicine check. This permits the Interrupt but does not restore HP. Field Pharmacy — During a Week’s Rest, prepare two doses of a non-unique medicine you can normally purchase or craft. Pay their normal Ryō and material costs. This preparation uses no Downtime Slot.

title: Mastery
text: Surgeon of the Corps — You may learn A-Rank Medical Ninjutsu without Advanced Medical Training. All other learning requirements still apply. In addition, once per battle when you successfully stabilize or restore HP to a character at 0 HP, they may immediately ignore the numerical penalties of one physical Wound until the end of their next Action. The Wound is not removed.

title: Natural Chakra
text: Natural Chakra is the chakra of the living world. A shinobi normally produces chakra from within; a Sage learns to draw balanced Natural Chakra from the world around them.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose a Sage Tradition from a creature, Summon Tribe or other valid Source capable of teaching Natural Chakra. Gain Sage Rank 1, a maximum Sage Chakra of 4, Gather Natural Chakra, Sage Mode, your Tradition's Signature Trait, and one Sage Art or Sage Kata you meet the requirements for.

title: Developments
text: Natural Chakra uses Sage Arts and Sage Kata as its Developments. Each time you Deepen this Talent, increase your Sage Rank by 1 and learn one additional Sage Art or Sage Kata you qualify for; the selected Art or Kata is that Development. The Art or Kata granted by the Core Talent is not a Development. You may Deepen Natural Chakra up to four times, to a maximum Sage Rank of 5. Mastery is gained after the third Development as normal; the fourth Deepening remains available after Mastery and still costs a Talent Point. Use the Natural Chakra & Sage Mode rules for Sage Chakra, Gather Natural Chakra, Sage Mode, Sage Traditions, Sage Arts and Sage Kata.

title: Mastery
text: Perfect Communion — After three Natural Chakra Developments, reduce Gather Natural Chakra's base Speed by 1 and its minimum Speed by 1. Reduce Sage Mode's Upkeep by 1, minimum 0. The first time you enter Sage Mode in each battle, gain 1 Sage Chakra after Sage Mode resolves, up to your maximum.

title: Exotic Venoms
text: You study and prepare the unusual toxins found in monsters and the Wastes.

title: Core Talent
text: You may acquire, harvest, craft, and use Exotic Venoms permitted by the Equipment and Crafting rules. Once per Hunt, when a defeated or studied creature could reasonably provide a venom, toxin, poisonous organ, paralytic secretion, or similar component, you may identify one additional toxin reagent that can be recovered from it. This reagent is still subject to normal harvesting and crafting requirements. You also gain Identify Toxin: [Speed 5, Utility] Identify Toxin — Examine a poison, poisoned wound, venomous organ, or contaminated sample you can safely access. Make an appropriate Medicine, Survival, or Crafting check. On success, learn its broad effect, delivery method, and the kind of treatment or antidote that would normally oppose it.

title: Developments
text: Toxicologist — Gain +5 Medicine on checks made specifically to identify, treat, or create antidotes for poisons and venoms you have encountered before. Rapid Application — Actions used specifically to apply a poison to a weapon, tool, trap, or prepared delivery system have their final Speed reduced by 3, minimum 1. Refined Dose — Poisons you personally prepare impose +2 to the relevant Resistance TN, if they use one. A creature cannot suffer this bonus from more than one of your doses at a time. Stable Mixture — A poisoned weapon or delivery tool you prepared does not lose its applied dose merely because its first Attack misses, unless the item or poison rules explicitly say the dose is destroyed on use. Field Harvester — Gain +3 on Hunt Prepare, Survival, or Crafting rolls made specifically to recover or preserve poisonous monster components. The additional toxin reagent from the Core Talent may be recovered even if another party member also possesses Exotic Venoms, but each character still needs a distinct recoverable component.

title: Mastery
text: Signature Toxin — During a Week's Rest, you may designate one poison you personally create as your Signature Toxin. Until your next Week's Rest, its relevant Resistance TN increases by an additional +1 and any numerical duration it has increases by 20%, rounding down. You may only maintain one Signature Toxin formula at a time.

title: Seal Training
text: Fūinjutsu uses inscribed formulae to store, bind and direct chakra.

title: Core Talent
text: You may learn C- and B-Rank Sealing Ninjutsu. During each Week's Rest, choose one Sealing Ninjutsu you know as a Prepared Formula. The first time you use that technique before your next Week's Rest, reduce its final Seal Speed by 2 and its final Action Speed by 2, minimum 1. You may only have one Prepared Formula at a time unless a Development increases this limit.

title: Developments
text: Combat Scribe — All Sealing Ninjutsu you perform have their final Seal Speed reduced by 2, minimum 0. Barrier Specialist — Gain +2 on Attack, Defense, or Skill rolls made specifically to establish, reinforce, contest, or repair a sealing barrier. If the barrier does not use such a roll, gain +10% to any HP or durability the barrier receives from your own stats, rounding down. Suppression Specialist — Gain +2 Accuracy on Sealing Ninjutsu used specifically to suppress, bind, contain, or interfere with an active Chakra effect, summon, spirit, transformation, or creature when the technique is capable of doing so. Storage Specialist — Retrieval and storage Actions made through your Sealing Ninjutsu have their final Speed reduced by 2, minimum 1. Seal Architect — You may maintain two Prepared Formulae at once. Once per Mission or Hunt, after one of your Prepared Formulae successfully resolves, regain 1 AP up to your normal maximum.

title: Mastery
text: Grand Formula — You may learn A-Rank Sealing Ninjutsu without Advanced Seal Training. All other learning requirements still apply. During each Week's Rest, choose one of your Prepared Formulae as a Grand Formula. Its first use before your next Week's Rest reduces final Seal Speed by 5 and final Action Speed by 2, minimum 1, instead of the normal Prepared Formula reduction.

title: Master Artisan
text: You work with rare materials recovered from monsters and old-world sites.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose mastery of two Wondrous Materials from the current list: Skysteel, Ironheart, Angelskin, Crypstone, Mindglass, Voidglass, Feathersteel, Deepstone, Echo Brass, Shiversteel, Living Wood, Prismite, Anchorite, Ghostsilver, Bloodglass, Stormsilver, Black Jade, and Phaseglass. You may use their special properties when crafting weapons or other equipment as permitted by the Crafting rules.

title: Developments
text: Material Savant — Master two additional Wondrous Materials from the available list. Monsterwright — Gain +5 on Crafting checks where a meaningful Trophy or monster component is one of the primary materials. You may also identify whether a recovered monster component is suitable for weapon, armor, tool, pharmaceutical, or seal work without needing a separate Downtime action if the answer would be apparent to an expert. Efficient Workshop — Reduce the time required for your ordinary Crafting Downtime actions by 25%, minimum the shortest unit the Crafting rules normally permit. This does not reduce special story requirements or time gates on unique projects. Field Repair — Once per Mission or Hunt, you may perform emergency maintenance on a damaged ordinary weapon, armor piece, tool, puppet component, or similar crafted item you can reach. Gain +5 on the relevant Crafting check and make one roll using the normal Repairing rules without a Downtime Slot. In combat, this is a Speed 15 Utility Action; outside combat, it takes ten uninterrupted minutes. Signature Work — Choose one permanent item you personally crafted. When modifying or repairing that item, gain +5 on the Crafting check and treat one failed Crafting roll per Week's Rest as though it had succeeded by the minimum required amount. This cannot create materials or properties you do not possess.

title: Mastery
text: Magnum Opus — You may work with every Wondrous Material currently available to ordinary Master Artisans. You may also maintain one Magnum Opus: a permanent item you personally crafted which may contain a second Wondrous Material you have mastered. Both materials count toward normal Property Load and crafting cost. Creating or changing the item uses normal crafting.

title: Elemental Mastery
text: You have specialised in shaping one chakra nature.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose one standard elemental affinity you possess: Katon, Fūton, Raiton, Doton, or Suiton. This choice is permanent. When declaring a Ninjutsu with your chosen element, choose one Elemental Control: Efficient Moulding — Reduce its Chakra cost by 3, minimum 1. Clean Release — Reduce its final Seal Speed by 2, minimum 0.

title: Developments
text: Elemental Precision — Attacks using your chosen element gain +1 Accuracy. Efficient Nature — Efficient Moulding reduces Chakra cost by 5 instead of 3. Rapid Weaving — Clean Release reduces final Seal Speed by 4 instead of 2. Elemental Counter — Gain +2 on Defensive Rolls made against techniques of your chosen element. After you successfully Defend against one, your next Attack using your chosen element gains +1 Accuracy. Environmental Conduit — When a technique of your chosen element can meaningfully draw from or propagate through a large amount of naturally present matching material or conditions, reduce its Chakra cost by 2, minimum 1. The technique’s environmental requirements still apply.

title: Mastery
text: True Nature — When using Elemental Control, apply both Efficient Moulding and Clean Release to the same technique. If both would already apply from another rule, instead gain +1 Accuracy on that technique.

title: Interrogator
text: You assess a subject’s reactions and adapt your questioning to obtain useful information.

title: Core Talent
text: You gain Read the Subject: [Speed 10, Utility, Social] Read the Subject — After at least a brief meaningful exchange with a creature capable of communicating with you, make an Espionage check opposed by their Espionage or another appropriate defensive social roll. On success, choose one: Learn whether they are deliberately withholding something relevant to the current subject. Identify the person, topic, place, or consequence that produces the strongest visible emotional reaction during the exchange. Identify the broad kind of leverage currently driving them: fear, loyalty, greed, duty, pride, desperation, or something similarly apparent. Determine whether one statement they made conflicts with information you have already independently confirmed. Read the Subject does not compel speech, reveal thoughts, or tell you that a statement is objectively true. It reads behaviour, inconsistencies, and pressure.

title: Developments
text: Rapport — Gain +3 Espionage when gathering information from a willing, cooperative, or conversational target rather than threatening or restraining them. Pressure — Once per scene, after a target refuses to answer, deliberately evades a question, or ends an exchange, you may immediately make another Read the Subject check against them with +3. Cross-Examination — When a target contradicts something they previously told you during the same scene, gain +5 on your next Read the Subject check against them. Field Debrief — Once per Hunt or Mission, when you use testimony from a witness, survivor, captive, or local informant as a meaningful part of a Research, Track, or Study Weakness roll, add +5 to that roll. Closed Book — Gain +3 on Espionage, Willpower, or other rolls made specifically to resist interrogation, coercive questioning, or attempts to extract information from you without Genjutsu.

title: Mastery
text: Break the Story — Once per scene, after you have succeeded on at least two Read the Subject checks against the same target, you may ask one direct question. The target is never compelled to answer. If they answer, you automatically recognize whether the response is a deliberate lie, a deliberate evasion, or something they sincerely believe. This does not reveal what the truth actually is. Against another player character, use this only when the normal social/PvP rules permit such information to be established.

title: Weapon Savant
text: Long practice has made your chosen weapon familiar in attack, defence and movement.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose one weapon family or closely related group of weapons you are proficient with. The choice should describe one coherent fighting discipline, such as swords, spears, axes, bows, staves, or thrown weapons, rather than all melee or all ranged weapons. Attacks made with your chosen weapon family gain +1 Accuracy.

title: Developments
text: Guard Mastery — Gain +2 to Take the Hit and Parry rolls with your chosen weapon Quick Draw — The first Attack you declare after drawing, readying, or switching to a weapon from your chosen family has its final Speed reduced by 2, minimum 1. Tempo — After successfully Blocking or Parrying with your chosen weapon family, reduce the final Speed of your next Attack with that weapon family by 2, minimum 1. Weapon Control — Gain +3 on rolls made specifically to Disarm, bind, trap, contest, or otherwise control an enemy's weapon using a weapon from your chosen family, where the relevant combat action permits such a roll. Footwork — After a full hit with your chosen weapon family or a successful Block or Parry using it, move up to 1 yard without AP or additional Speed. This movement must follow a legal path and cannot pass through occupied spaces.

title: Mastery
text: Extension of the Body — When declaring an Attack with your chosen weapon family, choose one: gain +3 Accuracy, or reduce the Attack's final Speed by 3, minimum 1. Declare the choice before rolling.

title: Sensor Training
text: You detect chakra sources and learn to distinguish their signatures.

title: Core Talent
text: You gain Chakra Sense: [Speed 10, Chakra 5, Utility, Concentration] Chakra Sense — Until the end of your next Action, you can sense unsuppressed Chakra sources within 30 yards even without line of sight, unless a barrier or effect specifically blocks Chakra sensing. You learn the number of distinct sources you can sense and their rough direction. This does not automatically reveal identity, exact position, elemental affinities, techniques, or whether a source is hostile. When a creature is deliberately suppressing its Chakra, use Chakra Control in place of Awareness for any opposed roll required to detect its signature.

title: Developments
text: Wide Field — Increase Chakra Sense range to 100 yards. Beyond 30 yards you learn only the number and broad direction of signatures unless another Development says otherwise. Signature Memory — After sensing the same creature for at least 20 IC or spending meaningful time around them, you may memorize their Chakra signature. Gain +5 on later Chakra Control rolls made specifically to recognize that creature by Chakra. You may retain a number of memorized signatures equal to 3 + XP/1000; replacing one is your choice. Fine Sense — Within 30 yards, Chakra Sense also tells you whether a sensed creature is currently moulding significant Chakra and gives a rough comparison of its Chakra presence to your own: much weaker, weaker, similar, stronger, or much stronger. Combat Sensor — While Chakra Sense is active, gain +2 on Defensive Rolls against Attacks made by creatures you can sense but cannot clearly see. Sensing a creature this way prevents you from being treated as completely unaware of that creature, but does not remove concealment, invisibility, or other visual penalties. Residual Chakra — You may use Chakra Sense to examine fresh Chakra residue left on a creature, object, or location. Gain +3 on Track, Research, Awareness, or Espionage rolls where identifying or following that residue is directly relevant.

title: Mastery
text: Mind's Eye — While conscious, you passively sense unsuppressed Chakra sources within 15 yards without activating Chakra Sense or paying its Chakra cost. You learn only presence and rough direction through this passive sense. Suppressed signatures still require the normal opposed roll, and Fine Sense or Wide Field information still requires active Chakra Sense.

title: Chakra Suppression
text: You conceal your chakra signature from trained sensors.

title: Core Talent
text: You gain Still the Coils: [Speed 10, Utility, Self, Concentration] Still the Coils — Suppress your Chakra signature until you end this effect or perform an Action that spends Chakra. While suppressed, Chakra sensing does not automatically detect you. When a sensor attempts to locate or identify your signature, oppose their sensing roll with Espionage and gain +10 to your result. Still the Coils conceals your Chakra presence; it does not make your body invisible, silence you, erase footprints, or prevent ordinary Awareness from finding you.

title: Developments
text: Quiet Circulation — Still the Coils becomes Speed 5. The bonus on opposed rolls to conceal your signature becomes +15. Muffled Technique — A Utility or Defensive Action that spends Chakra does not end Still the Coils. An Attack that spends Chakra always ends it unless another rule explicitly says otherwise. False Reading — When you activate Still the Coils, you may choose to leave behind a deliberately misleading surface signature. A sensor who detects you but does not beat your opposed Espionage roll reads you as non-shinobi or as possessing a much weaker Chakra presence. A sensor who beats the roll recognizes the deception. Ghost Trail — Gain +5 on Espionage or Survival rolls made specifically to conceal, break, or falsify a trail of Chakra residue you left behind. Cold Start — The first Ninjutsu you declare after ending Still the Coils has its final Seal Speed reduced by 2, minimum 0.

title: Mastery
text: Zero Presence — While Still the Coils is active, your bonus on opposed rolls to hide your Chakra becomes +15. Once per battle, when an Action that spends Chakra would end Still the Coils, you may keep the suppression until that Action fully resolves. Observers can still perceive the Action by ordinary means; this only delays the reappearance of your Chakra signature.

title: Enhancements
text: Enhancements

title: Celerity
text: Training has sharpened your reactions and shortened wasted movement.

title: Core Talent
text: All of your Actions and Interrupts have their final Speed reduced by 1. This cannot reduce the Speed of an Interrupt below 3. You may choose not to apply this reduction, or only partially apply it, to a given Action.

title: Developments
text: Quick Hands — Actions primarily involving drawing, stowing, reloading, manipulating equipment, or performing handseals have their final Speed reduced by an additional 1, minimum 3. Quick Feet — After resolving a non-Movement Action, you may move up to 2 yards without AP or additional Speed. This is still movement and must follow a legal path. Quick Reflexes — Defensive Interrupts have their final Speed reduced by an additional 1, but cannot be reduced below 3 by this Development. Flow State — If your current non-Interrupt Action has a different primary purpose from your previous non-Interrupt Action — Attack, Defense, Utility, or Movement — reduce its final Speed by 1, minimum 3.

title: Mastery
text: Too Fast to Follow — The Core Talent reduction from Celerity becomes 2 instead of 1. The normal minimums still apply.

title: Generalist
text: You have trained across several Corps disciplines.

title: Core Talent
text: Gain any two non-Automatic Rank Benefits you currently or previously qualified for.

title: Developments
text: Cross-Training — Gain one additional non-Automatic Rank Benefit you currently or previously qualify for. You may select this Development only once. Broad Curriculum — Gain an additional XP/300 Skill Points. This scales as your total XP increases. Improvised Expertise — Once per scene, after making a Skill Check with a Skill in which you do not possess Specialization, add +5 before the result is resolved. Reassignment — During a Week's Rest, you may replace one Rank Benefit granted by Generalist with another non-Automatic Rank Benefit you currently or previously qualify for.

title: Mastery
text: Master of None — Gain one additional non-Automatic Rank Benefit you currently or previously qualify for. During each Week's Rest, you may now replace any number of Rank Benefits granted by Generalist rather than only one.

title: Prodigy
text: You learn advanced techniques unusually quickly.

title: Core Talent
text: Gain one non-Automatic Rank Benefit from any Rank, including a Rank you have never held.

title: Developments
text: Precocious — Gain one additional non-Automatic Rank Benefit from one Rank above your current Rank or lower. Fast Study — Reduce the required training time for learning Jutsu and Capability Talents by 25%, minimum one training action or the shortest unit the relevant rule normally permits. Seen It Once — Once per Mission or Hunt, after you witness another character successfully perform a non-Heritage Jutsu, Skill use, or combat technique, gain +3 to your next attempt at the same broad type of action during that scene. Unfairly Talented — Whenever you spend Willpower to reroll a Skill Check or a roll made specifically to learn, imitate, understand, or reproduce a technique, add +3 to the reroll.

title: Mastery
text: Ahead of the Curve — Gain one additional non-Automatic Rank Benefit from any Rank. Prodigy still never grants Automatic Rank Benefits.

title: Skill Specialist
text: You have devoted extensive practice to a particular field.

title: Core Talent
text: Gain an additional XP/200 Skill Points. This scales as your total XP increases.

title: Developments
text: Deep Study — Choose one Skill. Increase your maximum ranks in that Skill by 2. Specialized Practice — Choose one Skill in which you possess Specialization. When your Specialization directly applies, gain an additional +2. Reliable — Choose one Skill. Once per scene, when the natural d20 result for that Skill is lower than 7, treat the die as though it rolled a 7. Applied Expertise — Once per scene, after succeeding on a Skill Check, you may grant yourself or an ally who can act on your work +3 to one directly related Skill Check made before the end of the scene.

title: Mastery
text: Recognized Expert — Choose one Skill when you gain this Mastery. Once per scene, after rolling that Skill but before the result is resolved, you may treat the natural d20 result as a 15.

title: Hunter Classes
text: Hunter Classes

title: Class Benefits
text: Hunter Classes are Corps specialties. To join one, complete its qualification tasks with staff and record approval on your character sheet. Staff provide the current qualification requirements through the server’s class application process. Your class benefits begin when the application is approved.

title: Pathfinder
text: Scouts, trackers and navigators who find routes through the Wastes.

title: Always a Way
text: Gain +3 Survival and Awareness when tracking, navigating, locating something or identifying environmental hazards. Once per Hunt or Mission, after you or an ally fails a navigation, tracking, search or environmental-hazard check, that character may reroll it with +5 and must keep the new result. On success, ask the GM for one relevant environmental detail, such as a safer route, shelter, signs of passage or unstable terrain.

title: Slayer
text: Hunters trained to bring down dangerous creatures.

title: Bring it Down
text: Treat damage you deal as 25% higher for Wound determination only.

title: Anchor
text: Defenders who protect crews, caravans and settlements.

title: Nobody Gets Through
text: When an ally within 3 yards is attacked, spend 1 Willpower to use Take the Hit at its normal Speed without a roll or distance penalty. You must be able to reach the ally through a legal path and meet Take the Hit’s other restrictions. On success, you become the attack’s target; defend and resolve area attacks using the normal Take the Hit rules. After successfully defending against an attack or taking one for an ally, you may Hold the Line. Gain RES/2 DR and +5 to Defensive rolls until after your next non-Interrupt Action. These benefits apply after the triggering attack resolves. Further activations refresh the duration; they do not stack.

title: Trapper
text: Specialists in snares, seals, explosives, bait and ambushes. Whenever you successfully complete Prepare during a Hunt, create one additional Preparation, subject to the Hunt’s normal Preparation limit. Once per battle, reveal one preparation you could have established before the encounter. Describe its location and purpose when revealed; the GM must confirm that it was feasible. It grants one of the following: - +5 to one relevant Skill check. - +3 Accuracy to one attack that exploits it. - A snare: make a Survival Status Roll against the Resistance of one creature triggering it. On a failed defence, apply Immobilization 5 for 20 IC. - Reduce one environmental or enemy-created numerical penalty by 5 for you and allies within 3 yards, for 20 IC. This does not remove the underlying effect. Pay the normal costs of any equipment used. This cannot supply rare items or change events that have already resolved.

title: Scavenger
text: Salvagers who recover useful equipment and monster materials. After a Hunt, Mission or expedition with recoverable salvage, identify one additional usable Salvage or Trophy component. The GM selects a component appropriate to what remains; it must still be recovered normally. Once per Week’s Rest, convert expendable salvage worth at least 2,500 Ryō into one Field Supply. You may keep one at a time. Outside combat, spend it to assemble one ordinary consumable or tool worth up to 2,500 Ryō that can reasonably be made from those materials. It cannot provide weapons, armour, explosives or rare items. Alternatively, expend it before rolling to gain +5 on one Prepare, Artisan, Survival or Medicine check during a Hunt.

title: Chirurgeon
text: Medics and anatomists trained to treat Hunters and study beasts. Gain +3 Medicine on checks to treat Wounds or Stabilise an injured character. Once per battle, use Emergency Field Treatment [Speed 10, Utility, Touch] on a willing or helpless living creature with a Severe or Critical Wound, or at 0 HP or lower. It cannot treat a dead creature. On resolution: - If below 1 HP, restore it to 1 HP. - End one non-permanent injury-caused Bleed, Burn or Stun. - Suppress the numerical penalties of one Wound until the battle ends. The Wound remains; missing or unusable body parts remain unusable. Using this treatment on yourself costs 1 Willpower and requires you to be conscious and able to act.

title: Hound
text: Tracking and pursuit specialists. Increase Movement Speed by 50% while pursuing a target you can reliably locate through sight, tracking, scent or another sense. This increases distance travelled, not Action Speed. Gain +3 Survival and Awareness to locate or pursue creatures you have previously encountered.

title: Breaker
text: Hunters trained to breach armour, barriers and fortifications. Your attacks ignore 2 DR. Treat damage dealt to armour, barriers, structures and other defensive objects as 25% higher for durability loss only. Once per battle, declare Crack It Open after a hit is confirmed but before damage is rolled. That attack ignores 50% of the target’s DR instead of the flat 2, and its damage against armour, barriers, objects and structures is treated as 50% higher instead of 25%. If it Wounds a creature, you may choose the location from the legal results for that damage type. The defender retains its normal Wound mitigation.

title: Bear
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Bear Species
text: Role: Guardian / Grapple Bears are slow, brutally durable protectors. They excel at bodyguarding, grappling and forcing enemies to deal with them first.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 5 3 3 1 Basic Attack: Speed 11 Melee 100% Monster Damage Blunt Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground

title: Guardian's Bulk
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Bear may Take the Hit for an adjacent ally at Speed 4. The Bear gains +2 on checks to initiate or maintain Grapples.

title: Mauling Hold
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: When the Bear's Basic Attack hits by 5 or more, it may immediately attempt a Grapple. This costs no Command AP and adds no Speed.

title: Get Behind Me
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Speed: 5 Interrupt Trigger: An ally within 3 yards is targeted by an Attack the Bear could physically intercept. Effects: Move the Bear up to 2 yards. If it can interpose itself, it becomes the target and defends normally.

title: Unmoving Guardian
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: While Grappling a hostile creature or adjacent to an ally, the Bear gains 15 DR and reduces forced movement suffered by 2 yards, minimum 0.

title: Mountain With Teeth
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Bear counts as one Size larger for Grapples, carrying and forced movement. When it successfully initiates a Grapple, knock that target Prone. Its Basic Attacks against creatures it is Grappling deal +25% Final Damage.

title: Thick Fur
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Heavy Paws
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against Prone or Grappled targets.

title: Powerful Frame
text: Type: Utility Gain +3 on physical checks to lift, drag, break or brace mundane objects.

title: Trail Shelter
text: Type: Utility Outside Initiative, the bear can rapidly dig, clear or reinforce a rough campsite or emergency shelter, granting +3 to one relevant Survival check.

title: Bodyguard
text: Type: One-Time Get Behind Me becomes Speed 4 instead of Speed 5. When used to protect the tamer, the Bear may move up to 3 yards instead of 2.

title: Mauler
text: Type: One-Time Mauling Hold triggers on any full hit rather than requiring the Basic Attack to hit by 5 or more.

title: Mauling Grip
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Make an Attack for 100% Monster Damage. On a hit by 5 or more, Grapple the target; while maintained, the target suffers -2 Defence against the bear.

title: Roaring Challenge
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 5 Area: 8 yards Effects: Enemies that can hear the bear must make Resistance against Monster Save TN. On failure, they suffer -2 Accuracy against creatures other than the bear until the bear's next Action. This is a fear-based effect.

title: Guardian Rush
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 8 Effects: Move up to 6 yards toward an ally, then either make a Basic Attack or grant that ally +3 on its next Defensive Roll before the bear's next Action.

title: Avalanche Maul
text: Speed: 16 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Make an Attack for 140% Monster Damage. On a full hit, knock the target Prone and inflict Stun 4. Against a Grappled target, damage becomes 160% instead.

title: Temperament
text: Bears form strong protective routines around familiar people. They readily hold a line or cover a retreat, but forcing one to abandon a helpless creature it has been trained to guard can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Beetle
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Beetle Species
text: Role: Siege / Defence Beetles are armoured laborers and siege bodies. They trade speed for carrying power, stubborn defence, burrowing and horn-driven control.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 5 2 4 1 Basic Attack: Speed 11 Melee 100% Monster Damage Blunt Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground

title: Carapace
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Beetle gains 10 DR against physical damage.

title: Burrower
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Beetle may burrow through ordinary soil and loose earth at half Movement, leaving a crawlable tunnel when the terrain can support it.

title: Horn Drive
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: When the Beetle's Basic Attack fully hits, choose one: inflict Knockback 2, or move the target up to 2 yards to a legal space.

title: Siege Body
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Beetle counts as one Size larger for carrying, bracing and forced-movement contests. Its Attacks deal +50% Final Damage against unattended objects and mundane structures.

title: Immovable Engine
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Carapace becomes 15 DR against physical damage. The Beetle reduces Knockback suffered by 4, minimum 0, and gains +3 against forced movement. Destroying a mundane obstacle during its movement does not stop that movement if a legal path remains.

title: Carapace Layers
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Horn Leverage
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, increase Knockback or forced movement caused by Beetle Monster Techniques by 1 yard.

title: Burrower
text: Type: Utility Burrower functions at normal Movement instead of half Movement and may also excavate packed ordinary earth when the terrain can support a tunnel.

title: Pack Beast
text: Type: Utility The monster can carry or drag up to two human-sized willing or unconscious creatures, or an equivalent mundane load, without slowing ordinary overland travel.

title: Armoured Underside
text: Type: One-Time Increase the physical DR granted by Carapace by 5.

title: Anchor Claws
text: Type: One-Time Immovable Engine reduces Knockback by an additional 2 and grants an additional +2 against forced movement.

title: Horn Toss
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Attack for 100% Monster Damage. On a full hit, move the target up to 4 yards and knock it Prone.

title: Burrow Break
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: If standing on diggable ground, the monster burrows and emerges within 6 yards. Its next Basic Attack before the end of the Action gains +2 Accuracy.

title: Carapace Guard
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Trigger: the monster or an adjacent ally is hit by a physical Attack. Reduce Final Damage by 20%; if protecting an ally, the monster takes unreducible Vitality damage equal to half the amount prevented.

title: Siege Horn
text: Speed: 16 Base Command AP: 12 Line: 10 yards Effects: Move through the Line and Attack each creature for 110% Monster Damage. Unattended objects and physical barriers take +75% Final Damage; a destroyed mundane obstacle does not stop the movement.

title: Temperament
text: Beetles are steady working monsters that respond well to repeated hauling, digging and breaching routines. Needless destruction or constantly abandoning trained tasks halfway through for no reason can make them increasingly difficult to handle. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Boar
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Boar Species
text: Role: Breach / Frontline Boars are creatures of commitment: heavy, direct and practical. They break formations, clear roads and turn their bodies into moving obstacles.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 4 4 2 2 Basic Attack: Speed 10 Melee 100% Monster Damage Blunt Command AP Modifier: +1 Movement: Ground

title: Driving Mass
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: Reduce Knockback suffered by the Boar by 2, minimum 0. It gains +2 against effects that would forcibly reposition it.

title: Headlong Charge
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: If the Boar moved at least 3 yards in a straight line immediately before its Basic Attack, that Attack deals +15% Final Damage. On a full hit, also inflict Knockback 2.

title: Trample Through
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: Once per Move Action, the Boar may attempt to pass through the space of one human-sized hostile creature. Contest the Boar's Accuracy against that creature's Defence. On success, move the creature 1 yard to a legal space and continue moving. On failure, the Boar's movement ends before entering that space.

title: Living Wallback
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: Adjacent allies gain 5 DR against physical Attacks while the Boar can act. The Boar may Take the Hit for an ally within 2 yards at Speed 5 when it can physically interpose itself.

title: Battering Ram
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Boar counts as one Size larger for carrying and forced movement. Its Attacks deal +50% Final Damage against unattended objects and mundane structures. A full hit after Headlong Charge inflicts Knockback 4 and Prone instead of Knockback 2.

title: Ironhide
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Driving Mass
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, increase Knockback or forced movement caused by Boar Monster Techniques by 1 yard.

title: Root Work
text: Type: Utility Outside Initiative, halve the time needed to clear brambles, loose rubble, shallow earth, mud or similar mundane obstructions when the monster can simply dig or shove through them.

title: Hauler
text: Type: Utility The monster can carry or drag one additional human-sized willing or unconscious creature, or an equivalent mundane load, without slowing ordinary overland travel.

title: Broad Back
text: Type: One-Time Living Wallback grants adjacent allies 10 DR against physical Attacks instead of 5.

title: Planted Feet
text: Type: One-Time Driving Mass reduces Knockback by 3 instead of 2, and its bonus against forced repositioning becomes +3.

title: Boar Road
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 7 Line: 8 yards Effects: The monster charges along the Line and makes an Attack against each creature in it for 80% Monster Damage. On a hit, inflict Knockback 3.

title: Furrow the Earth
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Create a 3-yard-wide path up to 12 yards long through loose earth, rubble or brush. The path becomes Rocky Terrain 3 for 20 IC; shallow traps, wires or caches may be exposed with an appropriate check.

title: Wallback
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 7 Range: 2 yards Effects: Trigger: an ally is hit by an Attack the monster could physically intercept. Move up to 2 yards, become the target, and defend normally. If it cannot interpose itself, this cannot be used.

title: Breakthrough Charge
text: Speed: 15 Base Command AP: 12 Line: 12 yards Effects: Move along the Line and Attack each creature for 120% Monster Damage. On a hit inflict Knockback 6; on a full hit also inflict Stun 4. Unattended mundane obstacles take +50% Final Damage.

title: Temperament
text: Boars are stubborn working beasts that respond well to direct routes, obvious obstacles and committed movement. Pointless destruction or repeatedly driving one into the same obviously suicidal charge can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Crab
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Crab Species
text: Role: Defence / Grapple Crabs are defensive controllers. Their shell and pincers dominate narrow spaces, punish movement and hold targets in place.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 4 2 5 1 Basic Attack: Speed 11 Melee 100% Monster Damage Blunt Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground

title: Shell Wall
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Crab gains 10 DR against physical damage. Adjacent allies gain 5 DR against physical Attacks while the Crab can act.

title: Vice Grip
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Crab gains +1 on checks to initiate or maintain a Grapple with its pincers. When its Basic Attack hits by 5 or more, it may immediately attempt a Grapple for no Command AP and no additional Speed.

title: Amphibious
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: Shallow water, surf and seabeds do not impose mundane Movement penalties on the Crab. It may swim at half normal Movement and remain underwater for an entire scene without Suffocation checks.

title: Sideways Guard
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: After successfully Dodging an Attack, the Crab may move 1 yard without changing Initiative. This can occur once between its Actions.

title: Control Zone
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: A hostile creature voluntarily leaves the Crab's melee reach. Effects: Attempt a Grapple. On success, the triggering movement ends. Shell Wall also becomes 15 DR against physical damage and grants adjacent allies 10 DR against physical Attacks, and the Crab reduces Knockback suffered by 2, minimum 0.

title: Shell Layers
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Vice Grip
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 on checks to initiate or maintain a Grapple with the pincers.

title: Amphibious
text: Type: Utility Amphibious improves the Crab's swimming Movement from half to full normal Movement and grants +3 on checks to resist currents or aquatic forced movement.

title: Burrowing Crab
text: Type: Utility Outside Initiative, the monster can dig shallow pits, trenches or hiding hollows in sand or loose soil at half normal working time.

title: Sideways Guard
text: Type: One-Time Sideways Guard may move 2 yards instead of 1 after a successful Dodge.

title: Wall of Shell
text: Type: One-Time Increase the DR Shell Wall grants adjacent allies by 5.

title: Pincer Hold
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Attack for 80% Monster Damage and attempt a Grapple on hit. A target Grappled this way suffers -2 to actions that require the held limb.

title: Shell Wall
text: Speed: 4 Base Command AP: 5 Effects: Until the monster's next Action, gain +3 Defence and grant adjacent allies 15 DR against physical Attacks, but Movement is halved.

title: Undertow
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 7 Requires: water or loose sand Effects: Attack a creature within 5 yards for 70% Monster Damage; on hit pull it 4 yards toward the crab.

title: Crushing Clamp
text: Speed: 15 Base Command AP: 11 Requires: a Grappled target Effects: Attack for 140% Monster Damage. On a full hit, inflict Immobilization 4 until the Grapple ends.

title: Temperament
text: Crabs are territorial and settle quickly into guarding a chosen space. They will hold that space under heavy pressure, but repeatedly forcing one to abandon creatures or positions it has been trained to shelter can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Crocodile
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Crocodile Species
text: Role: Ambush / Grapple Crocodiles are ambush grapplers. They are difficult to dislodge, frightening in water and built to turn one clean bite into control.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 4 4 3 1 Basic Attack: Speed 11 Melee 100% Monster Damage Piercing Command AP Modifier: +2 Movement: Ground; swims at normal Movement

title: River Predator
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Crocodile swims at twice its normal Movement and may remain submerged for an entire scene without Suffocation checks. It gains +1 on Stealth checks while substantially submerged.

title: Lockjaw
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: When the Crocodile's Basic Attack hits by 5 or more, it may immediately attempt a Grapple. This costs no Command AP and adds no Speed.

title: Low Profile
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: While Prone or substantially submerged, ranged Attacks originating more than 5 yards away suffer -1 Accuracy against the Crocodile.

title: Crushing Hold
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: A creature Grappled by the Crocodile suffers -1 Defence against it. The Crocodile's Basic Attacks against that creature deal +15% Final Damage.

title: Drag Below
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: While in water and Grappling a creature, the Crocodile may carry that creature at full Movement. A submerged target that cannot breathe immediately begins the normal Suffocation rules. The Crocodile counts as one Size larger for Grapples.

title: Armoured Scutes
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Crushing Jaws
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against Grappled targets.

title: River Hunter
text: Type: Utility River Predator's swimming Movement becomes 2.5 times normal Movement. The Crocodile also gains +3 Awareness on checks made to detect creatures moving through the same body of water.

title: Waterline Ambush
text: Type: Utility When substantially submerged or concealed in marsh, grant +3 to an allied Stealth or ambush preparation check involving the monster.

title: Lockjaw
text: Type: One-Time The monster gains +3 on checks to maintain a Grapple it initiated.

title: Low Profile
text: Type: One-Time Low Profile imposes -2 Accuracy instead of -1 against ranged Attacks from more than 5 yards away.

title: Jaw Lock
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Make an Attack for 100% Monster Damage. If it hits by 5 or more, immediately Grapple the target.

title: Death Roll
text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 8 Requires: a Grappled target Effects: Make an Attack for 120% Monster Damage; on a hit, knock the target Prone and move both creatures up to 2 yards.

title: Drag Under
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 7 Requires: the monster to be in water and Grappling a target Effects: Move up to the monster's full Movement, carrying the target. The target immediately begins normal Suffocation rules if submerged and unable to breathe.

title: Blackwater Ambush
text: Speed: 15 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: The monster may move up to 8 yards from concealment or water and Attack for 150% Monster Damage. If the target had not detected the monster, this Attack gains +3 Accuracy.

title: Temperament
text: Crocodiles are patient ambush predators. They respond well to stillness, water and decisive attacks, but become difficult when repeatedly forced into noisy pursuit, dragged away from secure territory without purpose, or made to kill purely for sport. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Elk
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Elk Species
text: Role: Escort / Mobility Elk are mobile guides and protective escorts. They excel at travel, terrain crossing, carrying allies and using antlers to redirect danger.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 3 2 3 4 Basic Attack: Speed 8 Melee 100% Monster Damage Blunt Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Ground

title: Sure-Footed Guide
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Elk ignores mundane Movement penalties from shallow snow, mud, roots, undergrowth and steep natural slopes where a hoofed animal could reasonably pass. It may carry one willing human-sized rider at half Movement.

title: Antler Catch
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: After successfully Parrying a Melee Attack, the Elk may move the attacker 1 yard to either side of itself if a legal space exists.

title: Escort Step
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: When the Elk takes a Move Action, one willing adjacent ally may move up to half the distance the Elk moved after it finishes, without changing that ally's Initiative. The ally must follow a legal path and end within 2 yards of the Elk.

title: Protective Herd
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Elk's rider and allies within 2 yards gain +1 Defence against Melee Attacks and forced-movement effects while the Elk is conscious and able to move.

title: Great Crossing
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Elk may carry up to two willing human-sized allies at full Movement. It ignores mundane Difficult Terrain and may cross ordinary gaps up to 2 yards without a check when a physically plausible landing exists.

title: Long Stride
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases Movement by 0.1 yard per IC.

title: Branching Guard
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 Parry against Melee Attacks made by creatures that moved at least 3 yards before attacking.

title: Wayfinder
text: Type: Utility Grant +3 to Survival checks for navigation, weather sense, finding safe trails or selecting an overland route.

title: Sure-Footed
text: Type: Utility Sure-Footed Guide also grants +3 Defence against forced movement and effects that would knock the Elk Prone while standing on natural terrain.

title: Rider
text: Type: One-Time The Elk may carry one additional human-sized willing rider. Before Great Crossing, carrying the additional rider reduces Movement by half; Great Crossing removes this penalty.

title: Antler Catch
text: Type: One-Time Antler Catch also grants +2 Parry against Melee Attacks made by creatures that moved at least 3 yards immediately before attacking.

title: Antler Guard
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Range: 2 yards Effects: Trigger: an ally is targeted by a Melee Attack. The elk moves up to 2 yards and Parries on that ally's behalf if it can interpose its antlers.

title: Trailblazer
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 5 Effects: The elk and one adjacent willing ally move up to 6 yards. That movement ignores mundane Difficult Terrain.

title: Stampede Line
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 9 Line: 10 yards Effects: Move along the Line and Attack creatures in it for 90% Monster Damage. On a hit, inflict Knockback 4.

title: Great Crossing
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 11 Effects: The elk moves up to twice its normal Movement and may carry up to two willing human-sized allies during this movement. It can cross ordinary gaps, shallow water and rough natural terrain without checks if a physically plausible route exists.

title: Temperament
text: Elk are herd-minded, route-oriented monsters that settle best with familiar trails and calm handling. Needless destruction of habitat, slaughter around them, or repeatedly forcing them to trample safe ground without purpose can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Long Arms

text: Speed: 14 Base Command AP: 8 Requires: a Grappled target or unattended object Effects: Throw it up to 5 yards. A creature takes 80% Monster Damage and lands Prone; an unwilling creature may oppose with Grapple Defence.

text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Range: 2 yards Effects: Trigger: an enemy moves past the monster toward an ally. Attempt a Grapple. On success, the triggering movement ends.

text: Speed: 16 Base Command AP: 12 Area: 4 yards Effects: The gorilla slams the ground; creatures in Area defend separately. On a hit take 110% Monster Damage and suffer Knockback 4; on a full hit also become Prone.

text: Gorillas are social, practical and highly responsive to familiar handlers. They work hard when given clear physical tasks, but react poorly to pointless bullying or being made to destroy useful tools, shelter or supplies without purpose. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Hound
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Hound Species
text: Role: Tracking / Teamwork Hounds are reliable hunting partners. They specialize in scent, teamwork, takedowns and protecting the person they have accepted as their handler.

text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 3 3 2 4 Basic Attack: Speed 8 Melee 100% Monster Damage Piercing Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Ground

title: Tracking Hound

title: Handler's Guard
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: While within 2 yards of you, the Hound gains +1 Defence and you gain +1 Defence against Melee Attacks.

text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: When the Hound's Basic Attack hits by 5 or more, choose one: knock the target Prone, or immediately attempt a Grapple. This costs no Command AP and adds no Speed.

title: Handler Guard
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: You are hit by a Melee Attack. Effects: The Hound may move up to 3 yards toward you. If it becomes adjacent, reduce that Attack's Final Damage by 10%.

text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: When you fully hit a creature, the Hound's next Basic Attack against it before the end of its next Action gains +2 Accuracy and +20% Final Damage. title: Pack Hunt
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 11 Effects: Attack for 120% Monster Damage. If at least one ally is adjacent to the target, gain +2 Accuracy; on a full hit, that ally may move 2 yards without changing Initiative.

text: Hounds are strongly handler-focused and thrive on familiar routines, work and pack contact. Deliberate abandonment, disposable use, or knowingly sending one to die simply to save the tamer effort can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Endless Chase
