title: Cackling Pressure
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: When the Hyena fully hits a creature, that creature suffers -1 Defence against the next Attack made by one of the Hyena's allies before the target's next Action.

title: Feeding Frenzy
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Hyena's Basic Attacks against Prone, Wounded or Bleeding creatures deal +25% Final Damage. On a full hit against such a target, it also suffers -2 Defence until its next Action. This does not stack with Cackling Pressure.

title: Bonecracker
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against a target that has suffered a Wound this scene.

title: Endless Chase
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases Movement by 0.1 yard per IC while moving toward a Wounded or Bleeding enemy.

title: Carrion Wise
text: Type: Utility Grant +3 to Survival or Research checks involving carcasses, scavengers, feeding sites, disease signs or determining whether remains were disturbed.

title: Laughing Signal
text: Type: Utility The monster can coordinate simple warnings and directions over long distances by distinctive calls; allies familiar with it can distinguish danger, retreat, found trail and rally signals.

title: Pack Opportunist
text: Type: One-Time Pack Opportunist grants +2 Accuracy instead of +1, and Basic Attacks benefiting from it deal +10% Final Damage.

title: Unnerving Cackle
text: Type: One-Time Enemies within 5 yards suffer -2 to Resistance against fear-based effects created by the monster.

title: Cackling Feint
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 5 Range: 8 yards Effects: One target resists against Monster Save TN. On failure it suffers -2 Defence against the next Attack made against it before its next Action. This is a fear-based effect.

title: Harrier Bite
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Attack for 105% Monster Damage. If an ally hit the target since the monster's previous Action, gain +2 Accuracy.

title: Bonecrush
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 9 Effects: Attack for 130% Monster Damage. Against a Prone or Wounded target, increase damage to 150%.

title: Feeding Frenzy
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Make an Attack for 100% Monster Damage. If it hits, up to two allies within 3 yards may each move 2 yards toward the target without changing Initiative. The target suffers -2 Defence until its next Action.

title: Temperament
text: Hyenas are food-motivated pack hunters and learn quickly through shared hunts and consistent reward. Starving one of expected rewards, isolating it from familiar packmates without cause, or repeatedly wasting kills after encouraging it to hunt can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Jackal
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Jackal Species
text: Role: Pursuit / Tracking Jackals are relentless pursuit hunters. They excel at tracking, repositioning around wounded prey, and turning a retreat into a bad decision.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 2 4 2 4 Basic Attack: Speed 8 Melee 100% Monster Damage Piercing Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Ground

title: Blood-Scented Pursuit
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Jackal can establish and follow a physical scent trail from blood, fur, clothing, carcasses, campsites and similar evidence where one plausibly remains. Its Basic Attack gains +1 Accuracy against Bleeding creatures or creatures that have suffered a Wound this scene.

title: Cut the Line
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: When an enemy voluntarily moves farther away from the Jackal, it may move up to 2 yards after that Action resolves without changing Initiative. This can occur once between the Jackal's Actions.

title: Hamstring Bite
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: When the Jackal's Basic Attack fully hits a creature that moved at least 5 yards since its last Action, reduce all movement that creature makes before its next Action by 2 yards, minimum 0.

title: Relentless Chase
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: Increase the Jackal's Movement by 50% while it moves toward a Wounded or Bleeding creature. It ignores mundane Difficult Terrain during that movement.

title: Pack Execution
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: The Jackal's Basic Attacks against Wounded or Bleeding creatures gain +2 Accuracy and deal +25% Final Damage.

title: Longroad Legs
text: Type: Stackable Increase the monster's Movement by 0.1 yard per IC.

title: Harrier
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against a target that has suffered a Wound or moved at least 5 yards since its last Action.

title: Carrion Nose
text: Type: Utility Blood-Scented Pursuit becomes exceptionally precise. When the Jackal meaningfully helps a Track or investigation using scent, grant +5 to the relevant Survival or Research roll, and on success the Jackal can distinguish the freshest plausible trail from older overlapping trails.

title: Scavenger's Eye
text: Type: Utility Outside Initiative, the monster can quickly identify whether mundane meat, hides, tracks, remains, discarded equipment or disturbed ground are fresh, spoiled, recently moved or deliberately tampered with. It never creates additional salvage.

title: Cut Them Off
text: Type: One-Time Cut the Line may move up to 3 yards instead of 2, and the Jackal gains +2 Defence against movement-based reactions during that movement.

title: Blood in the Air
text: Type: One-Time Increase Blood-Scented Pursuit's Accuracy bonus against Bleeding or Wounded creatures by +1. Pack Execution therefore grants a total of +4 Accuracy against those targets.

title: Carrion Nose
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 4 Effects: Choose a creature, trail, body or disturbed site the monster can physically examine. It makes a focused scent search; gain +5 to one immediately related Survival, Awareness or Research roll and, on success, learn the freshest plausible direction of travel.

title: Harrier's Cut
text: Speed: 8 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Make a Basic Attack. If the target moved at least 5 yards since its last Action, increase Final Damage by 20% and reduce any movement it makes before its next Action by 2 yards, minimum 0.

title: Last-Mile Pack
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 9 Range: 15 yards Effects: The Jackal darts around one target, snapping from changing angles. Make one Attack using the monster's Accuracy for 80% Monster Damage. On a hit, end the target's current voluntary movement and knock it Prone if it moved at least 5 yards during that Action.

title: Run to Ground
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: The monster moves up to twice its normal Movement for this Action and makes an Attack for 130% Monster Damage. Against a Wounded or Bleeding target, gain +2 Accuracy and inflict Knockback 3 on a full hit.

title: Temperament
text: Jackals are driven by pursuit, scent and useful scavenging. They respond well to clear quarry and active work, but become difficult when repeatedly forced to remain idle as disposable guards or made to destroy food, salvage or a trail without purpose. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Leech
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Leech Species
text: Role: Sustain / Support Leeches are sustain monsters. They cling, drain, transfer vitality and purge harmful substances rather than winning through direct offence.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 4 2 3 3 Basic Attack: Speed 9 Melee 100% Monster Damage Piercing Command AP Modifier: +0 Movement: Ground; swims at normal Movement

title: Blood Feeder
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: When the Leech's Basic Attack deals damage, it restores Vitality equal to 15% of Final Damage dealt, up to 5% of its maximum Vitality per Action.

title: Clinging Body
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Leech gains +2 on checks to maintain Grapples. It may remain attached to a willing creature without impeding that creature's Movement.

title: Filter Feeder
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: The Leech gains +2 Resistance against Poison and disease-like biological effects. While attached to a willing creature, that creature also gains +2 Resistance against those effects.

title: Purging Bite
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Speed: 10 Range: Touch Tags: Utility Effects: Touch a willing creature and reduce one Poison, Burns or Bleed status by 1, minimum 0. The Leech loses Vitality equal to 5% of its maximum.

title: Red Feast
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Blood Feeder restores Vitality equal to 30% of Final Damage dealt, up to 10% of maximum Vitality per Action. Whenever Blood Feeder restores Vitality, one adjacent or attached living ally also restores HP equal to half the amount restored, to a maximum of 5% of the Leech's maximum Vitality per Action.

title: Blood Reservoir
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases maximum Vitality by 4% of the monster's unmodified maximum Vitality.

title: Efficient Feeder
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases Vitality restored by Leech Species Features and Monster Techniques by 4%.

title: Toxin Taster
text: Type: Utility The monster can detect whether a touched liquid, wound or food contains an obvious biological poison or contaminant, granting +3 to a relevant Medicine or Toxicology check.

title: Medicinal Saliva
text: Type: Utility When the monster assists mundane wound treatment outside Initiative, grant +3 to one Medicine check. It cannot replace required tools or medical jutsu.

title: Clinging Body
text: Type: One-Time Clinging Body's bonus to maintain Grapples becomes +3. While attached to a willing creature, forced movement affecting that creature does not automatically detach the Leech.

title: Filter Feeder
text: Type: One-Time Filter Feeder's Resistance bonus becomes +5 for the Leech and +3 for a willing creature it is attached to.

title: Blood Draw
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Attack for 80% Monster Damage. On hit, restore Vitality to the monster equal to 25% of Final Damage dealt, up to 10% of its maximum Vitality.

title: Transfusion
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 7 Range: 0 yards Effects: Transfer up to 15% of the monster's current Vitality to an adjacent living ally as restored Vitality. This cannot restore HP or repair Wounds.

title: Purge
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 8 Range: 0 yards Effects: Touch a willing creature. Reduce one Poison, Burns or Bleed status by 2, minimum 0. The monster loses Vitality equal to 5% of its maximum per level removed.

title: Red Feast
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Attack for 120% Monster Damage. Restore Vitality equal to 40% of Final Damage dealt, then distribute that restored amount between the monster and one adjacent ally. Once per battle.

title: Temperament
text: Leeches treat blood as food and respond strongly to feeding routines. They can be trained to drain enemies and aid familiar allies, but deliberately feeding one on helpless allies for cruelty, spectacle or convenience can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Lynx
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Lynx Species
text: Role: Reaction / Counterattack Lynxes are reactive hunters built around speed, awareness and sudden retaliation. They are at their best when an enemy commits first.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 2 3 2 5 Basic Attack: Speed 7 Melee 100% Monster Damage Slashing Command AP Modifier: -2 Movement: Ground; climbs ordinary surfaces at half Movement

title: Pre-Impact Read
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Lynx gains +1 Defence against the first Attack declared against it after each of its Actions.

title: Counterstep
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: After successfully Dodging or Parrying an Attack, the Lynx may move 1 yard without changing Initiative. This can occur once between its Actions.

title: Capacitor Coat
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: After successfully Dodging or Parrying a Melee Attack, the Lynx becomes Charged. Its next Basic Attack before the end of its next Action deals +15% Final Damage, then Charged ends.

title: Static Grounding
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Lynx gains +2 Defence against Lightning and electrical Energy Attacks and reduces Paralysis inflicted by those effects by 1, minimum 0.

title: Perfect Counter
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: The Lynx successfully Dodges or Parries an Attack from a creature within its melee reach. Effects: Make an immediate Attack against that creature for 80% Monster Damage.

title: Static Claws
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% against a target that used a Lightning or Energy effect since its previous Action.

title: Needle Ears
text: Type: Stackable Gain +1 on Awareness checks made through sound, vibration or electrical disturbance.

title: Storm Listener
text: Type: Utility Rain, fog and darkness do not penalize the monster's Awareness when the thing being detected could reasonably be heard. It can distinguish natural thunder from nearby chakra-driven electrical discharge.

title: High Perch
text: Type: Utility The monster can climb ordinary vertical surfaces at its normal Movement and can safely leap gaps up to twice its normal Movement without a check when a plausible landing exists.

title: Capacitor Fur
text: Type: One-Time Capacitor Coat's Charged bonus becomes +30% Final Damage instead of +15%.

title: Pre-Impact Read
text: Type: One-Time Pre-Impact Read grants +2 Defence against the first Attack declared against the Lynx after each of its Actions instead of +1.

title: Thunder-Ear
text: Speed: 7 Base Command AP: 4 Range: 20 yards Effects: The monster listens for movement, breathing, speech, impact or electrical disturbance. Make an Awareness check with +5; on success it may immediately Point Out one Hidden creature it could plausibly hear.

title: Forked Pounce
text: Speed: 8 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Move up to 5 yards, then Attack for 100% Monster Damage. On a hit, arc static to a different creature within 5 yards and make a second Attack at -2 Accuracy for 60% Monster Damage.

title: Grounding Guard
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Range: 2 yards Effects: Trigger: the monster or an ally is hit by an electrical Energy effect. Reduce that effect's Final Damage by 20% and reduce Paralysis inflicted by 1, minimum 0.

title: Thunderclaw
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 11 Effects: Make an Attack for 125% Monster Damage. On a full hit, inflict Paralysis 3 for 10 IC. If the monster is Charged, increase the damage to 150% and Paralysis to 4, then Charged ends.

title: Temperament
text: Lynxes are watchful, reactive hunters. They respond best to patient handling and room to choose their moment. Repeatedly using one as deliberate bait, or ignoring clear warning behaviour and forcing it back into obvious danger, can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Mantis
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Mantis Species
text: Role: Precision / Counter Mantises are precision predators. They favor stillness, reach, clean counters and attacks that punish exposed limbs or careless approaches.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 2 4 3 3 Basic Attack: Speed 9 Melee 100% Monster Damage Slashing Command AP Modifier: +0 Movement: Ground; climbs rough natural surfaces at half Movement

title: Predator's Reach
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: Increase the reach of the Mantis's Basic Attack by 1 yard.

title: Hooking Guard
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Mantis gains +1 Parry against Melee Attacks. After successfully Parrying a Melee Attack, it may move the attacker 1 yard to a legal adjacent space.

title: Patient Killer
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: If the Mantis has not voluntarily moved since its previous Action, its next Basic Attack deals +15% Final Damage.

title: Scything Reflex
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: The Mantis successfully Parries a Melee Attack. Effects: Make an immediate Attack against that attacker for 60% Monster Damage.

title: Killing Zone
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Speed: 4 Interrupt Trigger: A hostile creature voluntarily enters or leaves the Mantis's melee reach. Effects: Make an Attack against that creature for 80% Monster Damage. This can occur once between the Mantis's Actions and is an Independent Action.

title: Razor Forelimbs
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 Accuracy with the Basic Attack against a creature that attacked the monster since its previous Action.

title: Patient Killer
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the next Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% if the monster has not voluntarily moved since its previous Action.

title: Still as Grass
text: Type: Utility When the monster remains motionless and has suitable cover or vegetation, grant +3 to an allied Stealth or ambush preparation check involving it.

title: Fine Manipulators
text: Type: Utility Despite its anatomy, the monster can carefully cut rope, webbing, cloth, vines and similar non-reinforced material without damaging a restrained creature or nearby object.

title: Hooking Guard
text: Type: One-Time Hooking Guard grants +2 Parry against Melee Attacks instead of +1. The attacker may still be shifted 1 yard after a successful Parry.

title: Long Reach
text: Type: One-Time Increase the reach of the Basic Attack and Mantis Monster Techniques by 1 additional yard. This stacks with Predator's Reach.

title: Scything Counter
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Trigger: the monster successfully Parries a Melee Attack. Make an immediate Attack against that attacker for 70% Monster Damage.

title: Prayer-Still
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 4 Effects: The monster becomes braced until its next Action. It gains +3 Defence, but loses the bonus immediately if it voluntarily moves.

title: Severing Arc
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 8 Effects: Make an Attack for 115% Monster Damage. On a full hit, choose: inflict Bleed 3, or reduce the target's Movement by 20% for 20 IC.

title: Thousand-Cut Step
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Move up to 4 yards without provoking movement-based reactions, then make two Attacks against the same target at -2 Accuracy, each for 70% Monster Damage.

title: Temperament
text: Mantises are still, precise predators. They tolerate lethal work, but react poorly to frantic handling, needless torment and commands that repeatedly force them to abandon a clean position for spectacle. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Moth
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Moth Species
text: Role: Control / Scouting Moths are fragile evasive support monsters. They specialize in flight, dust, concealment, sensory disruption and battlefield utility.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 1 2 4 5 Basic Attack: Speed 7 Melee 100% Monster Damage Blunt Command AP Modifier: -2 Movement: Flight

title: Dust Wake
text: Unlock: Core Talent Speed: 8 Area: 3 yards Tags: Utility Effects: Create Visibility 2 in the Area until the Moth's next Action. The Moth ignores Visibility created by its own Species Features.

title: Fluttering Ghost
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: After moving at least 3 yards while airborne, the Moth gains +1 Defence against ranged Attacks until its next Action.

title: Powder Sense
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: The Moth and adjacent allies ignore up to 2 points of Visibility created by the Moth. The Moth also gains +2 Awareness against creatures moving inside its dust.

title: Lulling Dust
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The first time each hostile creature begins an Action inside Visibility created by the Moth, it must resist against Monster Save TN. On failure, it suffers -2 Awareness until the end of that Action. A creature can be affected once per Moth Action.

title: Moonwing Shroud
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: Dust Wake becomes Area 5 and Visibility 3. When used, choose any number of allies in the Area; those allies ignore that Dust Wake's Visibility.

title: Powdered Wings
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, increase the Visibility penalty created by Moth Species Features and Monster Techniques by 1.

title: Drifting Flight
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases flying Movement by 0.1 yard per IC.

title: Night Sense
text: Type: Utility The monster ignores up to 4 points of darkness-based Visibility penalty and grants +3 to one Awareness check involving light, vibration or air movement.

title: Pollen Reader
text: Type: Utility The monster can identify disturbed dust, pollen, ash and airborne residue, granting +3 to one Track, Research or Survival check where those traces matter.

title: Soft Landing
text: Type: One-Time The monster and one adjacent willing creature ignore ordinary falling damage from up to 10 yards; greater falls reduce their effective distance by 10 yards.

title: Evasive Flutter
text: Type: One-Time After the Moth successfully Dodges an Attack while airborne, it may move 1 yard without changing Initiative. This cannot happen more than once between its Actions.

title: Dust Veil
text: Speed: 8 Base Command AP: 5 Area: 5 yards Effects: Create Visibility 3 until the monster's next Action. The monster ignores its own Dust Veil.

title: Lulling Powder
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 7 Cone: 5 yards Effects: Targets resist against Monster Save TN. On failure, inflict Paralysis 2 and -2 Awareness for 10 IC.

title: Moonlit Mark
text: Speed: 7 Base Command AP: 5 Range: 15 yards Effects: Dust clings to one creature for 20 IC. That creature cannot benefit from more than 3 points of Visibility against the monster and allies who can see the glowing dust.

title: Wingstorm
text: Speed: 11 Base Command AP: 11 Area: 6 yards Effects: Make an Attack against each hostile creature for 70% Monster Damage and inflict Knockback 3 on a hit. Smoke, loose dust and mundane airborne obscurants in the Area are dispersed.

title: Temperament
text: Moths are curious creatures drawn to light, air currents and strange traces. They are easily distressed by uncontrolled flame and repeated exposure to toxins; deploying one purely to be burned, poisoned or destroyed as a disposable distraction can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Panther
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Panther Species
text: Role: Stealth / Assault Panthers are extreme offensive hunters. They are accurate, fast and lethal from concealment, but their poor Defence makes bad positioning costly.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 2 5 1 4 Basic Attack: Speed 8 Melee 100% Monster Damage Slashing Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Ground; climbs at half Movement

title: Silent Predator
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: The Panther gains +2 on Stealth checks involving stalking or ambushes. Its Basic Attacks made while Hidden gain +1 Accuracy.

title: Pounce
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: If the Panther moves at least 4 yards directly toward a target before making a Basic Attack, a full hit also knocks that target Prone.

title: Fade After Blood
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: After the Panther fully hits with a Basic Attack while it began the Action Hidden, it may move 1 yard without changing Initiative. This can occur once per Panther Action.

title: Ambush Killer
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Panther's Basic Attacks made while Hidden deal +20% Final Damage.

title: Apex Stalker
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Limit: Once per battle Effects: The Panther's first Attack against a creature that has not detected it gains +3 Accuracy and +25% Final Damage. On a full hit, inflict Bleed 3. After the Attack resolves, the Panther may move up to 3 yards toward concealment without changing Initiative.

title: Killing Claws
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% when made from Stealth or after moving at least 5 yards.

title: Predator's Focus
text: Type: Stackable For every 2 ranks, gain +1 Accuracy with the Basic Attack against a target that has not yet acted since the Panther's previous Action.

title: Silent Paws
text: Type: Utility Grant +3 to Stealth checks involving stalking, moving quietly or preparing an ambush with the panther.

title: Night Hunter
text: Type: Utility Ignore up to 4 points of darkness-based Visibility penalty for Awareness and movement.

title: Pounce
text: Type: One-Time When Pounce triggers, the Basic Attack also deals +10% Final Damage.

title: Fade After Blood
text: Type: One-Time Fade After Blood may move 2 yards instead of 1. If that movement ends in concealment, the Panther may immediately attempt to Hide.

title: Shadow Pounce
text: Speed: 8 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Move up to 6 yards and Attack for 110% Monster Damage. If the Panther began the Action Hidden, gain +2 Accuracy.

title: Throat Claw
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 8 Effects: Attack for 125% Monster Damage. If the target is Prone, Grappled, or has not detected the Panther, increase this to 150% Monster Damage.

title: Vanish Between Blows
text: Speed: 4 Base Command AP: 6 Effects: Move up to 4 yards to concealment and immediately attempt to Hide if the normal conditions for Hide are met. This Action does not by itself break existing Stealth.

title: Nightfall Kill
text: Speed: 12 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: Make an Attack for 160% Monster Damage at -2 Accuracy. If the Panther began this Action Hidden, remove the Accuracy penalty. On a full hit, inflict Bleed 4.

title: Temperament
text: Panthers value autonomy, patience and a clean hunt. They object to confinement, humiliating busywork, and pointless cruelty. A trained Panther may be aloof, but responds well to clear purpose, room to stalk, and handlers who do not waste its effort. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Roc
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Roc Species
text: Role: Mobility / Rescue Rocs are aerial control monsters. They trade raw durability for flight, transport, diving attacks and the ability to reposition allies or enemies.

text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 2 3 3 4 Basic Attack: Speed 8 Melee 100% Monster Damage Piercing Command AP Modifier: -1 Movement: Flight

title: Sky Carrier

title: Dive Hunter
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: If the Roc moved at least 5 yards immediately before making a Basic Attack, that Attack deals +15% Final Damage.

title: Wingover
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: After moving at least 4 yards while airborne, the Roc gains +1 Defence against ranged Attacks until its next Action.

title: Airlift
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Effects: The Roc may carry one willing human-sized creature at full Movement. Carrying that creature no longer reduces its Movement from Sky Carrier.

title: Sky Tyrant
text: Unlock: Development 4 — Elder Feature Effects: If the Roc begins at least 5 yards above or away from a target and moves at least 5 yards before its Basic Attack, that Attack deals an additional +25% Final Damage. On a full hit, also inflict Knockback 3 and Prone.

title: Broad Wings
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases flying Movement by 0.1 yard per IC.

title: Dive Hunter
text: Type: Stackable Each rank increases the Basic Attack's Final Damage by 4% if the monster moved at least 5 yards immediately before attacking.

title: Sky Carrier
text: Type: Utility The Roc may carry one additional human-sized willing creature. When carrying more than one creature, fly at half Movement unless Airlift or another rule says otherwise. This Utility Trait may be selected again for another passenger.

title: Far Sight
text: Type: Utility Gain +3 on Awareness checks based on long-distance vision, weather observation or locating large landmarks from the air.

title: Wing Buffer
text: Type: One-Time The monster and adjacent allies reduce forced movement caused by wind by 3 yards, minimum 0.

title: Wingover
text: Type: One-Time Wingover grants +2 Defence against ranged Attacks instead of +1.

title: Talon Snatch
text: Speed: 9 Base Command AP: 7 Effects: Move up to 5 yards, then Attack for 90% Monster Damage. On a hit by 5 or more, the monster may carry a human-sized target 2 yards in any direction; unwilling targets may oppose with Grapple Defence.

title: Gale Wing
text: Speed: 10 Base Command AP: 7 Cone: 6 yards Effects: Creatures in the cone make a Defence against the monster's Accuracy. On failure, suffer Knockback 4; unattended smoke, dust and similar light obscurants are dispersed.

title: Rescue Lift
text: Speed: 4 Interrupt Base Command AP: 6 Range: 4 yards Effects: Trigger: a willing ally would be hit by an Area effect the Roc could physically lift them out of. Move that ally up to 4 yards to a legal space; if this leaves the Area, the Attack no longer targets them.

title: Heavenfall Dive
text: Speed: 13 Base Command AP: 12 Effects: The Roc must begin at least 5 yards above or away from the target. Move up to 10 yards and Attack for 150% Monster Damage. On a full hit, inflict Knockback 5 and Prone.

title: Temperament
text: Rocs require space, height and a clear route to move. They can be trained to enter danger for transport or rescue, but deliberate confinement or repeatedly forcing one into a kill-zone with no route out can trigger Rebellion. ← ALL MONSTER SPECIES

title: Salamander
text: ← MONSTER TAMING RULES ALL SPECIES ↗

title: Salamander Species
text: Role: Control / Survival Salamanders are durable utility monsters, comfortable in hostile environments and difficult to keep injured or displaced.

title: Profile
text: Toughness Aggression Defence Agility --- --- --- --- 3 3 4 2 Basic Attack: Speed 10 Melee 100% Monster Damage Piercing Command AP Modifier: +1 Movement: Ground; swims at normal Movement

title: Regenerative Flesh
text: Unlock: Core Talent Effects: At the start of each of the Salamander's Actions, it restores 2% of its maximum Vitality.

title: Wall Clinger
text: Unlock: Development 1 — Lesser Feature Effects: The Salamander may move across walls and ceilings at half Movement without a check when the surface can physically support it.

title: Mucous Balance
text: Unlock: Development 2 — Greater Feature Effects: The Salamander gains +2 Resistance against Poison, Burns and corrosive environmental effects and reduces forced movement suffered by 2 yards, minimum 0.

title: Tail Shedding
text: Unlock: Development 3 — Elite Feature Limit: Once per battle Effects: After the Salamander would become Grappled, Prone or Immobilized, it may immediately end one of those conditions after the triggering effect resolves.

title: Regenerative Flesh

title: Clinging Toes

title: Wall Clinger

title: Mucous Coat
text: Type: One-Time Mucous Balance's Resistance bonus becomes +4 instead of +2.

title: Adhesive Lunge

title: Monster Taming
text: Monster Taming

title: Monster Taming
text: Monster Taming is the practice of acquiring, training and fielding dangerous creatures. Your monster might be captured during a Hunt, raised from an egg or young, bred for work, rescued, purchased, inherited, or obtained through another appropriate method. However you found it, the result is one named Tamed Monster that grows alongside you. Your Tamed Monster is a separate creature with its own position, Initiative, Vitality and IC track. Its Independent Actions do not spend your AP; Monster Techniques spend Command AP from your AP pool.

title: At a Glance
text: Use Talent Progression to build your partner, Growth for its statistics and Command AP for its trained techniques.

title: Talent Progression
text: Monster Taming is a Capability Talent. Your Source must plausibly give you access to a suitable creature, egg or young, breeder, handler, captured specimen, or another way to acquire and train the monster. Beast Seal: Release is the field-sealing technique used to safely transport and deploy it.

title: Core Talent
text: Choose one Standard Monster Species and create a named Tamed Monster using its profile. Your monster immediately gains that Species' Core Instinct. You may purchase Beast Seal: Release without meeting its normal rank requirement. While your monster is deployed, its prepared Beast Seal lets you sense its rough direction and whether it is conscious, incapacitated, or in immediate danger. You and your monster may communicate simple trained intent whenever normal communication is possible.

title: Developments
text: Each time you take a Monster Taming Development, choose one Tamer Development below, learn one Monster Technique from your monster's Species, and unlock its next Species Feature. You may take each Tamer Development and learn each Monster Technique only once unless stated otherwise. A Standard Species has four Monster Techniques and four Development-locked Species Features. You may normally take at most four Monster Taming Developments.

title: Quick Release
text: Effects: When using Beast Seal: Release to deploy your Tamed Monster, its Chakra cost becomes 20, its final Speed becomes 12, and its final Seal Speed becomes 12. If released after Initiative has begun, its first normal Action occurs 7 IC after appearing instead of 10 IC.

title: Efficient Command
text: Effects: Reduce the Command AP cost of your Tamed Monster's Monster Techniques by 1 after applying Agility, minimum 2.

title: Coordinated Assault
text: Effects: When your Tamed Monster fully hits a creature with an Attack, your next Attack against that creature before the end of your next Non-Interrupt Action gains +2 Accuracy. This benefit cannot stack with itself.

title: Handler's Read
text: Effects: Gain +3 Awareness and Survival when your Tamed Monster can meaningfully assist through its senses, tracking ability or position. You may act on information your monster communicates from things it can perceive but you cannot. This does not remove Visibility or other penalties from your own Attacks.

title: Protective Training
text: Effects: While you are within 3 yards of your Tamed Monster, both of you gain +1 to Defensive Rolls. This bonus ends while either creature is unconscious, helpless or otherwise unable to protect the other.

title: Emergency Release
text: Limit: Once per battle Effects: When using Beast Seal: Release to deploy your Tamed Monster, reduce its final Speed and final Seal Speed by 5, minimum 1. This stacks with Quick Release.

title: Homeward Seal
text: Effects: During a Week's Rest, establish a return formula at a permanent safe location where your Tamed Monster is normally kept, such as a kennel, stable, den, breeder's compound or laboratory. With enough uninterrupted time to perform the ritual, you may transport yourself there along with a number of willing creatures touching you up to 1 + your Monster Taming Developments. Homeward Seal cannot normally be performed during Initiative.

title: Mastery — Master Handler
text: After taking three Monster Taming Developments, gain Master Handler. Once per battle, when your Tamed Monster declares a Monster Technique, you may ignore its Command AP cost. When you do, choose one: gain +2 Accuracy on your next Attack before the end of your next Action; gain +2 to Defensive Rolls until the end of your next Action; or move up to 2 yards after the Technique resolves without spending AP or changing Initiative. This Talent grants one Standard Tamed Monster, not an Apex-class creature. Additional monsters require another explicit reward or rule; the deployment limit still applies.

title: Beast Seal: Release
text: Chakra: 25 Speed: 15 Seal Speed: 15 Range: 2 yards Tags: Utility, Sealing Effects: Release your Tamed Monster from its prepared Beast Seal into an unoccupied space within Range. The Beast Seal is a trained transport and safety tool; it does not control the monster's mind or force obedience. A Tamed Monster remains deployed until recalled, reduced to 0 Vitality, or the scene ends. You may recall it as a Speed 5 Action; the monster may voluntarily return to its Beast Seal as a Speed 5 Action. Recalling and releasing it again during the same scene does not restore Vitality, remove statuses, or refresh once-per-battle effects.

title: Entering Initiative
text: If your Tamed Monster is already present when Initiative is rolled, roll its Initiative normally. If it is released after Initiative begins, its first normal Action occurs 10 IC after it appears. It may use valid defensive Interrupts before then; those Interrupts advance its next Action normally.

title: Defeat and Recovery
text: A Tamed Monster reduced to 0 Vitality is immediately pulled back into its Beast Seal by the seal's safety tether. You cannot deploy it again until you complete a Week's Rest, at which point it returns at full Vitality. Permanent death requires an explicit story event.

title: Growth
text: Your Tamed Monster uses your Total XP. Growth Rank begins at 1 when you reach 1,000 Total XP and increases by 1 for every additional 500 Total XP. Growth Rank: 1 + floor((Total XP - 1,000) / 500), minimum 1 Growth Rank is also the number of Monster Traits your monster has earned. If you learn Monster Taming after 1,000 Total XP, immediately select every Trait your monster currently qualifies for. Total XP Growth Rank Monster Traits --- --- --- 1,000 1 1 1,500 2 2 2,000 3 3 2,500 4 4 3,000 5 5 3,500 6 6 4,000 7 7 4,500 8 8 5,000 9 9 5,500 10 10 6,000 11 11 6,500 12 12 Every +500 XP +1 +1

title: The Four Species Ratings
text: Every Standard Species has four ratings from 1 to 5, totaling 12: Toughness, Aggression, Defence and Agility. These ratings define the Species' base profile; Traits customize the individual partner.

title: Derived Profile
text: Base Vitality: 650 + 125 × (Growth Rank - 1), then apply Toughness Base Accuracy: 21 + (2 × Growth Rank) + 1 for every 2 Growth Ranks, to a maximum of +6; then apply Aggression. Base Defence: 14 + (2 × Growth Rank) + 1 for every 2 Growth Ranks after the first, to a maximum of +4; then apply Defence. Movement: Agility base + 0.1 yard per IC for each Growth Rank after the first Initiative: 1d20 + Agility contribution + floor(Growth Rank / 3) Monster Skill Bonus: 8 + (2 × Growth Rank) Monster Save TN: 17 + (2 × Growth Rank) The Defence value is used for all of the monster's defensive rolls, including Dodge and Parry. A partner initiating a Grapple uses Accuracy; one resisting or maintaining control against a hostile Grapple uses Defence, unless a Trait or Technique says otherwise. Rating Toughness Aggression / Defence --- --- --- 1 75% Vitality -4 2 90% Vitality -2 3 100% Vitality +0 4 115% Vitality +2 5 130% Vitality +4 Agility uses the same 1-5 rating, but its effects are shown separately: Agility Base Move Command AP Initiative --- --- --- --- 1 1.0 yd/IC +2 +2 2 1.2 yd/IC +1 +4 3 1.4 yd/IC +0 +6 4 1.6 yd/IC -1 +8 5 1.8 yd/IC -2 +10 Command AP modifiers apply only to Monster Techniques and other effects that explicitly list a Command AP cost. The adjusted cost cannot be lower than 2 AP.

title: Independent Actions
text: A Tamed Monster has its own IC track and no AP pool of its own. It may use Move, Dodge, Parry, Search, Point Out, Hide when legal, stand up, ordinary object interactions, and its printed Basic Attack without spending your AP. These Actions use their normal or printed Speed and advance the monster on its IC track normally. A Tamed Monster can Parry with its natural weapons as though they were appropriate unarmed weapons. It cannot use player equipment, Jutsu, Talents, Uniques or Clan abilities unless a Species rule explicitly grants them.

title: Command AP
text: Monster Techniques are coordinated trained Monster Actions. When your monster declares one, you pay its listed Base Command AP from your AP pool, modified by the Species' Agility. Paying Command AP does not take an Action and does not change your Initiative. Command AP is a cost, not AP spent to reduce Speed. Neither you nor your monster may spend AP to reduce a monster Action's Speed or Surge a monster roll unless a rule explicitly says otherwise. Command AP still counts as AP you spent for effects that care about AP expenditure. If you cannot pay the Command AP, the Monster Technique cannot be declared. If you are unconscious or otherwise unable to direct your monster, your monster may continue to use Independent Actions and its Basic Attack, but cannot use Monster Techniques. Outside Initiative, ignore Command AP costs.

title: Monster Damage
text: Tamed Monsters use the normal Ember Corps damage structure: Damage Dice + (Damage Bonus × Attack Speed). Their Damage Dice and Monster Damage Bonus come from Growth Rank rather than Attributes. Monster Damage Dice: (4 + ceiling(Growth Rank / 2))d8 Monster Damage Bonus (MDB): 3 + (Growth Rank / 2) When an Attack deals 100% Monster Damage, roll the Monster Damage Dice and add MDB × that Attack's Speed. If an effect deals 70%, 120%, or another percentage of Monster Damage, calculate 100% Monster Damage first, then apply the listed percentage to Final Damage, rounding down. Total XP Growth Rank Damage Dice MDB --- --- --- --- 1,000 1 5d8 3.5 2,500 4 6d8 5.0 4,000 7 8d8 6.5 6,500 12 10d8 9.0 Use each Action’s printed Speed; Agility does not alter it.

title: Monster Rules
text: - A Tamed Monster is a living creature and can be targeted by effects that target creatures or allies. It does not inherit your Attributes, Accuracy, Defence, Damage Bonuses, equipment, Talents, Uniques, Clan effects or temporary modifiers unless a rule explicitly says so. - A Tamed Monster uses Vitality instead of HP and cannot suffer Wounds or trigger Wound-dependent effects. See Defeat and Recovery at 0 Vitality. - Bleed, Burns, Poison, Paralysis, Immobilization, Suffocation and other statuses affect a Tamed Monster normally unless a Species rule says otherwise. - Tamed Monsters are Tireless: their listed Actions require no Stamina or Chakra Exhaustion rolls. - A Standard Tamed Monster is mechanically human-sized for reach, targeting, Grapple and carrying rules unless a Species Feature, Trait or Technique says otherwise. Its appearance may be larger or smaller without changing its mechanical Size. - Natural claws, teeth, horns, shells and similar anatomy cannot be Disarmed. Special movement modes are listed in the Species profile or granted by Species Features and Traits. - You may have only one Standard Tamed Monster active at a time unless a rule explicitly overrides this limit.

title: Species Features
text: Every Standard Species has five innate Species Features. You gain the Core Instinct with the Monster Taming Core Talent. Monster Taming Developments 1–4 then unlock the Lesser, Greater, Elite and Elder Features in order. Species Features are part of your monster's profile, not learned Monster Techniques. They cost no Command AP unless stated otherwise. Actions and Interrupts granted by Species Features are Independent Actions and remain available even if you cannot issue commands.

title: Monster Traits
text: Every Growth Rank grants one Trait from the monster's Species. Traits are chosen when earned and are permanent unless a rebuild or rules update allows them to change.

title: Stackable Trait
text: May be selected any number of times. Each selection adds one rank, and all ranks stack exactly as written.

title: Utility Trait
text: May normally be selected once. If a Utility Trait asks you to choose from several options, you may select it again only to take a different option unless it explicitly says otherwise.

title: One-Time Trait
text: May be selected once. "One-Time" limits how often you may select the Trait, not how often its effect may be used. Any use limit is stated in the Trait itself.

title: Temperament and Rebellion
text: A Tamed Monster is a living creature, not equipment or a mind-controlled tool. Ordinary danger, injury, defeat, retreat, or an imperfect command does not cause Rebellion. A trained monster can be expected to take real risks beside its handler. Rebellion occurs if you deliberately attack your own Tamed Monster, knowingly use it as a disposable suicide piece when a reasonable alternative exists, or knowingly violate its Temperament. Accidental friendly fire does not automatically cause Rebellion; intent and obvious disregard matter. On Rebellion, your monster withdraws into its Beast Seal or otherwise refuses to continue working with you, and cannot be fielded again until your next Week's Rest. Repeated or extreme mistreatment may have story consequences, but permanent loss of a paid Talent should only occur through an agreed story event or rebuild.

These benefits require the protecting monster to be able to act.

title: Rank Benefits
text: Rank Benefits

title: Rank Benefits
text: Corps ranks reflect training, responsibility and service to Haven Ember. Strays gain no Rank Benefits. On reaching Trailhand, Huntsman, Warden or Legend, gain that rank’s Automatic Benefit and choose one benefit from that rank or a lower rank. Each benefit may be selected once unless stated otherwise. A Talent that grants a Rank Benefit teaches the selected ability; it does not confer the rank, office or authority associated with it.

title: Stray
text: Strays train under veteran Hunters and have not yet earned Rank Benefits.

title: Trailhand
text: Trailhands are trusted to take assignments beyond Ember’s walls without constant supervision.

title: Take Point — Automatic
text: When you are the designated leader of a group, you may give a specific order to another Hunter up to 3 + XP/1000 times per in-character week. They gain +3 to one relevant roll made directly to carry out that order. If applicable, an ordered attack instead gains +3 Accuracy. Give a specific order, such as “Pin its left leg.” An attack order must name its subtype, such as “Use a damaging Katon Area attack.”

title: Something to Come Home To
text: Choose a promise, principle, person, or purpose that keeps you moving when you should have stopped. The GMs must approve your choice. Once every 7 OOC days, while directly acting in accordance with it, you may reset your Chakra Exhaustion and Stamina penalties to 0 and reduce your Fatigue by 1. If you knowingly betray that principle, you cannot use this Benefit for 14 OOC days.

title: Too Stubborn to Quit
text: You may spend multiple points of Willpower, activations of Limit Break, or similar effects on the same roll, limited only by what you have available.

title: Bring Them Home
text: Whenever an ally is Severely Wounded, Critically Wounded, or reduced to 0 HP, you may trigger this Benefit. Until after your next non-Interrupt Action, you ignore penalties from Fatigue and non-damaging Status Effects. Any Genjutsu currently affecting you is purged, and you gain +5 to defensive Genjutsu rolls during this time. Multiple triggers overlap, but do not stack.

title: Wasteland Conditioning
text: Whenever you Rest, reduce your Stamina penalty by 1 additional point and reduce Suffocation by 1. You may also spend Willpower to reroll a Fatigue Check. Doing so causes you to succeed, making the result of your dice the exact number you needed to pass, even if that number is above 20.

title: Trailwise
text: Once per Hunt, when you fail a Track, Research, Study Weakness or Prepare roll, you may reroll it. You must keep the new result.

title: Hard Country
text: As a Speed 0 Action, you may activate or deactivate this Benefit. While active, halve the numerical penalties caused by Fatigue and non-damaging Status Effects. You may maintain this for a total of 50 IC per battle. These ICs do not need to be consecutive.

title: Huntsman
text: Huntsmen lead expeditions, patrol Ember’s outer territory and train Strays.

title: Pass It Down — Automatic
text: You may formally train other Hunters in Jutsu you know, allowing them to learn techniques one rank beyond their normal imitation limit. Training takes one week per rank of the technique. You may also teach eligible Capability Talents you possess. This requires one month of training; the student gains the Talent immediately, but their next Talent must be spent paying for it. A character may only owe one Talent at a time.

title: Second Nature
text: If your DEX and always-active Uniques alone could reduce the Seal Speed of a Ninjutsu you know to 0, you may perform it without handseals. This does not apply to Genjutsu, Medical Ninjutsu or Sealing Ninjutsu.

title: Long Haul
text: Your bonus to Chakra Exhaustion and Stamina rolls from Fatigue increases by +2 per Fatigue category.

title: Call the Hunt
text: As a Speed 10 Action that cannot be reduced by AP, you may call out up to two Orders. Allies may choose whether to obey. These benefits last 50 IC, or until you issue another order this way. Fallback: +3 to Defensive rolls while withdrawing. An ally making a hostile Action loses this Order’s benefit until Call the Hunt ends. Mark It: +2 Accuracy on the next attack against a target within 3 yards of you. Regroup: +25% Movement while moving toward you or a point within 3 yards of you. Hold: Gain RES/2 Damage Reduction while within 3 yards of you.

title: Know What You're Killing
text: After your Hunting Team successfully completes Study Weakness against a creature, you gain +2 Accuracy against that creature for the resulting Hunt. Your damage against it is also treated as +25% higher for determining Wounds.

title: Take the Hit
text: Once per fight, after seeing the damage of an attack against you, you may spend 1 Willpower to halve the final damage taken.

title: Pack Hunter
text: When an ally successfully damages an enemy, your next attack against that same enemy gains +2 Accuracy. This cannot trigger from your own attacks and does not stack with itself.

title: Warden
text: Wardens oversee work vital to the Haven: research, medicine, supplies, engineering, archives and reconnaissance.

title: A Useful Trade — Automatic
text: Choose one Skill appropriate to your work as a Warden. You gain Specialization in that Skill if you did not already possess it. Your maximum ranks in that Skill increase by 3. When its natural d20 result is below 10, treat the die as a 10.

title: Practiced Hands
text: Whenever you spend Willpower to reroll a Skill Roll, add +5 to the final result. You also possess 1 temporary Willpower which can only be used to reroll Skill Rolls and recovers normally.

title: Quartermaster
text: Whenever you purchase ordinary consumable equipment or field supplies, you receive twice the normal quantity for the same price. This does not apply to Exploding Tags, permanent equipment, weapons, armor or unique items.

title: Expedition Planner
text: Once per Hunt, when a member of your Hunting Team fails a Track, Research, Study Weakness or Prepare roll, you may order a reroll with +3. The new result must be kept.

title: Field Notes
text: Once per Hunt, when you personally succeed on Research or Study Weakness, generate 1 additional Intel of the same type.

title: Keep Them Working
text: As a Speed 5 Action, you may end one instance of Stun or Paralysis affecting an ally you can reach and assist.

title: Contingency
text: Once per battle, after you fail a non-Attack Skill Roll, Fatigue Check, or defensive roll against an environmental hazard, you may declare a contingency and reroll it with +5. You must keep the second result.

title: Legend
text: Legends are Hunters whose deeds have become part of Haven Ember’s history.

title: A Name That Carries — Automatic
text: Within Haven Ember and settlements familiar with its Hunters, your identity is common knowledge. When your reputation would reasonably help you, gain +5 to social Skill Rolls involving authority, trust or intimidation. People may not like you. They have still heard the stories.

title: First to Move
text: Regardless of your Initiative roll, your first Action in combat always occurs on IC 0.

title: One Clean Hit
text: Once per battle, when Partial Defense would apply against your attack, you may spend 1 Willpower to ignore all effects of Partial Defense for that attack. Declare this before rolling damage. If the target subsequently avoids the attack entirely, the Willpower is not spent.

title: Marked Quarry
text: Choose one person or creature as your Quarry after spending significant time studying them. You gain +6 Survival to track them, +5 Awareness and Espionage against them, +3 Accuracy against them, and +25% Damage for determining Wounds against them. While fighting your Quarry, you gain 1 temporary Willpower, and another every 50 IC. You may only have one Quarry at a time. It takes a Downtime slot to change quarry.

title: Perfect Ambush
text: When attacking someone completely unaware of your presence, your attack gains +4 Accuracy and +25% Damage. You also prepare Sneak Attacks in half the normal required time. This cannot be used simply by hiding from somebody who already knows they are fighting you.

title: Still Standing
text: Once per fight, after taking damage, you may spend 1 Willpower to halve the final damage taken. If this would still reduce you to 0 HP, you may instead remain at 1 HP. Using the second effect exhausts this Benefit for the remainder of the fight.

title: Against the Impossible
text: When entering battle against a Dread-class or greater Beast, gain 1 temporary Willpower. Every 50 IC you remain actively engaged with that creature, regain that temporary Willpower if it has been spent.

title: Living Myth
text: When you spend a point of Willpower, choose one ally who can see or hear you. That ally gains 1 temporary Willpower which lasts until the end of the battle. A character can only benefit from your Living Myth once per battle.

title: Talents, Ranks & Hunter Classes
text: Milestone talents and rank benefits for long-term character growth.

title: Introduction
text: Talents grant rare training or exceptional aptitude. They cost Talent Points rather than XP.

title: Acquiring Talents
text: Gain one Talent Point at 1,000, 2,500, 4,000, 5,000 and 6,500 total XP, then every 1,500 XP thereafter. A character at 3,000 XP has two Talent Points. Unspent points may be saved. Learn each Talent once unless its entry explicitly allows multiple selections. Further points normally purchase Developments.

title: Learning and Deepening Talents
text: Whenever you gain a Talent Point, choose one of the following: Learn a Talent — Gain the Core Talent of a Talent you do not already possess. Deepen a Talent — Choose one Development from a Talent you already possess. Unless stated otherwise, a Development may only be selected once. When you possess three Developments from the same Talent, you automatically gain that Talent's Mastery. Mastery does not cost an additional Talent Point. Talent-granted Actions follow the normal Speed, cost and timing rules unless they state an explicit exception. Use the Core Speed limits.

title: Enhancements and Capabilities
text: Enhancements represent aptitude, conditioning or personal development. They require no external Source. Capabilities require a suitable Source of knowledge or training. This may be a mentor, recovered manual, training record, specimen, faction or discovery relevant to that Talent. A GM confirms that the Source meets its requirements. Use Mentoring to find a teacher through Downtime. The same Source may teach Developments unless an entry requires additional training or another discovery.

title: Team Attacks
text: Team Attacks

title: Team Attacks
text: Two to four Hunters may prepare a combined Attack. Each contributes one damaging Attack they can legally perform and names a lead attacker. Each Hunter may participate in only one Team Attack at a time. Clones, Puppets and Tamed Monsters do not provide additional Hunter slots or preparation contributions.

title: Preparation
text: Each Hunter joins on their own turn by entering a Variable Speed Utility Action. Declare the component Attack, its costs, Links, AP expenditure and final Speed at that point. Required handseals must be completed before joining. Pay the Attack's costs when joining; ammunition and consumables are committed then. Effects that require a target to be in Range are checked at release. The preparation target equals the sum of the components' final Speeds. Each IC a Hunter remains preparing contributes 1 toward that shared target. Every participating Hunter must join, pay their costs and contribute at least 1 IC before release. The total cannot be reduced by AP, time already spent on handseals, Delay or waiting before joining. Each participant also completes their component's Delay while preparing; release waits for both the shared target and every component's Delay to be complete. All components and the maximum four participants must be declared before the first preparation IC is credited. Hunters whose turns occur later may join the declared preparation when their turn arrives. Their component contributes to the target immediately but they contribute no IC before joining. Calculate every final Speed after applying the declared shared Links, then fix the preparation target before crediting its first IC. A participant may use Defensive Interrupts. Their preparation pauses for that Interrupt's final Speed; it resumes when their next action becomes available if they remain able to prepare. An Offensive Interrupt, another non-defensive Action, incapacitation or voluntary withdrawal removes their component and credited preparation. Recalculate the target for the remaining team. Paid costs are not refunded. If fewer than two remain, preparation ends. A team cannot release during resolution of an incoming Attack; finish that Attack and its defenses first.

title: Release
text: At the end of the IC that completes preparation, the lead declares the attack base using one component's printed attack form, Range and Area: targeted Melee, targeted Ranged, or AoE. Every component must be able to reach every chosen target from its contributor's position. A targeted component cannot be multiplied across an AoE; an AoE base requires every component to support that Area and its targets. Use the smallest legal Area where they differ. Any component that cannot legally contribute at release is removed and preparation is recalculated. Use the lead component's final Accuracy, including shared Links, for the combined Attack. Rank and defensive Speed are the highest component rank and final Speed. Combine all Keywords. A defense must be legal against the complete Attack: a projectile-only parry cannot stop a combined projectile-and-melee Attack, for example. AoE Parries must explicitly permit AoE defense and grant no Partial Defense. Parries against a non-AoE Team Attack use normal Partial Defense unless the Attack itself prohibits it. Each target declares one Defense against the entire Attack. Rolled-Accuracy Ballistic contributions prohibit Partial Defense for the whole Team Attack unless every Ballistic contributor chose Controlled Fire. If the lead component is rolled Accuracy, roll once at release. Every participant becomes free to act on the following IC; the preparation already paid the Attack's action time.

title: Damage, Links and Effects
text: Calculate each component's damage once using its own user's stats and its own final Speed, then sum the damage. The highest Speed is used for defense validity only. Shared Links modify each eligible component once, and their costs are paid once by the owner. Ownership of an ability or passive does not transfer; only declared Attack Links are shared. Each Link must be legal for every component it affects, with required resources supplied by its owner. Identical named Links apply once at their highest chosen value; mutually exclusive Links cannot be combined. Apply the one Defense's result to all components. Apply percentage mitigation and type-specific Armor to the relevant components; apply general flat DR and other once-per-Attack reductions once to the total. Allocate flat reductions proportionally across components, with rounding remainder assigned to the largest component. Determine one Wound from total damage: use the type contributing the most damage after mitigation, ties chosen by the lead. Apply a Wounding modifier only to its source component before totaling damage for Wounds. A location must be reachable by all components; a Called Shot requires every contributor to declare and pay its Called Shot penalty. Repeated instances of the same status use the highest severity and longest duration, rather than adding together. Different statuses may apply normally. Effects requiring a Special roll are rolled once per distinct status by the contributor supplying its highest severity. Each weapon gains matchup WDP only from its own contact with resistant armor. Once-per-Attack effects and Chain progression trigger once per contributor. A contributor may not add attacks created by this Team Attack back into the same Team Attack.

title: Combination Effects
text: Choose one combination benefit when releasing. An Attack can gain only one benefit, regardless of its number of qualifying pairs. - Concentrated Impact: Two components with the same physical damage type gain +10% damage against Armor Durability and breakable monster parts only. This does not increase damage to the creature's Vitality or HP. - Mixed Assault: Two different physical damage types reduce the Called Shot penalty by 1 for all contributors, if all target the same location. - Elemental Reinforcement: Two components with the same primary element gain +10% Final Damage on those components. - Elemental Combination: Katon + Fuuton, Suiton + Raiton, or Doton + Katon grant +10% Wounding on those two components. Choose one qualifying pair. This does not create a bloodline element or transfer elemental passives between components.

title: Example
text: Three Hunters contribute Speed 8, 10 and 12 Attacks: 30 preparation IC are needed. If they all join on IC 20 and remain uninterrupted, they contribute 3 per IC and release at the end of IC 30. The Attack is Speed 12 for defense validity. Its damage is calculated separately at Speeds 8, 10 and 12, then combined; each target makes one Defense.

title: Uniques
text: Rare gifts, habits, talents, and training that make one hunter different from another. “Two hunters can learn the same technique. They should never feel like the same person.”

title: Uniques
text: Uniques are unusual talents, habits, gifts, and kinds of training that set one hunter apart from another. They grant abilities and advantages that ordinary XP purchases usually cannot. At character creation you receive 6 Unique Points (UP). Heritage Cost from Volume III is paid from this same pool. Any UP you do not spend may be saved. Creation Uniques cost 1 UP each, may only be taken during character creation, and you may have no more than two. Clan Creation Uniques follow the same rules and count toward that maximum. After character creation, gain 1 additional UP at 2,000, 3,000, 4,500, 6,000, and 7,000 total XP. UP cannot be spent during combat or an event. Some Uniques list Upgrades Into or Upgrades From. If you own the earlier Unique, you may replace it with the later one by paying only the difference in UP cost. The old Unique and its effects are removed and the new Unique takes its place. You never have to follow an upgrade path; if you can take the later Unique normally, you may buy it directly for its full cost. Buying a later Unique does not grant a Creation Unique you did not choose at character creation. Unless an entry says otherwise, a Unique may be taken only once.

title: Analyst
text: Upgrades Into: Applied Knowledge You have a habit of watching before you act. Gain +5 Awareness. Rather than gaining AP every 20 IC in combat, you gain 60% as much (rounded up) every 10 IC. When the same creature uses the same broad kind of Attack against you consecutively—Katon into Katon, Weapon Taijutsu into Weapon Taijutsu, and so on—gain +1 on your Defensive roll and 1 AP, stacking for each consecutive use. Track this separately for each attacker; changing attack type resets it. You gain 5 Research ranks and 5 to your Max Research Ranks. Your tendency to stop and think gives you -4 Athletics and -2 to Dodge. Additionally, you reduce the Downtime TN of any roll that would use your Research by an amount equal to your Research Ranks + 10.

title: Berserker
text: You are difficult to frighten, difficult to stop, and not especially interested in avoiding a clean hit when you can answer with one of your own. Add RES × 2 to maximum Vitality. Berserk Counter — Speed 0 Interrupt: when an enemy attacks you, you may take no Defense. If the Attack does not incapacitate you, immediately use a Taijutsu Attack you know against that attacker. The counter gains +3 Accuracy, is made at half its normal final Speed, rounded up, to a minimum of 3, cannot have its Speed reduced further, and its Base Speed cannot exceed the Base Speed of the Attack that triggered it. Pay all normal costs. For every 25% of maximum Vitality you are missing, your Taijutsu deals +5% Final Damage, maximum +20%. When reduced to 10% Vitality or below, choose whether to surrender or keep fighting; if you keep fighting, you cannot willingly stop until every hostile creature you are fighting has been incapacitated or you are. Suffer -5 Stealth.

title: Chakra Sensitive
text: Even before formal sensor training, chakra has always been something you could feel. Increase current and maximum Chakra Control ranks by 3. Your passive sensing range is CHA × 2 yards. Within it, you can tell when an unfamiliar chakra source appears or disappears, feel whether a visible creature is maintaining Upkeep, and recognize a chakra signature you have personally sensed before. Scan — Speed 8: make Chakra Control opposed by Chakra Control or Espionage against any creatures you choose in range. A creature suffers a penalty equal to the total Upkeep it is maintaining. On success, know its exact location and whether its chakra feels weaker, stronger, or roughly comparable to yours. A creature you detect this way is not Hidden from you until the end of your next Action unless an effect specifically conceals chakra sensing. Suffer -4 Resistance. Upgrades Into: Chakra Sensor

title: Chosen One
text: Your character possesses an unusual personal gift. Submit its origin and proposed mechanics to the Storyteller team before approval. The gift should be recognisable in play and comparable in scope to a Core Talent. This Unique grants only the approved effects; its story does not waive other prerequisites or restrictions.

title: Competitive
text: Winning matters to you more than it probably should. Gain +2 on d20 rolls and +5% Final Damage with Attacks. Whenever you miss with an Attack, gain +1 Accuracy and suffer -1 on other d20 rolls, stacking to +5 Accuracy and -5 on other d20 rolls. Both reset when you hit with an Attack. Whenever your Fatigue level increases, gain 5 AP and +5 on your next Stamina or Chakra Exhaustion roll before the end of your next Action.

title: Defender
text: You have trained to make hitting you a poor decision. Gain DR equal to RES/3 and Block becomes a Speed 4 Interrupt. Whenever a damage-dealing adjacent unarmed Attack hits you, the attacker takes RES/2 damage after its Attack resolves; this damage cannot Wound. When you Block consecutive attacks of the same broad discipline, increase your Block percentage by 10 percentage points for each consecutive Block after the first, up to five increases. Changing your defensive response or the incoming discipline resets this bonus. Block cannot exceed 100%. Treat damage you take as 10% lower when determining Wounds, or 25% lower when you Block. Your caution carries into your offense: your Attacks count as 10% lower for determining Wounds. Upgrades Into: Protector

title: Energetic
text: You run longer, fight longer, and recover faster than most people can tolerate being around. You have 6 Fatigue levels instead of 5 and suffer ordinary Fatigue penalties as though you were one category lower while keeping the normal benefits of your actual Fatigue. Whenever you Rest, reduce Stamina Penalty by 1 additional point. Your inability to sit still makes careful study harder. Reduce the maximum rank of every Skill by 2.

title: Genius
text: Hunter techniques make sense to you in a way they simply do not to most people. Reduce the XP cost of Jutsu you learn by 25%, rounded up. You may learn Jutsu one Rank higher than your normal Rank limit, but this never bypasses a Talent, Ability, Aptitude, Heritage, or technique-specific requirement. Additionally, you gain advantage (2d20kh1) when rolling to make any roll relating to learning new things. A Jutsu you could not use without Genius costs +3 Chakra or Stamina each time you use it. Skill Focus has Scale 3 for you. You gain Specialization in every skill without paying its XP cost or meeting its rank prerequisite. These granted Specializations treat natural d20 results below 8 as 8 on non-combat skill rolls only; they do not apply to combat skill actions, offensive rolls, defensive rolls or status checks. Buying ordinary Specialization in a skill grants its normal use during combat; the two floors do not stack.

title: Juggernaut
text: You are built to absorb punishment and keep advancing. Use STR/14 instead of STR/18 for Physical Damage Bonus. Gain DR equal to STR/5 and reduce Stun applied to you by STR/20, after other reductions. All movement you receive is reduced by 10%, including ordinary movement, movement from Jutsu, and forced movement.

title: Large
text: You are bigger, heavier, or simply built on a scale most hunters are not. Use STR/10 instead of STR/18 for Physical Damage Bonus. Physical Attacks gain +1 yard Reach, add RES to maximum Vitality and maximum HP, and gain +3 on Stamina rolls. Attacks benefiting from this Unique have +1 Base Speed, and gain 1 Delay. Incompatible With: Small

title: Lucky
text: Things have an irritating habit of working out for you. Outside combat, roll 2d20 and keep the higher result on ordinary d20 rolls. You have 2 + total XP/750 Luck rerolls each in-character day, rounded down. Spend 1 after a roll to reroll your own eligible roll or a willing ally's; spend 2 to force a hostile creature to reroll an eligible roll. When you have no Luck rerolls remaining, suffer -2 Accuracy and -2 on d20 rolls until they refresh.

title: Naturalist
text: You understand the living world better than books ever taught you. Increase maximum Survival ranks by 3 and gain +3 to detect, disarm, or avoid traps. Use CHA/13 instead of CHA/18 for Ninjutsu Damage Bonus. Gain +1 on Chakra Exhaustion rolls per Rank of the Jutsu being used. You also gain the ability to communicate simple ideas with beasts, creatures and natural animals such as birds and bears. When rolling checks related to studying non-human creatures, you gain advantage. You may learn ordinary Elemental Ninjutsu using Survival alone: 5 ranks for D-rank, 10 for C-rank, 20 for B-rank and 30 for A-rank. This replaces the Chakra Control, Ninshou and combined skill requirements. Elemental Affinity reduces the Survival requirement by its rank. Reduce maximum Research ranks by 3. You also suffer a -3 to all Genjutsu Rolls

title: Nimble
text: Your body is built around never being where the hit lands. Gain +1 Accuracy and +1 on Defensive rolls. Reduce Base Speed of your non-Variable, non-Interrupt Actions by 1, minimum 3. When you are hit cleanly, however, it hurts. Damage against you counts as 10% higher when determining Wounds.

title: Small
text: You are short, light, and very difficult to pin down. Gain +2 Dodge and your Dodge Interrupt is Speed 1. If an effect raises Dodge Speed, you may still use Dodge even when that increase would normally make it too slow to be a valid Defense. Halve the Dodge penalty caused by being unable to reach the edge of an Area Attack, maximum penalty -10. Reduce maximum Vitality by RES. Incompatible With: Large

title: Skilled Hunter
text: Gain bonus Skill Points equal to total XP divided by 80, rounded down, in addition to the normal one Skill Point per 20 XP. When purchasing Skill Focus, reduce the number of ranks already held in that particular Skill Focus by floor(total XP/1,000), minimum 0, for its Scale calculation only. Your actual ranks, prerequisites and global surcharge are unchanged. Recalculate the cost of all purchased Skill Focus ranks at your current total XP; freed Skill Points may be reassigned between scenes. For example, at 2,000 XP you have 100 base Skill Points plus 25 bonus Skill Points. Your first three ranks in each Skill Focus cost its base 2 Skill Points each before the global surcharge. Later ranks resume normal scaling. Skilled Hunter has no Accuracy penalty.

title: Specialist
text: You have chosen one part of hunters combat and pushed it further than most people ever will. Choose Taijutsu, Ninjutsu, or Genjutsu as your Specialty. Choose one of the remaining two as your Incompetence. Taijutsu Specialty: +2 Taijutsu Accuracy, -2 Stamina cost with Taijutsu and Kenjutsu, minimum 1, and +10% Final Damage with them. Ninjutsu Specialty: +2 Ninjutsu Accuracy, -2 Chakra cost with Ninjutsu, minimum 1, and +10% Final Damage with them. Genjutsu Specialty: +3 on Genjutsu offense rolls and TNs, -2 Chakra cost with Genjutsu, minimum 1, and +10% Final Damage where applicable. Your Incompetence suffers -2 Accuracy, or -3 Genjutsu offense, costs +2 Chakra or Stamina, and deals -10% Final Damage where applicable. You also suffer a -2 to all defensive rolls against your Incompetence, or -3 to Genjutsu Defence. Upgrades Into: Pinnacle

title: Strong-Willed
text: When things go wrong, you have a habit of continuing anyway. Reduce the total temporary penalty to any Accuracy, Stamina, Chakra Exhaustion, or other d20 roll by 1. This does not reduce penalties printed as part of the Action or Jutsu itself, nor penalties from another Unique. You may ignore the mechanical penalties of one Wound you currently possess. When you suffer a new Wound, choose whether to continue ignoring the old one or ignore the new one instead. Gain +2 Genjutsu Defense. After failing Genjutsu Defense against a Genjutsu you recognized, spend 1 Willpower as a Speed 0 Interrupt to immediately end that Genjutsu on yourself. You cannot suffer from fear-based penalties. Upgrades Into: Surging Power

title: Surgeon
text: You know exactly where a body fails. Damaging Attacks count as +20% higher for determining Wounds. Non-AoE Called Shots suffer no additional Accuracy penalty. When making a Called Shot, you may declare a maximum Wound severity, including none; a Wound above that maximum is reduced by one severity. Begin with 5 Medicine ranks, or raise Medicine to 5 if it was lower, without spending Skill Points. Gain another Medicine rank for every full 200 total XP, up to your normal maximum. Suffer -1 on Defensive rolls. Upgrades Into: Combat Medic

title: Warder
text: You have trained to meet attacks head-on and brush them aside. Parry becomes a Speed 2 Interrupt and gains +2. Jutsu-based defenses that use an Accuracy roll gain +2 Accuracy and reduce Base Speed by 2, minimum 1. You may Parry weapons with your bare hands and Parry unarmed Attacks with a weapon. Whenever you parry an attack with your hands or a weapon, you may immediately make an attack of a speed equal to your Parry’s Final Speed, with an Accuracy of your Parry Roll. This attack deals damage equal to your Relevant Damage Bonus the final speed of the attack. Suffer -4 Dodge.

title: Clan Creation Uniques
text: These Uniques require the listed Primary Heritage. They cost 1 UP, may only be taken during character creation, and count toward the normal maximum of two Creation Uniques.

title: Sarutobi — A Thousand Lessons
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Sarutobi Choose two different broad disciplines from Weapon, Taijutsu, Ninjutsu, and Genjutsu. For every 200 XP that you earn, you may learn 1 technique from your chosen discipline with a Rank equal to your Maxumum Known Rank - 1, at no cost.. Whenever your previous hostile Action used a different broad discipline from the hostile Action you are declaring, gain +2 Accuracy and +2 on its Stamina or Chakra Exhaustion roll.

title: Fūma — Demon-Wind Savant
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Fūma Thrown Weapon Attacks gain +2 Accuracy and +20 yards maximum Range. After a thrown weapon misses or is Dodged, redirect one projectile to a second legal target within 10 yards at -1 Accuracy; it deals 75% Final Damage. If there is no second target, curve it back toward the original target for a second Defense at -3 Accuracy and 50% Final Damage.

title: Yotsuki — Thunder Bodyguard
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Yotsuki Take the Hit may include up to 4+(XP/100) yards of movement toward the protected creature. After a successful interception, gain +3 on the roll for your first valid Defensive Interrupt against the intercepted Attack and reduce Final Damage that reaches you by 15%. If you fully defend, the protected ally may immediately move up to 3 yards without increasing IC.

title: Ouyoku — Star-Sight Prodigy
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Ouyoku Junsugan activation is Speed 0 and its Upkeep is reduced by 2, minimum 0. Ignore the Visibility penalty from distance, darkness, smoke, or weather in addition to Junsugan's normal benefits. Search through Junsugan at Speed 0; on success, that creature cannot become Hidden from you by mundane means until the end of your next Action.

title: Karatachi Family — Mist Commander
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Karatachi Family Reduce Visibility penalties from mist, smoke, darkness, and weather by 4 for Awareness, Attack, and defensive rolls. Allies within 10 yards who can hear you reduce those same penalties by 2. Once per battle while inside mist or smoke, issue a Speed 3 command; up to two willing allies may immediately Search or move up to 3 yards without increasing IC.

title: Funato — Child of Open Water
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Funato While in a natural body of water, gain +2 Accuracy, +2 Dodge, +30% Movement, and +3 on Chakra Exhaustion rolls for Suiton. You may fight, make seals, and use ordinary equipment underwater without penalties caused solely by being submerged. A Suiton using at least 20 gallons of natural water reduces final Speed by 3 and Chakra cost by 5, minimum 1.

title: Iburi — Cohesive Smoke
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Iburi Smoke Body's Upkeep is reduced by 3, minimum 0. While active, ordinary forced movement against you is quartered, and you may pass through bars, mundane restraints, narrow openings, and gaps that smoke could reasonably traverse as ordinary movement. A Fūton Attack must fully hit to forcibly end Smoke Body.

title: Shiin — Memory Needle
text: Requires: Primary Heritage: Shiin Kioku Sōshitsu gains +3 Accuracy and reduces final Speed by 2. On a full hit, you may block one memory as normal, two closely linked details from the same event, or the target's memory of one creature's current position and most recent Action for 10 IC. A target gains no cumulative bonus to recovery merely from having attempted recovery before.

title: Kodon — Perfect Metabolizer
